 - This role is ideal for students interested in robotics, drones, mechatronics, and embedded systems, who enjoy hands-on work with hardware and system integration.

 - The intern will support the development team by assembling UAV platforms, integrating sensors and communication devices, and assisting with system-level bench and flight testing.



Responsibilities

 - Assist in assembling and maintaining UAV platforms used for research and development

 - Support integration of sensors, cameras, radios, and communication modules

 - Perform wiring, soldering, and hardware setup for onboard electronics

 - Help verify hardware functionality (power, communication, sensor outputs)

 - Assist with bench testing and flight testing preparation

 - Support integration of hardware with onboard compute systems

 - Help document wiring diagrams, system configurations, and integration procedures

 - Assist with scripting or software tasks when required (e.g., device testing, logging)

 - Travel to support field flight testing operations (~20% of the time)



Required Qualifications

 - Pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Robotics, Mechatronics, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or related field

 - Strong interest in robotics systems and UAVs

 - Basic knowledge of electronics and electrical systems

 - Experience with wiring, connectors, or soldering

 - Familiarity with Linux and basic programming (Python or C++)

 - Experience with ROS2

 - Ability to work hands-on with hardware and troubleshoot issues



Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience with drones or robotics platforms

 - Familiarity with embedded systems or microcontrollers

 - Experience with communication protocols (UART, SPI, CAN, I2C)

 - Experience with PX4 autopilot

 - Experience integrating sensors or cameras



What You'll Gain

 - Hands-on experience working with real UAV platforms

 - Exposure to sensor integration and autonomous system development

 - Opportunity to work alongside engineers developing next-generation autonomous vehicles

 - Experience with hardware-software integration in robotics systems

Applied Intuition, Inc. is powering the future of physical AI. Founded in 2017 and now valued at $15 billion, the Silicon Valley company is creating the digital infrastructure needed to bring intelligence to every moving machine on the planet. Applied Intuition services the automotive, defense, trucking, construction, mining and agriculture industries in three core areas: tools and infrastructure, operating systems, and autonomy. Applied Intuition is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, with offices in Washington, D.C.; San Diego; Ft. Walton Beach, Florida; Ann Arbor, Michigan; London; Stuttgart; Munich; Stockholm; Bangalore; Seoul; and Tokyo. Learn more at applied.co http://applied.co.

This in-office expectation does not apply to contractor positions


ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are looking for multiple passionate Research Interns to join the Research Group at Applied Intuition. The mission of the group is to create cutting-edge technology enabling next-generation physical AI, with emphasis on the two most challenging applications reshaping our everyday life: end-to-end autonomous driving and robotic generalist. We have a group composed of leading experts from top institutions and companies, recognized for their exceptional academic and industry contributions—including eight Best Paper awards at premier conferences and journals such as CVPR and ICRA. Learn more at appliedintuition.com/research.

Supported by industry-leading tools and infra, researchers can access millions of miles of data from large fleets, and deploy methods they develop into various autonomous and robotic systems including self-driving cars/trucks, autonomous mining/construction machines, humanoid robots and dexterous hands. In addition to your research contributions, you will contribute to and learn from best practices in the autonomy and robotics industries within our fast-paced and customer-focused culture. Improvements deployed to our system immediately help our customers with their programs and deliver value to our business.


AT APPLIED INTUITION, YOU WILL:

 - Conduct research on pretraining world-action foundation model with various world modalities including vision and physics associated with ego actions, serving the purpose for both robot action and simulation world generation.

 - Diving into relevant topics such as vision-physics modality association, feed-forward Gaussian splatting, world foundation model, human data incorporation, language modality, and spatial reasoning, deformable object modeling and simulation.

 - Work closely with the Research Scientists and Engineers on high quality research publications for submission to top-tier conferences


WE’RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS:

 - Strong research background and skills on relevant topics, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively on projects

 - Current PhD (or MSc) studies in machine learning, computer vision and graphics, robotics

 - 1+ year of research experience in autonomy, self-driving, or related field

 - Passion for next-generation, scalable autonomy and robotics

Don’t meet every single requirement? If you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

- Centific Physical AI Center of Excellence (PACE) build the hardware and software that powers robotics data collection — teleoperation, annotation, and model evaluation. - 3D-print, assemble, wire, and bench-test prototypes alongside our lab technician.
- Document hardware specs, BOMs, and reproducible setup procedures.

About Marvell
Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.
At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead.
Your Team, Your Impact
Marvell’s Physical Design teams span across multiple domains, giving you the opportunity to work on technologies that power next-generation cloud, AI, storage, and networking solutions. Some teams focus their design work on supporting architecture to GDSII (Graphic Data System) implementation of ASIC and processor designs. Other teams focus on timing analysis for future designs of our next-gen high-performance data center chips in a leading-edge CMOS process technology. Across all groups, you’ll collaborate with your direct team and cross-functional partners, working through technical design challenges to ensure we meet the performance, power, and area requirements of an active design.
What You Can Expect
- Perform synthesis, floor planning, place and route, clock insertion, timing analysis, and timing closure on complex logic blocks using industry standard EDA tools ( PrimeTime , Tempus)
- Write scripts in Python, TCL, Perl, and Shell to aid design and development activities
- Utilize problem solving skills to analyze, debug, and implement fixes for design violations using CAD tools
- Collaborate with RTL, S ynthesis, and other D esign teams to resolve congestion & timing bottleneck s, and ensure that all designs converge & integrate in a timely manner
What We're Looking For
- Currently enrolled in a Maste r' s Degree in Ele ctrical Engineeri ng , Computer Engineering, or a related field with an expected graduation date between Fall 2027 – Summer 2028
- Completed courses focusing on VLSI, digital logic, circuit design, computer architecture, RTL synthesis, V erilog or S ystemVerilog , place and route, static timing analysis, digital systems, or microelectronics
- Proficiency in programming & scripting languages like Python, TCL, Perl, and Shell
- Experience working in a Unix type environment
- Experience using tool s like Synopsys ( PrimeTime ) , Cadence ( Tempus ), and Mentor
- Strong analysis, problem solving, and communication skills
Expected Base Pay Range (USD)
34 - 68, $ per hour.
The successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location and market conditions. The expected base pay range for this role may be modified based on market conditions.
This role is eligible to participate in Marvell's bonus and equity plans, including a new hire equity grant and annual equity refreshers, ensuring you are rewarded for your contributions and remain invested in the company's long-term success.
Additional Compensation and Benefit Elements
Marvell is committed to providing exceptional, comprehensive benefits that support our employees at every stage - from internship to retirement and through life’s most important moments. Our offerings are built around four key pillars: financial well-being, family support, mental and physical health, and recognition. Highlights for our interns: medical, dental, and vision coverage, perks and discounts, robust mental health resources to prioritize emotional well-being, and paid holidays. Additional compensation may be available for intern PhD candidates. We look forward to sharing more with you during the interview process.
All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status.
Any applicant who requires a reasonable accommodation during the selection process should contact Marvell HR Helpdesk at TAOps@marvell.com .
Interview Integrity
To support fair and authentic hiring practices, candidates are not permitted to use AI tools (such as transcription apps, real-time answer generators like ChatGPT or Copilot, or automated note-taking bots) during interviews.
These tools must not be used to record, assist with, or enhance responses in any way. Our interviews are designed to evaluate your individual experience, thought process, and communication skills in real time. Use of AI tools without prior instruction from the interviewer will result in disqualification from the hiring process.
This position may require access to technology and/or software subject to U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). As such, applicants must be eligible to access export-controlled information as defined under applicable law. Marvell may be required to obtain export licensing approval from the U.S. Department of Commerce and/or the U.S. Department of State. Except for U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, or protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), all applicants may be subject to an export license review process prior to employment.

JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING ADVANCED AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and into the real world. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. Today, we're deploying autonomous systems on heavy construction equipment across the country, improving safety on job sites and accelerating schedules on critical infrastructure projects.

We're not here debating the future of AI. We're deploying it in the real world. In just two years, we've raised $350M and achieved the first fully autonomous excavator deployments in construction.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.




ABOUT THE ROLE & TEAM

As a Sensor Hardware Test intern, you'll work alongside our test engineering team to characterize and validate the sensors - cameras, lidar, and supporting hardware - that power Bedrock's autonomous excavators. You'll help build test fixtures, run structured lab test campaigns, and turn raw sensor data into clear conclusions that guide how we select and integrate hardware. You'll also get out to our field site to see how bench results hold up on a live construction machine. You’ll own a hands-on project involving sensor hardware testing end-to-end, and your results will directly shape what hardware ends up on the next generation of machines.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build and iterate on test fixtures and benchtop setups - mechanical mounts, wiring harnesses, DAQ integration - used to characterize camera, lidar, and other sensor hardware

 - Run structured sensor test campaigns in the lab, following defined test procedures and capturing repeatable, well-documented data

 - Help safely deploy test setups and instrumentation out at our field site, and support live field test campaigns on active construction equipment

 - Develop tools to automate data collection, process raw sensor logs, and summarize results against pass/fail criteria

 - Help scope and select test equipment (light meters, targets, DAQ hardware, valves and actuators for environmental or fluid test rigs) for new test setups

 - Support electrical and mechanical debugging of test hardware, including wiring, sensor interfacing, and basic CAD work for fixture design

 - Document test methods, results, and findings, and present conclusions to the test engineering team to inform sensor selection and system design decisions




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR


REQUIRED

 - Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Physics, Optics, Mechatronics, or a related field

 - Hands-on experience building or testing hardware through coursework, personal projects, or a prior internship

 - Working proficiency in Python for data processing, scripting, or automation

 - Comfortable with basic lab equipment and electrical debugging (multimeters, oscilloscopes, DAQ systems)

 - Comfortable working outdoors and around active construction equipment, and willing to spend time on-site at our field test location for deployment and field testing

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to document technical work clearly for a team




PREFERRED

 - Exposure to cameras, lidar, radar, or other sensing hardware through coursework, internship experience, or personal projects

 - Experience with CAD tools for mechanical fixture design

 - Familiarity with Git and working within a shared codebase

 - Prior coursework, internship, or project experience in robotics, autonomous systems, or controls
   
   

About This Internship

This is a fixed-term, project-based internship designed strictly for students (undergraduate or graduate) seeking resume-building experience, hands-on skill development, or industry exposure rather than a direct career launchpad. Candidates will own discrete, short-term projects that can be fully completed within the internship timeframe. Please note that while exceptional interns may occasionally be considered if business needs align, opportunities for full-time conversion are highly limited.



Bedrock Robotics is an Equal Opportunity Employer

We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic.

Reasonable Accommodations

We want our hiring process to be accessible to everyone. If you need an accommodation to participate in the application or interview process, please let your recruiter know so we can support you.

At Delta Faucet, we are committed to transforming everyday experiences with water through innovative products and exceptional service. As a leader in the plumbing industry, we take pride in our dedication to quality, sustainability, and customer satisfaction. We believe that diverse perspectives strengthen our mission to create solutions that inspire and elevate the lives of all our customers. We welcome individuals from all backgrounds to join us on this journey toward inclusivity and excellence.
Your Role at Delta Faucet
Delta Faucet Company has an opportunity for a Hardware Engineering Co-op to join our Connected Water Team to help deliver the next generation of product features and technology to our customers. In this role, you will support the development of new digital products through hands-on work with embedded systems and real product hardware.
You will spend most of your days in the lab doing hands-on and varied tasks: soldering and reworking assemblies, programming and bringing up circuit boards, running electrical and functional tests, laying out PCBs, and keeping our engineering lab and its equipment running as smoothly as possible.
You will report to the engineering manager and sit with the project teams, not apart from them. Within your first few weeks you will be assigned specific tasks, projects, and test processes to own — meaning you make the calls there, you document how it works, and you are the person others ask about it. When you find a better way to do something, we want to hear it, and we will give you a straight answer either way.
Every part of the role is scoped so that the skills you leave with — test methodology, debugging discipline, documentation, lab ownership — are the ones that help you with the rest of your college work and prepare you for your future career.
Responsibilities:
Build and Rework
- Solder, rework, and modify through-hole and surface-mount assemblies for prototypes, test fixtures, and engineering samples.
- Assemble and wire test fixtures, harnesses, and benchtop setups from schematics and written instructions.
- Program, flash, and bring up circuit boards; verify power rails, signal integrity, and basic functionality on new builds.
Test and Debug
- Execute electrical, functional, and reliability tests on products and subassemblies, and record results accurately.
- Investigate test failures: reproduce the issue, isolate it to a component or subsystem, and document what you found so an engineer can act on it.
- Write and maintain basic test scripts and data-logging routines to automate repetitive measurements.
- Operate and troubleshoot standard bench equipment — oscilloscopes, DMMs, power supplies, function generators, data acquisition systems, environmental chambers.
Design Support
- Produce PCB layouts for test fixtures, adapter boards, and design revisions under engineering guidance.
- Review schematics and layouts for manufacturability and testability, and raise concerns before boards are ordered.
- Suggest product and process improvements based on what you observe on the bench
Lab and Calibration Ownership
- Organize and manage the engineering lab: equipment inventory, tool and fixture storage, consumable stock, workspace layout, and bench readiness.
- Run the equipment calibration program — track calibration due dates, coordinate with vendors, maintain certificates, and keep instruments in a known-good state.
- Establish and document standard operating procedures for test setups, lab safety, and equipment use so results are repeatable across people and across time.
- Maintain clear technical documentation: test reports, procedures, wiring diagrams, bring-up notes, and change records.
Where this goes
We treat this co-op as the first step in a career here, not a temporary set of hands. The scope is designed to grow with you:
- In your first term, you will learn our products, our lab, and our test methods, supporting engineers on defined tasks.
- As you demonstrate judgment, you will take ownership of specific test areas, fixtures, and the calibration program — work that is yours, with your name on it.
- Strong co-ops are invited back for additional terms with expanded responsibility, and we actively look to convert high performers into full-time engineering or test roles at graduation.
You will finish with a portfolio of real work: products you helped validate, fixtures you designed, procedures you wrote, and failures you tracked down. That is experience that transfers anywhere — and we would rather you build it here and stay.
Qualifications
- Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical engineering, Electrical Engineering Technology, or related field
- Demonstrated hands-on experience — coursework labs, senior design, competition teams (IEEE, Robotics, etc.), maker projects, or personal builds. Show us what you have made.
- Excellent soldering experience, including small components and SMT rework
- Foundational understanding of analog and digital circuits. Comfort reading schematics and interpreting datasheets and basic specifications.
- Careful, methodical work habits. In test engineering, sloppy data is worse than no data, and this role is built on trustworthy measurements.
- Clear written communication — you will write procedures and failure reports that other people rely on.
- Familiarity with microcontrollers, embedded systems, and electronics lab equipment
- Strong problem-solving skills, curiosity, and a willingness to learn in a hands-on engineering environment
- Interest in IoT, connected products, or consumer electronics is a plus
The target compensation for the role is $22.00 hour.
Why Join Us?
At Delta Faucet Company, our people are our greatest assets. We value different perspectives and fostering an inclusive environment. You’ll have the opportunity to shape the future of our brand, working alongside passionate professionals committed to excellence and innovation. Join us to lead progressive growth and make a significant impact within a leading organization.
Here are some of the benefits we offer for your personal and professional growth:
- Culture: Recognized and award-winning reputation for equality, diversity and inclusion, flexibility, work-life balance, and more.
- Wellbeing: Comprehensive benefit plans; retirement, savings, tuition reimbursement, and employee incentive programs; resources for mental, physical, and financial wellbeing.
- Learning & Development: LinkedIn Learning access; internal opportunities to work on projects cross-company.
- Social Impact: Four employee-led and self-directed Business Resource Groups; Paid volunteer day annually; Employees share their time, skills and talent with charities and nonprofit organizations across the U.S. and around the globe.

Part time

It is the Company’s policy to prohibit discrimination in any employment opportunity (including but not limited to recruitment, employment, promotion, salary increases, benefits, termination and all other terms and conditions of employment) based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information, pregnancy, religious creed, national origin, ancestry, age, physical/mental disability, medical condition, marital/domestic partner status, military and veteran status, height, weight or any other such characteristic protected by federal, state or local law. The Company is committed to complying with all applicable laws providing equal employment opportunities. At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and into the real world. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. Today, we're deploying autonomous systems on heavy construction equipment across the country, improving safety on job sites and accelerating schedules on critical infrastructure projects.

We're not here debating the future of AI. We're deploying it in the real world. In just two years, we've raised $350M and achieved the first fully autonomous excavator deployments in construction.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.




ABOUT THE ROLE & TEAM

Bedrock is bringing autonomy to the construction industry! We're a group of veterans from the autonomous vehicle industry who are passionate about bringing the benefits of automation to areas in the construction industry currently underserved by the market. We're growing our sizable fleet of retrofitted autonomous construction machines and we're looking for a motivated hardware engineering intern to support system testing and integration. You will work alongside senior engineers who design these systems, and you will help deliver robust and capable autonomous HW systems to the field.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Support the design, characterization, integration, and validation of Bedrock autonomy hardware and related systems, under the guidance of senior engineers.

 - Assist with component evaluations for our autonomous HW platforms

 - Write sensor data analysis and test automation scripts (Python and/or C++/C/Rust)

 - Run tests, collect data, and document results clearly for the engineering team




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR


REQUIRED

 - Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related field

 - Solid foundational knowledge in HW engineering subjects such as mechanical, electrical, and embedded SW

 - Coursework or project experience with some or all of the following:
   
   -   Embedded compute platforms, including single-board computers or edge compute modules
   
   -   Common autonomous sensing technologies such as lidar, camera, radar, GNSS, or IMUs
   
   -   Packaging and integration of HW systems, including basic mechanical or thermal considerations
   
   -   Basic signaling and communication protocols such as CAN, UART, SPI, or Ethernet

 - Proficiency in one or more of Python, C/C++, or Rust, with the ability to write scripts for tests, data collection, or analysis

 - Strong fundamentals in circuits, signals, and basic mechanical design

 - Comfortable working in a lab environment with tools such as a multimeter, oscilloscope, function generator, soldering iron, or hammer when necessary :)




PREFERRED

 - Prior co-op terms, personal projects, or club experience (e.g. UW Robotics, Formula Electric, WATonomous) in hardware or embedded systems

 - Expertise with camera, lidar, radar, IMU, or GNSS

 - Embedded compute platforms, in particular the Nvidia Jetson lineup

 - Communication protocols (CAN, UART, SPI, RS232/422/485, Ethernet, etc.)

 - Curiosity about autonomy and prior work in this area

 - Basic PCB design or schematic capture tools (KiCad, Eagle, Altium, Cadence, etc.)

 - Experience with version control (git) and collaborative engineering workflows

 - Familiarity with construction, off-road, or heavy equipment

 - A portfolio of personal or academic hardware projects (robotics, embedded systems, etc.)

About This Internship

This is a fixed-term, project-based internship designed strictly for students (undergraduate or graduate) seeking resume-building experience, hands-on skill development, or industry exposure rather than a direct career launchpad. Candidates will own discrete, short-term projects that can be fully completed within the internship timeframe. Please note that while exceptional interns may occasionally be considered if business needs align, opportunities for full-time conversion are highly limited."

 

Bedrock Robotics is an Equal Opportunity Employer

We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic.

Reasonable Accommodations

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Integrate sensors, compute, and wiring onto machines alongside the hardware team

 - Design brackets, enclosures, and interface hardware in CAD, then help fabricate and install them

 - Build test stands for validating subsystems on the bench instead of in the field

 - Run lab tests, capture data, and iterate on designs based on what breaks

 - Document build and install procedures so the next machine goes faster than the last

 - Close the loop with the field team on what's working and what isn't


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR


REQUIRED

 - Currently pursuing a BS or MS in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, robotics, or a related field — or bringing equivalent hands-on experience

 - CAD proficiency (SolidWorks, Onshape, or similar)

 - Genuine hands-on shop skills — you've built physical things, not just modeled them

 - Basic electrical competence: harnessing, connectors, multimeter, reading a schematic

Robotics Engineering Intern
San Francisco · Onsite · Internship

About Bracket Bot

We believe planet earth can thrive and be alive. Robots should manufacture goods, clean roadways, tidy our rooms, build more homes, cook healthy food, and lower the cost of living. We aren’t quite there yet, robots are too expensive, too difficult to program, fragile, and unfriendly. Bracket Bot is changing that.

We believe that robots are currently in the ENIAC era and we are bringing them to the Macbook era. We believe in high performance engineering teams where everyone you work with is what you imagined Bell Labs employees to be like. Intelligent, scrappy, dedicated, kind.

At Bracket Bot, we have a few objectives. We are working to make the ideal role model of a company, one where everyone is at the top of their field, inventing new ways to solve the problems we face across mechanical, electrical, software, and machine learning. What does a company that creates entirely new ways that teams work together look like? A company that invents new materials for lighter weight actuators and structures? A company that creates and publishes new inverse kinematics algorithms for robots? A company that is thinking radically differently, and executing on another level.

In every field there are small teams who did something their peers had decided was impossible. The 10-second barrier in sprinting, or the eight engineers who left Motorola and made the 6502 for 10x lower cost than other chips at the time making the personal computer possible. SpaceX has landed the same rocket 36 times. Bracket Bot believes actuated, alive machines can be glorious, affordable, easy to use, and ubiquitous, and we are pulling that future forward.

Our products are a mirror of what we think about the world, on engineering & research, and what we think should be introduced into the world. In history, there are simply products that should exist, and only once created, are obvious in hindsight. Bracket Bot’s mission is to introduce as many of these products into the world as possible. We believe there are hundreds of these in the space of robotics. Across physical robot hardware, software and operating system; the infrastructure and distributed systems they connect to; the AI inference they run, both local and cloud, and so much more.

Our first product, Bracket Bot 1, exemplifies what a small team of highly talented people can do. At Bracket Bot, we genuinely believe 100x engineers exist, and a room full of them can create things that dozens of other companies have failed to do. We’ve brought to market a robot that is 10x lower cost than any other robot in its category, while out performing them on manipulation, autonomous navigation, speech interaction, and developer UX.

We’re backed by Fifty Years (Scott Phoenix), BoxGroup, SV Angel, Betaworks, Pace Capital, angels including Nat Friedman, Logan Kilpatrick (Google AI), Guillermo Rauch (Vercel) and others from Tesla AI, Physical Intelligence, and Markforged.

About the role

Robotics brings mechanical systems, electronics, software, and machine learning together. The fastest way to learn is to build, test, and debug the whole system.

We’re hiring a Robotics Engineering Intern to contribute to hands-on engineering projects with the Bracket Bot team. You’ll help build and improve robots, investigate failures, and take scoped projects from an idea to a tested result.

Your work will draw on your strengths while giving you exposure to the other disciplines that make a robot work.

What you’ll do

 - Build, integrate, and test robot hardware or software with the engineering team.

 - Help reproduce failures, collect useful measurements, and debug system behavior.

 - Develop prototypes, tools, or tests that support robot development.

 - Document results and communicate what worked, what failed, and what to try next.

 - Own a scoped engineering project through implementation and verification.

What we’re looking for

 - Hands-on engineering projects that show curiosity and follow-through.

 - A foundation in mechanical, electrical, software, or robotics engineering.

 - Willingness to build, measure, debug, and learn unfamiliar systems.

 - Clear communication and the ability to ask useful questions.

 - Care for the quality of your work and enthusiasm for physical robots.

Nice to have

 - Personal, university, lab, or competition robotics projects.

 - Experience with CAD, electronics, programming, or practical fabrication.

 - Experience building test tools or documenting technical projects.

Important notes

 - This is a hands-on internship based onsite in San Francisco.

 - We value evidence of things you’ve built and problems you’ve worked through.

 - You’ll collaborate closely with engineers on real robot development.

Bracket Bot is an equal opportunity employer. We’re building a diverse team and welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

- Perform simulation and validation of navigation algorithms using Python, C++, or Rust.
- Participate in flight test campaigns to validate software and algorithms on UAS.
- Work closely with senior engineers on research and prototyping efforts.
- Perform other duties as required.
Standard Essential Functions

- Responsible for exhibiting professional behavior with both internal and external business associates that reflects positively on the company and is consistent with the company's policies and practices.

Qualifications
- Strong programming skills in C/C++, Python, or Rust.
- Experience with ROS/ROS2.
- Demonstrated project or professional experience with one or more of the following:
- Computer vision and deep learning frameworks (OpenCV, PyTorch, TensorFlow).
- Autonomy/planning algorithm development.
- Control systems design/analysis
- Sensor fusion techniques (Kalman filters, particle filters, graph-based SLAM).
- Embedded systems and real-time computing (Jetson, Raspberry Pi, FPGA, or microcontrollers).

Experience

Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.
Waymo Hardware Systems Architecture defines and validates the foundational electrical, communication network, diagnostic, software update, and cybersecurity architecture—the digital "nervous system"—across multiple autonomous vehicle platforms. Sitting at the intersection of hardware and software co-design, we define vehicle-level network and security specifications and build the real-time diagnostic and automated verification infrastructure that keeps our fleet operating safely.
Waymo interns partner with leaders in the industry on projects that create impact to the company. We believe learning is a two-way street: applying your knowledge while providing you with opportunities to expand your skill-set. Interns are an important part of our culture and our recruiting pipeline. Join us at Waymo for a fun and rewarding internship!
You will:
-
Build Real-Time Network Monitoring & Diagnostics Infrastructure : Design and build Python infrastructure to enable real-time diagnostics and health monitoring for vehicle communication networks (CAN, CAN-FD, Ethernet) across multiple autonomous vehicle platforms.
-
Develop Automated Verification Pipelines : Build automated verification and validation pipelines that evaluate vehicle network communication, diagnostic functionality, and system health across test benches and vehicle fleets.
-
Monitor & Validate Security Mechanisms : Create diagnostic checks and monitoring workflows for in-vehicle network security and cryptographic mechanisms, analyzing network performance and timing margins.
-
Build Rapidly with AI Code Generation : Leverage AI-based developer tooling and AI code generation workflows to rapidly prototype, test, and scale modular diagnostic and verification software.
-
Collaborate Across Systems Engineering Customers : Partner with Systems Architects, Network Engineers, and Vehicle Security Engineers to analyze network data, troubleshoot integration issues, and refine multi-platform vehicle requirements.
You have:
- Currently pursuing a MS or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Robotics, Mechanical/Automotive Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field.
-
Strong proficiency in Python for building modular software infrastructure, automated verification pipelines, and data analysis tools.
-
High fluency with AI-based tooling and AI code generation : Very comfortable and experienced with coding and building end-to-end software projects using modern AI code generation tools.
- Solid foundational understanding of communication networks and protocols, ideally including CAN and CAN-FD .
We prefer:
- Hands-on experience with vehicle or embedded communication networks ( CAN , CAN-FD , Automotive Ethernet ) and diagnostic protocols, as well as Python network tooling (cantools, python-can).
- Basic understanding of cryptography and network security concepts (e.g., message authentication codes, cryptographic authentication, or secure embedded communications).
- Experience building automated test or verification pipelines (pytest, CI/CD) or working with hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) / embedded test benches.
- Hands-on experience in autonomous vehicles, robotics (ROS/ROS2), Formula SAE, EcoCAR, or embedded systems projects.

About Rivian
Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract.
As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations.
Role Summary
Rivian internships are experiences optimized for student candidates. To be eligible, you must be an undergraduate or graduate student in an accredited program during the internship term with an expected graduation date between December 2027 and 2029. Rivian's Internship Program requires active student enrollment. Information regarding your expected degree completion date is collected solely to verify eligibility and determine your availability for future full-time opportunities. Rivian is an equal opportunity employer and does not use graduation dates to determine the age of applicants or as a basis for discriminatory hiring decisions.
If you are not pursuing a degree, please see our full time positions on our Rivian careers site. Note that if your university has specific requirements for internship programs, it is your responsibility to fulfill those requirements.
Our Spring Co-op program runs from Jan-Aug 2027. In order to be considered for this role, you must be available to work onsite, full time (40 hours per week), for the entire duration. If you're unable to work during the spring semester, please instead apply to our Summer Internship Program.
In this role, you will evaluate methodologies for development of Neural Engine Silicon with focus on performance, power and functional safety. Work on AI based tools and setting up new infrastructure and flows for ADAS Silicon development.
Responsibilities
- Experiment with AI tools for Silicon development: Leverage LLMs and generative agents to automate RTL generation, code documentation, and bug localization within the DLA (Deep Learning Accelerator) pipeline.
- Understand system architecture and develop tools for performance modeling and testing: Build bit-accurate C++/SystemC models to validate the throughput of neural network layers against "golden" ML frameworks like PyTorch.
- Develop tools and verification collateral for large-scale ASIC development: Create scalable UVM-based testbench components and automated regression scripts to support high-complexity SoC integration.
- Interconnect & Latency Analysis: Architect and implement performance monitors for Interconnect/AXI interfaces to analyze how on chip network impacts real-time inference latency.
- Safety-Aware Verification & Fault Injection: Design automated verification collateral to simulate hardware-level faults, ensuring that safety mechanisms correctly detect errors according to ISO 26262 automotive standards.
Qualifications
- Must be currently pursuing a bachelors, masters, or PhD degree at an accredited university
- Actively pursuing a degree or one closely related in Electrical or Computer Engineering
- Fundamentals of Computer architecture
- CPU and Memory hierarchy
- C/Python coding skills
- System verilog language

To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology.
Group/Division
The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. The Film and Scatterometry Technology (FaST) division delivers industry-leading metrology solutions essential to advanced semiconductor manufacturing. Its portfolio includes systems for measuring film thickness, critical dimensions, composition, and resistivity—key to developing and scaling next-gen IC processes. FaST partners closely with customers from early R&D through high-volume production, ensuring performance and process alignment.
What You'll Do
In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise.
Responsibilities:
In this role you will be responsible for:
- Assisting in the development, release and support of KLA Film metrology products.
- Integral to this role is using one’s technical knowledge and skill for the development of a deep understanding on the customer applications and develop the
- technologies and products to resolve the challenging problems. The successful candidate will develop the ability to collect and appropriately filter observations to generate problem statements, produce data collection plans, analyze data and prescribe corrective actions.
- Greatcommunication is required, including oral, writing, and publishing after action reports, meeting minutes and project summaries.
Qualifications:
- PhD candidate with a background in Experimental Physics or Engineering (electrical, mechanical, optical, etc.)
- Understanding of optical, electrical, mechanical and software systems and their interactions in the context of complex industrial equipment is a plus.
- Enthusiastic communicator to provide detailed guidance to colleagues to solve problems, and technical summaries for internal functional teams and management.
Minimum Qualifications
PhD candidate with a background in Experimental Physics or Engineering (electrical, mechanical, optical, etc.)
About KLA
We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us.
Total Rewards
Base Pay Range: $56.00 - $56.00 per hour based on pursuit of a Ph.D.
Primary Location: USA-CA-Milpitas-KLA
KLA’s total rewards package for employees may also include participation in performance incentive programs and eligibility for additional benefits including but not limited to: medical, dental, vision, life, and other voluntary benefits, 401(K) including company matching, employee stock purchase program (ESPP), student debt assistance, tuition reimbursement program, development and career growth opportunities and programs, financial planning benefits, wellness benefits including an employee assistance program (EAP), paid time off and paid company holidays, and family care and bonding leave.
Interns are eligible for some of the benefits listed. Our pay ranges are determined by role, level, and location. The range displayed reflects the pay for this position in the primary location identified in this posting. Actual pay depends on several factors, including state minimum pay wage rates, location, job-related skills, experience, and relevant education level or training. We are committed to complying with all applicable federal and state minimum wage requirements where applicable. If applicable, your recruiter can share more about the specific pay range for your preferred location during the hiring process.

Use of these tools may interfere with our ability to evaluate your individual qualifications and affect your candidacy. About Astera Labs
Astera Labs is a semiconductor company developing intelligent connectivity solutions for AI and cloud infrastructure. Our products depend on high-performance interconnects and advanced semiconductor packaging to move data reliably across compute, memory, and storage systems.
Role overview
As a Semiconductor Packaging Intern, you will be part of the packaging team developing Astera Labs’ portfolio of connectivity products for leading cloud service providers and server and networking OEMs. You will help enhance key areas of the package development cycle, including package design, modeling, automation flows, and documentation.
You will work cross-functionally to understand project requirements and develop solutions throughout the packaging development cycle. This is a hands-on engineering role for someone interested in the interaction between electrical performance, power delivery, thermal behavior, mechanical constraints, and manufacturability. You will contribute to package-design and modeling work, document your results, and help the team make well-supported engineering decisions.
Responsibilities
-
Support package design, modeling, automation, and documentation for Astera Labs’ connectivity products.
-
Collaborate cross-functionally to understand project requirements and develop solutions throughout the packaging development cycle.
-
Support package definition by organizing inputs such as die files, pin-out details, signal- and power-integrity requirements, thermal requirements, board and footprint constraints, supplier design rules, cost considerations, and reliability needs.
-
Help maintain package Plan of Record (POR) information, including package structure, substrate stackup and materials, package SI/PI requirements, thermal requirements, development schedule, and open risks.
-
Generate or review package netlists from die files and package footprints, and support package layout work with internal or external design partners.
-
Import and prepare package layout data for analysis; verify nets, stackups, materials, vias, bumps, and BGA or solder-ball geometries against available design and manufacturing information.
-
Support package-level signal-integrity and power-integrity analysis using tools such as ANSYS Electronics Desktop, HFSS 3D Layout, SIwave, and Keysight ADS as appropriate to the project.
-
Set up ports and target nets, extract S-parameters, analyze insertion loss, return loss, crosstalk, impedance, and related channel behavior, and compare results with design requirements.
-
Support power-integrity studies such as DCIR, PDN impedance, and transient or frequency-domain analysis; help interpret voltage drop, current density, resonance, and impedance results.
-
Assist with thermal and mechanical analyses by organizing material and structural inputs, reviewing results, and helping identify risks related to temperature, stress, warpage, or reliability.
-
Review package layouts against substrate and OSAT design rules and support design-for-manufacturing activities such as density checks, degassing considerations, and design-rule checks.
-
Contribute to package tape-out and NPI readiness reviews by checking documentation and tracking open actions.
-
Help prepare and maintain package documentation, including bills of materials, netlists, package outline or lid information, substrate stackup drawings, and electrical, thermal, or mechanical models when applicable.
-
Support communication with substrate suppliers and OSAT partners by organizing questions, requirements, feedback, and manufacturing-readiness information.
-
Document assumptions, simulation setups, results, issues, and recommendations in a clear and reusable format; present project learnings at the end of the internship.
Basic qualifications
-
Working towards an M.S. or PhD in Electrical Engineering or a related field.
-
Cumulative GPA of 3.3/4.0 or higher.
-
Entrepreneurial, open-minded behavior and a hands-on work ethic, with the ability to prioritize a dynamic list of multiple tasks.
-
Ability to work with minimal supervision and deliver solutions in a fast-paced environment.
-
Strong time-management skills and strong written and verbal communication skills.
Required experience
-
Coursework in RF/microwave, communication systems and signal analysis, semiconductor manufacturing, or circuit design.
-
Understanding of or coursework in signal and power integrity is a plus.
-
Understanding of or coursework in semiconductor packaging is a plus.
-
Scripting or software-development experience in Python, Visual Basic, or equivalent programming languages.
-
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with careful attention to detail when working with geometry, models, data, and documentation.
-
Ability to communicate clearly, collaborate across disciplines, and follow through on defined tasks.
Preferred experience
-
Experience with physical-design or layout tools such as AutoCAD, Cadence Allegro, Cadence APD/SiP, or comparable tools.
-
Experience using 3D electromagnetic-simulation tools such as ANSYS Electronics Desktop, HFSS, HFSS 3D Layout, or SIwave.
-
Knowledge of semiconductor multilayer flip-chip packages, including FCBGA or FCCSP.
-
Experience with package substrate stackups, copper pillars, solder bumps, BGA balls, package-to-board transitions, or high-density interconnects.
-
Familiarity with S-parameter extraction and validation, including ports, Touchstone models, passivity, causality, de-embedding, or mixed-mode analysis.
-
Exposure to power-integrity concepts such as IR drop, DCIR, PDN impedance, decoupling, or current-density analysis.
-
Experience with thermal modeling, mechanical analysis, coefficient-of-thermal-expansion effects, warpage, reliability, or package materials.
-
Familiarity with design-for-manufacturing, supplier design rules, package assembly, reflow, underfill, or OSAT workflows.
-
Experience using Python, MATLAB, Visual Basic, spreadsheets, or similar tools to automate analysis, process engineering data, or communicate results.
-
Prior semiconductor, package-design, hardware, supplier, or manufacturing experience through coursework, research, projects, or an internship.
What success looks like
-
You learn the packaging development flow and the team’s analysis tools, then take ownership of a defined technical task with appropriate guidance.
-
You produce accurate, traceable analysis or documentation; communicate assumptions and risks early; and follow open actions through to closure.
-
By the end of the internship, you have contributed useful results to a package-design, SI/PI, thermal/mechanical, DFM, tape-out, or manufacturing-readiness workstream and can clearly explain your approach, findings, and impact.
Internship experience and compensation
This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges form $35/hour to $55/hour. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship. Interns participate in Early Career programming, including technical and professional-development sessions, community events, and an end-of-program project presentation.
Equal opportunity
Astera Labs is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. We encourage anyone with relevant experience to apply.

About Astera Labs
Astera Labs develops purpose-built connectivity solutions for rack-scale AI infrastructure. Our Intelligent Connectivity Platform brings together high-performance connectivity technologies for AI, cloud, server, and networking systems.
The role
As a Physical Design Engineer Intern in Toronto, you will gain hands-on experience taking a digital-design block through the physical-design flow, from RTL handoff and synthesis through floorplanning, placement, clock-tree synthesis, routing, timing closure, and signoff. You will read tool reports, debug flow issues, analyze power, performance, and area, and work with engineers across the ASIC implementation lifecycle.
This internship is an opportunity to build practical VLSI and backend-design skills while learning how physical implementation decisions affect timing, congestion, power integrity, reliability, and manufacturability.

-
Set up and run physical-design flow stages for a block using established methodologies and reproducible work areas.
-
Review RTL and physical-design inputs, including netlists, constraints, technology files, libraries, and parasitic or extraction data.
-
Support synthesis, floorplanning, power-grid planning, placement, clock-tree synthesis, routing, and implementation optimization.
-
Analyze timing reports, slack, skew, transition, congestion, utilization, and other quality-of-results metrics.
-
Help investigate setup and hold violations and evaluate fixes such as cell sizing, buffering, Vt swaps, useful skew, and routing optimization.
-
Review physical-verification and power-integrity results, including DRC, LVS, antenna, electromigration, and IR-drop findings.
-
Use Unix/Linux and Tcl or other scripting tools to automate runs, parse reports, compare experiments, and improve flow reproducibility.
-
Debug tool errors, warnings, broken stages, and unexpected QoR changes by examining logs, configurations, and generated reports.
-
Collaborate with front-end design, timing, EMIR, physical-verification, CAD, and other engineering teams across handoffs.
-
Document experiments, assumptions, results, and recommendations for future implementation work.
What you bring
Basic qualifications
-
Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field.
-
Coursework, project, research, or hands-on experience with digital logic, VLSI, ASIC design, computer architecture, or semiconductor engineering.
-
Foundational understanding of timing, setup and hold, clocks, power, placement, routing, or physical verification concepts.
-
Familiarity with Unix/Linux command-line environments and at least one scripting or programming language, such as Tcl, Python, shell, or C/C++.
-
Strong analytical and debugging skills, attention to detail, and interest in understanding how designs become manufacturable silicon.
-
Strong written and verbal communication, organization, and time-management skills.
-
A hands-on work ethic, curiosity, learning agility, and ability to take ownership of assigned deliverables.
Preferred qualifications
-
Experience with synthesis, floorplanning, placement, clock-tree synthesis, routing, static timing analysis, or physical-verification tools.
-
Familiarity with EDA tools such as Fusion or Genus, Innovus, PrimeTime, Calibre, Voltus, or equivalent tools.
-
Understanding of PVT corners, OCV/AOCV/LVF, timing closure, congestion, power planning, EMIR, DRC, LVS, or antenna checks.
-
Experience writing Tcl, Python, shell, or Make-based automation for design flows and report analysis.
-
Familiarity with standard-cell libraries, LEF/DEF, Liberty files, SDC constraints, SPEF extraction, or PDK concepts.
-
Interest in PPA optimization, reproducible flow infrastructure, and connectivity products used in AI, cloud, server, or networking systems.

To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology.
Group/Division
The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. The Film and Scatterometry Technology (FaST) division delivers industry-leading metrology solutions essential to advanced semiconductor manufacturing. Its portfolio includes systems for measuring film thickness, critical dimensions, composition, and resistivity—key to developing and scaling next-gen IC processes. FaST partners closely with customers from early R&D through high-volume production, ensuring performance and process alignment.
What You'll Do
In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise.
Responsibilities:
- KLA is seeking a talented and motivated individual for an internship position, working within the Systems Engineering Team.
- The job function is to conduct experiments and/or simulations to provide inputs to system design, develop software features to standardize simulation and data analysis, write reports and transfer knowledge to other team members.
- The position gains visibility by successfully completing the project, and presenting summary and learnings to senior management.
- Candidate will get exposure to the semiconductor industry, complex systems development, and working experience with cross functional teams.
Preferred Qualifications:
- PhD Level Degree with a background in Physics or Engineering (electrical, mechanical, optical, etc.)
- Proven experience in at least one programming language like Python, C# , etc. or Software like Matlab, Labview .
- Enthusiastic communicator to provide detailed guidance to colleagues to solve problems, and technical summaries for internal functional teams and management.
- Understanding of optical, electrical, mechanical and software systems and their interactions in the context of complex industrial equipment is a plus.
Minimum Qualifications
PhD Level Degree with a background in Physics or Engineering (electrical, mechanical, or optical)Requires less than 1 year of related experience
About KLA
We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us.

Meter is a vertically integrated networking company. Hardware, software, services, ISP, and autonomous networks run on a single data pipeline, from the local network to the data center.



Most of the networking industry treats hardware as a commodity–we don’t. Build the hardware right, and everything above it gets better. Meter designs its own Firewalls, Switches, Wireless Access Points, PDUs, and Gateways because customers subscribe to the network instead of buying individual boxes; we're accountable for how the hardware performs for years. We sweat details most people never see, like the logo stamped inside the enclosure and the sound spec on our fans. Great hardware takes more than designing circuits and shipping products: It means thinking hard about performance, reliability, manufacturability, supply chain, installation, sustainability, and the full product lifecycle.



We’re hiring Hardware Engineering Interns to solve real technical problems across Meter’s hardware engineering and operations teams. Over 12 weeks, you’ll own a well-scoped project picked to fit your interests, your experience, and the problems that matter most to Meter:

 - Next-generation power adapters: Prototype compact, efficient power supplies that could ship in future Meter products.

 - Hardware lifecycle and sustainability: Figure out how Meter hardware can be refurbished, reused, or recycled, and what it takes to extend its life.

 - Installer tooling: Build tools, fixtures, or diagnostic devices that make Meter networks faster to install and troubleshoot.

 - Acoustics and thermal systems: Design quiet, efficient cooling for future high-performance networking and data center products.

 - Supply chain intelligence: Use component and supplier data to spot risks and bottlenecks before they hit a hardware build.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

You’ll take a meaningful hardware problem from an open question to a recommendation backed by evidence, and leave behind something the hardware team can use: data, prototypes, test results, engineering requirements, supplier evaluations, or tools.

Your day-to-day will depend on your project, but you may:

 - Design, build, and test electrical or mechanical prototypes for future Meter products

 - Evaluate components, technologies, architectures, materials, and suppliers

 - Write test plans and characterize performance, reliability, thermals, acoustics, power, and other system-level behavior

 - Work with our manufacturing partners in Taiwan to understand their capabilities, constraints, cost, and scalability

 - Present your findings and recommendations to the hardware team at the end of the internship




WHO YOU ARE

You’re curious, hands-on, and you learn by building. You’re a good fit if:

 - You’re pursuing a degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related technical field

 - You like taking an ambiguous technical problem and breaking it into questions you can answer through engineering and experimentation

 - You’ve built, tested, debugged, or taken apart hardware on a design team, in a lab, or at home, or you’re eager to start

 - You’re comfortable working with physical systems: PCBAs, mechanical assemblies, test equipment, prototypes, manufacturing data, or supplier samples

 - You can explain technical findings clearly and turn your work into recommendations others can act on

Experience with PCB design, CAD, embedded systems, thermal design, or data analysis is a plus, but none of it is required.

Above all, we’re looking for people who want to understand how great hardware gets built.




WHY METER?

The internet runs the world. Every purchase you make and every video call you join is packets moving through networks. But those networks haven’t changed in decades. They’re brittle, complex, and surprisingly hard to set up for a business.

We started Meter to build better networks, and that meant building everything ourselves: our own enterprise hardware, intuitive software, and streamlined operations. Today we deploy those networks at scale. Bridgewater, Lyft, Reddit, and the San Antonio Spurs rely on Meter to keep thousands of employees and locations online.

Our bet is simple: Everyone will use the internet more than they do today. Meter is building the networking stack that makes connectivity as easy and reliable as water or electricity.




COMPENSATION

 - The estimated pay for this role is $40–$50 per hour. This role is also eligible for a relocation and housing stipend.

By applying to this job you acknowledge that you've read and understood Meter's Job Applicant Privacy Notice https://www.meter.com/careers/job-applicant-privacy.

The Camera Architecture team within Camera, Depth & Sensors (CDS) at Reality Labs defines the imaging hardware architecture for Meta's AI glasses, AR glasses, VR headsets, wearable devices, and Physical AI / Robotics platforms. We sit at the intersection of image sensor technology, optics, and the AI/imaging feature stack — translating product vision into camera hardware solutions that ship at scale. Our cameras serve photography, computer vision (SLAM, hand/eye tracking, passthrough), and contextual-AI features.
As a Hardware Engineer Intern on the Camera Architecture team, you will help build the quantitative foundation behind camera architecture decisions. Working alongside camera architects and sensor, lens, module, and AI teams, you will develop first-principles models and run trade studies that connect camera hardware parameters — resolution, pixel size, SNR, MTF, dynamic range, frame rate, shutter type, power — to the product features they enable. Depending on project and background, your work may also extend into how camera hardware choices affect on-device computer vision and AI performance. You will own a well-scoped project end to end, from problem definition through analysis and a recommendation presented to the team.
This is a 12-week internship.

About Moment Energy
Independent energy is here. Help us deploy it.
Energy should be free. Free from aging grids, fragile supply chains, and unnecessary extraction. At Moment Energy, we’re building a world where clean power is abundant, affordable, and uninterrupted for everyone.
The world doesn’t need another promise about energy; it needs proof that a freer future is possible. Moment Energy is the pragmatic liberator of power, the only company certified to turn the largest untapped energy supply into independent energy.
Now is the moment. While the industry scraps millions of batteries with decades of life left, we put them to work by repurposing large-format batteries into advanced battery energy storage systems that deliver real-world impact.
We were told second-life batteries would never be safe enough or scalable enough. We didn’t argue, we engineered the solution. Today, Moment Energy delivers 5x the energy density and holds the certifications required to deploy energy independence at scale.
Now is the moment. Join us.
The Opportunity
We are seeking a Test Engineering Co-op to join our Test Engineering team. We recently unveiled our new manufacturing facility, the largest second-life battery repurposing facility in the world, and are quickly ramping up our testing and production capacity..
This is a hands-on role, with lots of time in our new R&D lab and around the production floor. You will set up and run test benches, troubleshoot complex issues across multiple subsystems, and command massive amounts of electrical power. You’ll get exposure to every level of the stack from building custom prototyping harnesses to wrangling data from DAQs.
In this role, you will directly support the development and testing of our energy storage products while gaining hands-on experience working alongside experienced engineers.
Responsibilities and Duties
- Assist the test engineering team in validating and improving energy storage products
- Set up, configure, and maintain instruments and test benches for battery systems and power electronics
- Assemble and modify electrical assemblies including wire harnessing, soldering, crimping, and circuit board assembly
- Configure, debug, and operate devices via different communication protocols (CAN, Modbus, TCP/IP, serial)
- Develop test plans, execute testing, analyze data, and write technical reports
The Student we’re looking for:
- Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related field
- Strong preference for students with Design Team experience
- Career interest in clean tech, energy systems, or electronics
- Comfortable reading electrical schematics
- Some experience with Python or similar scripting tools
- Hands-on experience with soldering, circuit boards, wiring, harness building, system integration or prototyping (academic or project-based experience welcome)
- Ability to use 3D printing, hand tools, or power tools to build test fixtures
- Detail-oriented with strong documentation and communication skills
- Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced engineering environment
The Experience You’ll Gain:
- Hands-on experience developing real energy storage hardware
- Mentorship from experienced engineers
- Exposure to prototyping, testing, and certification processes
- The opportunity to contribute to technology that supports the clean energy transition
Moment Energy Co-op Benefits Highlights
Paid Time Off: Co-op’s receive three paid days off per term
Vibrant Culture & Perks: Open and collaborative office culture, frequent company socials and wellness programs (weekly yoga and fitness center), and free EV charging on-site.
Why join us?
- Today, we’re delivering 5x the energy density and have all the certifications needed to ship energy independence to the world.
- Be part of a mission-driven company focused on creating sustainable energy solutions and making a positive impact on the world.
- Collaborate closely with passionate co-founders and a team committed to innovation and excellence.
- Contribute to building and scaling a company from the ground up, where your work will have a direct and meaningful impact.
- Thrive in a workplace that values collaboration, wellness, and celebrating successes, with regular company socials, fitness sessions, and more.
We're a fast-paced and dynamic team.
Every day you'll be taking on a new challenge and learning something new. You'll take on a wide breadth of tasks and contribute to disrupting the battery industry. You'll be part of a tight-knit team that is working together to save the planet! Fun, health, and wellness are incorporated into our daily schedule and we encourage all our team members to bring innovative ideas to the table to create an interactive workplace.
Moment Energy Benefits Highlights (full time, permanent employees only)
Financial Growth: Employee equity and a robust RRSP matching program.
Comprehensive Health Coverage: Extended health, dental, and vision benefits for you and your dependents through Manulife.
Generous Time Off & Flexibility: Paid time off plus a paid company closure between Christmas and New Year's, with a generous paid sick leave.
Vibrant Culture & Perks: Open and collaborative office culture, frequent company socials and wellness programs (weekly yoga/fitness), and free EV charging on-site.
Company Dinner: Weekly Tuesday dinner provided by Moment Energy. We also have a generous supply of coffee and snacks for the office!
Our Commitments
Moment Energy is an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to inclusive, barrier-free recruitment and selection processes, including our work environment. We especially welcome applications from Indigenous peoples, members of racialized communities, persons with disabilities, women, and persons who identify as 2SLGBTQ+.
—---
Our Values
Our values are key to how we show up every day at Moment Energy! We keep them in the forefront of what we do, and they’re used everywhere. We refer to them when we have tough decisions to make, we give shoutouts based on living out these values, and we include them as part of our performance reviews.
We have 5 core values and 1 foundational pillar (Safety is our Foundation) which lays the groundwork for everything we do.
Safety is our Foundation
We prioritize the safety of our products, customers, employees, and the general public above all else. From the workshop to the field, we maintain the highest standards for our batteries in testing manufacturing and deployment, and daily operations. Safety is not only about procedures—it is about vigilance, responsibility, and speaking up when something does not feel right.
Safety is everyone's responsibility. We follow safety protocols, use proper equipment, and continuously improve our systems to prevent risks before they occur. If something is unsafe, we stop work and address it.
Safety also means protecting our colleagues, customers, and communities by designing reliable products, maintaining safe workspaces, and ensuring our work is done carefully and responsibly.
We’re Building a Greener Future Together:
We infuse passion for our cleantech mission into every aspect of our work and incorporate fun into the workplace. We motivate one another, celebrate our successes and embrace eco-friendly practices to reduce our carbon footprint.
We Prioritize our Customer’s Needs:
We place our customers at the core of everything we do, ensuring that every decision considers their needs and aims to provide increased value to them. We provide reliable support for our customers, every step of the way.
We’re Open, Honest and Accountable:
We prioritize open and honest communication to foster mutual understanding, strengthen knowledge sharing, and reduce miscommunication within the team. We admit when we’ve made a mistake, and remedy our actions. We transparently communicate outcomes whether good, bad, or unexpected.
We Think and Act like Owners:
We’re self-starters that proactively embrace new challenges along with personal and collective ownership of responsibilities in the organization. We focus on growth, not titles, and we do what needs to be done.
We Treat Everyone with Respect:
We actively listen, share openly, and work together towards common goals. We treat one another with mutual respect to cultivate an inclusive environment where everyone feels accepted, supported, and heard. We keep an open mind and are willing to learn.
