JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING ADVANCED AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and into the real world. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. Today, we're deploying autonomous systems on heavy construction equipment across the country, improving safety on job sites and accelerating schedules on critical infrastructure projects.

We're not here debating the future of AI. We're deploying it in the real world. In just two years, we've raised $350M and achieved the first fully autonomous excavator deployments in construction.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.




ABOUT THE ROLE & TEAM

Before an autonomous excavator digs its first trench on a new site, it's already dug thousands in simulation. The Simulation team builds the virtual environments our autonomy stack trains and tests against — and the closer sim looks and behaves like the real world, the faster we move. Neural rendering is the next step: replacing hand-authored assets and approximations with learned representations that capture the visual complexity of real jobsites — dust, lighting, deformable terrain, heavy equipment in motion. As our Simulation intern, you'll push neural rendering techniques into our sim pipeline and measure whether they actually close the visual gap that matters for downstream autonomy performance.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Research, implement, and benchmark neural rendering methods (NeRF, 3D Gaussian splatting, or related techniques) for generating realistic construction-site imagery within our simulation stack

 - Train models on real-world site data captured by our fleet and evaluate visual fidelity, temporal consistency, and render speed

 - Integrate neural rendering outputs into the simulation pipeline so perception and planning teams can train and test against them

 - Build evaluation metrics and tooling that quantify how well rendered scenes match real fleet data — and whether that improvement transfers to autonomy performance

 - Identify and address failure modes: dynamic objects, deformable terrain, dust, harsh lighting, and other construction-specific challenges

 - Document findings, limitations, and a recommendation on where neural rendering should (and shouldn't) replace traditional sim assets


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR


REQUIRED

 - Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in computer science, computer graphics, robotics, or a related field — or bringing equivalent research or industry experience

 - Strong Python and hands-on experience with PyTorch (or equivalent)

 - Solid understanding of 3D graphics fundamentals: rendering pipelines, scene representations, camera models, and coordinate systems

 - Familiarity with neural scene representations (NeRF, Gaussian splatting, neural radiance fields, or related methods)

 - Comfort with real-world data — construction sites are messy, dusty, and nothing like an indoor dataset


PREFERRED

 - Published work or substantial project experience in neural rendering, novel view synthesis, or differentiable rendering

 - Experience with simulation engines (Unreal, Unity, NVIDIA Isaac Sim, or similar)

 - Background in autonomous vehicle simulation or synthetic data generation

 - Familiarity with C++ and GPU programming (CUDA, OpenGL, Vulkan)

About This Internship

This is a fixed-term, project-based internship designed strictly for students (undergraduate or graduate) seeking resume-building experience, hands-on skill development, or industry exposure rather than a direct career launchpad. Candidates will own discrete, short-term projects that can be fully completed within the internship timeframe. Please note that while exceptional interns may occasionally be considered if business needs align, opportunities for full-time conversion are highly limited."

Job Description:
DataRobot delivers AI that maximizes impact and minimizes business risk. Our platform and applications integrate into core business processes so teams can develop, deliver, and govern AI at scale. DataRobot empowers practitioners to deliver predictive and generative AI, and enables leaders to secure their AI assets. Organizations worldwide rely on DataRobot for AI that makes sense for their business — today and in the future.
This effort is about building a multi-target joint probabilistic foundation model that can be used across industries to tackle some of the hardest real-world problems. The ambition goes beyond what tabular and time-series foundation models usually do: one model should support temporal forecasting, unordered tabular regression and classification, missing-data completion, and mixed-modality inputs and outputs while learning coherent joint structure across connected variables, rows, horizons, and scenarios. The primary objective is to create real value in serious use cases rather than optimize benchmark scores in isolation, although strong results on standard benchmarks are expected to follow closely.
This role is designed as a research-engineering internship for someone operating at post-doctoral level, or very close to it, who wants to shape the architecture of a probabilistic foundation model. The center of gravity is the model itself: the encoders that read temporal, tabular, and mixed-modality inputs, the attention and sequence mechanisms that carry structure across variables, rows, and horizons, and the distributional output heads and decoding schemes that turn hidden states into coherent joint predictions. We are looking for someone who can reason precisely about what an architecture can and cannot represent, and who then implements, trains, and evaluates the resulting PyTorch models in a production-quality codebase. A background in stochastic modeling is a strong plus rather than a prerequisite: the model is trained on synthetic data drawn from stochastic dynamics, so a candidate who can also reason about stochastic differential equations and design synthetic data generators can contribute on both sides of the training loop.
Required Skills:
- Strong PyTorch skills and hands-on experience building and training deep models.
- Solid understanding of Transformers, attention variants, and long-context or state-space sequence architectures, including the tradeoffs between quality, memory, and latency.
- Experience with probabilistic modeling in neural networks: distributional output heads, likelihood-based or proper-scoring-rule losses, mixture or flow models, or related uncertainty-aware learning setups.
- Strong foundation in probability and statistics, enough to reason about densities and masses, dependence between variables, and calibration.
- Ability to connect architectural ideas to working GPU-native implementations, controlled experiments, and diagnostics that show why a change helped.
- Strong engineering habits: readable code, tests, reproducible experiments, and disciplined evaluation of model changes.
- Ability to debug training instability, reason about why results changed, and iterate quickly from hypothesis to evidence.
Strong Plus:
- Working knowledge of stochastic processes and stochastic differential equations: drift and diffusion, jumps, regime switching, mean reversion, heavy tails, and how such dynamics are simulated numerically.
- Experience designing synthetic data generators or simulation-based training curricula, and an understanding of how the training distribution shapes what a model learns.
- Depth in a domain with rich stochastic structure such as finance, energy, commodities, or a similarly quantitative field.
- Familiarity with tabular or mixed-modality deep learning: categorical, ordinal, count, and bounded targets alongside continuous ones.
What You Can Expect To Work On:
- Designing and improving the core model architecture: input encoders for temporal, unordered tabular, and mixed-modality data; attention factorizations across variables, rows, and horizons; the distributional output heads and decoding strategies that produce coherent joint samples.
- Running controlled architecture studies, from ablations and scaling behavior to memory and throughput profiles, and turning the results into design decisions.
- Building scalable PyTorch implementations that support larger input and output spaces, better throughput, and tighter memory budgets.
- Studying how architectural choices, data-generation choices, and inference constraints interact to change benchmark quality and real-world usefulness.
- For candidates with the stochastic-modeling background: extending the synthetic-data engine with richer stochastic dynamics, constraints, dependence structures, heavy tails, and regime behavior.
- Turning research ideas into robust implementations and credible empirical results.
What You Should Expect:
- Work that sits close to the core of the project rather than at the edges.
- A fast research loop where good ideas can move quickly from hypothesis to implementation to benchmark.
- A real chance to contribute to research that aims for top-tier, state-of-the-art outcomes rather than only incremental internal work.
- A team that values rigorous thinking, clean code, and practical usefulness at the same time.
- Exposure to problems that combine deep learning, stochastic modeling, and real deployment constraints instead of isolating only one of those dimensions.
- A role that fits someone with broad interests who wants to work across both advanced modeling and serious implementation work rather than staying narrowly specialized.

You will work with experienced design and verification engineers to understand design specifications, develop and execute verification tests, debug simulation failures, and help assess the functionality and reliability of complex digital designs. You will collaborate with RTL design, architecture, and other engineering teams throughout the ASIC development process.
Key responsibilities
Functional verification and test development
-
Assist in developing and executing simulation-based test plans for digital ASIC blocks and subsystems.
-
Develop and maintain test cases using SystemVerilog and other verification languages under the guidance of experienced engineers.
-
Help identify functional scenarios, corner cases, and potential design issues from design specifications.
-
Run simulations and analyze results to verify that RTL behavior meets design requirements.
-
Contribute to test quality, verification efficiency, and functional coverage improvements.
Simulation debugging and design quality
-
Debug simulation failures using waveforms, simulation logs, and debugging tools.
-
Work with RTL design engineers to investigate functional issues and help identify root causes.
-
Assist with regression testing and track verification results.
-
Learn and apply verification best practices, including assertions, functional coverage, and systematic debugging.
-
Help maintain verification environments and test documentation.
Verification methodology and automation
-
Gain exposure to SystemVerilog-based verification environments and object-oriented programming concepts.
-
Learn Universal Verification Methodology (UVM) and contribute to existing testbenches as appropriate.
-
Assist with reusable verification components, test sequences, and checkers.
-
Use Python, Tcl, Shell, or similar scripting languages to automate repetitive verification tasks.
-
Participate in code reviews and contribute to verification-code quality and maintainability.
Cross-functional collaboration
-
Collaborate with RTL design, architecture, and verification engineers to understand design functionality and verification requirements.
-
Participate in design reviews, verification planning, and technical discussions.
-
Document test scenarios, debugging results, and verification progress.
-
Gain exposure to ASIC development milestones, including block integration, regression signoff, tapeout, and post-silicon validation.
Basic qualifications
-
Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
-
Fundamental understanding of digital logic design, including combinational and sequential logic, flip-flops, finite state machines, and basic datapaths.
-
Basic programming knowledge in at least one language such as C, C++, Python, or SystemVerilog.
-
Basic understanding of hardware design concepts, including clocks, resets, registers, and state machines.
-
Familiarity with digital simulation or hardware design through coursework, academic projects, research, or internships.
-
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills.
-
Willingness to learn new verification tools, methodologies, and technologies.
-
Good communication skills and the ability to work effectively in a collaborative team environment.
-
Ability and willingness to work onsite in San Jose, California.
-
No prior industry experience is required; relevant coursework, academic projects, research, and internships will be considered.
Preferred qualifications
-
Experience with Verilog or SystemVerilog through coursework, academic projects, or internships.
-
Exposure to RTL simulation tools and waveform debugging.
-
Familiarity with digital-design verification concepts, testbench development, or functional coverage.
-
Basic knowledge of object-oriented programming or SystemVerilog assertions.
-
Exposure to UVM or other constrained-random verification methodologies.
-
Experience with Python, Tcl, Perl, Shell, or other scripting languages for automation.
-
Familiarity with ASIC or FPGA development flows.
-
Exposure to high-speed interfaces or protocols such as PCI Express, Ethernet, AMBA, CXL, NVMe, or other networking and interconnect technologies.
-
Interest in high-performance ASICs, networking, data-center infrastructure, AI accelerators, or cloud computing.
-
Demonstrated ability to learn complex technical concepts and apply them to practical engineering problems.
Internship experience and compensation
This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges form $35/hour to $55/hour. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship. Interns participate in Early Career programming, including technical and professional-development sessions, community events, and an end-of-program project presentation.

Firmware Engineer Intern (Summer Co-op)
Location: Vancouver, BC
Job Description
Astera Labs is a global leader in purpose-built connectivity solutions that unlock the full potential of cloud and AI infrastructure.
Our Intelligent Connectivity Platform integrates PCIe, CXL and Ethernet semiconductor-based solutions based on a software-defined architecture that is both scalable and customizable.
Inspired by trusted partnerships with hyperscalers and the data center ecosystem, we are an innovation leader of products that are flexible, interoperable, and reliable.
We are headquartered in the heart of California’s Silicon Valley, with R&D centers and offices in Taiwan, China, Vancouver and Toronto, Canada, and Haifa, Israel.
The mission of this role is to architect and develop firmware and microcontroller subsystems for Astera Labs’ SoC and systems products.
Firmware is responsible for implementing the major differentiating features of Astera Labs’ products. As such, firmware is considered equally important to the hardware, and the firmware team is often customer-facing accordingly to ensure the needs of the customer are fully comprehended.
Basic Qualifications
-
Strong academic and technical background taking Computer Science, Electrical/Electronics/Software Engineering or equivalent.
-
Completed one or more Co-op terms of firmware or embedded software development.
-
Completed one or more courses in Real Time Operating Systems (RTOS) or detailed use of an RTOS during a prior coop term or project.
-
Professional attitude with the ability to formulate theories and well thought out questions as part of helping debug/develop complex systems.
-
Authorized to work in Canada and available for 4 or more months.
Required Experience
-
Proficiency in C (preferred) or C++, including development of firmware.
-
Proficient in Python for scripting.
-
Experience with developer workflows, SCM (preferably git), code reviews, CI.
-
Experience developing firmware to execute in on-chip microcontrollers.
-
Experience debugging firmware/hardware issues using JTAG, trace logs, or other lab tools.
Preferred Experience
-
Knowledge of tools like PyTest or GoogleTest is an asset.
-
Knowledge of software build environments, CI/CD, gcc/make is an asset.
-
Experience with lab hardware/firmware debug is an asset.
-
Experience developing firmware for PCIe/CXL/Ethernet is an asset.
Hourly compensation ranges between CAD $45/hour - CAD $55/hour.

FieldAI’s Irvine team is where embodied AI meets real robots, real sensors, and real field deployments. Based in the heart of Southern California’s robotics ecosystem, we build risk-aware, reliable, field-ready AI systems that solve the hardest problems in robotics and unlock the full potential of embodied intelligence. If you want your work to ship, get tested on hardware, and improve through real deployments, Irvine is the place. We go beyond typical data-driven approaches or pure transformer-only architectures, combining rigorous engineering with learning systems proven in globally deployed solutions that deliver results today and get better every time our robots run in the field.

About the Internship
We are offering Spring, Summer, and Fall 2027 research internships in the Irvine office for Master’s and PhD students advancing robotic manipulation.
You will investigate how robots can perform useful physical tasks reliably across diverse objects, environments, and robot platforms. Working closely with researchers and engineers, you will own a focused research project and help translate promising ideas into capabilities that can be tested on hardware and improved through real deployment experience.
Research directions and methods will be shaped by your expertise and the problems we encounter in the field. The goal is to produce original research with measurable impact on what our robots can accomplish.
What We Offer
-
Real deployment problems: Work on manipulation challenges grounded in customer use cases and operational needs, with opportunities to evaluate beyond controlled laboratory settings.
-
Physical robots and hardware: Develop and validate your work on robotic systems, including humanoids, mobile manipulators, and arm-equipped quadrupeds.
-
Research ownership: Shape a focused project, propose your approach, and carry it through implementation, experimentation, and hardware validation.
-
Deployment feedback: Use observations and failure cases from real operation to guide research and improve reliability.
-
Close technical collaboration: Work with researchers and engineers across robot learning, perception, control, hardware, and deployment.
-
Research contributions: Pursue work suitable for leading conferences and journals, with opportunities to release code, datasets, or other research artifacts.
What You Will Get To Do
-
Develop manipulation capabilities that address meaningful physical tasks in real environments.
-
Investigate how skills transfer across objects, tasks, environments, and robot platforms.
-
Address practical challenges such as uncertainty, contact, changing conditions, and failure recovery.
-
Design experiments that measure task success, generalization, and reliability under realistic operating conditions.
-
Integrate and validate research on physical robots, collaborating with engineering teams to address system constraints.
-
Document findings, present results, and contribute to publications or reusable research tools.
What You Have
-
Current master’s or PhD enrollment in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, AI/ML, or a closely related field.
-
Research experience in robotic manipulation, robot learning, embodied AI, or a related area.
-
A strong research or open-source track record, demonstrated through substantive publications, research software, or technically rigorous projects.
-
Clear ownership of original research or technical development, including implementation and evaluation.
-
Strong foundations in robotics, machine learning, and experimental design.
-
Proficiency in Python and/or C++.
-
Ability to work independently, communicate findings clearly, and collaborate across research and engineering disciplines.
The Extras That Set You Apart
-
First-author publications at venues such as RSS, CoRL, ICRA, IROS, NeurIPS, ICLR, or ICML, or journals such as RA-L, T-RO, or IJRR.
-
Significant contributions to open-source robotics or machine learning projects with demonstrated adoption.
-
Hands-on experience taking research from an initial idea to reliable operation on physical robots.
-
Experience evaluating robotic systems outside controlled laboratory conditions.
-
Public research code, datasets, or robot demonstrations showing technical depth and measurable results.
-
Experience with robot integration, sensing, control, or data collection infrastructure.
Our salary range is generous and we consider each individual’s background and experience when determining final compensation. Base pay may vary based on role scope, job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and the Irvine, California market.
 
Why Join FieldAI in Irvine?
In Irvine, you will work where the robots are. Our local team builds and tests systems on real hardware with real sensors, then ships them to operate in unstructured, previously unknown environments around the world. We are solving one of robotics’ hardest challenges: reliable deployment outside the lab. Our Field Foundational Models™ raise the bar for perception, planning, localization, and manipulation, with an emphasis on explainability and safety for real-world use.
You will collaborate with a world-class team that thrives on creativity, resilience, and bold thinking. We bring deep experience from organizations such as DeepMind, NASA JPL, Boston Dynamics, NVIDIA, Amazon, Tesla Autopilot, Cruise, Zoox, Toyota Research Institute, and SpaceX, along with a track record of field deployments and strong performance in DARPA challenge segments.
 
Be Part of the Next Robotics Revolution
We are looking for builders who want their work to leave the whiteboard and show up on robots. If you enjoy tackling tough, uncharted questions and working across disciplines, you will find your people here. Our teams span AI, software, robotics engineering, product, field deployment, and technical communication, all focused on shipping systems that perform in the real world.
 
Our headquarters is in Irvine, and we partner closely with teams there as well as colleagues across the US and around the world. Join us in Southern California and help define what dependable, field-ready autonomy looks like.
 
We value diverse perspectives and are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace. We evaluate candidates and employees based on merit, qualifications, and performance, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, gender, national origin, ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, or any other legally protected status.

Rebuild how the world works, to make institutions work better for the people they serve.




ABOUT BRAIN CO.

Brain Co. builds AI-native operating systems for large, regulated institutions. Each system is built for a specific industry, powered by agents that push real workflows forward. Underneath it all is Atlas, our proprietary platform that keeps customers in control, secure by design, and never locked into one model.




WHY NOW

Brain Co. is entering its next phase of production deployments on a national scale with an elite team built from Palantir, Google, Meta, and Nvidia, and a growing footprint across government, insurance, health, and financial services.

Joining now means shaping both the company and a new category of applied AI. Every project here ships to production and is expected to create measurable customer value and impact.

You'll work alongside exceptional peers on some of the hardest problems in applied AI. It’s the kind of work you'll still be proud of in ten years from now.


ABOUT THE ROLE

As an AI Product Intern, you will work closely with engineers, researchers, and product leaders to help design, build, and deploy AI-powered software solving real-world problems. This is a highly hands-on role where you’ll gain exposure to the full product lifecycle, from understanding customer needs to shipping production-grade AI applications.

You’ll contribute directly to live projects used by governments, healthcare systems, and industrial partners, while learning how cutting-edge AI is turned into real, scalable products.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

Build & Ship Real Products: Support the design and development of AI-powered features across front-end, back-end, and data workflows. Help prototype and ship internal tools and customer-facing applications using modern web technologies

Learn Product + Engineering in Practice: Work with product managers and engineers to translate customer problems into clear product requirements. Gain exposure to how AI models are integrated into real-world software systems

Collaborate Closely: Partner with engineers, researchers, and operators to test, iterate, and improve AI-driven workflows. Participate in design discussions, sprint planning, and code reviews

Optimize & Improve: Assist with improving performance, reliability, and usability of deployed applications. Help analyze data, evaluate AI outputs, and iterate based on real customer feedback

Make a Real Impact: Contribute to projects modernizing government workflows, improving healthcare outcomes, or optimizing critical infrastructure. See your work deployed and used by real users — not just internal demos




YOU WILL THRIVE IF YOU:

 - Have experience with software development fundamentals (through coursework, internships, or personal projects).

 - Are familiar with or excited to learn technologies like Python, TypeScript, React, REST APIs, and cloud platforms

 - Are curious about AI systems, product thinking, and real-world applications of machine learning

 - Enjoy solving ambiguous problems and learning quickly in fast-paced environments

 - Communicate clearly, collaborate well, and take ownership of your work

 - Are excited to work directly on impactful problems rather than purely theoretical projects


CO-OP DETAILS & BENEFITS

 - Winter / Spring Co-Op: January 11, 2027 - April 30, 2027

 - Competitive co-op compensation

 - Hands-on mentorship from experienced AI engineers and researchers

 - Opportunity to work on real production systems used globally

 - Potential return-offer consideration for future internships or full-time roles

 - Daily lunches (if onsite)

Tenstorrent is leading the industry on cutting-edge AI technology, revolutionizing performance expectations, ease of use, and cost efficiency. With AI redefining the computing paradigm, solutions must evolve to unify innovations in software models, compilers, platforms, networking, and semiconductors. Our diverse team of technologists have developed a high performance RISC-V CPU from scratch, and share a passion for AI and a deep desire to build the best AI platform possible. We value collaboration, curiosity, and a commitment to solving hard problems. We are growing our team and looking for contributors of all seniorities.
Overview: A chip isn't a product until it's a working system. These teams cover both ends of that: getting silicon to boot and validate correctly,building the board, power, mechanical, thermal, packaging and IO around it. You submit one application, you have one recruiter screen - then we match you to the specific team below and location that fits best.
- Systems & Silicon Validation: Post-silicon testing of physical chips and integrated systems to ensure they meet all functional, electrical, and performance specs.
- System Software: Development of foundational software, including firmware, drivers, and operating systems, that directly controls and interfaces with hardware.
- System Design: The process of defining, integrating, and mapping out hardware components such as PCBs, software modules, and interfaces into a complete product blueprint.
- System Architecture: Define the high-level structural framework, interfaces, and data-flow pathways between the CPU, memory, and peripherals.
- Packaging: A package is what is placed between the silicon and the board; and its design requires detailed electrical, electromagnetic, and mechanical simulations and analysis.
This role is on-site based out of Toronto, Ontario or Vancouver, British Columbia.
Who You Are
- Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in EE, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or Mechanical Engineering
- Coursework or projects in embedded systems, microwave and signal integrity, board-level design, or thermal/mechanical engineering using low-level programming (C/C++, Python) or hardware design and/or simulation tools (e.g., CAD, FEA, Verilog).
- Problem solver with strong foundational knowledge in one of these areas: electrical engineering, digital logic, computer architecture, or thermal/mechanical.
- Curious learner who is passionate about the intersection of software, silicon architecture, and the physical constraints of chip packaging and printed circuit boards (PCBs).
What We Need
- Systems & Silicon Validation: Assist in post-silicon testing of physical microchips under real-world workloads to ensure they meet all functional, electrical, and performance specifications.
- System Software: Contribute to developing foundational software—including firmware, drivers, and operating systems—that directly controls and interfaces with the semiconductor hardware.
- System Design & Architecture: Help map out, define, and evaluate high-level structural frameworks, optimizing the power delivery and high-speed performance benchmarks of both the silicon components and the underlying PCBs.
- Semiconductor Packaging & Mechanical Design: Design and layout, Electromagnetic (signal integrity and power integrity), mechanical design, and stress analysis
What You Will Learn
- Hands-on silicon experience using industry-standard lab equipment to bridge the gap between theoretical hardware design, physical packaging layouts, and real-world chips.
- Low-level software development by writing production-grade firmware, device drivers, and diagnostic tools that run directly on bare metal.
- Mechanical & thermal engineering for electronics by learning how structural stress, heat dissipation, thermal expansion, and mechanical shock affect the structural integrity and performance of PCBs and packages.
- Cross-functional collaboration working alongside world-class architects, mechanical designers, package engineers, and software teams to understand how complex, large-scale chip ecosystems are built from scratch.
Tenstorrent offers a highly competitive compensation package and benefits, and we are an equal opportunity employer.

About the Hiring Team
Level Infinite is Tencent’s global gaming brand. It is a global game publisher offering a comprehensive network of services for games, development teams, and studios around the world.
We are dedicated to delivering engaging and original gaming experiences to a worldwide audience, whenever and wherever they choose to play while building a community that fosters inclusivity, connection, and accessibility. Level Infinite also provides a wide range of services and resources to our network of developers and partner studios around the world to help them unlock the true potential of their games.
What the Role Entails
We are hiring a research intern to train LLM agents that play in-game characters. The agent has to stay in persona across multi-turn dialogue, use memory and game context, and keep relationship, tone, and world rules intact. The work sits on a live role-play NPC model: supervised fine-tuning today, with preference optimization and verifiable-reward reinforcement learning as the next training stages. 1. Train role-play agents with supervised fine-tuning (SFT), then post-train them with direct preference optimization (DPO) and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). Iterate on persona consistency, multi-turn coherence, and instruction following.

About the Team
The Embodied AI Research team advances artificial intelligence methods for autonomous vehicles and embodied systems. We explore how models can combine visual and sensor understanding, language and other modalities, reasoning, prediction, and action to address challenging problems in autonomous driving.
Our work includes foundation models, vision-language and vision-language-action architectures, generative and world models, self-supervised learning, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, multimodal learning, and methods for learning from large-scale driving data. We work closely with engineering teams to translate research into reliable systems for real-world autonomy.
About the Role
As an Embodied AI Research Intern, you will conduct applied research on a well-scoped project at the intersection of machine learning, robotics, and autonomous driving. You will work with experienced researchers and engineers to develop hypotheses, design experiments, train and evaluate models, analyze results, and communicate findings.
Potential focus areas include:
- Foundation Models for Autonomy: Develop or adapt large-scale models that learn useful representations and capabilities from diverse driving data.
- Vision-Language-Action Models: Explore architectures that connect multimodal perception and high-level reasoning with autonomous vehicle decisions and actions.
- Generative and World Models: Use generative techniques to model complex driving environments, improve scenario understanding, or support planning and simulation.
- Learning for Planning and Control: Apply imitation learning, reinforcement learning, or other learning methods to improve prediction, decision-making, and vehicle behavior.
- Multimodal and Temporal Learning: Build methods that reason over camera, lidar, radar, map, language, and time-series information.
What You’ll Do
- Formulate research problems and develop prototypes for autonomous driving applications.
- Design and run experiments, ablation studies, and quantitative evaluations.
- Train and benchmark models using large-scale datasets and distributed compute infrastructure.
- Analyze model behavior, failure cases, generalization, and performance tradeoffs.
- Collaborate with perception, planning, robotics, controls, and systems engineering teams.
- Contribute to technical discussions, research documentation, publications, patents, or open-source work where appropriate.
- Present findings clearly to technical and cross-functional audiences.
Required Qualifications
- Currently pursuing or in the process of obtaining a Masters in Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, Robotics, or a related technical field.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with experience designing experiments and interpreting results.
- Ability to work collaboratively in a cross-functional, team-oriented environment.
- Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills.
- Availability to work full-time, 40 hours per week, during the internship period.
Preferred Qualifications
- Experience with transformers, large language models, vision-language models, vision-language-action models, diffusion models, or other generative architectures.
- Experience with reinforcement learning, imitation learning, self-supervised learning, world models, multimodal learning, or temporal modeling.
- Familiarity with autonomous vehicles, advanced driver assistance systems, robotics, or embodied AI.
- Experience working with large-scale datasets, distributed training, high-performance computing, or model scaling.
- Evidence of significant technical results through first-authored publications, grants, fellowships, patents, or open-source contributions. Relevant venues may include NeurIPS, CVPR, ICML, ICLR, AAAI, ECCV, RSS, ICRA, CoRL, or similar conferences and workshops.

Position Title: DoW Forward Deployed Engineer Intern
Location: Hybrid to Joint Base Lewis McChord
Clearance Requirement: Active Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility
Employment type: SkillBridge Internship
 
Research Innovations, Inc. (RII) is breaking through the big, slow, status quo with transformative technology that fundamentally changes and improves the world. We develop cutting-edge software for all levels of the government and military. Using agile development practices and user-centered design, we create innovative software solutions for complex real-world problems. 
 
We are looking for a Skill Bridge Intern to learn the Forward Deployed Engineer position with our CJADC2 business area. This role requires a candidate to be approved for Skillbridge or Career Skills internship programs through their respective branch of the military. You will learn to be the technical engine bridging the front lines of defense with our engineering teams. Your mission is to build, code, and architect high-stakes software directly in the operational environment. You don't just bridge the gap—you translate complex, messy operational requirements into stable software solutions, while simultaneously serving as the systems architect responsible for data ontology, schema coordination, and engineering requirements that define our platform's integration strategy.

This position requires an active U.S.Top Secret security clearance with SCI eligibility.

WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING
-
Learn to architect and design scalable solutions for complex, high-stakes technical problems in both cloud and disconnected, tactical edge environments.
-
Develop custom, high-impact applications (Python, Java, C++, TypeScript) to bridge legacy limitations, while concurrently architecting stable data pipelines and defining schema ontologies for large-scale integration.
-
Decompose mission-critical operational workflows into clear, deliberate technical requirements and engineering specs that drive the development of scalable, secure product features.
Collaborate with internal engineering teams to drive projects from initial ideation and prototyping through to full-scale, secure deployment.
-
Learn to lead systems integration efforts, linking modern software to legacy military C2 and targeting platforms, and troubleshooting system-of-systems architecture at the tactical edge.
-
Rapidly iterate on solutions based on direct user feedback, maintaining a high pain threshold to deliver measurable, real-world value.
WHAT YOU HAVE DONE
-
1+ years of relevant, post-college software engineering or development experience.
-
Strong systems engineering background—with the ability to draft technical specs and manage system-wide data models—alongside a robust foundation in Computer Science or Software Engineering.
-
Proven proficiency as a coder in one or more modern programming languages, and demonstrated experience in systems integration, schema design, or data modeling within complex environments.
-
Demonstrated ability to build, deploy, and maintain software solutions that handle data, logic, and operational complexity.
Experience engaging with non-technical stakeholders or mission users to turn abstract requirements into concrete code.
-
History of success in unstructured, rapidly evolving environments where initiative and high-quality output are required.
EVEN BETTER
-
Advanced expertise in data structures, storage systems, cloud infrastructure (e.g., AWS, Azure), and container orchestration (e.g., Kubernetes).
-
Practical experience working with large-scale data and applying AI/ML libraries to address practical operational challenges.
Hands-on experience developing in disconnected (DDIL), air-gapped, or tactical edge environments.
-
Deep curiosity about the underlying technical architecture and a "low ego" approach that values the mission outcome over personal recognition.
At RII, we believe that diversity in our workforce is critical to our success. We strive to hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds, not just because it’s the right thing to do, but because it makes us stronger. We work to help your intellectual passions and creativity thrive. It’s one of our core values: Let your geek flag fly.
We also offer all employees comprehensive benefits including: flexible work schedules, health insurance coverage, paid time off, 401k with a company match, paid parental leave, access to wellness programs and much more. You get this all from day one, and all paid for by RII.
It’s all part of another of our core values: Stay human. It’s why our comfortable and colorful offices such as our headquarters, include a community game room, pantry, massage chair, and an escape room, among other amenities. It’s why we have community ambassadors and regular community events.
Research Innovations, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, national origin, genetics, disability status, protected veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by state, federal or local law.

To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology.
What You'll Do
In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise.
KLA is looking for summer interns at our Ann Arbor, Michigan location. This position provides an opportunity to work with engineering teams on projects aiming to develop and characterize laser plasma light sources for KLA’s next generation inspection and metrology tools! In particular, the intern would work in the following areas:
- Develop methods and test plans for characterization of laser plasmas
- Design optical systems for imaging, shadowgraphy, and interferometry
- Work with vacuum chambers and related equipment.
- Design, set up and execute multi-disciplinary experiments.
- Analyze data and prepare summary reports.
- Work with simulations based on physical models and build correlations with experimental data.
- Collaborate with scientists at external partner organizations.
Qualifications:
- Experience with plasma metrology (e.g. pump/probe, spectroscopy, imaging)
- Experience with high power lasers
- Strong academic record.
- Familiarity with optical design software (e.g., Zemax, Code V, LightTools) or simulation tools (e.g., COMSOL, ANSYS) is desirable.
- Experience with laboratory equipment and data acquisition systems.
- Proficiency in programming languages such as Python, MATLAB, or C++ is a plus.
- Excellent problem-solving skills and a strong analytical mindset.
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
- Effective written and verbal communication skills.
Minimum Qualifications
Currently enrolled in 4-year graduate program in Physics, Optical Engineering or related field with immigration authorization to undertake corporate internship projects.
About KLA
We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us.
Total Rewards
Base Pay Range: $27.00 - $48.00 per hour based on pursuit of a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Ph.D.
Primary Location: USA-MI-Ann Arbor-KLA
KLA’s total rewards package for employees may also include participation in performance incentive programs and eligibility for additional benefits including but not limited to: medical, dental, vision, life, and other voluntary benefits, 401(K) including company matching, employee stock purchase program (ESPP), student debt assistance, tuition reimbursement program, development and career growth opportunities and programs, financial planning benefits, wellness benefits including an employee assistance program (EAP), paid time off and paid company holidays, and family care and bonding leave.
Interns are eligible for some of the benefits listed. Our pay ranges are determined by role, level, and location. The range displayed reflects the pay for this position in the primary location identified in this posting. Actual pay depends on several factors, including state minimum pay wage rates, location, job-related skills, experience, and relevant education level or training. We are committed to complying with all applicable federal and state minimum wage requirements where applicable. If applicable, your recruiter can share more about the specific pay range for your preferred location during the hiring process.

At KLA, our interviews seek to understand your individual skills, problem-solving approach and authentic thinking. GlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors, enabling AI at scale from the cloud to the physical world. As an intern at GF, you’ll experience one-on-one mentorship, work assignments that prioritize your growth and potential, professional development opportunities, and the chance to network with executives.
Summary of Role:
Support GF Labs' R&D portfolio by collaborating with university researchers, Value Added Partners, and the GF External R&D team on a variety of requests including Account Management (AM) and Field Application Engineering (FAE tasks) as well as identifying and analyzing recurring requirements with the goal to automate them. This internship will contribute to portfolio management, data-driven reporting, AI-enabled process improvements, and the execution of new research partnership opportunities across complex initiatives.
Essential Responsibilities include:
- Support new in-kind collaborations and requests for government funded proposals out of GF Labs with D365 support incl. AM, FAE, and sales tasks enabling tapeouts and ROM
- Contribute to identification, evaluation, and tracking of new collaboration opportunities through active research, competitive analysis, and selection
- Optimization of in-kind tracking and accounting processes by developing and maintaining tools for analysis and reporting of portfolio, status, and results
- Work with internal team on shaping the new look of the web database presenting the collaborations and their results: create a concept of organization and representation
- Implement new views using Power BI while building on the existing data representations & systems including TeamCenter, Microsoft D365, Anaplan
- Use AI (including agents) to streamline internal tasks within ExR&D such as program tracking, reporting, data organization etc. that improve data analysis and evaluation
- Individual has strong background in IT systems like PowerBi and databases
Other Responsibilities:
- Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs.
Required Qualifications:
- Education – At least a sophomore at time of application and actively pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s in Business, Engineering, Data Science, Finance, Public Policy, Research Administration or related field through an accredited degree program during the time of internship.
- Must have at least an overall 3.0 GPA and be in good academic standing.
- Language Fluency - English (Written & Verbal)
- Ability to work at least 40 hours per week during the internship.

- Prior related internship or co-op experience
- Demonstrated prior leadership experience in the workplace, school projects, competitions, etc.
- Project management skills, i.e., the ability to innovate and execute on solutions that matter; the ability to navigate ambiguity.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills
- Strong planning & organizational skills
- Experience with data analytics, dashboarding, Excel, Power BI, Python, or similar reporting tools.

The Meta Reality Labs Research Team brings together a world-class team of researchers, developers, and engineers to create the future of virtual and augmented reality, which together will become as universal and essential as smartphones and personal computers are today.
In particular, the Meta Reality Labs Research Audio team works on technologies that help people hear and communicate better in everyday life, from spatial audio to hearing assistance on AI glasses. Recent work includes Conversation Focus, which helps people hear the person they're talking to in noisy environments. As wearable devices become part of daily life, understanding how people actually listen, attend, and communicate in real-world settings is central to building audio experiences that adapt to each person.
We are looking for interns who want to model how people listen and communicate in the real world. Using multimodal, egocentric data from wearable devices (eye and head movement, speech and vocal behavior, gesture, and the acoustic scene), the intern will build models that infer listening and communication states such as auditory attention, listening effort, and conversational engagement. Ground truth for these states is often sparse or ambiguous. The goal is to inform hearing assistance and audio technologies that adapt to the listener.
The role suits candidates with a background in machine learning, computer science, hearing science, or auditory or cognitive neuroscience, who want to work at the intersection of those fields. Successful candidates will combine strong quantitative and machine learning skills with an understanding of human hearing and communication. Specific projects will be designed with successful applicants to match their skills and experience to current research needs.
Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

The Speculative Decoding team at Together AI builds the draft models and algorithms that let large language models generate faster without changing their outputs. Our speculators run in production on frontier open models such as DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM. Our work sits at the intersection of model training, inference algorithms and serving systems, and we co-design all three to lower the cost and latency of generation.
As a research intern, you will dive into open questions in speculative decoding: new drafter architectures and verification schemes, knowledge distillation and training recipes that align draft and target models, and drafters that adapt as traffic shifts. You will train and fine-tune draft models at scale on dedicated GPU clusters, and test your ideas against realistic serving workloads, including long-context and agentic traffic.
Projects aim to answer important research questions in speculative decoding, enabling faster generation on frontier models, drafters that keep pace with changing workloads, and robust, reproducible evaluation under real traffic.

- Speculative Speculative Decoding (ICLR 2026)

- Beat the Long Tail: Distribution-Aware Speculative Decoding for RL Training (MLSys 2026)

About Didi Autonomous Driving
Founded in 2016, DiDi's autonomous driving unit is dedicated to developing Level 4 autonomous driving technology to make transportation safer, more efficient, and accessible. In 2019, the unit became an independent company, Voyager, to accelerate technology development, commercialization, and large-scale deployment. By combining DiDi's unique data advantage, operational expertise, and mobility ecosystem, we aim to build a reliable, scalable autonomous fleet that integrates seamlessly with human-driven services. Driven by real-world customer needs and a strong commitment to safety and user experience , our mission is to deliver autonomous mobility solutions that create meaningful value for riders and communities.
About the Role
We want our vehicles to understand the physical world as it is right now, instead of relying on a map drawn long ago. Roads change, and the world a car actually drives in is always more complex than any static record of it. We are seeking a Research Intern to help give our planner a m ore accurate and up-to-date picture of the world, so the vehicle handles complex real-world scenes more robustly. In this role, you will take on hard, open problems from real-world driving and solve them with frontier research methods. You will report directly to the team lead and work on the problem from definition to validated solution. Strong results will often be worth publishing, and we will support you in writing them up, but the goal is to solve problems that matter to the product.
Responsibilities
-
Survey the latest research in scene understanding, prediction, and planning, and turn it into practical approaches that fit our system and constraints.
-
Design and implement deep learning models that build a richer, real-time understanding of the driving environment from onboard sensors and other available sources.
-
Train and evaluate models on large-scale data from our driving logs and on public benchmarks, and lead failure analysis to find out where and why models fall short.
-
Define metrics and evaluation methods that connect perception quality to how the vehicle actually drives.
-
Turn successful prototypes into solutions that work with our planning stack, with help from production engineers.
-
Collaborate with Perception, Prediction, Planning, and Mapping teams so results move from experiment to product.
Qualifications
-
Currently enrolled in an M.S. or Ph.D. program in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Machine Learning, or a related field, for the full duration of the internship.
-
Available for a full-time onsite internship of 3–6 months; start dates are flexible.
-
Strong programming skills in Python, and experience with modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX.
-
Hands-on experience designing, training, and debugging deep learning models for computer vision, 3D perception, or sequential decision-making.
-
Solid understanding of autonomous driving fundamentals, including perception, prediction, and motion planning.
-
Ability to read research critically, form hypotheses, and turn them into well-controlled experiments.
-
Excellent communication and collaboration skills.
Preferred Qualifications
-
Publications at top venues such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, ICRA, IROS, CoRL or IV.
-
Experience with multi-modal sensor fusion (camera, lidar, radar) or BEV representations.
-
Experience with transformers, graph neural networks, or other structured scene representations.
-
Experience with uncertainty estimation, or with learning-based prediction or planning.
-
Experience with large-scale model training and data pipelines.
-
Experience with public autonomous driving datasets such as nuScenes, Argoverse 2, or the Waymo Open Dataset.
-
Proficiency in C++ (CUDA is a plus) and experience with robotics systems.

SpAItial is pioneering the next generation of World Models, pushing the boundaries of generative AI, computer vision, and the simulation of reality. We are moving beyond 2D pixels to build models that natively understand the physics and geometry of our world. Our mission is to redefine how industries, from robotics and AR/VR to gaming and cinema, generate and interact with physically-grounded 3D environments.

 

We're looking for bold, innovative individuals driven by a passion for pushing the boundaries of generative 3D AI. You should thrive in an environment where creativity meets technical challenge and be fearless in tackling the hardest problems in 3D world modeling. Our team is built on a foundation of dedication and a shared commitment to excellence, so we value people who take immense pride in their work and place the collective goals of the team above personal ambition. As a part of SpAItial, you'll be at the forefront of building World Models that bridge generative AI and the physical world. If you're ready to make an impact, embrace the unknown, and collaborate with a talented group of visionaries, we want to hear from you.

 

We're seeking PhD Research Interns to work with our research team on open problems in 3D generation and reconstruction. You should have strong knowledge of at least one of our core areas, such as generative video and diffusion models, scene representations like Gaussian splats and radiance fields, or 3D reconstruction from per-scene optimization to feed-forward models. Over a 5-7 month internship, you will own a well-defined research question with the goal of publishing a paper. 

 

Responsibilities

 - You will explore novel research directions in 3D generation, reconstruction, and world models. 

 - You will design, implement, and evaluate state-of-the-art methods, turning innovative research ideas into working systems and prototypes. 

 - You will be working closely with our research team.

 -  You will also present your findings and contribute to scientific publications targeting leading conferences in computer vision, computer graphics, and machine learning, such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, SIGGRAPH, NeurIPS, and ICLR.

Key Qualifications

 - Currently enrolled in the third year or beyond of a PhD in computer science, computer vision, computer graphics, machine learning, or a related field.

 - 2-3 first-author papers at top-tier conferences such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, SIGGRAPH, NeurIPS, or ICLR.

 - Knowledge of at least one of: generative models (diffusion or video models), neural scene representations, or 3D reconstruction.

 

At SpAItial, we are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer and ensure all candidates are treated fairly throughout the recruitment process.

Explore a career at Graphcore through a 12-week summer internship, gaining hands-on experience on real projects. Put your programming skills to work exploring how firmware brings AI hardware to life, from first boot to system monitoring.

Working closely to with our silicon and hardware teams, you’ll contribute to software that supports hardware bootup and provides telemetry and monitoring data that helps data centre operators understand what the hardware is doing.

- Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to document complex system designs coherently

ABOUT METAMORPHIC

Metamorphic is developing new approaches to intelligence by combining machine learning with large-scale experimental neuroscience, informed by the principles that make the brain efficient, flexible, and robust. We are building foundation models trained on rich, continuous neural data — a high-resolution model of the brain at a scale never before possible.

Our founding team spans machine learning, neuroscience, and neurotechnology, with prior work including the MICrONS project https://www.nature.com/immersive/d42859-025-00001-w/index.html, Neuropixels http://neuropixels.org/, and the Enigma project https://www.enigmaproject.ai/, as well as foundational scientific contributions in learning, neural computation, and generative modeling. Our work sits at the frontier of AI research, and we believe the highest-impact discoveries will come from researchers and engineers working as a single, tightly collaborative team.

The name Metamorphic reflects our belief that the next advances in intelligence will come from a change in form, beyond scale — from artificial to natural intelligence.

We are seeking interns across a broad range of roles including computer vision, embodied AI and RL, robotics, agentic systems, language modeling, computational neuroscience, and ML engineering to join our growing AI research team for the summer. We offer:

 - The chance to work on one of the most scientifically consequential AI projects being pursued today

 - A small, world-class team where your contributions directly shape the science and the company

 - Strong mentorship and career development

$6-8k/month depending on seniority.

Application Deadline: November 10th, 2026

Interviews: November 11th - November 26th, 2026

Decision Release: December 1st, 2026

About FSH

FSH Tech builds modern software that just works for the public sector. When we deliver, taxpayer dollars go further, agencies move faster, and millions of Americans get tangibly better service and quality of life.

Local governments, schools, libraries, and emergency services run on brittle software that was built decades ago. This results in wasted budgets, broken workflows, and bad outcomes for the public. We believe that the institutions closest to people's daily lives deserve products as good as anything in the private sector. We're building them.

We're a small, high-agency team. The people who do their best work here are:

 - Relentlessly optimistic in creating a better world now

 - Driven to maximize societal impact

 - Brilliant and creative

 

About FSH Engineering

Our ideal candidate is an expert in their craft. They gain energy from understanding how their chosen tools work, and have used their tools to build software many times. Our ideal candidate is obsessively curious, motivated by customer outcomes, and is a technical artist.

We use Python, Postgres, Unix, TypeScript and React to build software. We maintain a set of internal tools to deterministically generate Python and Typescript. We obsess over how to build compounding advantages in tooling, software, and product. You don’t need to know our stack coming in. Strong fundamentals and fast learning matter more.

 

About the Internship

This is a 10-week paid internship opportunity.

We want to work with people who love to learn and do so quickly! Much of an engineer’s job involves learning by doing, and this is our pathway for those with less experience to do just that. You'll be building real projects for real customers.

Our work balances the deeply technical with the fundamentally human; we switch from technical architecture to design critique to product construction quickly. You will be paired with a senior engineer who focuses on mentorship. They'll help you set goals from the start, expand your scope and ownership, and pair with you often when you're stuck.

There is no predefined destination for this role and we don’t believe in having others do work we wouldn’t do ourselves (e.g. this isn’t a cover for ‘you will simply respond to tickets'). We want to help you ship customer value and will enable you to do so throughout your internship. 

Strong interns will be considered for a full-time offer.

 

What You'll Do

 - Build and maintain software for customers

 - Seek and ingest feedback

 - Iterate quickly

 

What You'll Need (optional)

 - Experience shipping software to users

 

You’re the right person for the job if many of these are true:

 - You believe programming is a creative pursuit

 - You are a perennial tinkerer

 - You gain energy from being close to the customer, always

 - You are obsessed with focused learning

 - You believe abstractions can simplify complexity

 - You love pattern seeking, e.g.:
   
   - Modern inventory management is best handled through Venetian double entry accounting
   
   - Buddhist meditation and dialectical behavior therapy are closely related
   
   - The distribution of crater sizes on the moon follow a power law
   
   - Rivers and their tributaries, blood vessels, lunch bronchi, broccoli, and lightning bolts all demonstrate related patterns

 

Interns are expected to live in New York City or Philadelphia and work out of our office in either location.

Job Details
About Salesforce
Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.
Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.
The Experience
Salesforce AI Research is a global leader in Enterprise AI, driving innovations that advance the state of AI while powering enterprise products at worldwide scale.
Our research has helped shape multiple generations of modern AI: we helped pioneer prompt engineering through DecaNLP; introduced BLIP, a foundational breakthrough in multimodal AI; trained state-of-the-art large language models including CodeGen; and pioneered foundation models for time series with Moirai. Today, we continue to advance the frontier of enterprise AI through innovations in AI simulation environments like eVerse, our simulation and agent-training environment; the Atlas Reasoning Engine, which powers Agentforce reasoning capabilities; and other AI systems that are redefining how enterprises reason, plan, and act.
What makes our team unique is our ability to take ideas from research to real-world impact at scale. We work closely with product teams and enterprise customers to translate cutting-edge research into production AI capabilities used by millions of users. We also continue to publish at the world's top AI conferences, open source influential research, and collaborate with leading academic institutions. Learn more at Salesforce AI Research .
We are looking for entrepreneurial Research Interns for Summer 2027 who want to help build the next generation of Enterprise AI. This is not a traditional research internship. You will work like a founder within Salesforce: exploring high-impact research directions, prototyping cutting-edge AI capabilities, and seeing how ideas are validated with customers and turned into production-ready solutions. You will have the freedom to propose and explore new ideas, alongside mentors and research scientists, with access to Salesforce's global customer and product ecosystem. We are looking for people who are comfortable with ambiguity, bring energy and focus to their work, and care as much about customer adoption as technical innovation. If you want the pace and ownership of a startup, combined with the reach and resources of Salesforce, this internship offers a unique opportunity to do research with global impact.
What You'll Actually Be Doing
- Collaborate with research scientists and engineers on a project focused on real-world product impact, with the opportunity to publish your work at top-tier conferences.
- Explore research directions with the potential to transform Enterprise AI.
- Help turn promising ideas into zero-to-one AI product prototypes.
- Build models, agents, and AI systems for real-world enterprise use.
- Learn how research partners with product, engineering, and go-to-market teams to bring solutions to market.
You're Our Person If...

- You have experience with Python and deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, or DeepSpeed.
- You are motivated by real-world impact and care about seeing your research leave the lab and reach users at scale.
- You bring expertise in one or more core focus areas:
- Agentic AI and Reasoning: LLM-powered agents, reinforcement learning (RL), reasoning and planning, autonomous workflows, computer use agents, deep research agents, and coding agents.
- Multimodal and Computer Vision: Vision-language models, video understanding, and multimodal AI agents.
- Speech Intelligence: Voice intelligence, text-to-speech/automatic speech recognition, and low-latency audio processing.
- Core Modeling and Post-Training: Pre-training and post-training techniques including RLHF and direct preference optimization, model distillation, evaluation, and time series modeling.
- You can conduct research with guidance from mentors, and you are ready to grow toward independence and translate ideas into impactful systems.
Even Better If...
- You are a PhD or MS candidate in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or a related technical field.
- You have experience building and scaling ML models for real-world applications.
- You have strong programming skills (competitive programming, e.g., ACM-ICPC, or open source experience).
- You are thoughtful about responsible AI, trust, and the real-world impact of the systems you build.
- You are a fantastic problem solver, able to tackle challenges the world hasn't solved before.
- You have excellent written and spoken communication skills.
- You collaborate effectively with teammates.

PROGRAM OVERVIEW

The ClickHouse PhD Research Internship Program offers doctoral students the opportunity to pursue ambitious research alongside ClickHouse Labs researchers and engineers working on some of the most interesting challenges in databases, systems, and data infrastructure.

Research interns join ClickHouse Labs for approximately 10-12 weeks to explore meaningful research questions, develop new ideas, and investigate technologies that have the potential to advance both the broader research community and the future of ClickHouse.

The program is intentionally designed around research collaboration. Interns are paired with experienced researchers and have the opportunity to pursue work that aligns with their academic interests, ongoing research, and areas of interest within ClickHouse Labs. In some cases, an internship may build on research, a prototype, or a system the student has already begun exploring at their university.

We believe the strongest research relationships extend beyond a single summer. Interns may continue their work after returning to their university through academic research, open-source contributions, publications, or other forms of collaboration. Where there is a strong mutual fit, an internship may become the beginning of a longer-term relationship between the researcher, ClickHouse Labs, and the broader academic community.

During their internship, researchers will have the opportunity to work closely with ClickHouse Labs, engage with ClickHouse's open-source technology and engineering community, share their findings, and contribute to the intellectual life of the broader research community.

Program length: 10-12 weeks, with flexibility based on academic calendars and research needs

Typical timing: Summer, beginning approximately June 1

Locations: Opportunities available across the US and Europe, subject to role and employment requirements. Remote first.

Research environment: ClickHouse Labs

Internship format: Research-focused, mentor-supported, and shaped around areas of mutual research interest

Compensation: commensurate with experience, a monthly stipend will be paid




RESEARCH AT CLICKHOUSE LABS

ClickHouse Labs explores ambitious ideas at the intersection of databases, distributed systems, data infrastructure, and the broader systems research community.

We believe some of the most interesting advances in these areas happen through close collaboration between industry and academia. ClickHouse Labs brings together researchers and engineers to explore new ideas, investigate challenging technical problems, and connect academic research with real-world systems at scale.

Research interns are an important part of that community. Interns have the opportunity to bring their own research interests and perspectives into ClickHouse Labs while working alongside researchers and engineers who are deeply engaged with both the practical challenges and open research questions shaping the future of data systems.




PROGRAM GOALS

 1. Identify exceptional PhD researchers working in areas directly relevant to ClickHouse.

 2. Give researchers the opportunity to work on meaningful, open-ended problems with ClickHouse Labs.

 3. Build long-term relationships with researchers and academic institutions.

 4. Encourage continued research and open-source contributions after the internship.

 5. Create opportunities for co-authored papers, thesis advising, or other academic collaboration.

 6. Increase ClickHouse's visibility within the database and systems research community.

 7. Publish and share meaningful research outcomes through the ClickHouse website and other appropriate channels.


WHAT MAKES THE PROGRAM DIFFERENT

This is intentionally not a highly structured engineering internship and should not detailed planning. ****But the high-level problem area and expectations should defined several months before the internship begins. This flexibility is intentional and allows ClickHouse Labs to respond to:

 - Emerging research questions

 - Current ClickHouse priorities

 - New academic research

 - Interesting systems or database prototypes

 - Work candidates have already completed

 - Opportunities to apply new research ideas to ClickHouse

The goal is to identify researchers whose work is already closely aligned with areas ClickHouse cares about and then determine the most valuable research problem to pursue together.




CANDIDATE PROFILE

We are looking for exceptional PhD students conducting research directly relevant to ClickHouse and the broader database/systems space.




IDEAL CANDIDATES

 - Currently pursuing a PhD in computer science or a closely related field

 - Conducting research in areas relevant to ClickHouse

 - Demonstrated research excellence

 - Strong database systems, distributed systems, hardware, or related technical background

 - Has demonstrated ability to independently pursue complex research questions

 - Ideally has prior experience with ClickHouse open source but not required**.**

 - Has research, prototypes, or publications that could translate into meaningful work with ClickHouse

 - Interested in continuing research beyond the internship

 - Potential interest in open-source contribution and academic collaboration


CANDIDATE SELECTION PHILOSOPHY

The strongest candidates will be researchers whose work is specifically relevant to what ClickHouse Labs wants to explore.

A candidate who has already:

 - Worked with ClickHouse

 - Built a relevant database or systems prototype

 - Published research in an area relevant to ClickHouse

 - Explored a technical problem ClickHouse is interested in

may be significantly more valuable than a candidate with an otherwise impressive academic profile but no meaningful connection to our research areas.




RESEARCH AREAS & PROJECT SCOPE

Unlike an engineering internship program, specific projects do not need to be defined when recruiting begins.

Research projects may emerge from:

 - A candidate's existing research

 - A recent academic paper

 - A prototype or system the candidate has developed

 - An emerging ClickHouse Labs research priority

 - An opportunity to test or extend an existing research concept within ClickHouse

Meta was built to help people connect and share, and over the last decade our tools have played a critical part in changing how people around the world communicate with one another. With over a billion people using the service and more than fifty offices around the globe, a career at Meta offers countless ways to make an impact in a fast growing organization.
Meta is seeking Research Interns to join our AI Search research team. We are committed to advancing the field of artificial intelligence by making fundamental advances in how AI agents learn from their own experience — improving their search and reasoning workflows, retaining useful knowledge, and transferring those gains to unfamiliar tasks. A central research challenge is making repeated self-improvement reliable when feedback is sparse or noisy.
The intern will work in one of three directions, scoped closer to the start date together with the intern manager:
-Learning to improve research workflows — agents learn better search, tool-use and verification strategies from prior attempts by improving their harness: the workflow, memory, tools and feedback loop around the model. Topics include meta-learning across tasks, automated agent design, and learning from natural-language feedback.
-Persistent memory and continual learning — agents retain useful lessons and update knowledge across tasks, whether in context, in compressed memory, or in weights, without forgetting what they already know. Topics include long-context modeling, context compression, continual learning, and test-time training.
-Learning from imperfect feedback — turning noisy judgments and failed attempts into useful learning signals, and improving the strategy an agent uses to learn, including how it selects and evaluates its next improvement. Topics include reward learning, credit assignment, and learning to learn.
Across all three directions, the key test is whether improvements transfer to new tasks. The goal is to develop novel methods and experiments toward a first-author submission at a leading ML/NLP venue. Recent internships on this team have produced work such as REFRAG, a new architecture for retrieval-augmented generation.
Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.

The Rack Scale Switch Chip Validation team validates and delivers the high-performance switching silicon and system-level solutions used inside modern AI and cloud data center racks. As an intern, you will contribute to day-to-day engineering work such as running emulation and verification tests, debugging silicon and hardware issues, troubleshooting switch performance and efficiency, and writing scripts to automate workflows, all alongside experienced engineers. Your work will support the team's efforts to deliver reliable, high-bandwidth, low-latency switch products that are a key part of Marvell's data infrastructure portfolio. Support post-silicon validation of high-speed switch silicon under the guidance of senior engineers.

· Assist in debugging silicon and hardware issues, and in troubleshooting switch performance and efficiency.

· Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, with a willingness to learn.
