· Coursework or project experience with PCIe, Ethernet, or other high-speed interfaces.
· Exposure to the physical and protocol layers of high-speed interfaces (for example PHY, PCS, MAC).
· Experience with emulation, simulation, or verification environments.
· Ability to read board schematics and layouts.
· Familiarity with signal integrity concepts such as eye diagrams, jitter, and BER.

28 - 56, $ per hour.

Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all .
Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.
Department Overview
The Storage and Memory Systems (SMS) Pathfinding team explores next-generation memory, storage, and interconnect technologies that will enable future AI, cloud, and high-performance computing systems. The team evaluates emerging architectures, advanced memory solutions, and innovative technologies to help shape Micron's long-term product strategy and technology roadmap.
Position Overview
As an intern in the Storage and Memory Systems (SMS) Pathfinding group, you will research photonic interconnect technologies that enable disaggregated memory architectures for future AI systems. You will develop modeling and analysis tools to evaluate silicon photonic memory fabrics, assess system-level tradeoffs, and explore how optical interconnects can improve memory capacity, latency, bandwidth, energy efficiency, and scalability for next-generation AI workloads.
Responsibilities
- Develop parameterized photonic link budget and system-level models to evaluate optical memory fabrics, including lasers, modulators, waveguides, switches, photodetectors, and interconnect architectures.
- Analyze performance, latency, bandwidth, power efficiency, reliability, and scalability tradeoffs across photonic memory architectures and memory technologies such as HBM, DDR5, and LPDDR.

Future AR and VR devices occupy ever-smaller, glasses-like form factors and thus require ever-tighter power budgets. At the same time, we require higher-quality passthrough rendering and scene understanding. In particular, depth estimation, which reconstructs scene geometry in real time from sensor signals, is one of the biggest power consumers in AR and VR devices. However, most existing work targets datacenter GPUs, or at best mobile silicon with an order of magnitude more power headroom than what glasses form factors allow.
Reality Labs is Meta's innovation engine for next-generation AR/VR and wearable technology and XR Graphics is involved in building the next-generation imaging and reconstruction stack that closes this gap. We are looking for a Research Scientist Intern to work on low-power real-time reconstruction of scene geometry for AR/VR.
Today, VR passthrough, hand interaction, and environment understanding run on separate pipelines, each tuned for different accuracy, latency and power target. We are interested in deduplicating the compute (and thus reducing power):
- What is the right depth estimation and processing strategy, from the ground up, for a glasses power budget?
- Can we train a single lightweight scene representation that can serve passthrough, hand occlusions, and background occlusions simultaneously?
These are open questions, and you would help define the approach. This is a research internship. You will own a genuinely open problem, choose the methods, build the evaluation, and present your results, with support for publication where the work warrants it.

The Meta Reality Labs Research Team brings together a world-class team of researchers, developers, and engineers to create the future of virtual and augmented reality, which together will become as universal and essential as smartphones and personal computers are today. Just as personal computers have done over the past 45 years, AR, VR and MR will ultimately change everything about how we work, play, and connect. We are developing all the technologies needed to enable breakthrough AR glasses and VR headsets, including optics and displays, computer vision, audio, graphics, brain-computer interfaces, haptic interaction, eye/hand/face/body tracking, perception science, and true telepresence. Some of those will advance much faster than others, but they all need to happen to enable AR, VR and MR that are so compelling that they become an integral part of our lives.
In particular, the Meta Reality Labs Research Audio team is focused on two goals; creating virtual sounds that are perceptually indistinguishable from reality and redefining the human hearing.
These two initiatives will allow us to connect people by allowing them to feel together despite being physically apart and allow them to converse in even the most difficult listening environments. The Devices and Hardware Research team of the Reality Labs Research Audio is looking for innovative PhD student interns interested in one or more of the following areas:
> Electrophysiological and bio-signal sensing technologies and the associated signal processing — EEG, EMG, EOG, ECG, PPG, EDA, and other wearable biopotential/physiological modalities, including electrode and front-end design, artifact rejection, and robust on-body signal quality.
> Extremely low-power, energy-autonomous wearable design — sub-milliwatt and duty-cycled sensing architectures, analog/mixed-signal front ends, event-driven and always-on wake-up circuits, and self-powered operation via energy harvesting.
> Embedded real-time signal processing on resource-constrained hardware — ANC, echo cancellation, hear-through, adaptive filtering, and efficient implementations on MCUs and DSPs.
> Hearing biomechanics characterized through experimentation and numerical simulation.
> Conventional and ML-based signal processing — feature extraction, classification, regression and event detection, sequence/temporal modeling, self-supervised and transfer learning for scarce physiological labels, subject-independent generalization and calibration, sensor fusion across modalities, and on-device/TinyML inference (quantization, pruning, distillation) under tight compute and energy budgets.
This internship can be twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks, with various start dates throughout the year.

About our Reading Innovation Centre
This role is available in our Reading Innovation Centre which is home to over 200+ scientists and engineers responsible for innovating consumer products in several business areas including Personal Health Care (Vicks) Oral Care (Oral-B), Grooming (Gillette and Venus) and Beauty Care (Olay).
The site is a specialist Healthcare & Grooming Research & Development Hub in Europe and supports our European Beauty Franchise business. The site is friendly, diverse and has a rich history in innovation in multiple business areas.

Research and Development (R&D) at P&G will help you to discover the essence behind crafting some of the world's most renowned brands. Delve into a realm where science takes centre stage. - Full Time Role: Successful interns have the potential to secure a full-time position with P&G after graduation. url:https://www.metacareers.com/jobs/290:
Meta was built to help people connect and share, and over the last decade our tools have played a critical part in changing how people around the world communicate with one another. With over a billion people using the service and more than fifty offices around the globe, a career at Meta offers countless ways to make an impact in a fast growing organization.
Meta is seeking Research Interns to join our Feed Recommendation team within Facebook. This org is directly in charge of recommending all sorts of contents to users the time they open the app, and thus always gets the first-hand experience of critical pain points to solve. Our interns will have the opportunity to participate in the process of framing practical, high-impact challenges in recommendation into rigorous machine learning problems, and bring their own expertise to build innovative solutions under the guidance from our research scientists and software engineers.
More concretely, while the generative AI innovations in NLP are mainly focusing on optimizing the probabilities of selecting the next word token, in recommendation the vocabulary (contents to suggest) is at a much larger scale and also changing at a fast speed. The preference for these contents can also vary dramatically across users and time. If you’re excited about how to generate the correct sequences of “words” any time the giant number of Facebook users open or scroll down the blue app, come to join us!
Our internships are twelve (12) to sixteen (16), or twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

Meta is seeking Research Interns to join our Fundamental AI Research (FAIR) Communication & Language teams working on multi-agent systems and memory. These teams are committed to advancing artificial intelligence through fundamental breakthroughs that enable agents to reason, learn from experience, and collaborate on complex tasks. We are looking for individuals passionate about large language models, agentic systems, machine learning, and reinforcement learning. Multi-agent systems, collaboration, coordination, communication, and shared knowledge
Agentic memory, long-term memory, implicit or parametric memory, and memory retrieval and utilization
Long-context modeling, context compression and compaction, and KV-cache compression
Self-improving agents, adaptive agent workflows, agent harness optimization, and test-time learning and adaptation
Reasoning, planning, tool use, reinforcement learning, and automated scientific research

This role is located at the GM Global Technical Center in Warren, Michigan.
The Enterprise Data Governance Office is seeking an early careers Data Governance Engineer to help expand data literacy, data stewardship growth, governance enablement, and community engagement across General Motors. This entry-level role combines technical learning with business and process support. The Data Governance Engineer will help make governance concepts, learning resources, onboarding steps, and practical guidance easier to understand, find, and apply across technical and business audiences.
Working under the guidance of experienced data governance and data literacy team members, the Data Governance Engineer will support steward onboarding, community growth, training coordination, communications, learning-path development, documentation, reporting, stakeholder follow-up, and measurement. This is an opportunity to gain practical experience in enterprise data governance, data literacy, data stewardship, change enablement, and cross-functional program execution.
The Role
At General Motors, data literacy helps employees understand, question, and responsibly use data and artificial intelligence to make informed decisions. Data stewardship helps ensure that data has clear ownership, useful metadata, appropriate classification, measurable quality, and accountable support across its lifecycle. The Data Governance &
Data Literacy team supports these outcomes through role-based learning, steward onboarding, data transfer documentation/tracking, hands-on workshops, enterprise events, communications, community meetings, reusable job aids, reporting, and governance enablement.
The Data Governance Engineer will contribute to the operating work that turns these activities into a repeatable capability. The role is well suited for a student who enjoys connecting technology, business needs, and practical processes; communicating with different audiences; organizing work; using metrics to understand participation and adoption; and learning how governed data is used across a large enterprise.
What You’ll Do
• Coordinate data literacy events, workshops, office hours, community meetings, and learning campaigns, including calendars, registrations, materials, attendance, and follow-up.
• Help grow the Data Stewardship community by supporting invitations, agendas, discussion topics, feedback collection, recaps, and approved collaboration channels.
• Support Data Steward onboarding, including required learning, Atlan onboarding steps, approved access tracking, cataloging activities, office-hours participation, and follow-up actions.
• Assist with intake and triage of data governance, data literacy, and data transfer documentation; route policy, privacy, access, data-quality, and tool-specific questions to the appropriate subject-matter expert.
• Research and organize content on data governance, metadata, ownership, inbound and outbound data exchange documentation/tracking, stewardship, data quality, responsible data use and analytics.
• Create and maintain plain-language communications and reusable materials, including FAQs, job aids, onboarding checklists, quick-start guides, presentations,
announcements, learning paths, recordings, and documentation.
• Under supervision, help verify approved metadata such as ownership, descriptions, and classifications.
• Maintain metric definitions, source notes, reporting trackers, and simple dashboard quality checks; prepare status updates, dashboard summaries, community recaps, and presentations.
• Coordinate with data stewards, domain representatives, technical teams,
communications partners, learning partners, and governance subject-matter experts while following GM requirements for data protection, privacy, cybersecurity, access, and responsible use of data and artificial intelligence.
• Perform other related duties as assigned.
Your Skills & Abilities
• Currently enrolled in an accredited bachelor’s or master’s degree program in Management Information Systems, Information Systems, Business Analytics, Data Analytics, Computer Information Systems, Business Administration, Computer Science, or a related field.
• Basic understanding of how business processes, information systems, and data support organizational decisions.
• Interest in data governance, data literacy, data stewardship, analytics enablement, responsible artificial intelligence, or related areas.
• Ability to organize information, manage details, follow established processes, and complete assignments on time.
• Strong written, verbal, and visual communication skills, including the ability to explain technical or process topics to non-technical audiences.
• Ability to collaborate with multiple stakeholders and work effectively in a team environment.
• Demonstrated curiosity, willingness to learn, and ability to receive and apply feedback.
• Basic proficiency with Microsoft Office or comparable productivity tools, including document, presentation, spreadsheet, and collaboration applications.
• Ability to work at the GM Global Technical Center in Warren, Michigan and
participate in virtual and in-person meetings as required by the team.
What Can Give You a Competitive Advantage
• Coursework, project work, or internship experience involving data governance, data stewardship, data quality, business process analysis, learning design, communications, community engagement, or program coordination.
• Familiarity with SQL, spreadsheets, data visualization, survey tools, reporting, or dashboard development.
• Exposure to data catalogs, metadata, ownership, classification, data quality, data privacy, data contracts, or lifecycle concepts.
• Exposure to steward onboarding, communities of practice, office hours,
enablement programs, or adoption measurement.
• Exposure to tools such as Atlan, Immuta, Anomalo, Databricks, Power BI,
Confluence, Degreed, Slack, or similar platforms.
• Strong documentation, collaboration, analytical, and communication skills with both technical and business audiences.

The salary range for this role is from $84,900 - $130,500. The actual base salary a successful candidate will be offered within this range will vary based on factors relevant to the position.
Bonus Potential: An incentive pay program offers payouts based on company performance, job level, and individual performance.

The fab2 team can build anything. We design all the hardware and software needed to make chips and we make the fabs, tools, and components ourselves.

We're looking for exceptional, hands-on people who can iterate to the limits of what's possible.

 

fab2 was founded by Sam Zeloof https://www.youtube.com/@SamZeloof and Jim Keller https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Keller_(engineer). Sam is best known for making chips in his garage, and Jim has been a leader in the semiconductor industry for the past 40 years.

 

About the Role

We're hiring Process Engineering Interns for the winter term. The internship begins in January, with a preferred commitment of 4 to 8 months. We’re rebuilding the chip fabrication process from the ground-up, so you’ll be exposed to some really interesting and impactful work. This is a hands-on process engineering role—you’ll be responsible for experiment design and execution of new semiconductor and thin-film fabrication methods. We're looking for someone with both a strong understanding of traditional semiconductor processing methods and an open-mindedness to new techniques. 



This is a high-ownership role with lots of autonomy in a fast-moving startup environment. You’ll have the opportunity to contribute to novel R&D processes and influence tool design.  - Learn and operate a range of semiconductor tools, including deposition, etch, lithography, and metrology systems

 - Analyze process data, troubleshoot recipe or equipment issues, and clearly document findings and results for the team

 

Required Experience

 - Pursuing a Bachelor’s Degree or higher in engineering

 - Ability to learn quickly and troubleshoot technical problems

 - Hands-on experience with wafer fabrication tools (etch, deposition, patterning) and metrology tools (AFM, SEM, thin film measurement, etc.)

 - Recipe development and optimization for some subset of thin film deposition, dry etch, or lithography.

 - Strong foundation in theoretical semiconductor knowledge (devices, fabrication, etc.)

 

Nice-to-have

 - Familiarity with data processing in Python

 - Mechanical or maintenance experience with fab tools

Location

About Us
BorgWarner is a global product leader in delivering innovative and sustainable mobility solutions. We are a company of innovators and independent thinkers that brings together talented employees, meaningful work and amazing technology in a unique environment. At BorgWarner, we constantly work towards our vision of a clean and energy-efficient world.
Our Culture
BorgWarner promotes and nurtures a diverse and inclusive environment, honors integrity, strives for excellence, commits to responsibility for our communities and the environment, and builds on the power of collaboration. We believe the health and safety of our employees are a top priority.
Career Opportunities
We manage talent as seriously as we manage our businesses and encourage you to learn about our proud history, strong culture, technologies, and vision for the future. We offer positions locally and globally with over 80 locations in 19 countries.
If this position energizes you and you feel you can help us achieve our mission and vision, you are invited to submit an application for consideration.
You may see the list of requirements and feel you do not meet all of them. However, remember that BorgWarner thinks differently. If your qualifications align with the majority of those outlined in this job description, we encourage you to apply and share your experience and skills with us.
Job Purpose
BorgWarner PowerDrive Systems is currently looking for “dynamic, results driven” individual to join as an Electronics Hardware Design Intern in our Summer Internship Program.
The Electronics Hardware Design Intern will be focused on day-to-day support and assisting engineers in designing, characterizing, and testing various aspects of automotive power conversion products. Further, the intern will assist in related problem resolution in the exciting and growing field of power electronics for hybrid and electric cars.
Key Responsibilities
- Assist in the electrical design, simulation and analysis of power electronics circuits and systems to meet technical product requirements
- Perform the electrical debug, test, characterization, and verification of power electronics designs
- Assist in specifying, identifying, and testing of key, critical electrical components
- Support BorgWarner product development team with technical design analysis, trade off studies, and design reviews
- Gain understanding of the vehicle system components and functions that interface to the power electronics subsystem
- Work with other engineering competencies and suppliers to aid in the development and verification of electronics products
- Use a broad range of electronic lab equipment to build, analyse, test, and verify designs functionally. Examples of tests are:
- Embedded controller verification
- Power Electronics efficiency, static and dynamic performance
- Thermal test bench
- Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC)
What We Are Looking For
- Currently enrolled in an accredited college, university, or be a graduate from an accredited college; however, students pursuing a Master’s degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering with a focus in Power Electronics will be preferred
- GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, or B average, upon initial hire date
- Candidate needs to have a strong interest in the automotive and / or power electronics field
- Experience in Power Electronics is preferred through one of the following: organizations, research programs, internships
- Knowledge of modelling, simulating, and/or circuit design required
What We Believe
- Inclusion - We value diversity in people, ideas, and experiences
- Integrity - We believe in transparency, authenticity, and depend on each other to deliver what we promise
- Excellence - We contribute to our developments by seeking knowledge and sharing information
- Responsibility - We care about our local communities and the global environment

wd:rbs:r-00285732:
Why Engineering?
Engineering drives the innovation and solutions that power our growth and success, connecting ideas to real-world impact and delivering value at scale. Our Engineers create cutting-edge solutions that make a real difference for millions of customers. Whether it's enhancing mobile apps, leveraging AI and emerging agentic technologies for personalised experiences, or simplifying core systems, our engineers are shaping the future of banking.
We’re not just building tech, we’re building better customer journeys, smarter systems, and a more secure digital future.
Your internship journey
Our Engineering internship is structured differently to all other internships and is designed to give you a real appreciation of what it means to work for us as an Engineer. The programme emphasises agile ways of working and immerses you in a dynamic and collaborative environment in which you’ll get to work in Scrums on real business projects supported by engineering experts.
At the end of the internship, we’ll assess you on what you’ve learned. Complete this successfully and you could be offered a place on our Engineering graduate programme, where you can carry forward the skills you’ve learnt into the next stage of your career.
Over the course of this eight-week programme, you can look forward to:
- Actively participating and contributing to real engineering projects
- Attending daily stand ups in your scrum project teams to drive real business progress as well as participation in end of sprint demos, retros, and feedback sessions
- Developing your engineering skills and application through agile methodologies, AI-assisted engineering practices and NatWest ways of working
- The opportunity to attend regular business and engineering spotlight so you can understand how our engineers contribute to the broader business and our customers
- Learning about how we operate, and how the contribution of Engineering makes a difference across our business technology functions including Retail, Wealth, Commercial & Institutional and Customer & Operations
- Learning how engineers collaborate with AI tools and emerging agentic technologies to solve complex problems while applying human judgement and critical thinking
- Building an understanding of the products and services we provide for our customers and colleagues
- Attending Engineering specific networking events, social engagements and the opportunity to hear from senior leaders across the bank
How you’ll benefit
We’ll reward you with a starting salary of £29,400 pro rata.
Plus, you can expect to:
- Learn from industry experts and immediately apply your learnings
- Enrich your learning with access to our Learning Academy
- Test and learn new approaches in a safe, inclusive environment
- Start building a professional network
- Grow your confidence, build your resilience, and elevate your presence
- Experience first-hand what it’s like working in a purpose-driven organisation
Entry requirements
To be eligible for our Engineering internship, you’ll need:
- To be in your penultimate year of university
- To be on course to achieving a 2:1 in a STEM subject
- Clear communication skills, and the ability to break down complex problems and explain your ideas
- A curious, logical mindset with a passion for solving problems and exploring emerging technologies, including AI
- Confidence working with data, statistics, and experimentation, and evidence-based decision making
- A flexible attitude, comfortable with change and ambiguity and continuous learning in a rapidly evolving technology landscape
- A drive to learn, grow, and make a real impact
Ready to apply?
The application window for this programme will be open until we receive enough applications to fill our cohort. When that happens, we’ll close the programme to new applications. It’s important to take the time to make sure you’re making the right decision about the programme you want to apply for (you can only apply for one programme) but please complete your application as soon as you can to make sure you don’t miss out!
Have another question?
Head over to our ‘Applying and eligibility support’ page now for answers to some of our most commonly asked questions.
Hours
35
Job Posting Closing Date:
Job Posting Closing Date is not yet published.
Ways of Working:Hybrid

Overview
Keysight is at the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. Our ~16,800 employees create world-class solutions in communications, 5G, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets for customers in over 100 countries. Learn more about what we do.
Our award-winning culture embraces a bold vision of where technology can take us and a passion for tackling challenging problems with industry-first solutions. We believe that when people feel a sense of belonging, they can be more creative, innovative, and thrive at all points in their careers.
About the Job:
Keysight is looking for an electrical engineering intern to join our R&D team in Colorado Springs, CO. This individual will be responsible for designing next-generation technology for test and measurement applications, including electronic elements for oscilloscope products, modular RF products, and/or probes and accessories products.
The ideal candidate is working towards a BS or MS in EE or ECE and shows proficiency in PCA circuit design and simulation. The candidate should be a self-starter with strong communication skills.
About the Team:
Come make an impact with Keysight’s Digital and Photonics Center of Excellence located in Colorado Springs, Colorado. Enjoy Colorado’s abundance of outdoor recreational opportunities while working in an engineering environment dedicated to innovation, contribution, trust, respect and teamwork. As part of our R&D team you will be a member of our diverse group of world-class electrical, mechanical, and software engineers, helping you transform your designs into high-demand products.
Responsibilities
- Design PCAs for cutting-edge electronic measurement products.
- Own the component selection and schematic design of PCAs under your control.
- Use simulation software as necessary to validate conceptual circuit designs.
- Work closely with PCA layout resources to ensure placement and routing meet your design requirements.
- Work closely with other engineering disciplines on your team to capture and incorporate their requirements into your designs, such as mounting locations, interconnections, heat sinks, RF shields, etc.
- Document your designs for ongoing and future reference.
- Test, debug, and characterize your designs to ensure they function as intended.
- In general, apply EE knowledge and skills to represent your discipline among a collaborative design team. Help your team weigh tradeoffs and solve problems.
- Continue to grow in your discipline and learn new skills as necessary to make your team successful.
Qualifications
Requirements:
- Working towards a BS or MS in EE/ECE or have applicable experience and education
- Familiarity with circuit design and analysis, PCA design, component selection, etc.
- Knowledge of simulation tools for concept validation
- Familiarity with schematic and layout tools
- Experience using electronic test and measurement equipment
- Passion to continuously investigate new technologies, tools, and processes within your discipline
- Self-motivation – must enjoy solving difficult and sometimes open-ended design problems in a team environment
- Strong work ethic
- Strong communication and documentation skills, ability to collaborate cross-functionally with a team-oriented mindset
Desired Qualifications:
- Working towards an MS in EE/ECE
- Familiarity with digital and RF components such samplers, filters, mixers and transmission lines
- Experience with Mentor Graphics
- Experience with Keysight’s ADS software package
- Ability to perform hands-on measurements with VNAs, oscilloscopes and signal generators
- Experience with the complete design-prototype-analyze cycle.
The level of role will be based on applicable experience, education and skills; most offers will be between the minimum and the midpoint of the salary listed below.
Colorado Pay Range: MIN $29.65 - MAX $38.66

Are you a problem solver looking for a hands-on internship position with a market-leading company that will help develop your career and reward you intellectually and professionally?
About Analog Devices
Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI ) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and X .
At ADI, you will learn from the brightest minds who are here to help you grow and succeed. During your internship, you will make an impact through work on meaningful projects alongside a team of experts. Collaborating with colleagues in an environment of respect and responsibility, you will create connections that will become a part of your professional network.
ADI’s culture values aligned goals, work-life balance, continuous and life-long learning opportunities, and shared rewards. The internship program features various lunch-and-learn topics and social events with other interns and full-time employees.
At ADI, our goal is to develop our interns so they are the first to be considered for full-time roles.
Apply now for the opportunity to grow your career and help innovate ahead of what’s possible.
About the Role
We are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Design Verification Intern to join our CSS DV team. You will work alongside experienced design and verification engineers to validate IP and subsystem-level designs for high-performance semiconductor products in consumer markets.
This role offers hands-on experience with System Verilog based verification, simulation environments, testbench development, and functional coverage Ideal for students or early-career engineers exploring a path into ASIC/SoC development.
Key Responsibilities
- Assist in developing and executing verification plans for digital IP blocks and subsystems.
- Develop, enhance, and maintain testbench components using System Verilog, UVM, or similar methodologies.
- Run simulations, analyze results, identify failures, and help debug issues.
- Create directed and constrained-random tests to validate functionality and corner cases.
- Perform functional, code, and assertion coverage reporting, review, and tracking.
- Work closely with design and architecture teams to clarify specifications and ensure coverage completeness.
- Support automation flows and continuous regression infrastructure with scripting.
- Document verification environments, methodologies, and results.
Required Skills & Qualifications
- Pursuing a Bachelor’s / Master’s / PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related discipline.
- Strong understanding of digital logic design and computer architecture.
- Coursework or practical exposure to:
- Verilog/System Verilog or VHDL
- RTL design principles
- Simulation workflows
- Familiarity with scripting languages (Python, Perl, Tcl, Bash, etc.).
- Good analytical and debugging skills.
- Strong communication and willingness to learn in a fast-paced engineering environment.
Nice-to-Have Skills
- Experience with UVM-based verification.
- Familiarity with EDA tools (Xcelium, etc.).
- Knowledge of:
- SoC design concepts
- Bus protocols (AXI, AHB, APB)
- Assertions (SVA)
- Coverage-driven verification
What You Will Learn
- Industry-standard ASIC/SoC verification methodologies.
- Writing and debugging System Verilog-UVM testbench components.
- Simulation and coverage-driven verification flows.
- Collaboration with digital design, architecture, and modelling teams.
Why Join Us
- Gain hands-on verification experience with real silicon IP.
- Work with experienced engineers who provide mentorship and guidance.
- Exposure to modern EDA tools and methodologies.
- Opportunity to convert to full-time/graduate roles.
- Collaborative, learning-driven workplace culture.

PREDICTING WHAT HAPPENS NEXT IS JUST THE beginning OF YOUR JOURNEY.
The Opportunity
If building models that help people make better decisions, understanding uncertainty, and turning complex systems into meaningful predictions sounds like your kind of challenge, we’re looking for you.
As an Architecture Research Intern, you’ll use simulation and queueing theory to understand how business changes (new service channels, process redesigns, demand shifts) ripple through operations and shape the customer experience. You’ll contribute to initiatives in Queue Management, Estimated Wait Time, and Predictive Simulation. From forecasting wait times to modelling the dynamics of complex operational systems, you’ll help develop solutions that improve experiences for our members.
Your background might be in queueing theory, simulation science, applied mathematics, stochastic processes, differential equations, or optimization. Either way, you’ll apply your research skills to real-world problems where uncertainty isn’t a complication, it’s part of the solution.
*This role is for a 12-month opportunity with the possibility of extension.*
The Team You’ve Been Looking For
AMA is more than a workplace; it’s a family. Together, we help protect the things that matter most to our more than one-million members—everything from roadside safety to retail savings, food security to childhood well-being. And with operations that span automotive, registries, travel, insurance, and more, the opportunities to grow with us are almost limitless!
Building on a century of proud service in Alberta communities, we’re passionate about making a meaningful difference in the places where we live and work. And that all begins with our people. As part of the AMA team, you’ll enjoy:
- Competitive wage
- Employee-exclusive discounts on travel, insurance, memberships, and more
- Ongoing professional development
- Vacation earnings paid out with each pay period
- Flexible work models that makes sense for your lifestyle
For us, curiosity fuels innovation. We value people who are eager to explore new ideas and who are comfortable putting emerging technologies into practice. We see experience with AI‑powered tools like ChatGPT, Copilot, and similar platforms as a real plus - especially when it’s used to work smarter, increase efficiency, and find better ways to get things done.
Who You Are
- You’re fascinated by uncertainty and enjoy understanding how complex systems behave over time.
- You see queues everywhere and naturally think in terms of arrivals, service, congestion, and waiting.
- You naturally think in terms of probabilities, outcomes, and trade-offs.
- You ask “what if we changed this?” and know how to build a model that answers it rigorously.
- You’re comfortable working with incomplete information and building models that help make sense of it.
- You can balance model fidelity against computational cost and decision deadlines.
- You communicate technical concepts clearly and can explain uncertainty without creating confusion.
- You’re analytical, curious, and motivated by solving real-world problems.
- You enjoy collaborating and know the best solutions come from combining different perspectives.
- You love turning research ideas into practical models that create measurable value.
How You’ll Make an Impact
- Contribute to predictive models and simulation frameworks that support queue management and estimated wait-time forecasting.
- Apply queueing theory to model customer flow, congestion, and waiting (for example multi-server queues, priority queues, queues with abandonment and retrials, and queueing networks) and use it to derive fast, interpretable wait-time estimates.
- Build simulation models (discrete-event, agent-based, and/or system dynamics) to evaluate how proposed business changes affect wait times, service levels, abandonment, and overall customer experience before they are implemented.
- Compare analytical queueing results against detailed simulation and real operational data to determine where theory holds, where it breaks down, and which approach best suits each decision.
- Formulate and analyze continuous-time models of system behavior using ordinary and stochastic differential equations (for example fluid and diffusion approximations of queues, including heavy-traffic limits based on reflected Brownian motion), and validate them against detailed simulation and real operational data.
- Design and apply time-constrained optimization algorithms (such as simulation-based optimization, parameter tuning, and anytime or heuristic methods) that deliver good decisions within real operational time limits.
- Design, test, and refine models that capture uncertainty, customer behavior, and system dynamics.
- Apply probabilistic and statistical techniques to evaluate performance, calibrate and validate models, and improve predictive accuracy.
- Run scenario, sensitivity, and what-if analyses that help business leaders understand bottlenecks, trade-offs, and future outcomes.
- Analyze results and communicate key insights, assumptions, limitations, and recommendations to stakeholders.
- Collaborate with researchers, engineers, and business teams to turn theory into practical, deployable solutions.
- Explore innovative approaches that improve decision-making across AMA’s products, services, and operations.
What You Bring to the Table
- You’re currently pursuing, or have completed, an MSc or PhD in Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, Physics, Statistics, Operations Research, Computational Science, or a closely related quantitative discipline.
- You have in-depth knowledge and hands-on experience of queueing theory, including Markovian and general queues (M/M/c, M/G/1, G/G/c), Little’s Law, queues with abandonment and priorities, queueing networks, transient and steady-state analysis, and heavy-traffic and diffusion approximations. You can fit queueing models to real data and judge when their assumptions hold.
- You have in-depth knowledge of simulation science, including discrete-event and/or agent-based simulation, Monte Carlo methods, variance reduction, input modelling, model verification and validation, and experimental design for simulation studies.
- You have a strong foundation in differential equations (ordinary, partial, and/or stochastic), including Brownian motion and diffusion processes, Fokker-Planck equations, and numerical methods for SDEs, and can apply them to model the dynamics of real systems.
- You have working knowledge of optimization, particularly time-constrained or real-time settings: simulation optimization, stochastic and dynamic programming, metaheuristics, or anytime algorithms.
- You have a strong foundation in probability and stochastic processes, with experience in one or more of the following:
-
- Markov chains and Markov decision processes
- Renewal and point processes (for example Poisson and non-homogeneous Poisson arrival processes)
- Statistical mechanics
- Stochastic differential equations
- You have strong statistical judgment and understand the nuances of uncertainty, including the distinction between prediction intervals and confidence intervals.
- You’re proficient in Python and can independently translate models and research concepts into reliable, well-tested code (for example NumPy, SciPy, SimPy, and optimization libraries).
Belonging Matters Here
AMA is committed to providing an inclusive, respectful, and accessible environment. If you require an accommodation at any time during our recruitment process, please contact recruitment@ama.ab.ca . We’ll work with you to feel supported throughout your journey with us.

About Trace

 

Trace is building the data, infrastructure, and research that enable robots to learn from the real world. General-purpose robotics requires a deeper understanding of how robots learn from real-world data. Our research explores how to transform human experiences, including egocentric video, demonstrations, hand-object interactions, and multimodal sensory signals, into transferable representations, actionable knowledge, and generalizable robot behaviors. At our Brooklyn research lab, we combine fundamental research in robot learning, computer vision, and embodied AI with large-scale datasets, machine learning infrastructure, and real-world robotic experimentation. Our goal is to advance the science of robot learning while developing the datasets and learning foundations for increasingly capable, adaptable, and reliable robots.

 
 

About the role

 

We are looking for highly motivated Research Interns to join our research team and work on challenging, high-impact problems at the intersection of robot learning, embodied AI, and learning from human experience. This internship is designed for PhD students and exceptional Master's students who are passionate about advancing the state of the art in robotics and machine learning.

 
 

As a Research Intern, you will take ownership of a focused research project, working closely with our scientists and engineers to formulate research questions, develop novel methods, design rigorous experiments, and evaluate results using real-world datasets, simulation, and/or robotic platforms. We encourage ambitious, scientifically grounded research with the potential to contribute to top-tier robotics, machine learning, and computer vision conferences. You will have opportunities to pursue original research, collaborate with an interdisciplinary team, and help shape Trace's long-term research directions.

 
 

Research areas

 

Research projects may span one or more of the following areas, but are not limited to:

 
 

• Learning from Human Experience and Egocentric Data

 

• Human-to-Robot and Cross-Embodiment Transfer

 

• Foundation Models for Robot Learning

 

• Visual-Tactile and Multimodal Robot Learning

 

• Data-Centric Robot Learning and Scaling

 

• Dexterous Manipulation and Generalizable Robot Skills

 

• Robustness, Generalization, and Reliable Robot Learning

 
 

We particularly welcome candidates who bring novel perspectives, strong methodological expertise, or creative research ideas that complement these directions.

 
 

What you'll do

 

• Lead an original research project from problem formulation and hypothesis development through method design, implementation, experimentation, and evaluation, with guidance and collaboration from Trace's research team.

 

• Develop and evaluate novel robot learning methods, including learning algorithms, representations, models, or training strategies that leverage human demonstrations, multimodal datasets, and robotic interaction data.

 

• Design rigorous experiments and benchmarks to investigate fundamental questions about data quality, human-to-robot transfer, policy learning, generalization, and real-world robotic performance.

 

• Work with diverse data modalities, potentially including egocentric video, human hand and body motion, teleoperation demonstrations, visual-tactile signals, force measurements, and robot trajectories.

 

• Collaborate with research scientists and engineers to build reproducible experimental pipelines, train and evaluate models, and validate research findings in simulation and/or on real robotic platforms.

 

• Analyze experimental results and failure modes, draw actionable scientific insights, and communicate findings through technical discussions, presentations, and written reports.

 

• Contribute to high-quality research publications and open research artifacts, with opportunities to submit work to leading robotics and machine learning venues.

 
 

What we're looking for

 

• Currently pursuing a PhD or Master's degree in Robotics, Machine Learning, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a closely related field.

 

• Strong research background in at least one relevant area, such as robot learning, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, computer vision, embodied AI, foundation models, dexterous manipulation, multimodal learning, or learning from human demonstrations.

 

• Demonstrated research excellence and potential, evidenced by high-quality publications, impactful research projects, open-source contributions, or other substantial research accomplishments. Publications at leading venues such as RSS, CoRL, ICRA, IROS, T-RO, IJRR, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, or CVPR are highly valued. First-author or co-first-author publications are a strong plus.

 

• Excellent programming skills in Python and hands-on experience with modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX. Experience with C++ and parallel programming, such as CUDA, is a plus.

 

• Strong communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, interdisciplinary research environment.

 
 

Nice to have

 

• Experience with real-world robot learning experiments, robotic manipulation platforms, or deployment of learned policies on physical robots.

 

• Experience with egocentric video, human demonstrations, hand tracking, pose estimation, motion retargeting, or cross-embodiment learning.

 

• Experience with vision-language-action models, diffusion-based policies, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, or world models.

 

• Experience with tactile sensing, force estimation, multimodal sensor fusion, or contact-rich manipulation.

 

• Experience with robotics simulation environments and tools such as MuJoCo, Isaac Sim, or related frameworks.

 

• Previous research experience in an industrial research lab or a collaborative, interdisciplinary research environment.

 
 

How to apply

 

Please submit your CV/resume, along with links to your Google Scholar profile, personal website, GitHub, or other relevant research portfolio, if available. Internship start dates are flexible. Academic credit may be available if required by your degree program, subject to institutional requirements.

 
 

Trace is an equal opportunity employer.

Job Description:
About Altera
At Altera™, our independence as the world’s largest pure‑play FPGA solutions provider gives us the focus, speed, and agility to innovate without compromise. With more than four decades of industry‑leading FPGA expertise, our singular mission is to deliver the programmable technologies that help customers differentiate, innovate, and scale across rapidly evolving markets like AI, cloud, networking, and edge. As an independent company, we move faster, invest deeper, and partner more closely—empowering our teams to drive breakthrough innovation and shape the future of the FPGA industry.
About the Role
Join Altera IP solutions team and work on cutting edge FPGA RTL and IP design!  Altera's IP Solutions Engineering (IPSE) team develops comprehensive solutions to provide customers easy and efficient access to the capabilities of Altera’s FPGA devices. These solutions are provided as highly configurable intellectual property (IP) cores that are fully integrated with Altera's software CAD tool, Quartus Prime. The External Memory Interfaces (EMIF) and IO team is responsible for developing IPs for communication with state-of-the-art DDR and LPDDR devices, MIPI cameras and sensors, and other high-speed I/O applications. The ever-growing demand for faster I/O interfaces - especially in the data center and machine learning sectors - presents a challenging design problem that requires system-level knowledge of silicon, software, IP, and customer applications.
You will work with a team of engineers to develop and verify state-of-the-art IP cores for interfacing with external memories and other I/O devices. You will be working on advanced FPGA architectures, design definition, implementation, and verification. Additionally, you will also be developing design examples and simulation models, accompanied by a rich set of technical documentation. In this role, you will work closely with multiple teams, including silicon design and validation, post-silicon validation, application engineering, and customer experience teams, to ensure seamless development, integration, and optimization of high-speed interface IP solutions.
Your specific responsibilities will include, but are not limited to the following:
- Architecture and Design based on the latest protocol specifications for DDR, LPDDR, and MIPI devices
- RTL development
- Device support and CAD tool integration
- Verification (e.g. verification IP, methodologies, frameworks, bus functional models, regression tests)
- Hardware power-on and debug
- New product release and rollout support
- Customer technical support

- Strong skills in communication, initiative, innovation, and teamwork
- Highly motivated to learn and adapt to fast-changing technologies and environments
- Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail
- Demonstrate fundamental values such as accountability, integrity, and a winning mindset
- Collaborative mindset, strong influencing skills, and a willingness to work across geographical locations

About Orbital Operations
At Orbital Operations, we’re building the future of dynamic space maneuvering. Our mission is to enable rapid-response orbital capabilities, executing maneuvers without hesitation and without regret.
Our flagship technology, the Cryogenic Propulsion Management System (CPMS), is redefining what’s possible in space mobility. Designed for military and commercial spacecraft, CPMS delivers sustained, high-thrust maneuverability in geosynchronous and cislunar orbits. It integrates low-loss cryogenic storage, reverse Brayton cycle (RBC) thermal control, and turbomachinery-driven propulsion to make spacecraft more agile, resilient, and responsive.
Beyond defense, CPMS is poised to transform commercial orbital logistics. By powering next-generation orbital transfer vehicles (OTVs), it can slash LEO-to-GEO transit times from six months to just eight hours—unlocking new possibilities for satellite servicing, deployment, and beyond.
Join us in building the infrastructure for a more maneuverable and mission-ready space domain.
About the Role
At Orbital Operations, we believe bold missions demand exceptional builders. We’re assembling a world-class team to push the boundaries of dynamic space maneuvering, and we’re looking for engineering interns who have already demonstrated that they can take real hardware from an idea to a tested result.
This is not an internship where you’ll spend the your time observing from the sidelines or working on isolated analysis. You’ll own a meaningful hardware project with a clear technical objective and be responsible for driving it through execution. Depending on the project, that may include defining requirements, performing analysis, designing components, creating drawings, working with vendors or manufacturing equipment, assembling hardware, developing test plans, running tests, analyzing results, troubleshooting failures, and implementing the next iteration.
You’ll be paired with a dedicated mentor, but you’ll be expected to take initiative, make sound engineering decisions, communicate blockers, and keep your project moving. You’ll work directly alongside engineers across design, analysis, manufacturing, test, and operations while contributing to hardware that supports our cryogenic propulsion and orbital mobility systems.
We are specifically looking for interns who have previously owned hardware through most or all of its lifecycle. That experience may come from a student engineering team, research laboratory, previous internship, personal project, machine shop, startup, or other hands-on environment. The scale of the project matters less than the depth of your ownership.
Strong candidates can clearly explain:
- What they personally owned and delivered
- How they translated a need into engineering requirements
- Which design decisions and tradeoffs they made
- How the hardware was manufactured and assembled
- How they tested it and determined whether it worked
- What failed, what they learned, and what they changed
- What they would do differently on the next iteration
Internship opportunities are available across our engineering teams, including:
- Mechanical Design
- Fluid Systems Design and Analysis
- Test and Integration
- Manufacturing and Assembly
- Avionics
If you want to be judged by the hardware you deliver and are ready to take a project from concept through test we’d love to hear from you.
Qualifications
- Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related STEM field
- Demonstrated ownership of at least one hands on engineering project from concept or requirements through fabrication, assembly, testing, and iteration
- Strong command of engineering fundamentals and the ability to apply them to practical, open ended problems
- Experience designing, building, integrating, or testing physical hardware through a student team, internship, research program, employment, or personal project
- Ability to make engineering tradeoffs and move forward when requirements or information are incomplete
- Willingness to work directly with hardware, including assembly, instrumentation, troubleshooting, and test operations
- Ability to independently plan and execute a complex technical project while identifying and communicating risks and blockers
- Resourceful, self-directed, and comfortable learning unfamiliar tools or technical subjects quickly
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document designs, test results, failures, and lessons learned
- Able to work full-time and onsite in Long Beach, California, for a minimum of 10–12 consecutive weeks
Preferred Qualifications
- Experience with CAD, engineering drawings, tolerance analysis, machining, additive manufacturing, composite fabrication, electronics, instrumentation, or fluid-system assembly
- Experience creating and executing test plans, collecting data, and comparing results against analytical predictions or requirements
- Participation in a hands-on engineering organization such as Formula SAE, Baja SAE, liquid or solid rocketry, CubeSat, robotics, Design/Build/Fly, or a similar project team
- A portfolio, technical report, project page, or other work sample that clearly demonstrates your individual contribution to completed hardware
- Experience diagnosing a hardware failure and carrying the resulting lessons into a successful design iteration

The Company operates Snapchat , a visual messaging app that enhances your relationships with friends, family, and the world, and Specs Inc. , a wholly-owned subsidiary dedicated to making computing more human, in addition to Bitmoji , Saturn, and other digital services.
At Snap, we create new technology that inspires our Product and Design teams, and we partner with Engineering to help develop and deliver innovative new features and products. We explore opportunities for technology transfers and academic publications, and regularly publish in leading journals and conferences. We are especially interested in fostering ongoing collaborations and are open to projects that last beyond the internship. We strive to create an environment that is both productive and fun.
We are looking for interns who are excited about pushing the state of the art technology and research in large generative models, GenAI efficiency, personalization, 3D & 4D generation and understanding, visual-language models, large scale data, and inference frameworks.
At Snap Inc. we believe that being together in person helps us build our culture faster, reinforce our values, and serve our community, customers and partners better through dynamic collaboration. To reflect this, we practice a “default together” approach and expect our team members to work in an office at least 80% of the time (an average of 4 days per week)
What you'll do:
- Collaborate with world class researchers and engineers in your area of expertise
- Develop state of the art technology that will impact our products
- Work toward publishing and/or patenting your research
Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities:
- Strong problem-solving skills
- Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic, and collaborative work environment
- Proven ability solving tough technical challenges
Minimum Qualifications:
- Enrolled in a graduate program (PhD preferred) in a technical field, such as Computer Science, Graduating no sooner than May 2027
- Experience conducting academic research and applying technical concepts to real-world problems
- Strong academic performance in technical coursework
- Clear vision for how research initiatives could contribute to future innovation at Snap
- Must be able to work in office for a 13-16 week internship in 2027
Preferred Qualifications:
- Strong publication records in world’s top venues in our field: CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, SIGGRAPH and similar venues.
- Previous experience with large generative models: large scale training and tuning, large scale data, large scale inference, model post-training, model efficiency.
- A passion for research and Snap Inc. products.
"Default Together" Policy at Snap: At Snap Inc. we believe that being together in person helps us build our culture faster, reinforce our values, and serve our community, customers and partners better through dynamic collaboration. To reflect this, we practice a “default together” approach and expect our team members to work in an office 4+ days per week.
At Snap, we believe that having a team of diverse backgrounds and voices working together will enable us to create innovative products that improve the way people live and communicate. Snap is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and committed to providing employment opportunities regardless of race, religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, pregnancy, childbirth and breastfeeding, age, sexual orientation, military or veteran status, or any other protected classification, in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws. EOE, including disability/vets.
We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and will consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable law (by example, the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance and the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring, where applicable).
Our Benefits : Snap Inc. is its own community, so we’ve got your back! We do our best to make sure you and your loved ones have everything you need to be happy and healthy, on your own terms. Our benefits are built around your needs and include paid parental leave, comprehensive medical coverage, emotional and mental health support programs, and compensation packages that let you share in Snap’s long-term success!

Overview
Join us to explore bold ideas and turn them into working prototypes.
As an R&D intern, you will investigate emerging technologies, explore real-world challenges, and develop innovative prototypes at the intersection of GIS, digital twins, urban planning, architecture, and mixed reality.
We are part of Esri, the global leader in geographic information system (GIS) technology, creating solutions that help people better understand the world and make more informed decisions.
You will collaborate with an international R&D team developing innovative web, desktop, and mixed reality applications for 3D GIS, digital twins, urban planning, and design. Your work will connect advanced technology with practical challenges and help shape how people understand, design, and improve the world around them.
This paid, full-time internship offers hands-on experience, close mentorship, and the opportunity to take ownership of a meaningful project from research and experimentation through to a working prototype and final demonstration.
What We Offer
We are a curious, collaborative, and international team that values experimentation, thoughtful engineering, and continuous learning. As an intern, you can expect:
- Meaningful ownership of a project with real impact
- Dedicated mentorship and opportunities to learn through training, technical exchange, and team development
- A supportive and inclusive culture built on trust, respect, and open communication
- Flexible working arrangements within a 40-hour work week
- Competitive compensation
- Team activities and opportunities to connect with colleagues across our global R&D community
Responsibilities
- Own and deliver an R&D project in areas such as 3D Web GIS, digital twins, spatial analysis, web applications, visualization, or UI/UX design
- Research emerging technologies and evaluate their potential for real-world applications
- Identify opportunities, propose solutions, and define a project roadmap together with your supervisor
- Design, build, and iterate on a working prototype while regularly sharing progress and findings
- Document your work and communicate results through presentations, demonstrations, and a showcase video
Requirements
- Experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or modern web development frameworks
- Experience developing web applications using modern web technologies
- Interest in creating intuitive, user-centred experiences and interactive applications
- Curiosity, initiative, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively
- Strong written and verbal communication skills in English
- Final-year undergraduate or postgraduate student in computer science, GIS, architecture, UI/UX design, or a related field
- Existing work authorization in Singapore for the full internship period
Recommended Qualifications
- Familiarity with ArcGIS or other geospatial platforms
- Interest in digital twins, 3D visualisation, urban planning, architecture, civil engineering, street design, or mixed reality technologies

About the Company
We are a renewable energy and ocean technology company committed to rapidly developing and deploying technologies that will ensure a sustainable future for Earth by unlocking the vast energy potential of its oceans. Our focus is on capturing civilizational levels of ultra-low-cost renewable energy for applications including computing and affordable renewable fuels delivered to shore.
The company is a public benefit corporation headquartered in Portland, Oregon, and backed by leading venture capitalists, philanthropic investors, university endowments, and private investment offices. We operate as an idea meritocracy in which the best ideas change the company’s direction on a regular basis.
Our staff have worked at organizations such as SpaceX, Blue Origin, Boeing, Tesla, Apple, Virgin Orbit, Astra, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, New Relic, Bridgewater, Raytheon, Disney Imagineering, and the US Army and Air Force, as well as research universities, startups, and small companies across a range of industries.
About the Job
Our core technology is the node, a device that produces energy in the ocean’s harshest conditions for years at a time without human maintenance or intervention.
As a Summer 2027 Engineering Intern, you will work on real technical problems that directly support the development and scaling of our Node technology.
We expect to hire interns across several engineering disciplines, including mechanical engineering, manufacturing, and software. Your specific project and responsibilities will depend on your background, interests, and the highest-priority technical needs of the team. You will work alongside experienced engineers, technicians, and operators.
We are looking for exceptional students who have demonstrated technical ability, intellectual curiosity, initiative, and a track record of building, solving, or shipping difficult things.
You will be expected to learn quickly, ask thoughtful questions, document your work, communicate openly, and take meaningful ownership of your project. Candidates should have effective interpersonal skills and be able to thrive in a creative, scrappy, and collaborative environment.
Responsibilities
Responsibilities will vary by discipline and project, but may include:
- Own and execute a clearly defined technical project supporting our Node technology with guidance from experienced team members.
- Apply engineering fundamentals and analytical reasoning to solve technical problems.
- Build, test, troubleshoot, or improve physical or software systems.
- Analyze technical data and use results to inform engineering or process decisions.
- Create clear technical documentation, including designs, analyses, test results, software documentation, or process records.
- Participate in technical reviews and clearly communicate findings, tradeoffs, and recommendations.
- Take ownership of assigned work and proactively communicate progress and blockers.
- Incorporate feedback quickly and adapt as project priorities or requirements evolve.
Required Qualifications
- Currently pursuing a bachelor’s, master’s, or doctoral degree in an engineering, computer science, physics, or other closely related technical field.
- Strong technical fundamentals relevant to your area of study.
- Demonstrated experience applying technical skills through coursework, research, internships, student teams, independent projects, or other hands-on work.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Comfortable working on problems where requirements or solutions may initially be ambiguous.
- Able to work full-time and on-site in Portland, Oregon for the duration of the internship, approximately mid-June through early September 2027.
- Authorization to work in the United States for the full duration of the internship.
Desired Qualifications
- Mechanical design, CAD, structural or thermal analysis, or hardware testing.
- Manufacturing engineering, process development, tooling, automation, quality, production systems, or design for manufacturability.
- Software development, data systems, automation, simulation, controls, infrastructure, or developer tooling.
- Skills with machining, fabrication, welding, electronics assembly, and prototyping.
- Designing and executing technical tests and analyzing the resulting data.
- Participation in technically demanding student teams or projects such as Formula SAE, Baja SAE, robotics, rocketry, solar car, marine engineering, or similar programs.
- Experience taking a project from an ambiguous initial problem through implementation and validation.
- Exposure to renewable energy, marine systems, robotics, aerospace, industrial systems, manufacturing, or other complex hardware environments.
- Experience working in a fast-moving technical environment where designs, processes, or software are tested and iterated quickly.
The above qualifications are desired, not required. We encourage you to apply if you are a strong candidate with only some of the desired skills and experience listed.
Compensation
If hired for this internship, you will receive:
- Cash compensation of $42.00 per hour.
Location and Duration
- This is an on-site position. Our offices, lab, and shop are located in Portland, Oregon . You must commit to being in person, in Portland, for the duration of this internship.
- This internship will run from mid-June through early September , with exact dates to be confirmed.
This is a short-term posting, and we will be accepting applications until end of day Tuesday, November 10th 2026 . Please ensure your application is submitted by this date as we will not be accepting late applications. We will begin reviewing submissions after the posting closes.

Together with you, we aim to revolutionize space services and help improve life on Earth. Sounds interesting? Then join our journey and become part of the team driving the New Space movement in Europe.
About the Team
Our international and agile team is looking for support from a motivated person as a Intern (m/f/d) Systems Engineering . Do you want to revolutionize space travel in New Space? Then you've come to the right place.
Your Tasks
- Draft and manage piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs) and power and signal diagrams (P&SDs) for vehicle and launch site.
- Formulate and document requirements for launch vehicle and launch site systems.
- Support verification and validation (V&V) activities and ensure end-to-end traceability of requirements.
- Trade-off architecture decisions and perform risk analysis (FMEA, FMECA, and FTA) for critical systems.
- Help maintain, and document internal software, and develop tools in Python.
- Coordinate between different teams to solve multi-disciplinary technical problems.
Your Qualifications

- Passionate about rocketry.
- Demonstrated practical/hands-on experience in design projects or student teams (Rockets/UAVs/Automotive).
- Experience designing / operating fluid systems is ideal.
- Working knowledge of launcher/aerospace systems, systems engineering processes, V&V, and risk analysis.
- Comfortable with object-oriented programming in Python, experience using Git for software version control.
- Fluent English, oral and written. Able to communicate complex topics in a clear and simple manner.
We Offer
Atmosphere: Experience life in an international & dynamic New Space start-up
Flexibility: Fit your working schedule to your needs with flexible working hours
Health: Sweat, stretch or squat it out with EGYM Wellpass
Paid Time Off: 30 days annual leave and speacial leave days
Team Culture: Join regular company and team events

At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. Lyft Urban Solutions designs, builds, and operates bikeshare systems in more than 50 cities worldwide, including New York, Chicago, London, Barcelona, Mexico City, Rio de Janeiro, and Montréal. Our Longueuil facility is the birthplace of BIXI, North America's first automated bikeshare system, and today builds the bikes and stations behind some of the world's largest bikeshare networks.
We are looking for a Hardware Field Quality Engineer Intern to join our Field Quality team at our Longueuil facility. Once our bikes, e-bikes, batteries, and stations leave the factory, Field Quality owns how they hold up in the real world: millions of rides, all four seasons, in cities across the globe. You will work alongside field quality engineers to help spot emerging hardware issues, investigate their root cause, and support fixes with engineering, manufacturing, and market operations teams. You will spend time hands-on with failed parts in the lab, and just as much time in the data working out how big a problem really is.
Responsibilities:
- Support failure analysis on parts returned from the field, including requests from enterprise customers, by helping with teardown, inspection, and electrical testing and documenting findings with photos.
- Help monitor field data, such as vehicle and station alerts and repair records, and flag emerging issues to the team.
- Build and update dashboards and queries that track reliability metrics and retrofit progress.
- Assist with field retrofit campaigns by helping identify affected units and tracking progress.
- Help review repair SOPs and troubleshooting guides used by market mechanics, and suggest improvements.
- Contribute to field failure investigations in Jira, working with engineers on root cause and corrective actions.
Experience:
- Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's program in Mechanical, Electrical, Mechatronics, or Industrial Engineering, or a related field, at a Canadian university, graduating between December 2027 and summer 2028 (required) . Master's students who worked between degrees should have less than 2 years of full-time experience.
- Professional proficiency in French and English , written and spoken (required)
- Hands-on comfort with electromechanical hardware, including disassembly, inspection, and basic electrical troubleshooting with tools like a multimeter
- Strong analytical skills and comfort working with large, imperfect datasets to reach clear conclusions
- Familiarity with structured problem-solving methods (5 Whys, fishbone diagrams, 8D, FMEA)
- Curious and detail-oriented, with clear written communication
- Previous internship or co-op in quality, reliability, test, or failure analysis is a plus
- SQL or Python, and experience with Mode, Hex, Tableau, or Power BI, is a plus
- Familiarity with Jira or similar ticketing tools is a plus
- Exposure to e-bikes, batteries, automotive, or other electromechanical products, or to reading wiring diagrams, is a plus
Benefits:
- Mental health benefits
- In addition to holidays, interns receive 2 days paid time off and 3 days sick time off
- Subsidized commuter benefits and Lyft ride credits
