The Internship Programme at Graphcore
Explore a career at Graphcore through a 12-week summer internship, gaining hands-on experience on real projects. You’ll bring fresh ideas, put your learning into practice and help shape what we’re creating. Along the way, you’ll tackle challenging problems with a team who welcome your questions and support you as you build your skills and confidence.
What you’ll be doing
Put your engineering foundations to work exploring the electronic hardware behind Graphcore’s AI compute platforms.
Your internship could focus on Hardware Design, Signal Integrity or elements of both, depending on your interests, the available projects and how your strengths develop. You’ll contribute to a clearly scoped design, analysis, validation or debugging task, with guidance as you work towards a conclusion supported by evidence.
In Hardware Design, your tasks could include schematic and circuit design, component evaluation, PCB development, board bring-up or laboratory testing. You could help check power rails and clocks, exercise interfaces, investigate faults or develop test and debug access.
In Signal Integrity, you could explore high-speed links such as PCIe and Ethernet, DDR and other memory interfaces, or clocks and timing-critical signals. Tasks could include reviewing PCB layouts and routing, simulating interconnect behaviour or comparing laboratory measurements with analysis to understand design trade-offs.
Your team and support
Hardware Design and Signal Integrity engineers work closely with PCB layout, silicon, validation, firmware, mechanical and thermal engineering, manufacturing and system teams. You’ll see how different engineering perspectives come together to make complex boards work.
Staff Hardware Engineers and Team Leads will support you with clearly scoped work and regular technical guidance. You can ask for help as you explore unfamiliar concepts, discuss your findings and use feedback to improve your approach.
Decisions are shaped by simulation, measurement and engineering judgement. As an intern, you’ll be encouraged to ask questions, speak up and try out ideas early, with support from experienced engineers as you learn.
How you’ll learn and grow
Over the 12 weeks, you’ll connect your studies with how boards are designed, analysed, brought up and validated. Your project will help you develop a methodical approach to defining a problem, testing your thinking and explaining what the evidence shows.
You’ll gain exposure to professional tools such as Mentor Expedition, Ansys HFSS and Keysight ADS, as relevant to your work. Comparing simulations, design choices and laboratory results will help you understand how real hardware behaves and which areas of hardware engineering you’d like to explore further.
Your internship is a chance to explore a future at Graphcore. Depending on your performance and the roles available, there may be an opportunity to join one of our graduate programmes once you’ve graduated.
What we're looking for
- Currently studying towards a degree in Electronic Engineering, Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Computer Engineering, Physics or a closely related technical discipline
- Strong electrical and electronic engineering foundations, with an interest in hardware design or signal integrity and how real electronic systems work
- A logical, first-principles approach to unfamiliar problems, with practical engineering experience from university projects, laboratory work, personal projects or activities such as Formula Student, robotics or engineering societies
- The ability to work with measurements or technical data and explain your conclusions clearly, with curiosity, willingness to take ownership and openness to feedback and collaboration
Your interests might include schematic design, PCBs, component selection, bring-up, validation, test or fault finding; or transmission lines, impedance, reflections, crosstalk, simulation and electronic measurement.
Previous industry experience and professional experience with the tools listed above are not required. Tell us what you built or investigated, how you approached it and what you learned.
Benefits
- Flexible working: Find a balance between your internship and life outside work
- 5 days of annual leave: Take time to rest and recharge during your 12-week internship
- Life in the office: Get to know your colleagues in spaces designed for collaboration, with free food, a great selection of ice cream and an on-site barista
- Learning and development: Build your skills and explore your interests with access to O’Reilly, our online learning platform
We welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences and are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work.
We’re an equal opportunity employer and recognise that everyone brings different strengths and perspectives. If you need any adjustments during the interview process, just let us know - we’re happy to support you.
Sponsorship
Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK for the full duration of the programme, without requiring visa sponsorship. We are unable to sponsor work visas for our Early Careers opportunities.
Introduction to Graphcore
At Graphcore, we’re building next generation AI compute: From semiconductors and software to systems at datacenter scale. We are proud to be owned by SoftBank Group and work with other companies in the SoftBank family to deliver AI compute to customers working at the AI frontier.
An internship at Graphcore gives you the chance to explore where your interests and skills could take you. You’ll work alongside people with different backgrounds and expertise, from AI researchers to chip designers and software engineers. Together, you’ll share ideas and solve challenging problems, building experience and confidence to help you decide what comes next.
How to apply and what to expect
To apply, answer the application questions below and upload your CV and cover letter. We’ll let you know the outcome of your application by early December at the latest. Curious about where your skills could take you? Apply for a summer internship at Graphcore and help us build what comes next.

Crystal Dynamics is constantly seeking the best gaming talent worldwide to add to our 30-plus year legacy of game development creating new and iconic franchises. We are committed to making great games with great people and living the dream while doing it.
Benefits for our regular full-time positions include, but are not limited to, a competitive regional salary, 100% employer-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance options, professional development reimbursement, flexible hybrid on-site/off-site work opportunities, company paid holidays, plus additional paid days in December when the studio is closed for holiday break, and the ability to accrue additional paid time-off.
Join us and help shape an amazing studio culture, where we’re building award-winning franchises like Tomb Raider and more!
JOB DESCRIPTION
Crystal Dynamics is now accepting applications for a remote spring internship, open to candidates across most U.S. states. As part of this 12-week program, you will take part in meaningful, hands-on work that contributes directly to active AAA projects. Throughout the program, you will step into a professional development environment where ongoing projects, experienced mentors, and collaborative teams give you a direct view into AAA game creation. This internship is designed to help you build industry ready skills, form strong professional relationships, and deepen your understanding of how world class games are made!
Eligibility Criteria:
- Graduated from a college or university program in 2026 (Spring, Summer, Fall, or Winter).
- Degree in Animation, Art, Game Art, Technical Art, Game Design, Game Development, Engineering, or related fields.
- Availability to work full-time (40 hrs / week), during core business hours, for the duration of the program (February 1st – April 23rd, 2027), including the first week onsite at our studio in San Carlos, CA for onboarding.
- Legal eligibility to work in the United States.
- Submission of a complete application that includes a resume, cover letter, and a link to your GitHub or portfolio.
What You Will Gain:
- Practical Project Involvement: Contribute to active game development efforts while learning production scope, workflows, and the advanced tools used across modern AAA pipelines.
- Professional Mentorship: Receive guidance from experienced professionals with deep industry knowledge.
- Skill Development: Expand your skill set, establishing a solid foundation for your professional journey.
- Team Collaboration: Work alongside our dedicated onsite and remote teams including fellow interns, building valuable professional relationships within the gaming industry.
What You Will Do:
- Work with engineers and designers to implement gameplay features in Unreal Engine, using both C++ and visual scripting workflows to support production needs.
- Participate in game development tasks including debugging, testing, implementation support, and code integration within Unreal Engine.
- Build essential skills using industry-standard tools such as Unreal Engine, development environments, source control tools, and code review workflows.
- Support engineers by assisting with coding, debugging, optimizing, and contributions to gameplay systems, tools, and supporting code.
- Deepen your understanding of Unreal Engine development workflows and collaborative engineering practices in a production environment.
What Makes You Stand Out:
- Portfolio, GitHub, or coursework demonstrating foundational engineering skills, including one or more of the following:
- Experience with C++ game development, especially within Unreal Engine.
- Familiarity with Unreal Engine Blueprints or visual scripting, with an interest in building reliable gameplay code.
- Strong debugging, problem-solving, and linear algebra fundamentals.
- Exposure to industry-standard development software, tools and engines.
- Industry involvement outside classroom curriculum such as game jams, personal projects and/or contributions to group projects that show going above and beyond.
- Willingness to tackle challenges, learn from feedback, and adapt to new tools or workflows.
- Ability to communicate your ideas with eagerness to learn and turn feedback into action.
INTERNSHIP FAQ
Interns are vital to our innovation and growth. Below are answers to some of the most frequently asked questions about our internship program. Given the volume of applications we receive, we aren’t able to accept resumes directly via email or provide individual updates through outreach. To be considered, please submit your application through our careers site so your materials are routed to the hiring team for review.
Q: When and how long will the internship take place?
A: The internship is a 12-week, full-time program, with interns working 40 hours per week. The exact dates will vary year over year, and may be subject to change.
Please see our upcoming schedule below for details:
Spring 2027 Internship
- February 1st – April 23rd, 2027
Q: Where will the internship be located?
A: This is a remote internship for candidates living in eligible US states. However, the first week will be on-site at our studio in San Carlos, California for onboarding and a chance to meet people who you will be working with throughout the internship.
Q: Will this be a paid internship?
A: Yes, the internship will be paid. Hourly rates for each position will be detailed in the job description. Compensation for this internship is $20-23/hr. Compensation is location-based and will be aligned to the intern’s confirmed work location during the program. Interns are also eligible for a medical, dental, and vision benefits package. Your recruiter can provide more information about total compensation.
Q: What are we expecting an intern to do?
A: Interns will be selected based on our current project needs. Specific responsibilities and expectations for each intern will be outlined in the job description for the internship position you apply for. This will provide valuable hands-on experience within your chosen field at our studio.
Q: Does Crystal Dynamics have a dress code?
A: At Crystal Dynamics, we believe that creativity thrives when you can be yourself. That’s why we encourage you to wear what makes you comfortable and confident, as long as it’s within the bounds of professionalism and respect for others. Whether it’s casual wear or your favorite gaming tee, feel free to showcase your individuality. Just remember, any attire that could be considered offensive or inappropriate is not allowed.
Q: How do I apply?
A: To apply for an internship, please visit our careers page , where you will find detailed information on our current internship openings and the application process. We encourage you to apply since we’re looking at your skills, experience, and potential, not every requirement! Please note that incomplete applications or attempts to submit outside of the careers page will not be considered. If you make our shortlist, we’ll be in touch for further assessments and interviews. We look forward to receiving your application!
Q: What can I do to make my application stand out from the crowd?
A: To make your application stand out, focus on tailoring your resume to the specific internship role you’re interested in and put together a thoughtful cover letter. Highlight any relevant experience or coursework related to game development and consider including a well-organized portfolio if it showcases your skills effectively. Emphasize your ability to work collaboratively in teams, stay informed about industry trends and the studio’s projects, and ensure your application materials are error-free and professional. If you have references who can vouch for your skills, consider including them. Lastly, closely follow application instructions and be thoroughly prepared for interviews, demonstrating your passion and suitability for the role.
Q: Do I need a degree?
A: At Crystal Dynamics, we value diverse backgrounds, including various levels of education and experience. Having a university degree is not a strict requirement for all of our regular full-time positions. However, if you’re interested in our internship program, eligibility is as follows:
Spring 2027 Internship:
- Recent college or university graduates from Spring/Summer/Fall/Winter 2026 with a relevant degree.
Q: Is there a possibility for an intern to become a full-time employee?
A : We value the impact our interns bring to the teams and projects. Our goal is to give interns the experience they need to be successful after schooling is complete . These opportunities are limited and depend entirely on business needs at the time. Interns are encouraged to make the most of their internship and explore future opportunities with us as they become available.
Q: What perks and benefits does Crystal Dynamics offer to interns?
A: Interns at Crystal Dynamics enjoy a range of perks and benefits. These include competitive compensation, access to industry professionals, networking opportunities, and a supportive learning environment. Additionally, interns will be eligible for medical, dental, and vision benefits and have access to unlimited snacks in the office! Detailed information about these perks and benefits will be provided to successful candidates during the onboarding process.
Q: If I’m not eligible for the program at this time, can I be considered for any future internship programs?
A: If you are not eligible for the program at this time, we encourage you to keep an eye on our future internship opportunities. We regularly assess our needs and welcome talented individuals to apply when suitable positions become available.
The pay for this internship role includes the base hourly rate, and does not include the medical, dental and vision benefits package that interns will also be eligible for.
Your recruiter will be able to share more information about total compensation.

At Spaceium, we are building spacecraft systems designed to push the boundaries of what's possible in orbit. As an Electrical Intern, you will work alongside our electrical engineering team on real spacecraft hardware. This is a hands-on role where you will contribute directly to the design, testing, and integration of electrical and electronic systems for our missions.
Responsibilities
- Support schematic capture and PCB layout for spacecraft avionics
- Assist with harness design, wiring, and integration
- Help bring up, test, and debug electronic boards and subsystems
- Support electrical testing including power, signal integrity, and functional tests
- Contribute to documentation, test reports, and design reviews
- Assist with lab setup, instrumentation, and test equipment
- Collaborate with mechanical, software, and systems engineers
Basic Qualifications
- Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field
- Familiarity with basic electronics, circuit analysis, and lab instrumentation
- Exposure to at least one programming language (Python, C, or C++)
- Eagerness to learn and work in a fast-paced startup environment
What We're Looking For
We're building technology that hasn't been done before. Experience is helpful, but curiosity, drive, and the ability to learn quickly matter more. If you're excited about spacecraft, enjoy solving hard engineering problems, and want to help build something new, we encourage you to apply.
Preferred Skills
- Creative problem solver with strong first-principles thinking, capable of assessing risk and making decisions with limited data.
- Experience in a nimble, technical engineering role, with a scrappy, entrepreneurial approach to meeting tight time or budget constraints.
- Hands-on experience with personal or academic electronics projects
- Familiarity with schematic capture and PCB layout tools (Altium, KiCad, or similar)
- Experience with microcontrollers, sensors, or embedded systems
- Comfort with oscilloscopes, multimeters, and lab test equipment
- Strong written and verbal communication skills
Additional Requirements
- Extended hours and weekend work may be required to support critical project and mission milestones.
- This role requires a physical presence at the Ottawa facility.
Please submit any exciting project that you have worked on.

We’re a fast-growing, global company building the world’s best clean energy products to electrify all homes and connect communities to form clean, resilient virtual power plants.

About the Program
The Human Frontier Collective (HFC) brings researchers and scientists together to tackle consequential problems in AI. In partnership with Scale Labs, we are building a small cohort of researchers to work on the empirical foundations of AI safety.
That work includes finding where models fail, checking whether safety controls hold up under pressure in realistic settings, and studying how AI agents (mis-)behave over long-horizon tasks. Scholars take open research questions like these and turn them into work that improves how frontier AI systems are evaluated and safeguarded.
Each scholar owns a substantial part of a safety research project. You'll work alongside a mentor from the research question through the experiments to deciding what to test next.
Research Areas
Mentors will guide Research Scholars on projects in selected AI safety research areas in select AI safety research areas, such as:
- AI control and chain-of-thought monitoring: Developing techniques to oversee and constrain AIs, including detecting harmful intent or deception.
- Alignment auditing and evaluations: Building scalable methods to test whether models have hidden goals, misaligned behaviors or unsafe tendencies.
- Multi-agent safety: Studying the risks that emerge when multiple agents interact, such as collusion, coordinated failures, or unexpected collective behavior.
- Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) safety: Investigating how to keep AI systems safe and aligned as AIs increasingly contribute to their own development.
- Science of Evaluations: examining when and how models recognize they're being tested, and how situational awareness affects the reliability/validity of evaluations.
- Misuse risks and evaluations: Developing methods to assess how AI systems could be exploited by malicious actors, including evaluating their potential to enable harmful activities.
Projects are matched to demonstrated expertise; we don’t expect any candidate to cover every area.
Representative Research
- ASPI : 728 task–attack scenarios testing how clarification-seeking changes prompt-injection vulnerability in LLM agents.
- PropensityBench : simulating real-world pressure to choose between safe or harmful behavior
- BioRiskEval : evaluating whether safeguards for open-weight bio-foundation models remain robust under fine-tuning and probing.
- See more work from the Human Frontier Collective .
What You'll Do
Projects are mentor-guided. By default, you will be given a list of research proposals and match you with one based on your research interests and background. You’ll meet weekly with a Scale researcher who sets the direction and gives feedback, and you will drive the day-to-day work.
- Own research end to end: Turn a high-level safety question into hypotheses, baselines, and controlled experiments, and produce work that others can inspect and build on.
- Build the measurement: Implement and debug evaluation harnesses, agent environments, datasets, monitoring methods, or post-training experiments.
- Exercise research judgment: Identify confounds, separate what a model can do from what it tends to do, make sense of negative results, and decide what to try next without step-by-step direction.
- Make the work legible: Produce reproducible code, experiment logs, analysis, and precise technical writing. External outputs, where appropriate, remain subject to research, security, and communications review. Outputs also include research papers, which will be submitted to top ML conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR).
Who We're Looking For
You may be a good fit if you:
- are motivated by ensuring the safe and responsible development of advanced AI systems;
- are interested in technical safety research, such as alignment evaluations, AI control, monitoring, multi-agent safety, or open-weight model safety;
- are pursuing or have completed a PhD in CS, ML, statistics, mathematics, or a related field (we also encourage researchers with an equivalent track record to apply);
- can make progress with high-level guidance, including implementing, debugging, getting unstuck, interpreting results, and proposing next experiments;
- communicate research clearly and handle confidential information and internal systems responsibly.
Application Process
- Apply: Submit your resume or CV, your Google Scholar profile if you have one, and one research project you substantially owned, with 2–3 sentences on your contribution.
- Research background discussion: Walk us through a past project, including what you tried, what didn't work, and what you learned.
- Research design: Work through a research problem with us and propose how you'd approach it.
- Onboarding: Successful candidates complete the applicable recruiting, work-authorization, security, and project-onboarding steps.
About the Role
- Location: Remote within the United States, including California and New York
- Hours: 20 hours per week
- Term: 3 months, with the option to extend to 6–12 months for exceptional candidates (part-time Internship structure)
- Compensation: $100/hour
PLEASE NOTE: Our policy requires a 90-day waiting period before reconsidering candidates for the same role. This allows us to ensure a fair and thorough evaluation of all applicants.

At Scale, our mission is to develop reliable AI systems for the world's most important decisions. We work closely with industry leaders like Meta, Ernst & Young, Mayo Clinic, Time Inc., the Government of Qatar, and U.S. government agencies including the Army and Air Force. Meta was created to foster connection and sharing worldwide. Over the past decade, our platforms have transformed global communication. With over a billion active users, joining Meta provides extraordinary opportunities to make a meaningful impact within a rapidly evolving organization.
Meta is seeking Research Scientist Interns to join our Scam and Trust team within Facebook. Scams are a global financial threat. At Meta’s scale, proactive detection and prevention are essential for protecting billions of users worldwide, making addressing scams one of the top priorities at Meta. The space is highly adversarial as bad actors continually change tactics and operate across content, behavior, and social networks, making isolated signals and static models insufficient. You will develop novel modeling and evaluation methods that address these challenges.
You will work alongside research scientists and engineers to translate a real-world scam-detection and prevention challenge into a focused research project. Research opportunities include combining large language model (LLM) reasoning with actor representations and content or behavioral signals, and developing agentic systems that use tools to gather evidence, investigate suspicious activity, and adapt their reasoning.
You may also investigate recursive self-improvement methods that enable LLM-based systems to identify weaknesses, propose improvements to their strategies or workflows, and validate those improvements through rigorous evaluation. Other research opportunities include learning from noisy and limited labels, transferring methods across surfaces, and maintaining robustness under distribution shift as adversaries evolve. Promising research may inform production systems that protect people from scams and contribute to research publications.
Our internships are twelve (12) to sixteen (16), or twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

Meta was built to help people connect and share, and over the last decade our tools have played a critical part in changing how people around the world communicate with one another. With over a billion people using the service and more than fifty offices around the globe, a career at Meta offers countless ways to make an impact in a fast growing organization.
Meta is seeking Research Interns to join the Integrity (Trust and Safety) team within Facebook. We are the applied ML team developing cutting-edge AI solutions to detect harm from bad actors. Our models decide when a group spreading severe harm should be taken down, when a creator is faking engagement, when a page is impersonating someone, and when an enforcement should be reversed on appeal, across a platform used by billions of people.
Our work has moved from per-post classifiers to advanced agentic AI systems that reason over an entire entity (its content, members, admins and history) and apply written policy the way an expert would, pushing the precision/recall boundaries on adversarial actor detection. The open research problems are about making that judgment efficient, reliable:
-Pushing the performance boundaries for agentic AI applied to bad actor detection
-Distilling large reasoning models into solutions that can scale cost-efficiently, including pushing the boundaries of decision-style models like Jev
-Improving shared multi-harm model improving without regressing other harms
Interns own one focused research problem end to end, from framing to experiments to publication, under the guidance of our research scientists and machine learning engineers. You will own E2E ML workflows including AI-driven agentic workflows with Gemini/Claude/Muse as well as scaled solutions through data analysis, feature engineering, model development and deployment.

Genius AI is building technology to help local businesses run themselves. Genius AI products do the admin work that keeps practitioners from the work they love and the people they serve. From GlossGenius to Reception, its products work 24/7 on busywork like booking, marketing, client management, finances, staff and inventory management, and more.

About the Role

As we continue to expand our reach and impact, we are seeking highly motivated and talented engineering interns to join our team for Summer of 2027.

Position: Engineering Intern 

Location: NYC  

Duration: June 8th 2027 to August 20th 2027

This internship puts you inside a live engineering team shipping product that hundreds of thousands of service businesses and their clients touch every day. You'll work on real features headed to production, not a side project built to keep you busy. Genius AI is scaling an agentic product at a pace where decisions ship in days, and this role exists so you get real exposure to how that speed and judgment work together. 

You will report to an engineering manager on our team. You must be commutable to our NYC headquarters in Union Square, and will operate in an in-person environment. We default to being in-office 3-4 days per week with required attendance on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

What You'll Do

 - Build and test features for our web and mobile products alongside senior engineers, shaping experiences used by our customers and their clients

 - Architect small pieces of automation with AI, not just use it as an assistant: identify repeatable work in your own project and build the system that removes it

 - Write clean, efficient code that meets Genius AI engineering standards, and own debugging and troubleshooting 

 - Partner with data analysts to collect and interpret usage data, and use those insights to inform how AI gets applied across the product

 - Ship fast, learn faster: iterate on your projects with AI-assisted development on a tight cadence, adjusting based on feedback from senior engineers

 - Expand your technical range deliberately, picking up new languages, frameworks, and AI-native development practices as the team's needs shift

 - Currently pursuing a B.S. in Computer Science or related technical field, graduating between 2027 and 2028, with coursework or project experience in software engineering

 - You use AI to learn faster, debug, and ship, and can point to something you've built with it

 - You dig into a problem before waiting for someone to hand you the answer, and you ask for help once you're stuck, not before you've tried

 - Proficient in one or more of JavaScript, TypeScript, Ruby, or Kotlin, with real project experience beyond coursework

 - Comfortable picking up new frameworks and tools quickly, ideally with some exposure to React, Postgres, SQL, or gRPC

 - Strong problem-solving instincts and equally comfortable working independently or pairing with a teammate

 - Clear, direct communicator who can explain technical tradeoffs to both engineers and non-engineers

The NYISO is seeking a Research and Engineering Intern to support the development of quantitative metrics that measure differences between Physical Dispatch and Economic Dispatch solutions. These two market-clearing processes can produce differences between physically feasible generator dispatch instructions and the prices produced by the market.
Working with the Research and Engineering team, the intern will design and implement a reusable software tool that calculates and visualizes these differences across market scenarios. The resulting analysis will help the team evaluate the pricing and scheduling effects of proposed electricity market enhancements.
Responsibilities
- Develop quantitative metrics that measure and characterize differences between Physical Dispatch and Economic Dispatch solutions.

At Toyota Research Institute (TRI), we’re on a mission to improve the quality of human life. We’re developing new tools and capabilities to amplify the human experience. To lead this transformative shift in mobility, we’ve built a world-class team advancing the state of the art in AI, robotics, driving, and material sciences.
This is a paid 12-week internship opportunity and is a hybrid, in-office role.
Here’s a glimpse into the Internship experience from some of our TRI interns!


The Team
The long-term vision of TRI’s Accelerated Materials Design and Discovery (AMDD) program is to accelerate the development of truly emissions-free mobility. Realizing this vision will require the discovery of new materials and devices for batteries, fuel cells, and more. Our aim at TRI is to merge cutting-edge computational materials modeling, experimental data, artificial intelligence, and automation to significantly accelerate materials research. Our focus is on developing tools and capabilities to enable this acceleration. We collaborate closely with a dozen universities and national labs and colleagues across global Toyota. AMDD seeks to develop and translate the newest technologies into practice, both within Toyota and the open research community more broadly.
The Internship
We’re looking for a researcher/engineer interested in how machine learning models represent molecules and materials, and whether different models discover the same underlying physical structure. In this role, you’ll collaborate with TRI researchers to investigate how training data, learning objectives, and model architectures shape learned representations. The work will combine mathematical reasoning with computational experiments to study when models arrive at shared representations, what information those representations capture, and how they connect to the physics of the systems being studied.

Responsibilities
-
Implement and evaluate machine learning models for molecules and materials using reproducible training and analysis workflows.
-
Design controlled experiments to study how learned representations vary across training runs, model architectures, and learning objectives.
-
Investigate the geometry and information content of learned representations and their relationship to physical quantities.
-
Develop evaluation methods to distinguish meaningful shared structure from similarities introduced by model parameterization or analysis choices.
-
Contribute high-quality, well-documented code to an internal codebase and help translate results into internal reports, publications, and/or patent disclosures (as appropriate).
Qualifications
-
Currently enrolled in a doctoral program in materials science, computer science, statistics, applied math, machine learning, physics, or a related discipline.
-
Strong foundations in machine learning, linear algebra, probability, and optimization, with demonstrated experience training models on real datasets.
-
Familiarity with representation learning or scientific machine learning; experience studying model convergence, learning dynamics, symmetries, or identifiability is a plus.
-
Proficiency in Python and modern ML tooling (e.g., PyTorch, experiment tracking, reproducibility best practices).
-
Ability to work collaboratively across disciplines and to translate research ideas into working code.

Introduction
Are you interested in applying advanced modeling, data analysis, and semiconductor process knowledge to solve some of the industry's most complex manufacturing challenges? As a Product Engineer Computational Model Intern, you will contribute to innovative solutions that help enable the next generation of semiconductor devices.
Your assignment
The Product Engineer Computational Model Intern role supports ASML Brion's mission of advancing lithography-driven design and manufacturing solutions. Working at the intersection of product development and customer applications, you will participate in pattern coverage studies, computational lithography investigations, and technology evaluations that help improve modeling accuracy and product performance. This internship offers hands-on experience with advanced semiconductor technologies, data-driven problem solving, and industry-leading computational lithography solutions. The Product Engineer Computational Model intern will collaborate with engineers and domain experts while gaining exposure to real-world challenges in semiconductor manufacturing and process optimization.
Role and Responsibilities
As a Product Engineer Computational Model intern, you will support engineering activities that connect product development with customer application needs. You will help evaluate lithography-related challenges, analyze data, and contribute to technology solutions that enable future semiconductor innovations.
- Conduct pattern coverage studies to support computational lithography modeling and product development.
- Analyze semiconductor manufacturing data to identify trends, opportunities, and process improvements.
- Support feasibility studies and technical evaluations for new product capabilities and customer requirements.
- Assist in developing best-practice approaches for standard and customized application solutions.
- Collaborate with product engineers and application teams to validate technical requirements.
- Utilize simulation and modeling tools to evaluate lithography and process performance.
- Document findings and present technical results to engineering stakeholders.
Education and Experience
- Currently pursuing a master's degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Chemical Engineering, Semiconductor Manufacturing, Process Technology, or a related technical field.
- Experience through research, coursework, academic projects, or internships related to semiconductor technology, optics, modeling, or lithography.
- Familiarity with scientific computing, simulation tools, or data analysis techniques.
- Experience with programming or scripting languages such as Python, MATLAB, Perl, or similar technologies is preferred.
- Exposure to machine learning, optimization methods, or semiconductor process modeling is beneficial.

Sit at the edge of research and production. You'll take a real workflow from a real team, make its failure modes measurable, construct the reward system, and post-train models that beat the frontier baseline on the work that matters. We hire interns who want to be researchers who ship.


WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Evaluation suites built from production traces: deciding what to measure, building the graders, and proving they track real quality.

 - Verifiers and reward models. Turning human corrections, outcomes, and standards of good work into training signal.

 - Post-training experiments end-to-end: hypothesis, data, SFT/DPO/RL runs, ablations, analysis, and the write-up that defends the win with numbers.

 - RL environments and agentic harnesses for the workflows we're specializing models for.

 - Reproducing recent post-training, reasoning, and agent papers, and translating the ones that work into our stack.


ABOUT YOU

 - Currently a student (BS / MS / PhD) in CS, ML, or an adjacent field, or recently graduated.

 - Strong empirical ML background. You've run post-training or RL experiments on LLMs and can explain what worked, what didn't, and why.

 - Rigorous about evaluation. You can spot a benchmark that lies and design one that doesn't.

 - Comfortable in messy production data. Real traces, not curated datasets, are your raw material.

 - Bias to ship. Your experiments end in a deployed model or a killed hypothesis, not just a doc.

 - Available for at least 12 weeks at meaningful intensity.


BONUS

 - Publications or OSS in post-training, RL, evals, or agents.

 - Experience with verifier models, synthetic data, or RL environments at scale.

 - Shipped research into a production system before.

 - Strong taste for what the field is over- vs. under-investing in.

Meta is seeking AI Research interns to join our Video Recommendations team within Facebook. Videos (Reels, long videos, and Live streams) are increasingly the formats of choice across the social media industry, and making all these formats successful is a top priority for Facebook, and the core mission owned by this org. Time spent on Facebook watching videos accounts for 1.2+ Billion hours/day, which is over 56% of time spent globally on the App, and this number is expected to continue growing.
This team is directly in charge of recommending all sorts of videos to users, powered by our large-scale unified video recommendation models. In this role, you will work on Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI): building AI agents that autonomously propose, run, evaluate, and learn from improvements to these models, closing the loop between ML experimentation and model quality. Our interns will have the opportunity to frame practical, high-impact challenges in recommendation into rigorous machine learning problems, and bring their own expertise to build innovative solutions under the guidance of our Research Scientists and Software Engineers.
More concretely, you will develop an agent-driven RSI prototype that continuously proposes, evaluates, and refines improvements for a selected video recommendation task. The scope spans training data improvement, environment and experiment setup, automated offline model evaluation, and feedback collection from model quality signals such as normalized entropy (NE) and recall. You will use experiment outcomes to improve both the agent's intervention strategy and its evaluation criteria, and deliver a working end-to-end prototype with evidence against a fixed baseline. Work will be mentored by the team, with production changes and online experiments subject to owner review and approval.
Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

MorphLabs · New York City · 5-month internship, on-site · Rolling applications
About MorphLabs
MorphLabs is building non-invasive telekinesis: a brain interface that turns movement intent into action, starting with people underserved by existing technology.
We are starting with continuous, intuitive prosthetic control for upper-limb amputees, decoding movement intent from EEG in real time, without surgery or reliance on muscle sensors. We develop the hardware and models together, treating signal quality, learning and control as one problem. Prosthetics are where we start, not where we stop.
We are a small, scrappy, high-throughput team in NYC. We have raised a substantial pre-seed round, with our seed round underway, and we move quickly between research and building.
The role
We build our own headset, electrodes and amplifier, and the core hardware already works. The work now is making it smaller, longer-lasting and more capable, and integrating it with prosthetic hands, so an amputee can move a hand just by intending to.
As an Electrical Engineering Intern, you'll spend five months on one well-scoped hardware project, working directly with the founders. You'll own it from the first question to the result, and be expected to ship something real: a board revision we build, a measured gain in battery life, or a clear finding that changes what we try next.
This is not a side project. Interns work on the same boards, firmware and open problems as the rest of the team.
What you'll do
- Miniaturization. Shrink our boards through layout, component choice and stackup, so the headset gets smaller and lighter.
- Battery life and power management. Find where the power goes, cut it, and verify the gain with measurements. Improve charging and battery management.
- RF and wireless. Diagnose and improve wireless links on real hardware: range, reliability and latency.
- Embedded firmware. Write and debug firmware close to the hardware, and chase bugs across the hardware and software boundary.
- New capabilities. Adding new modalities to existing designs and optimizing function.
- Prosthetic integration. Connect our system electrically to prosthetic and robotic hands.
- Bring-up and validation. Build and bring up boards in the lab, measure signal quality with the research team, and help validate our headset against third-party systems.
- Ship what works. Turn working prototypes into documented, repeatable builds, and write up what worked and what didn't.
What you'll have
- Ownership. Your boards go into the headset we build and test, not a demo.
- Direct access to the founders. You'll work beside the people making the decisions, with no layers in between.
- Data, every day. We record new EEG daily, so your hardware gets tested on real people constantly.
- Our own hardware. We design the full stack in house, from electrodes to amplifier to firmware, so no part of the system is off limits.
- An IRB already in place , covering both healthy participants and patients.
- The resources to do the work. Equipment and components won't be the bottleneck.
Who we're looking for
We're hiring a small number of exceptional engineers: students, recent grads, or anyone already building serious hardware. We judge what you've built, not your school, degree or résumé. You don't need a background in biomedical engineering, neuroscience or prosthetics. You do need to be unusually strong at electrical engineering and unusually fast at turning a schematic into a working board.
What we expect:
- One or more boards you designed and laid out yourself, end to end, that powered on, worked and got used. Owning one block of a team project doesn't count.
- A design you made meaningfully smaller, cheaper or lower power, with before and after numbers to prove it
- Bring-up you led: you can walk through each failure, how you isolated it on the bench, and what fixed it, without notes
- Firmware you wrote running on hardware you designed
- Fundamentals deep enough to reason from first principles on the spot: noise, grounding, power integrity, impedance matching, and why a board fails EMC
- A record of speed: idea to working prototype in days or weeks, not semesters
- Ownership without supervision: you find the next problem, fix it, and report what you learned
What sets candidates apart:
- Flight hardware: CubeSat, rocketry or satellite boards where mass, power and RF budgets were hard limits and failure was final
- Wireless designs you tuned and measured yourself: antenna matching, range testing, coexistence
- Battery-powered devices where you profiled current down to the µA and extended runtime by a factor you can name
- Low-noise analog front ends or biosignal acquisition at the microvolt level
- Hardware other people actually use: a product, an open-source design or a competition win
- Published research, patents or a public build log that shows your work
The bar is high on purpose. If your hardware clears it, apply, whatever your background.
Logistics and Compensation
- Duration: 5 months, full-time
- Location: Onsite, New York City
- Compensation: $8000/Mo
- Start Date(s): December 1st or January 5th
- Rolling applications

MorphLabs · New York City · 5-month internship, on-site · Rolling applications
About MorphLabs
MorphLabs is building non-invasive telekinesis: a brain interface that turns movement intent into action, starting with people underserved by existing technology.
We are starting with continuous, intuitive prosthetic control for upper-limb amputees, decoding movement intent from EEG in real time, without surgery or reliance on muscle sensors. We develop the hardware and models together, treating signal quality, learning and control as one problem. Prosthetics are where we start, not where we stop.
We are a small, scrappy, high-throughput team in NYC. We have raised a substantial pre-seed round, with our seed round underway, and we move quickly between research and building.
The role
The central problem at MorphLabs is learning a mapping from EEG to intended movement that holds up across people and over time. Those models drive prosthetic and robotic hands, on-screen cursors and more.
As a Research Intern, you'll spend five months on one well-scoped research project at the center of that problem. You'll work directly with our CTO and the founding team, own your project from the first question to the result, and be expected to ship something real: a decoder running in our system, a benchmark we adopt, or a clear finding that changes what we try next.
This is not a side project. Interns work on the same data, hardware and open problems as the rest of the team.
What you'll do
- Transfer learning across subjects, sessions and devices. Help build decoders that adapt to new users from minimal calibration data and stay robust to drift between sessions and headsets.
- Self-supervised pretraining. Try pretraining objectives on our growing, largely unlabeled EEG corpus, and measure how well they transfer to real control.
- Online closed-loop decoding. Help move models from offline benchmarks to causal, low-latency decoders, and look into why offline accuracy doesn't always predict online performance.
- Paradigm design. Help design the tasks and data-collection protocols that produce informative training data, and use each result to shape the next experiment.
- Evaluation and benchmarking. Contribute to the metrics, held-out splits and benchmarks we use to judge decoders, offline and online.
- Inform the hardware. Share what the models reveal about signal quality with our hardware team, and help validate our custom headset against third-party systems.
- Ship what works. Turn promising results into reproducible decoders running in our system, and write up what worked and what didn't.
What you'll have
- Data, every day. We record new EEG daily, and our corpus already spans thousands of hours.
- Our own hardware. We build our own headset, electrodes and amplifier, and also work with data from third-party headsets.
- An IRB already in place , covering both healthy participants and patients.
- The resources to do the work. Compute and equipment won't be the bottleneck.
Who we're looking for
We're looking for students and early-career researchers (undergraduate, master's or PhD) who have already built things. What you've done matters more than your year, school or degree. You don't need a background in neuroscience or BCI; strong researchers can pick up the domain.
You may be a good fit if you have:
- Research you can point to, such as papers, reports or code, and a clear account of what you did yourself
- Models you built and trained yourself on noisy time series (speech, audio, sensors, robotics and neural data all count), and can explain your architecture and objective choices and how you debugged training and generalization
- Models that kept working when the data shifted, across people, sessions, devices or environments, and an understanding of why
- Rigorous, reproducible work: fair baselines, ablation studies, test sets that hold out whole sessions or people, and results others can reproduce
- Math and statistics you actually use in modeling decisions: probability, optimization, linear algebra and uncertainty
- An experiment or task you designed that produced useful data, or human-subjects research, including under IRB-approved protocols
- The ability to run experiments quickly and let each result sharpen the next one, while working independently and writing clearly
Strong candidates may also have:
- A background in dynamical systems, geometry or information theory that shapes how you think about representations, time structure or model design
- Experience with biosignals, neural data or non-invasive BCIs
- Experience with real-time or closed-loop systems, where latency matters and offline accuracy isn't the whole story
- Experience learning from limited data: self-supervision, and choosing the next experiment when data is scarce
- Pretraining experience where the results carried over to a downstream task
- First-author papers or other substantial research results. Quality matters more than venue.
These are guidelines, not a checklist. Exceptional researchers often come from unconventional backgrounds, so apply even if you're not an exact fit.
Logistics and Compensation
- Duration: 5 months, full-time
- Location: Onsite, New York City
- Compensation: $10000/Mo
- Start Date(s): December 1st or January 5th
- Rolling applications
Our process
- Quick screen
- Technical interview
- Culture fit call with the full founding team
- Chat with references
- Offer

ABOUT US

Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.

We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.

Our co-founders are Bret Taylor https://www.linkedin.com/in/brettaylor/ and Clay Bavor https://www.linkedin.com/in/claybavor/. Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace.

Sierra’s Applied Research team works to make the models behind our agents better, faster, and cheaper across many kinds of tasks. Our work covers post-training open-weight models for specialized capabilities, new approaches to voice AI, and the benchmarks the field uses to measure agents, including τ-bench.

As an Applied Research Intern, you’ll join the team for a research project, working with a mentor, you’ll pick a problem that matters to how AI agents perform in the real world, run rigorous experiments, and potentially write up what you find for a top venue. If you want your research to reach both the research community and production agents used by millions of people, come do it at Sierra.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own a research project from start to finish, from framing the question and running experiments to writing and submitting a paper.

 - Push agent evaluation forward, for example by extending τ-bench to new domains, modalities, or long-horizon tasks, or by building new ways to measure reliability and consistency.

 - Study how agents reason, use tools, and follow policies over multi-turn conversations, and find out where and why they fail.

 - Explore post-training methods such as supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to improve agent behavior, and measure the gains rigorously.

 - Work with large-scale, proprietary datasets of text and audio interactions to find research questions grounded in real customer problems.

 - Work with researchers and engineers across Sierra, and where it makes sense, turn your findings into improvements in production.


WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Currently pursuing a PhD in computer science, machine learning, or a related field.

 - A research track record, such as first-author publications or submissions at venues like NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, Interspeech or ICASSP.

 - Strong experimental skills: you design clean experiments, build careful baselines, and are honest about what the results do and do not show.

 - Fluency in Python and modern ML tooling (for example, PyTorch, and LLM inference and training stacks).

 - High agency and a builder’s mindset. You’ll work across the stack to get an experiment running.

 - Clear, direct communication, both in writing and when presenting research.


EVEN BETTER

 - Research experience with LLM agents, tool use, or multi-turn dialogue.

 - Experience designing benchmarks or evaluations, especially ones tied to real-world outcomes.

 - Experience with supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, or long-horizon optimization.

 - Experience with speech, voice, or multimodal models.

 - Open-source contributions to ML research code or benchmarks.


INTERN QUALIFICATIONS

 - The internship is open to students currently enrolled in a PhD program.

 - Duration and start dates are flexible. Interns are embedded with the Applied Research team and work under the guidance of a mentor.

 - The internship is based in our San Francisco office. We are in person Monday through Thursday.


OUR VALUES

 - Trust: We build trust with our customers with our accountability, empathy, quality, and responsiveness. We build trust in AI by making it more accessible, safe, and useful. We build trust with each other by showing up for each other professionally and personally, creating an environment that enables all of us to do our best work.

 - Customer Obsession: We deeply understand our customers’ business goals and relentlessly focus on driving outcomes, not just technical milestones. Everyone at the company knows and spends time with our customers. When our customer is having an issue, we drop everything and fix it.

 - Craftsmanship: We get the details right, from the words on the page to the system architecture. We have good taste. When we notice something isn’t right, we take the time to fix it. We are proud of the products we produce. We continuously self-reflect to continuously self-improve.

 - Intensity: We know we don’t have the luxury of patience. We play to win. We care about our product being the best, and when it isn’t, we fix it. When we fail, we talk about it openly and without blame so we succeed the next time.

 - Family: We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. We are the best technology company for parents. We support and respect each other and celebrate each other’s personal and professional achievements.


WHAT WE OFFER

We want our benefits to reflect our values and offer the following to full-time employees:

 - Flexible (unlimited) paid time off

 - Medical, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family

 - Life insurance and disability benefits

 - Retirement plan dependent on country of employment

 - Parental leave

 - Fertility and family building benefits through Carrot

 - Lunch, as well as delicious snacks and coffee to keep you energized 

 - Discretionary benefit stipend giving people the ability to spend where it matters most

 - Free alphorn lessons

These benefits are further detailed in Sierra's policies, may vary by region, and are subject to change at any time, consistent with the terms of any applicable compensation or benefits plans. Eligible full-time employees can participate in Sierra's equity plans subject to the terms of the applicable plans and policies.


BE YOU, WITH US

We're working to bring the transformative power of AI to every organization in the world. To do so, it is important to us that the diversity of our employees represents the diversity of our customers. We believe that our work and culture are better when we encourage, support, and respect different skills and experiences represented within our team. We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. We strive to evaluate all applicants consistently without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

We are seeking motivated Electronics Summer Placement Students to join our team for a summer placement based full-time at our Cambridge office. This is an exciting opportunity for a student with a strong grounding in electronics to gain hands-on industry experience.
The placement will last 12 weeks. Successful candidates should be available to start their placement between May and October 2027.
There is no deadline for this role, as we recruit on a rolling basis. Once the position is filled, we will close the advert. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible.
The Opportunity
During the placement, your time will be split between contributing to a dedicated internal development project and supporting a range of live client projects. You will work alongside experienced engineers, gaining practical exposure to electronics design, simulation, testing, and measurement in a professional consultancy environment.
You will also have access to our extensive in-house facilities.  These include:
- Prototype PCB manufacturing facilities, including SMT pick-and-place, vapour-phase reflow and x-ray inspection
- EMC emissions test facility
- 5GHz 360° antenna test facility
Some interesting electronics projects that we’ve previously worked on:
Overcoming smart meter challenges for the last 5%  by developing a custom ZigBee to Long-Range Radio Bridge
Design of a low-power, high-performance smart wearable for Accesso  integrating multiple radios
Collaborating with LEGO® to develop LEGO® SMART Play™ combining custom wireless charging, BLE, a novel magnetic positioning system and NFC tag reading all in one device
Developing a novel air-interface and bespoke communication systems for the Ocado Smart Platform controlling hundreds of robots in grocery distribution centres
Next-generation Explosive Ordnance Disposal for the British Army
What you'll be doing
- Field experiments to validate concepts
- PCB level circuit design and laboratory-based design validation
- Development of system models
- As required, present designs, results and conclusions
- Work as part of a close-knit, multi-disciplinary project team focused on delivering design solutions to our clients
What you can bring
We are looking for someone currently in their penultimate year studying towards a MEng degree in Electronic Engineering or a closely related discipline, on track to achieve a 2.1 or above.
You will also have:
- A solid foundation in electronic principles.
- Familiarity with electronics lab equipment (such as soldering irons and oscilloscopes),
- Knowledge of electronics simulation tools, and experience in electronics design and schematic capture would be highly advantageous.
- An understanding of electronics measurements and lab-based debugging is also desirable.
A motivated and detail-oriented engineer who is motivated towards working in a hands-on laboratory environment will thrive in this role.
Some projects at Cambridge Consultants are subject to security restrictions. This role requires you to obtain a Security Check (SC) level security clearance ( United Kingdom Security Vetting: Applicant ). You must be able to work in the UK without restrictions in accordance with UK National Law and be prepared to successfully undertake an appropriate level of UK National Security Vetting according to UK Government National Security Vetting criteria.
Please be aware that, for roles requiring Security Check clearance, applicants will typically need to have been continuously resident in the UK for a minimum of 5 years immediately prior to applying for this role in order to meet the requirements for Security Check (SC) clearance.
Please ensure your CV includes your A Level (or equivalent) subjects and grades, as well as any relevant university modules.
Covering statements are advantageous though by no means a necessity.

Introduction
We are looking for an enthusiastic engineering student to join our Electronics & Software team, contributing to exciting projects across Telecommunications and Healthcare industries.
When you join us, you will work on cutting-edge products, develop your electronics design skills, and see firsthand how technology can improve people’s health and well-being. You will be surrounded by passionate experts who will support and mentor you, helping you grow into a world-class engineer of tomorrow.
Successful candidates can join us between May-September 2027.
There is no deadline for this role, as we recruit on a rolling basis. Once the position is filled, we will close the advert. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible.
Overview
From day one, you’ll be an integral part of our team, tackling real technical challenges while receiving guidance and training from experienced engineers. You’ll gain hands-on experience with a wide range of applications, from tiny, wirelessly powered medical implants to large-scale diagnostic equipment. You might find yourself working with analogue circuits, digital systems, FPGAs, antennas, signal processing, and much more.
What you'll be doing
During your internship, you will likely:
- Design and support electronics for multi-disciplinary projects, collaborating with engineers across all development stages.
- Create and implement your own printed circuit boards using Altium.
- Build experience using and automating precision test and measurement equipment.
- Contribute to innovation in workshops and technical reviews.
- Analyse experimental data and develop conclusions to shape project outcomes.
- Learn and apply modern soldering techniques.
- Document your work through technical analyses, test plans, and reports.
- Present your technical findings to both specialist and non-specialist audiences.
- Balance your time effectively across multiple project commitments.
- Gain invaluable insight from the talented professionals around you.
What You Can Bring
We’re looking for applicants who:
- Are currently pursuing a degree in a relevant field such as Engineering, Electronics, Mathematics, or Physics.
- Are eligible to undertake a 12-month industrial placement as part of their course.
- Demonstrate curiosity, a passion for learning, and a drive to see the bigger picture.
- Have hands-on experience with electronics lab equipment and soldering tools.
- Have a solid understanding of electronics fundamentals.
- Have exposure to software development.

About FOSSA Systems
FOSSA Systems is a leading space engineering and telecommunications company with +50 employees, specializing in developing and deploying IoT satellite solutions for remote asset management. Leveraging advanced miniaturization and mass production techniques, FOSSA has launched over 25 satellites and is actively deploying a groundbreaking satellite constellation to deliver cost-effective, cutting-edge connectivity solutions.
With headquarters in Madrid and an R&D center in Lisbon, FOSSA Systems is at the forefront of innovation in satellite manufacturing, operations, and IoT connectivity.
Who are we looking for?
We are looking for a motivated student to join our Aerospace department as an intern. You will support the day-to-day design and flight dynamics operations of the FOSSA satellite fleet, working alongside experienced engineers.
We are searching for curious, proactive people who enjoy learning in dynamic, young and agile teams and want to get hands-on experience with both hardware and software solutions for space applications. During your internship you will get exposure to different stages of the development cycle across our ground, space and user segments.
Responsibilities
- Support the design and operation of AOCS subsystems
- Assist in the conceptual and preliminary design of FOSSA space platforms
- Take part in testing and integration activities of space subsystems
- Contribute to the development of Flight Dynamics tools and products
- Help develop and test flight and ground aerospace software
Profile
- Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mathematics, Physics or similar, and able to sign an internship agreement with your university
- Programming skills in at least one science-oriented language (C, Python, Matlab, Julia)
- Good foundations in applied mathematics and numerical methods
- Good knowledge of Astrodynamics / Space Mechanics
- Ability to write clear technical documentation
- Good level of English (professional working proficiency)
Preferably
- Coursework or projects in Control Theory (e.g. Kalman filters)
- Academic projects in mission design, trajectory optimization or space navigation
- Participation in a rocketry team, CubeSat project, engineering club or similar
- Contributions to open-source space-oriented software
Why FOSSA?
- A real-world internship in a pioneering company transforming the satellite IoT connectivity landscape
- Hands-on experience with cutting-edge space technology in a fast-paced, innovative environment
- Mentorship from experienced aerospace engineers and real responsibility from day one
- Flexible schedule compatible with your studies and a strong focus on work-life balance
FOSSA is a fast growing, revolutionary and dynamic company that works every day to find the latest technology on the market and make wonderful and functional things with it.
We trust each and every one of our employees and give them the space to contribute ideas, to grow, to investigate, to try and learn from their mistakes.
We are a company that believes in equal opportunities, all applications will be considered and no discrimination for any reason will be tolerated.
Location: Las Rozas, Madrid

FPGA Designer Co-Op Student
Reference # 43980
L3HARRIS WESCAM Division
Hamilton, Ontario
About L3HARRIS WESCAM
As a subsidiary of L3Harris Technologies and within the Integrated Mission Systems Segment, the WESCAM division develops the most advanced optical sensor and targeting systems for global defense and military sectors, National Security, Search & Rescue and Airborne law enforcement agencies. From long-range covert surveillance missions to search and rescue operations, our MX-series systems, and the mission systems solutions they are a part of, produce stabilized high-magnification electro-optical and infrared images from airborne, marine and ground based platforms, enabling our customers to see first and act first.
About the Role
We are a team full of bright and exceptionally friendly people who work together to create a wide variety of solutions to complex and challenging problems. In order to ensure exceptional results, our team creates reusable IP by following a rigorous process that begins with requirements, is supported by documentation and ends with verification.
Are you tired of critical customer bugs causing you to work every weekend? If so, you may be ready to trade some of your frustration for a process that has been proven to produce nearly perfect designs. Our team follows a standardized work flow and an efficient process that enables us to consistently create robust and reliable designs that our customers can rely upon. We focus our energy on future solutions, not fixing past mistakes.
Our team is split into two equally valuable groups. The Design team owns the design and is responsible for creating innovative solutions for our customers. The Verification team is committed to confirming that the modules we produce behave exactly as specified. Neither group could stand on its own, but together are successful. Our team of highly skilled individuals have both a depth and breadth in their roles. We all perform some level of verification; we all participate in requirements definition & design engineering and we all take an active role in developing new design concepts and product launches.
An FPGA design cannot live in isolation and we collaborate regularly with other departments to ensure the best solution at the system level. This collaboration has earned us a reputation for producing high quality designs that are easy to integrate and actively supported. We track and report design progress so that our Leadership team can be well informed as they allocate resources.
We also understand the complex world of FPGA designs as a marathon, not a sprint. We recognize that being excellent in life goes well beyond engineering and includes actively participating in our communities and spending time with friends and family. With this in mind, we set aggressive but achievable goals that allow us to feel challenged while maintaining a work life balance.
Our team is full of people who are:
-
- Passionate about being excellent, yet humble enough to learn from others
- Collaborators who know that teamwork improves the results of independent work
- Excited to follow a workflow and process that will produce high quality designs
- Respectful while interacting with others, especially when they are wrong
Meaningful work and an exceptional culture make this a great place to work and grow!
As a Co-Op student you will join the FPGA Design team and actively participate in the new product introduction (NPI) design process by creating solutions using digital design techniques primarily in the context of FPGA technology.
Primary Responsibilities
-
- Writing and validating FPGA design requirements
- Generating high quality documentation
- Creating FPGA designs using the VHDL language to achieve the requirements
- Integrating library modules within a larger FPGA design
- Verifying, testing and debugging in simulation (Questa Sim) and hardware
- Assisting the verification team as required
- Utilizing Xilinx design tools for synthesis, implementation, debugging and timing closure
- Following departmental practices and coding guidelines
- Participating in regular design reviews
- Supporting product sustaining operations
- Contributing to the team’s knowledge by sharing lessons learned
- Participate in company educational events and training as needed
- Propose ideas for, and participate in, continuous inter and intra-group innovation
Required Capabilities
-
- Able to learn from and teach others
- Adept at solving problems
- Attention to detail, able to find the subtle errors and identify corner cases
- Comfortable with basic VHDL syntax
- An understanding of timing constraints and how to achieve timing closure
- Experience with revision control systems such as SVN or GIT
- Competent in English to support development of written requirements, design descriptions and user documentation
Desired Education and Experiences
- Working knowledge of Linux command line interfaces
- Working knowledge of Python, System Verilog, TCL and Matlab
- Knowledge of digital signal processing techniques
- Experience with Digital Video
- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering
- Must be able to complete a 16 month Co-Op term starting May 2027
- Currently enrolled and in good standing with co-op program through accredited university
- Able to obtain Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP) clearance
Pay Transparency
In the province of Ontario, Canada, the pay range for this position will be $25.00/hr

We are committed to diversity and inclusion within our L3Harris WESCAM family, and our community by welcoming and encouraging applications from anyone interested without regard to race, colour, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran's status, Aboriginal status or any other legally-protected groups. About the Role
The Test Engineering – Electrical team at L3Harris WESCAM is responsible for designing, developing, and validating functional and system-level test equipment, including test boxes, circuit card assemblies (CCAs), and cables that are deployed throughout the factory as well as at contract manufacturers. The team also develops robust, reliable test software and firmware to simulate a range of signals, including mixed-signal I/O, EO/IR camera sensor data, and digital communication protocols, maximizing UUT test coverage and product quality. Working closely with design engineering and cross-functional NPI teams, the team defines test requirements, assesses product testability, and ensures Design for Testability (DFT) principles are embedded throughout the product lifecycle.
Essential Skills Required
- Can work well and integrate within a team environment.
- Self-driven and motivated with the ability to learn new technologies quickly.
- Strong troubleshooting/debugging and problem-solving skills.

- Excellent verbal and written communication and collaboration skills.

- Support quality practices (AS9100 and ISO9001)

- Design, develop and support functional and system-level test boxes, and test wiring harnesses
- Define test requirements, developing schematics, PCB layouts, and test interface wiring harnesses for simple to intermediate UUT designs
- Follow departmental processes for test development including design reviews, configuration management, requirements management and test equipment qualification
- Design, develop and manage Boundary Scan tests and pass thru’ assembly tests
- Involved in technical reviews and provide feedback on the designs of fellow Test Engineers/Test Engineering Designer
- Engage in continuous improvement to enhance Test Automation and Test architecture
Technical Skills Required
- Familiar with various technologies in Electronics and Test Engineering.
- Familiar with circuit card assemblies, wiring harnesses, and circuit card manufacturing processes.
- Familiar with designing custom circuit cards using OrCad Capture and Allegro PCB layout.
- Familiar with designing with microcontrollers, FPGA's and programming in VHDL.
- Familiar with communications protocols (i.e. RS232, RS422, USB, I2C, CAN Bus, Ethernet etc.).

Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.
Within Perception, the Sensing Resilience team's job is to make sure that sensors "just work" for the entire self-driving car software stack. We make sure that all sensors are properly calibrated and consistently monitored at all times. We are often the firsts to algorithmically process data from next-generation sensors on next-generation vehicle platforms and work closely with both hardware and software teams to provide the best possible sensor data from our many sensors perfectly aligned to our upstream customers. To this end, we develop sensor data alignment and calibration algorithms, a growing sensor health backend, and deploy our systems both into the Waymo Driver and our log processing backend.
Waymo interns partner with leaders in the industry on projects that create impact to the company. We believe learning is a two-way street: applying your knowledge while providing you with opportunities to expand your skill-set. Interns are an important part of our culture and our recruiting pipeline. Join us at Waymo for a fun and rewarding internship!
You will:
- Help Waymo scale the sensor calibration algorithms to seamlessly support many different hardware architectures by developing the next-generation calibration system
- Develop, evaluate, and deploy new initiatives for the next-generation calibration system
- Evaluate and deploy ML-based calibration systems in new areas not yet covered in the literature
- Collaborate with highly experienced colleagues across hardware, software, and operations on deploying real world robotic system
