- Enrolled in a MS/PhD program in Computer Science, Robotics, or a similar technical field of study
- Experience in C++
We prefer:
- Experience deploying software as part of a complex system
- Experience calibrating multi-sensor robotic systems
- Experience evaluating and deploying ML systems

ABOUT ADVANCED ENERGY
Advanced Energy (Nasdaq: AEIS) is a global leader in the design and manufacturing of highly engineered, precision power conversion, measurement and control solutions for mission-critical applications and processes. AE’s power solutions enable customer innovation in complex applications for a wide range of industries including semiconductor equipment, industrial, manufacturing, telecommunications, data center computing and healthcare. Advanced Energy has devoted four decades to perfecting power for its global customers and is headquartered in Denver, Colorado.
WHY BE A PART OF ADVANCED ENERGY?
Some people say it’s like working in the best of two worlds. We operate like an agile, growing, small company – you can see your work make a difference to the company every day. Things move quickly and you can see and feel it. At the same time, we’re a global company founded in 1981 and have been publicly traded for more than 28 years. We have a strong cash position, deep trust and partnership with leading customers, a global best-in-class operations capability, and a proven leadership team. We have a track record and resources to make things happen both organically and inorganically. Being part of a nimble company with a solid foundation attracts team members that are capable, driven and like a challenge. Our employees collaborate and know how to have fun inventing, working, building and winning together. At our core, we are Advanced Energy – powering the future, together.
POSITION SUMMARY:
Advanced Energy is currently seeking Firmware / Software Design Engineering Interns and Co-Ops to support development activities across our North American design sites. Successful candidates will carry out their internships at Advanced Energy’s sites in Colorado, Minnesota, Massachusetts, or California. They will work with an experienced engineering team, closely collaborating on the development of high-performance, precision, efficient and cost-effective power conversion, metrology, or controls solutions. Only post-graduate candidates will be considered for summer and school-year internships. Candidates should be actively pursuing degree programs at one of the following institutions: University of Colorado, Colorado State University, University of Minnesota, Northeastern University, San Jose State University, Stanford University, or University of California-Berkley.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Candidates may perform and support design activities related to any of the following:
- Active participant in a core team to meet schedule, cost, and customer satisfaction goals
- Assisting in the development, testing, and de-bugging of prototype power supply units
- Analyze test data and reports against functional and performance specifications
- Interfacing with internal departments to ensure cost and schedule goals are met
- Circuit design of analog and digital circuits, EMI filters, and power circuits
- Development and implementation of control algorithms
- Design and analysis of magnetic components
- Modeling and simulation of devices, circuits or systems using commercial or proprietary tools
WORK ENVIRONMENT:
- Location: Fort Collins, CO
- Environment: in office and lab environment.
QUALIFICATIONS :
Required:
- Ability to work in a lab environment debugging circuits and evaluating product spec compliance using tools including oscilloscopes, power meters, multimeters, logic analyzers, and firmware interface tools
- Demonstrated proficiency with Windows-based platforms and with computer-based design and analysis tools, working knowledge of MS Office Suite
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team
- Ability to meet schedule requirements and define priorities without direct supervision
Preferred:
- Familiarity with CAD tools, for schematics, analysis, and modeling/simulation
- History of firmware programming for embedded systems is a plus
- Ability to work with serial communication protocols such as UART, SPI and I2C
EDUCATION:
- Candidates working towards Bachelors, MS or Ph.D. degrees in Firmware Engineering, Computer Engineering, or Electrical Engineering. Preference will be given to those with a Power Electronics and/or Controls focus, but other fields consistent with Advanced Energy’s needs will also be considered
- GPA > 3.25
COMPENSATION:
As required by multiple state pay transparency laws, Advanced Energy provides a reasonable range of compensation for each job posting. Actual compensation is influenced by an array of factors including, but not limited to, skill set, level of experience, and specific office location. The range of starting pay for this role is $26 to $36 per hour.
BENEFITS:
As part of our total rewards philosophy, we believe in offering and maintaining competitive compensation and benefits programs for our employees to attract and retain a talented, highly engaged workforce. Our compensation programs are focused on equitable, fair pay practices including market-based base pay, an annual pay-for-performance incentive plan, and discounted Employee Stock Purchase Plan.
In addition to our competitive compensation practices, we offer a strong benefits package in each of the countries in which we operate. In the U.S., we offer a rich benefits package that includes:
- Medical - multiple medical plans are available to choose from
- Short and long-term disability and life insurance
- Health savings and flexible spending accounts
- Generous time off policy starting with 3 weeks of paid vacation, 7 days of paid sick time, and 12 paid holidays
- 8 hours of paid volunteer time off
- 8 weeks of paid parental leave for both Moms and Dads
- Company matched 401(k)
- Tuition reimbursement
- Expanded mental health coverage and employee assistance programs
- Other voluntary benefits include critical illness, accident and hospital indemnity, pet insurance, identify theft, and legal assistance
Advanced Energy is committed to diversity in its workforce including Equal Employment Opportunity for Minorities, Females, Protected Veterans, and Individuals with Disabilities.

As the global leader in high-speed connectivity, Ciena builds the critical infrastructure powering the AI era. We’re a technology company shaping the future of networking, guided by innovation, integrity, and collaboration. Through development opportunities, meaningful work, and flexibility, Ciena supports growth and well-being—on and off the job. Connect with a career that matters.
Lieu de travail: 2351 Alfred Nobel Blvd #300, Saint-Laurent, QC H4S 2A9
Durée: 8 mois avec possibilité de renouvellement
Horaire de travail : 40 heures par semaine, du lundi au vendredi avec possibilité de voyager
Mode de travail : En présentiel avec possibilité de travailler hybride à l’occasion
Description du rôle
L’équipe d’introduction de nouveaux produits est à la recherche d’un candidat dynamique pour rejoindre le groupe responsable du développement et de l’amélioration des tests des produits photoniques. Le candidat retenu travaillera sur les produits photoniques de la nouvelle plateforme RLS ( En apprendre plus ) et sera responsable de valider des nouvelles stations de tests, possiblement de développer des nouveaux tests sur des prototypes ainsi que faire des améliorations des tests existants. Les tâches suivantes seront sous sa responsabilité: analyser la répétabilité des tests sur les nouvelles stations, développer des séquences de test automatisés, analyser les résultats de tests, concevoir des modifications aux stations de tests photonique, analyser des circuits électroniques et optiques.
Responsabilités
- Valider des stations de tests de la nouvelle génération de produits photoniques
- Développer des tests automatisés en laboratoire sur des cartes photoniques
- Développer des outils et des guides de déverminage
- Participer au développement des outils logiciels
- Validation des nouveaux équipements optiques (laser, atténuateurs, matrices, etc.)
Exigences
- Inscrit dans un baccalauréat en génie électrique
- Connaissances en design électronique : composants, schémas, PCB, procédés de fabrication, etc.
- Habileté à saisir des concepts techniques et bonnes compétences de déduction
- Aptitude pour le déverminage et l’analyse de problèmes
- Maîtrise de l'anglais et du français, niveau fonctionnel, tant à l'oral qu'à l'écrit
Atouts
- Connaissances des langages de programmation C ou C#
- Connaissances de la suite NI (Labview, Teststand, CVI)
- Expérience dans la prise de mesures optiques
- Base en télécommunication et en photonique
Avantages
- Accès gratuit à une salle d’entrainement
- Café et thé gratuit
- Terrain de volleyball et softball
- Stationnement sur place
- Événements d'entreprise
New Product Introduction – Photonic Test Engineer (Co-op)
Location: 2351 Alfred Nobel Blvd #300, Saint-Laurent, QC H4S 2A9
Duration: 8 months (possibility of extension)
Work Mode: 40 hours/week, Monday–Friday, primarily on-site, with occasional hybrid flexibility with potential travel opportunities
About the Role
Join our New Product Introduction (NPI) team and become part of the group responsible for developing and enhancing testing processes for cutting-edge photonic products. You’ll work on Ciena’s next-generation Reconfigurable Line System (RLS) platform ( Learn more here ) and play a key role in validating new test stations, designing automated test sequences, and improving existing processes.
This is an outstanding opportunity for an Electrical Engineering student with strong technical problem-solving skills and an interest in photonics, optical systems, and telecommunications.
Key Responsibilities
- Validate testing stations for next-generation photonic products
- Develop automated laboratory tests for photonic boards
- Create debugging tools and user guides
- Collaborate on the development of software tools for testing
- Validate new optical equipment (including lasers, attenuators, switches, etc.)
- Analyze electronic and optical circuits to improve test efficiency and accuracy
Qualifications
- Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering
- Solid understanding of electronic design: components, schematics, PCB design, manufacturing processes
- Strong technical comprehension and deductive reasoning skills
- Skilled in troubleshooting and problem analysis
- Functional proficiency in both English and French (spoken and written)
Preferred Skills (Assets)
- Programming experience in C or C#
- Familiarity with the NI software suite (LabView, TestStand, CVI)
- Hands-on experience with optical measurements
- Foundational knowledge in telecommunications and photonics
Perks & Benefits
- Free on-site gym access
- Complimentary coffee and tea
- Volleyball and softball courts
- On-site parking
- Fun company events and team activities
Pay Range:
The hourly pay range for this position is $25.00 - $34.00
Pay ranges at Ciena are designed to accommodate variations in knowledge, skills, experience, market conditions, and locations, reflecting our diverse products, industries, and lines of business. Please note that the pay range information provided in this posting pertains specifically to the primary location, which is the top location listed in case multiple locations are available.
In addition to competitive compensation, Ciena offers students access to the Employee Assistance Program (EAP), company-paid holidays, paid sick leave, and vacation pay as required by applicable laws.

Company Description
Join us and make YOUR mark on the World!
Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) has turned bold ideas into world-changing impact advancing science and technology to strengthen U.S. security and promote global stability.
Our mission spans four critical national security areas nuclear deterrence, threat preparedness, energy security, and multi-domain defense empowering teams to take on the toughest challenges of today and tomorrow. With a culture built on innovation and operational excellence, LLNL is a place where your expertise can make a real impact.
Job Description
We have an opening for an Ab Initio Nuclear Theory - Postdoctoral Researcher to conduct research in ab initio nuclear structure and reaction theory. You will participate in innovative research utilizing state of the art many-body approaches, high-performance computing, and modern statistics methods to accurately describe the structure of exotic nuclei and low-energy reactions that take place during the Big Bang and other astrophysical settings. You will receive regular technical and soft skill training and benefit from committed and active mentoring both at the personal and institutional level. This position is in the Nuclear Data and Theory group of the Nuclear and Chemical Sciences Division, a diverse group that collaborates extensively to provide state-of-the-art theoretical predictions and validated nuclear data.
This position requires full-time on-site presence due to the nature of the work.
You will
- Conduct innovative research in ab initio theory and/or simulation of light-nuclei structural and reaction properties and their impact to astrophysical processes.
- Combine ab initio approaches, high-performance computing capabilities and modern statistical methods to deliver accurate predictions of nuclear observables with quantified uncertainties.
- Design and carry out numerical simulations on supercomputers at LLNL and other national laboratories.
- Engage in collaborations between the Nuclear Data and Theory group, internal (LLNL), and external collaborators.
- Pursue complementary research interests and interact with a broad spectrum of scientists internally and externally to the Laboratory.
- Present research results at scientific conferences and meetings and in peer reviewed publications.
- Contribute to proposal submissions.
- Perform other duties as assigned.
Qualifications
- Ph.D. in theoretical physics or related field.
- Experience in theoretical methods applied to nuclear structure, reactions, or astrophysical simulations.
- Experience developing computer codes for the solution of physics problems.
- Ability to develop innovative approaches to tackle scientific and technical problems.
- Proficient verbal and written communications skills necessary to author technical and scientific reports and publications, and to deliver scientific presentations.
- Initiative and interpersonal skills with desire and ability to work in a collaborative, multidisciplinary team environment.
Qualifications We Desire
- Documented publication record in peer-reviewed literature with experience presenting research results to a large audience.
- Experience with few- or many-body methods applied to atomic nuclei.
- Familiarity with statistical methods and/or machine learning applied to uncertainty quantification.
- Familiarity with any of C++, C, Fortran, Python, or equivalent computer programming languages, parallel programming, and general interest in developing large-scale HPC solutions to physical problems leveraging advanced architectures.

Meta was built to help people connect and share, and over the last decade our tools have played a critical part in changing how people around the world communicate with one another. With over a billion people using the service and more than fifty offices around the globe, a career at Meta offers countless ways to make an impact in a fast growing organization.
Meta is seeking Research Interns to join the FM Quality ML team within Facebook Ads Ecosystem. FM Quality sits at the intersection of machine learning and system optimization across Meta's family of apps. We answer three fundamental questions: how many ads to show, which ads are best for each person, and how to deliver them, balancing revenue growth with user experience. Our team applies state-of-the-art ML, Generative AI, Reinforcement Learning, and large-scale systems to personalize ad quality across Feed, Videos, Reels, and Stories. We own 0→1 initiatives end-to-end and collaborate broadly across Facebook and Instagram to build the foundation for sustainable business growth. Our interns will have the opportunity to frame practical, high-impact ads quality problems as rigorous machine learning problems, and bring their own expertise to build innovative solutions under the guidance of our research scientists and software engineers.
The central research challenge is to build a quality system that understands each person and each ad deeply enough to reason about long-term user value, and to show people the ads they will like and trust. People tell us about their ad experience through many quality signals, such as survey ratings, hiding or reporting an ad, and their experience after a click. Each signal captures only part of the picture, and their effects add up across a session and over weeks. We are post-training large language models into a quality foundation model that reasons over a person's ad and organic interaction history together with the ad's content, and returns both an explanation grounded in that history and calibrated predictions for many quality signals at once. Open problems include post-training recipes and reward design that make reasoning measurably improve prediction and calibration, representing ads and user behavior in a shared semantic vocabulary the model can reason over, evaluating reasoning against people's own judgments, and distilling the model's reasoning into efficient production models that serve within strict latency and compute constraints. Offline evaluation and online experiments help us connect model improvements to better ad experiences and long-term value for people and advertisers.
If you are excited about using LLM reasoning to help billions of people see ads they like and trust, come join us!
Our internships are twelve (12) to sixteen (16), or twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

Job Description
About the role
Help develop an FPGA-based research prototyping platform for real-time audio and active noise reduction experimentation. This hands-on role emphasizes electrical hardware and FPGA development, with opportunities to work across system architecture, circuit integration, digital signal processing, and audio testing.
Working with research engineers, you will help turn platform requirements into a working, characterized system that enables researchers to implement and evaluate new algorithms.
Responsibilities
- Evaluate and integrate FPGA hardware, audio ADCs/DACs, clocking, power supplies, and analog and digital interfaces.
- Design or modify supporting circuits and interface boards as needed.
- Develop FPGA logic for audio acquisition, routing, processing, and output.
- Bring up and troubleshoot hardware using laboratory instruments and FPGA debugging tools.
- Investigate MATLAB/Simulink integration to simplify deployment of research algorithms.
- Implement pass-through, gain, and basic FIR/IIR filter examples; compare hardware results with simulation.
- Characterize noise, dynamic range, frequency response, distortion, latency, crosstalk, and channel synchronization.
- Set up and conduct acoustic transfer-function measurements, loudspeaker-based testing, and active noise reduction evaluations.
- Develop repeatable measurement scripts and document setup procedures, results, limitations, and troubleshooting steps.
Required qualifications
- Pursuing a degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or a related field.
- Hands-on FPGA development experience with Verilog, VHDL, or equivalent tools.
- Strong understanding of digital electronics and electrical engineering fundamentals.
- Familiarity with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and systematic hardware troubleshooting.
- Basic understanding of sampling, digital filters, and DSP.
- Ability to work independently on defined engineering tasks and communicate results clearly.
Preferred experience
- Mixed-signal circuits, audio converters, or PCB design and bring-up.
- Digital interfaces such as I²S, TDM, or SPI.
- MATLAB/Simulink, HDL generation, or embedded programming.
- Audio measurements and automated hardware testing.
Expected outcomes
A working research prototype with verified audio paths, representative processing examples, documented performance, and clear instructions that allow another engineer to reproduce the setup and measurements.
Must be able to work in hybrid capacity January 11- June 25, 2027
Must be currently enrolled in college/university

About Marvell
Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.
At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead.
Your Team, Your Impact
The Cloud Platform Optics team builds highly integrated component platforms with high-speed Silicon photonics, transmit and receive amplifiers, controller ASIC’s with Marvell DSP’s. These components are made operational with a highly functional embedded firmware. The team is responsible for design, verification, and validation of these integrated high speed optical components. The team performs system level testing under various operating conditions, and validates the performance of the hardware, firmware and control loops. An engineer in this team will be involved in a full product lifecycle and will carry new products from inception all the way to NPI.

We are seeking a motivated and talented Electrical Hardware Engineering Intern to join our dynamic team. The ideal candidate will have a foundational understanding of electrical hardware design and development, with a keen interest in developing platform solutions for the AI market. - Help develop and maintain detailed design documentation, including schematics, PCB layouts, and BOMs.

- Currently enrolled in a Bachelors or Master’s Degree in CS/EE, or a related field with an expected graduation date of Fall 2027 – Summer 2028

- Strong understanding of electrical engineering principles and practices.
- Familiarity with CAD tools for schematic capture and PCB layout (e.g., Allegro, OrCAD).
- Proficiency in using lab equipment, with a good understanding of electrical measurement and testing methodologies.

Overview
At PNNL, our core capabilities are divided among major departments that we refer to as Directorates within the Lab, focused on a specific area of scientific research or other function, with its own leadership team and dedicated budget.
Our Science & Technology directorates include National Security, Earth and Biological Sciences, Physical and Computational Sciences, and Energy and Environment. In addition, we have an Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory, a Department of Energy, Office of Science user facility housed on the PNNL campus.
The National Security Directorate (NSD) drives science-based, mission-focused solutions to take on complex, real-world threats to our nation and the world.
The Physical Detection Systems and Deployment Division, part of the National Security Directorate, delivers policy-informed technology solutions by removing barriers to real-world implementation. We strive to understand end-user environments to transition technology from the developmental stage to deployment. Our diverse expertise in operational systems provides tools, technologies, and approaches for combating a range of threats, both at home and in more than 100 countries around the globe.
Please note: this internship is for the winter semester and will start as soon as possible. It is not a summer 2027 internship.
Responsibilities
- Assist with assembling, wiring, testing, and troubleshooting research prototypes and electronic subsystems under technical guidance.
- Support laboratory experiments for RF imaging and electromagnetic actuator projects by setting up equipment, following test procedures, collecting data, and recording results.
- Help with introductory schematic, component-selection, PCB assembly, board bring-up, or circuit-testing tasks appropriate to the intern’s experience.
- Contribute to small, well-defined firmware, FPGA, scripting, or data-analysis tasks with mentoring and code review.
- Connect and test sensors, actuators, microcontrollers, development boards, GPIO, and common interfaces such as SPI, I2C, or UART.
- Assist with basic power-supply, DC-DC regulation, control-system, and hardware/software integration experiments.
- Support electromagnetic actuator assembly and characterization, including supervised control tests, coil measurements, impedance measurements, and comparison of experimental data with expected behavior.
- Observe or assist with high-voltage analog electronics only under direct supervision and in accordance with established laboratory safety procedures.
- Maintain an engineering notebook, organize data and files, document test configurations, and share progress with mentors and the project team.
- Participate in team discussions and ask questions to build understanding of multidisciplinary research and engineering practices.
Qualifications
Minimum Qualifications:
- Candidates must have a high school diploma /GED or higher
- Candidates must be degree-seeking undergraduate students enrolled at an accredited college or university
- Candidates must be taking at least 6 credit hours and have an overall cumulative GPA of 2.5
Preferred Qualifications:
- Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a closely related technical field.
- Completion of introductory coursework in programming, circuits, digital logic, embedded systems, electronics, controls, electromagnetics, or a related area.
- Basic programming ability in at least one language, such as C, C++, or Python.
- Interest in hands-on laboratory work, electronics, embedded systems, or hardware/software integration; prior professional experience is not required.
- Ability to follow instructions and safety procedures, document work carefully, communicate questions and results, and collaborate with a technical team.
- Ability to meet applicable eligibility requirements for work on the assigned projects.
Hazardous Working Conditions/Environment
Not Applicable.
Additional Information
This position involves access to sensitive systems and information. U.S. Citizenship is required. Pacific Northwest National Laboratory is subject to the Department of Energy Unclassified Foreign Visits & Assignments Program site, information, technologies, and equipment access requirements.
Testing Designated Position
This is not a Testing Designated Position (TDP).
About PNNL
Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) is a world-class research institution powered by a highly educated, diverse workforce committed to the values of Integrity, Creativity, Collaboration, Impact, and Courage. Every year, scores of dynamic, driven people come to PNNL to work with renowned researchers on meaningful science, innovations and outcomes for the U.S. Department of Energy and other sponsors; here is your chance to be one of them!
At PNNL, you will find an exciting research environment and excellent benefits including health insurance, and flexible work schedules. PNNL is located in eastern Washington State—the dry side of Washington known for its stellar outdoor recreation and affordable cost of living. The Lab’s campus is only a 45-minute flight (or ~3 hour drive) from Seattle or Portland, and is serviced by the convenient PSC airport, connected to 8 major hubs.

About the Team
The DoorDash Research Fellowship is a 3-month program (extendable to 6 months) looking for Summer and Fall 2026 cohorts, for researchers and engineers who want to work on the hardest applied ML and AI problems in local commerce. Fellows are given the resources, autonomy, and access to real-world operational data needed to pursue ambitious research directions — with the goal of producing work that influences both the field and how DoorDash operates at scale.
This program is modeled on the best external research fellowships: fellows are treated as independent researchers, not as junior employees on a product team. You pick the problem (within a set of priority areas), you own the direction, and you publish or ship the outcome.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will receive…
- Dedicated compute allocation sized to the research agenda — GPU clusters for training and inference budgets for experimentation
- Full access to DoorDash's research infrastructure — our internal RL stack, training and evaluation pipelines, RL environments built on real operational systems, agent evaluation harnesses, and the tooling our own research teams use day-to-day. Fellows are first-class users, not sandboxed visitors.
- Access to DoorDash operational data — real-world datasets spanning logistics, merchant operations, consumer behavior, and marketplace dynamics, under appropriate data governance
- Research mentorship from senior researchers and engineering leaders at DoorDash, plus a named research sponsor for each fellow who meets with you weekly and is accountable for unblocking your work
- Speaker series featuring leading researchers and practitioners from academia and industry — faculty from top ML programs, research leads from frontier AI labs, and senior operators from across tech. Fellows get dedicated 1:1 time with speakers when possible.
- A cohort of fellows working alongside you — a small, tight-knit group of researchers tackling different problems but sharing ideas, drafts, and reading groups. The community extends to DoorDash research alumni and the broader fellowship network.
- Publication support — fellows are encouraged to publish at top venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, KDD, etc.) and DoorDash will support the legal and review process
- Relocation support, housing stipend, and competitive pay
Structure
- Kickoff (2 weeks, in-person in SF): Onboarding, scoping the research agenda with your sponsor, meeting teams across Research, ML Platform, and relevant product orgs
- Core research period (~10 weeks, hybrid from SF DoorDash office): Focused research work with regular check-ins, internal talks, and working sessions. Extension to 6 months decided at the midpoint based on research progress and mutual fit.
- Closeout: Final write-up, internal presentation, and publication or productionization path
Priority Research Areas
Fellows are welcome to propose their own direction, but we are particularly interested in work across:
- Reinforcement learning environments for real-world operations — building high-fidelity simulators and training environments from operational data, including the tradeoffs between real-data fidelity and synthetic generalization
- Agentic systems for logistics and local commerce — long-horizon planning, tool use, and evaluation methodologies for agents operating in physical-world marketplaces
- Foundation models for marketplace dynamics — forecasting, pricing, matching, and personalization at marketplace scale
- Evaluation and measurement — new benchmarks and evaluation methods for ML systems deployed in messy, real-world operational settings
- Multimodal understanding — vision, speech, and language applied to merchant catalogs, operations, and consumer interfaces
We’re excited about you because…
- You’re a researcher with a strong track record — PhD candidates (rising 4th year or beyond), recent PhDs, or independent researchers with published work at top ML venues or equivalent demonstrated output
- You’re an engineer with deep research instincts who have shipped ambitious ML or systems work and want dedicated time to pursue a research direction
- You can operate independently — set a research agenda, scope it, and execute without heavy supervision
- You have strong written and verbal communication; comfort presenting work to mixed research and engineering audiences
We are not looking for specific years of experience or specific degrees. Exceptional candidates from non-traditional backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply.
Compensation
The fellowship is 12 weeks long with potential opportunity for extension. The fellow’s starting pay will fall within the monthly pay range listed below and is determined based on job-related factors including education, work location, and market conditions.
Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future. In addition to base pay, fellows are eligible for both a housing stipend and relocation stipend. DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer our fellows a wellness reimbursement benefit, access to an employee assistance program, in-office lunch credits and more!
Base Pay (Monthly)
$8,500 — $16,000 USD
About DoorDash
At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods.
DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers.  - Build and deploy LLM agents wired into our engineering workflows via tool-calling and MCP.

 - Help build execution environments where agents can verify their own work, with sandboxed access to simulators, compilers, profilers, and real hardware.

 - Ship internal products end to end, including the interfaces, data pipelines, and infrastructure behind them.

 - Design evals and track adoption to measure which tools are working and which aren’t.

 - Support special projects with the founders across the company.



You may be a good fit if you have

 - Progress towards a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD degree in computer science, computer engineering, or a related field

 - Strong software engineering fundamentals and a record of shipping projects other people use

 - Built agents for multi-step tasks beyond calling an API: tool design, context management, evals, and failure analysis

 - Heavy use of coding agents, including reading their transcripts and changing the system when an agent is confidently wrong

 - High agency in unfamiliar domains, product sense, and extreme attention to detail



Strong candidates may have some experience with

 - Chip development, GPU kernels, hardware, or manufacturing

 - Infrastructure, data engineering, or DevOps

 - Fine-tuning, RAG over technical data, or multi-agent orchestration

 - Hackathons, startups, or side projects with real users

Program details

 - 12-week paid internship

 - Generous housing support for those relocating

 - Daily lunch and dinner in our office

 - Based at our office in San Jose, CA

 - Direct mentorship from industry leaders and world-class engineers

 - Opportunity to work on one of the most important problems of our time

For any questions, contact internships@etched.com.

Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference, unlike many of our competitors.

The ML Innovation for Products (MLIP) team is an applied machine learning and research team within Meta's Ranking & Foundational AI org, focused on the state-of-the-art (SOTA) 0-to-1 ML that powers retrieval, ranking, and auction across Meta's ads systems. This is a very unique team that functions like an applied research lab with a production deploy button: we imagine, evaluate, prototype, and ship 10x ideas into one of the largest recommender systems in the world, a system that serves billion-scale users every single day and is the engine behind Meta's revenue. As a horizontal team, we have the unique leverage to develop SOTA techniques alongside expert engineers and researchers, then scale them into the head models powering Facebook, Instagram, and beyond.
What you would work on
Because the team works at the boundary of research and production, our research and its applications are intertwined, and much of the work is published at major ML and recommender systems conferences. Some of the work the team is involved in includes:
Memora, a new scaling paradigm for ads recommendation inspired by memory research in LLMs. Learned representations in large recommenders turn out to be highly concentrated, so much of the input signal is effectively ignored and further architectural scaling yields flattening returns. We build memory modules that store and retrieve historical model-generated representations and inject them back as differentiating signals, improving model quality without proportionally scaling compute. Two workstreams: Learning from Memory (LFM) and Enriched Ad Sequences (EAS).
Graph Learning at billion-node scale. We build heterogeneous graph representations of users, ads, and their interactions, including user journey graphs, and we push the modeling frontier: k-hop induced subgraph methods, temporal GNNs, graph transformers, and deeper architectures with residual and spectral rewiring to counter over-smoothing and over-squashing. A parallel track turns this into a self-serve platform so that experiment throughput, not infrastructure, is the bottleneck.
LLM and Multimodal Fusion. Ad-side and user-side content understanding are both crowded research areas, but almost no one combines them with graph-structured relational signals. That gap is the opening. Our SELF workstream, for Semantic-Engagement LLM Fusion, contrastively trains ad and user encoders so that engagement structure from the interaction graph and semantic content from multimodal LLMs land in one shared embedding space that retrieval can search directly.
Agentic AI. We are building a shared agentic layer that abstracts planning, tool orchestration, memory, and execution into reusable services. The flagship is IDEA, which has already taken techniques from paper to validated production model improvements end to end, with domain overlays that specialize it for memory, sequences, graph learning, retrieval policies, and foundation models. The research questions it raises about autonomous experimentation are wide open.
Reinforcement Learning. Large parts of the ads retrieval flow are still tuned by hand: how many candidates to keep at each stage, how to mix retrieval routes, where to set recall cutoffs. These decisions have no clean ground-truth label to supervise against, which is exactly the gap RL is built to close. We replace static global constants with per-request policies learned from logged traffic that optimize the realized system outcome directly rather than a low-fidelity offline proxy. Our first production policy personalizes a retrieval keep ratio per request on Facebook Mobile Feed. The longer-term direction is joint multi-knob optimization across the flow on one shared reward and off-policy evaluation foundation.
Who we are:
We are a team of 15 ML engineers and research scientists spanning Sunnyvale and the Bay Area, supported by senior technical leads with deep experience taking research from idea to production. We partner closely with product groups across Meta, so the surface area available to an intern is much wider than any single pod. The team values knowledge sharing and continuous learning, and runs regular technical deep dives and AI best-practice workshops alongside a buddy system for onboarding.

Roku is changing how the world watches TV
Roku is the #1 TV streaming platform in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico, and we've set our sights on powering every television in the world. Roku pioneered streaming to the TV. Our mission is to be the TV streaming platform that connects the entire TV ecosystem. We connect consumers to the content they love, enable content publishers to build and monetize large audiences, and provide advertisers unique capabilities to engage consumers.
From your first day at Roku, you'll make a valuable - and valued - contribution. We're a fast-growing public company where no one is a bystander. We offer you the opportunity to delight millions of TV streamers around the world while gaining meaningful experience across a variety of disciplines.
About the role
Join Roku as an Engineering Intern and help build the agentic AI powering America’s #1 TV streaming platform. Roku reaches more than 100 million households worldwide, and we’re building production-grade AI agents across the products and platforms that serve them. We offer a paid 12-week internship, running from June to early September 2027.
As an Engineering Intern, you’ll be assigned a scoped project with one of our engineering teams and matched to the team that best fits your skills and interests. You’ll work on real problems, such as agents that investigate failures, automate workflows, review or generate code, or help people make complex decisions. You’ll learn how to take an AI-powered idea from prototype to something people actually use, with a mentor alongside you and real ownership from day one.
Our teams work across a variety of languages and technologies, from user interfaces and embedded software to platform services, automation and developer tooling, and embrace AI-assisted development to boost productivity and quality.
What you’ll be doing
- Own a well-defined project that contributes to the success of your team, from defining the problem through to delivery.
- Build and test AI agents, copilots and automated workflows that perform meaningful, multi-step work.
- Connect agents to trusted data, services and internal tools, using approaches such as retrieval, tool calling and orchestration, and help define what an agent may do on its own and when it should hand over to a person.
- Evaluate your work: measure whether it does the job well, check its reliability and failure modes, and keep improving it based on real feedback.
- Use AI coding tools every day to move faster, and validate everything they produce through testing, review and your own judgment.
- Write clean, well-tested, documented code, take part in code reviews, and collaborate with engineers, mentors and cross-functional partners.
Apply if
- You are a penultimate-year student, or a final-year student planning to go on to a one-year master’s course.
- You hold a permanent right to work in the UK. Unfortunately, we are unable to consider candidates on a student visa.
- You are available for full-time work for the whole 12-week program, from June to early September in Manchester.
- You are keen to work with AI technologies and have previous experience building AI agents and automated workflows.
We’re excited if you have
- Currently enrolled in a degree program in Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, Engineering or a related field.
- Proficiency in Python, ideally with projects, open source or hackathon work beyond your coursework.
- Hands-on experience building an LLM-powered or agentic system that does multi-step work, and ideally that someone other than you has used.
- Familiarity with agentic patterns such as grounding and retrieval, tool use, orchestration, memory or conversational interfaces.
- Sound engineering judgment: you check AI-generated work, understand how it can fail, and recognise when simple automation or a human review is the better approach.
- A solid grounding in computer science fundamentals such as data structures, algorithms, and operating systems or networking concepts.
- Strong problem-solving and technical communication abilities, and the ability to break down ambiguous problems and deliver in small steps.
- Proactive mindset with passion for continuous learning and fast iteration.
How will I use AI at Roku?
At Roku, we don’t just use AI, we work with it. AI agents and smart tools help power drafts, analysis, and repetitive workflows, while our people bring direction, judgment, and accountability. We’re looking for curious, adaptable builders who can show how they’ve used AI or automation to move faster, raise the bar, and scale their impact.
We value your AI skills if you have built fluency across the agentic engineering toolchain — coding harnesses like Claude Code or Cursor, MCP servers, custom skills, or agent frameworks. You know how to drive an agent, verify its output, and ramp on an unfamiliar codebase with an agent helping you.
What's Roku's approach to hybrid working?
Roku fosters an inclusive and collaborative environment where teams generally work in the office Monday through Thursday. Fridays are generally flexible for remote work, except for employees whose specific roles or assigned office location require five days' a week attendance.
What are some of the benefits?
Roku is committed to offering a diverse range of benefits as part of our compensation package to support our employees and their families. Our comprehensive benefits include global access to mental health and financial wellness support and resources. Local benefits include statutory and voluntary benefits which may include healthcare (medical, dental, and vision), life, accident, disability, commuter, and retirement options (401(k)/pension). Employees are supported in taking time off, in accordance with local leave policies and other personal needs to support their evolving work and life needs. It's important to note that not every benefit is available in all locations or for every role. For details specific to your location, please consult with your recruiter.
Accommodations
Roku welcomes applicants of all backgrounds and provides reasonable accommodations and adjustments in accordance with applicable law. If you require reasonable accommodation at any point in the hiring process, please direct your inquiries to EmployeeRelations@Roku.com .
What should I know about Roku's culture?
Roku is a great place for people who want to work in a fast-paced environment where everyone is focused on the company's success rather than their own. We try to surround ourselves with people who are great at their jobs, who are easy to work with, and who keep their egos in check. We appreciate a sense of humor. We believe a fewer number of very talented folks can do more for less cost than a larger number of less talented teams. We're independent thinkers with big ideas who act boldly, move fast and accomplish extraordinary things through collaboration and trust. In short, at Roku you'll be part of a company that's changing how the world watches TV.
We have a unique culture that we are proud of. We think of ourselves primarily as problem-solvers, which itself is a two-part idea. We come up with the solution, but the solution isn't real until it is built and delivered to the customer. That penchant for action gives us a pragmatic approach to innovation, one that has served us well since 2002.
To learn more about Roku, our global footprint, and how we've grown, visit https://www.weareroku.com/factsheet .
By providing your information, you acknowledge that you want Roku to contact you about job roles, that you have read Roku's Applicant Privacy Notice , and understand that Roku will use your information as described in that notice. If you do not wish to receive any communications from Roku regarding this role or similar roles in the future, you may unsubscribe at any time by emailing WorkforcePrivacy@Roku.com .

Company Description
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Job Description
Primary Function of Position
The Robotics Engineering Intern will report to future forward research lad and contribute to creating a sim-to-real-to-sim platform for the Intuitive surgical robot system. The intern will enable rapid prototyping and de-risking of new controller architectures, particularly semi-supervised and supervised autonomous systems that are data-hungry and require extensive validation. Key functions include developing tools that systematically transfer and test controllers from simulation to robot hardware, building virtual models of the surgical field for simulation interaction, and closing the loop between simulation and reality to accelerate development and evaluation of autonomous controllers.
Essential Job Duties
- Implement novel control architectures in high-level (e.g., MATLAB) and low-level (e.g., embedded C++) targets.
- Systematically test controller performance in simulation and on robot hardware.
- Create simulation environments that integrate constrained rigid-body dynamics (e.g., MuJoCo) and realistic texture and lighting (e.g., Isaac Sim).
- Synthesize simulated environments from video data, including geometry, texture, and inferred stiffness.
- Execute closed-loop round-trip tests: train a controller in simulation, test it experimentally, and use experimental data to construct new simulation environments.
Qualifications
Required Skills and Experience
University Hiring Program Eligibility Requirements:
- University Enrollment: Must be currently enrolled in and returning to an accredited degree-seeking academic program after the internship.
- Internship Work Period: Must be available to work full-time (approximately 40 hours per week) during a 10-12 week period starting May or June. Specific start dates are shared during the recruiting process.
Required Education and Training
- Current enrollment in a Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, or related degree-seeking program at the Master's or Doctorate level.
Working Conditions
- None.
Preferred Skills and Experience
- Experience with MATLAB and/or Python for control system design and analysis.
- Experience with MuJoCo or similar constrained rigid-body dynamics simulators.
- Experience with sim-to-real transfer methods for robotic systems.
- Familiarity with NVIDIA Isaac Sim or similar platforms for realistic rendering and simulation.
- Familiarity with embedded C++ for low-level controller implementation.
- Awareness of video-based 3D reconstruction and environment synthesis techniques.
- Awareness of autonomous or semi-autonomous control architectures.
Additional Information
Due to the nature of our business and the role, please note that Intuitive and/or your customer(s) may require that you show current proof of vaccination against certain diseases including COVID-19. Details can vary by role.

Join the Future of Robotic Biomanufacturing!
Multiply Labs is a robotics company on a mission to solve a significant bottleneck in modern medicine: the manufacturing of life-saving advanced biologics, from gene and cell therapies to antibodies and more.
Today, these therapies are produced through manual, labor-intensive processes. Costs are extremely high—often $500K–$2M per patient—limiting access to only a small fraction of those who need them.
As product complexity increases and the cost of failure and scientific labor rises, the industry is shifting toward automation. Robotics and AI are making automated biologics manufacturing feasible, reliable, and economically scalable.
We believe the future of biomanufacturing is robotic—closed, automated, and scalable—ensuring critical therapeutics are accessible to every patient who needs them.
Why This Matters
We don’t just build robots—we’re building the essential infrastructure for next-generation biologics. Our technology enables biopharma companies to scale production without redesigning their science, reducing regulatory hurdles and lowering costs so these treatments can reach more patients.
The Stack & the Scale
-
The Mission: Build the world’s best robots to make life-saving therapies accessible to all.
-
The Technology: Advanced robotic orchestration, high-precision automation, cloud-integrated hardware-software systems, dexterous manipulation, and imitation learning.
-
The Location: Headquartered in San Francisco, CA.
-

To learn more and to view a video of our robots in action, visit us at www.multiplylabs.com and follow us on LinkedIn .

You’ll work directly with a cross-functional hardware and software team on designing and building the current and next generations of Multiply Labs’ robotic consumables. The work spans selecting and designing consumables, setting high-level design goals, building prototypes, and taking designs to production.
You’ll succeed in this role if you can optimize designs using first-principles engineering approaches. We run several projects at once, so you’ll need strong documentation skills and the ability to turn ideas into action. You’ll help drive decisions on major projects while coordinating with colleagues.

There was a time when all of America believed that the future of the physical world could be radically different. The engineers of the mid-1900s put a man on the moon in eight years, designed and built planes and submarines from scratch in under three, and conceived of building things we wouldn’t even be able to dream up today.
Today, the last of the engineers who imagined and built these systems are retiring. As they go, we lose not only the engineering knowledge gained from their decades of imagination and trial-and-error, but also the spirit that made that imagination possible.
Amca is working day-in and day-out to restore America’s ability to engineer anything that our critical systems depend on, and reinvigorate the cycle of creation that allows imagination to shape physical reality. We rapidly develop and manufacture new critical components and subsystems required to build and sustain the planes, military vehicles, and core infrastructure America needs. By restoring the capability of our antiquated supply chains, we increase the country’s capacity to imagine and realize new systems, and make a physical world that looks very different from today.
Overview
The Mechanical Design Engineering Intern works alongside our design team to develop flight hardware for new and existing airframes. You will own a scoped hardware project from concept through prototype and test, with a dedicated mentor and daily access to the engineers responsible for the systems around you. Your summer will consist of designing, analyzing, and building fluid and structural components, and learning how customer level requirements translate into parts that get built and qualified.
This is not a shadowing program. Interns at Amca ship hardware. You should expect your work to be reviewed with the same rigor as a full-time engineer's, and to see your parts on the bench before you leave.
Responsibilities
- Design and prototype mechanical hardware under the guidance of a mentor engineer
- Contribute to avionics hardware (buttons, switches, dials), flow control devices (valves, regulators, solenoids), or mechanisms (actuators, pistons)
- Question requirements, look for simplification, and help accelerate component deliveries
- Generate and maintain detailed drawings, component specifications, and supporting analysis
- We believe design engineers should perform their own concept design, technical analysis, and first unit builds, and we hold interns to the same expectation at an appropriate scope
- Support root cause investigations arising in development, production, and test, and help implement corrective actions
- Build and test your own prototypes in our in-house R&D lab
- Work with test engineering to help define and execute qualification plans for the components you own
- Work with build engineers to understand manufacturability constraints and incorporate DFM feedback into your designs
- Present your project and results to the engineering team at the end of the internship
Basic Qualifications
- Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD program in aerospace engineering, manufacturing engineering, materials engineering, mechanical engineering, or engineering physics
- Returning to school in Fall 2027, or graduating in Spring 2027 and interested in a full-time role

- Hands-on design, analysis, or build experience through coursework, a student project team, personal projects, or a prior internship
Preferred Skills and Experience
- Experience on a student project team building physical hardware, such as rocketry, Formula SAE, Baja, or a design build fly team
- Familiarity with GD&T concepts
- Experience with Siemens NX, SolidWorks, or a similar CAD package

- Strong interpersonal and collaborative skills, enthusiasm for problem solving, and interest in modern aerospace production and design
Additional Requirements

- Occasional travel to vendors or other Amca sites may be required

COMPANY OVERVIEW

Each year, 2.5 trillion hours are spent on household chores. At Matic, we’re on a mission to recapture that lost time, and we’re doing it by revolutionizing home robotics.

Our first product, also called Matic, is a Wall-E-esque floor cleaning robot. We've built what amounts to "full self-driving in the home” with real-time 3D mapping, adaptive path-tracking, and a precise semantic understanding of the home. Our breakthroughs in spatial AI allow Matic to work reliably in real homes, using only RGB cameras and neural networks running on-device.




PRIVACY FIRST

What happens in the home, stays in the home. Our robots are private by design, with all data processing performed by the robot itself, not in the cloud.




OUR APPROACH

Before the iPhone, consumers adopted several distinct devices; cell phones, PDAs, and portable music players each served a particular need. We believe in a similar progression for home robotics, starting with single-purpose robots and building iteratively toward more complex capabilities over time.




OUR CULTURE

Matic is a tight-knit and collaborative team, singularly focused on building products our customers will cherish. We're ultra-hardworking people committed to solving tough problems that save precious time and energy.




ABOUT THE ROLE

You'll own parts and sub-assemblies with support from experienced engineers, contributing from concept through high volume production. Our robots are shipping to customers today, which means the parts you work on get tooled, built at volume, and used daily in someone's home. You'll have the opportunity to see your work in the field within months, not years.

This is an internship for someone who wants to get their hands on real hardware immediately and build the judgment that comes from watching designs succeed and fail in production.



What you'll do

 - Design parts and sub-assemblies within a defined architecture, and help carry them through to mass production

 - Build your own prototypes, break them, and iterate fast

 - Run component level testing for performance, durability, and part to part variability

 - Help write and execute accelerated test plans that predict field behavior

 - Create production-ready 2D drawings with guidance and review from the team

 - Work with engineers, vendors, and CMs on DFM feedback, tooling reviews, and first article inspection

 - Collaborate with EE, firmware, software, and industrial design to keep your parts balanced against the rest of the system



What we look for

 - Parts or assemblies you personally designed and built through internships, project teams, research, or personal projects, and the ability to explain your design decisions

 - Familiarity with high volume manufacturing processes such as injection molding, die casting, stamping, or metal injection molding, and an interest in learning how they shape a design

 - An understanding of tolerances and how individual part dimensions affect an assembly

 - Familiarity with engineering drawings and basic GD&T

 - SolidWorks proficiency and experience using CAD to build real hardware

 - A hands-on approach to prototyping, testing, and troubleshooting

 - An ability to reason from a failure back to a possible design or manufacturing cause

 - Comfort in a fast-paced startup where the answer is often “go build it and find out”

Currently pursuing a degree in mechanical engineering or a related technical field, or demonstrating equivalent hands-on experience. Prior experience with FEA, PDM/PLM, or production hardware is a plus, but not required.



Engineering Culture at Matic

We're a small team building a hard product. The work doesn't sort itself into a clean design lane.

During your internship, you'll work on concepts and CAD. You'll also build test fixtures, run tolerance studies, troubleshoot life tests, tear down returned units, update drawings, and learn how parts move from a design to a production line.

None of that is beneath the job. All of it is the job, and most of it is where you'll get good.

Our engineers own their parts from the first sketch to the last field failure, including every unglamorous step in between. As an intern, you'll take on meaningful pieces of that work with support and feedback from the team. We keep design, testing, supplier work, and documentation together on purpose, because that's how you build the judgment to design something that actually survives a home.

The same goes past your own scope. If a fixture in the lab is broken, if data needs cleaning, if a different subsystem is blocking the build, people here move toward it. Scope is how we plan the work, not how we decide what's ours.

That's the shape of the team we're building. Being excited about a particular kind of engineering is great and we want that. But the people who've done the most for this company are the ones who wanted Matic to win first and picked up whatever that took.



We'd love to hear from you if...

 - You are genuinely motivated to help those around you

 - You are passionate about learning outside your normal comfort zones

 - You love diagnosing complex technical issues

 - You take pride in details nobody else would notice




COMPENSATION

Base: $25- $35/hour.

Actual Compensation will depend on skills, experience, and qualifications.

FieldAI is transforming how robots interact with the real world. Our growing R&D team is based in Boston, where we develop risk-aware, reliable, field-ready AI systems that tackle the hardest problems in robotics and unlock the potential of embodied intelligence. We take a pragmatic approach that goes beyond off-the-shelf, purely data-driven methods or transformer-only architectures, combining cutting-edge research with real-world deployment. Our solutions are already deployed globally, and we continuously improve model performance through rapid iteration driven by real field use.


Hardware Team: The Hardware Team at Field AI develops perception and compute payloads that power autonomous robotics systems in complex real world environments. Our work spans the full hardware stack designing and integrating sensing systems (LiDAR, camera, TOF, IMU, GPS), embedded compute (CPUs, GPUs, microcontrollers, Linux, ROS), electrical systems (power distribution, communication), and mechanical components (structures, thermal regulation, ingress protection). The team focuses on both development (research, design, prototyping, testing) and operations (production, testing, QA, debugging). We’re a small, fast-moving team, and we care deeply about improving: 1) core capabilities, 2) system reliability, 3) system scalability. As a growing team we are also building operational systems and procedures from the ground up. 
 
Mechanical Systems Intern Role: As a Mechanical Engineer Intern on the Hardware Team at Field AI, you will contribute to the design and implementation of mechanical systems that house and support sensing and compute platforms in real-world environments. From ruggedized enclosures to thermal management to manufacturability, your work will be critical to ensuring our systems operate reliably in the field. Responsibilities may span the full lifecycle from CAD through production to field support. You will collaborate closely with electrical, compute, and systems engineers to build tightly integrated solutions ready for deployment in challenging field environments.  Additionally while your focus will be on mechanical systems you will likely contribute across all hardware domains.

What You Will Get To Do
Mechanical System Design
-
Structures: Design and model mechanical structures including external enclosures, internal compute frames, and load-bearing chassis.
-
Mounts: Design and validate robust sensor mounts, payload attachment points, and mechanical interfaces.
-
Ingress Protection: Implement IP-rated solutions with gaskets, seals, membranes, and coatings to meet water/dust ingress standards.
-
Thermal Management: Incorporate thermal mitigation strategies such as fans, heat sinks, conductive paths, and airflow guides.
-
Mass & Volume Budgets: Ensure adherence to payload constraints, including tight volumetric envelopes and weight limitations.
Mechanical System Implementation
-
CAD & Simulation: Build detailed SolidWorks CAD assemblies. Run FEA and thermal simulations to validate strength, durability, and heat dissipation.
-
Material & Component Selection: Choose materials and components to meet mass, strength, thermal, and manufacturability constraints. Design for Production: Apply DFM, DFA, DFS principles throughout the design lifecycle.
-
System Testing: Conduct mechanical load testing (shock, vibration), thermal validation, ingress tests, and sensor alignment assessments.
-
Prototyping: Rapidly iterate on prototypes for fit checks, thermal evaluations, and integration trials.
-
Documentation & Budgets: Generate mechanical drawings, GD&T annotations, BOMs, and assembly instructions for fabrication and QA. Manage weight, volume, and thermal budgets.
Mechanical System Production & Servicing
-

Build what most people think is impossible.
Hypersonica is building sovereign European hypersonic capability.
We are developing technologies that sit at the edge of what is currently possible, and we are doing it with small, talent dense teams of exceptional people.
Our culture takes inspiration from the operating philosophy behind Skunk Works. Small teams. Exceptional talent. High trust. Minimal bureaucracy. The freedom, tools and responsibility to solve problems that have not been solved before.
We are looking for interns who want to work in that environment.

The Opportunity
This is not an internship where you spend three months shadowing someone, preparing slides or waiting to be given something meaningful to do.
You will work alongside some of the best engineers and operators in Europe on real problems connected to real hardware and real programmes.
Depending on your background, that could mean contributing to areas such as:
- Engineering, propulsion, aerodynamics, structures, materials, avionics, GNC, software, electronics, manufacturing, test, quality, simulation, data or operations.
The exact problem matters less than how you approach it.
You will be given responsibility early, expected to think independently and encouraged to challenge assumptions.
If you see a better way of doing something, we want to hear it.
Who we are looking for
We are not simply looking for the highest grades. We are looking for people with exceptional potential. People who are deeply curious. People who ask why something has to be done a certain way. People who are not restricted by what they already know, what has been done before, or what others believe to be possible.
You might be a great fit if:
- You learn extraordinarily quickly.
- You enjoy solving difficult problems with incomplete information.
- You naturally break problems down to first principles.
- You build things because you are curious about whether they can be built.
- You are comfortable being wrong, learning quickly and trying again.
- You care deeply about the quality of your work.
- You want feedback and are equally comfortable giving it.
- You can communicate clearly with people very different from yourself.
- You want responsibility rather than supervision.
- You would rather create something than inherit a finished system.
What we value
- Mission alignment.
- Exceptional subject matter ability.
- The ability to execute in ambiguity.
- A builder mindset.
- A willingness to be on site, close to the hardware and the people building it.
- We believe in radical candour. High performing people should be able to challenge one another, give direct feedback and change their minds when the evidence demands it.
- We also believe that the strongest teams are built from different perspectives, backgrounds and ways of thinking.
What you will get
- The chance to work on technology that very few people in the world ever get close to.
- Direct exposure to exceptional engineers and technical leaders.
- Real ownership.
- Real hardware.
- Real problems.
- A very steep learning curve.
- And, if you are exceptional, the opportunity to build a career with us after university.
Who should apply
We are interested in outstanding students from leading universities across the UK and Europe, including Oxford, Cambridge, Cranfield, Imperial and others, however:
- Your university matters less than your ability.
- Your degree matters less than what you can do with it.
- Your experience matters less than how quickly you can learn.
- We are particularly interested in people who can point to something they have built, researched, competed in, broken, redesigned, coded, tested or taught themselves simply because they wanted to understand whether it could be done.
Security and Eligibility Requirement
Due to the nature of the work with the UK MOD, applicants must be a British Citizen (or Dual UK national with British citizenship) and eligible for UK Security Clearance (SC) and, where required, Developed Vetting (DV)
One final thing
If you are looking for a comfortable internship with a clearly defined playbook, Hypersonica probably is not for you.
If you want to spend your internship surrounded by exceptional people trying to build technology years ahead of where most believe it should be possible, we would like to hear from you.
Come and build something that does not yet exist.

Overview
Working at Atlassian
Atlassians have the flexibility to work where they can collaborate most effectively with their team, whether at home, one of our global offices, or both.
As a distributed-first company, all interviews are conducted virtually. We hire in any country where we have a legal entity. Learn how we work at go.atlassian.com/distributed .
Your Future Org
Atlassian’s Intern program combines hands-on technical design training, professional growth opportunities, dedicated mentorship, and building strong professional connections. This holistic approach empowers students to hit the ground running and sets them up for a successful and impactful career at Atlassian.
This role is located in the Pacific Time Zone (PT). You must be willing and able to work out of this time zone to qualify.
This position is not eligible for F1 and J1 students. It is not available for any work sponsorship.
Our paid internship program runs for 12 weeks between May/June 2027 - August/September 2027.
Your Future Team
Atlassian helps teams unleash their potential through the Teamwork Graph, the intelligent context layer powering 85% of the Fortune 500. Over 300,000 customers globally, including NASA, SpaceX, Netflix, Spotify, Airbnb, and the Atlassian Williams Racing Formula 1 team, all use our apps to build AI-first experiences through a transformed SDLC.
As a Product Design Intern, you’ll work on real design challenges that solve for the beautiful mess of modern work and gain firsthand insight into how we are transforming the way work gets done in an AI-first company. Atlassian Design turns complex teamwork into clear, connected, and inclusive experiences. You’ll work alongside designers, product managers, and engineers across our global organization, learning how to understand real customer problems, explore and test ideas, communicate decisions, and turn them into high-quality technical prototypes with our world-class AI tooling.
We’re building an AI-native company and rethinking how people and intelligent systems work together. Our teams are exploring new interaction models for AI, including Rovo and AI-powered experiences across Jira, Confluence, and our wider cloud platform. If you’re curious, collaborative, and excited to make a difference while learning from a global design community, Atlassian is the place to start your career and help build the future of teamwork.
Responsibilities
Responsibilities
- Apply strong interaction, visual, and systems-design craft to turn ambiguous customer problems into simple, accessible product experiences across Atlassian products.
- Partner with product managers, engineers, researchers, and senior designers to understand customer needs, evaluate technical constraints, and make informed design decisions.
- Use research insights, product data, technical prototyping and usability testing to explore assumptions, iterate quickly and improve the quality of shipped experiences.
- Contribute to design systems, patterns and documentation while learning how AI and connected teamwork shape modern collaboration at scale.
Minimum Qualifications
- Able to commit to a 12 week full-time (40hrs/week) program during Summer 2027
- Currently enrolled full-time in a 4-year bachelors or 2-year masters degree program and returning to the program after the completion of the internship, graduating by June 2028
- Please note: At this time, this role is only open to entry-level candidates with less than a year of professional experience (this does not include internships/co-ops)
Preferred Qualifications
- Experience with user-focused design
- Demonstrate the ability to plan while juggling multiple simultaneous projects
- Experience collaborating with team members, like engineers and product managers, and other designers
Qualifications

Job Description:
We are seeking a motivated Thermal/Mechanical Engineering Intern to support the design, analysis, testing, and validation of next-generation server hardware. Working alongside experienced mechanical, thermal, electrical, firmware, and system engineers, the intern will help develop reliable cooling and mechanical solutions for compute-intensive platforms containing CPUs, GPUs, memory, storage, power supplies, and high-speed I/O devices. This role offers hands-on exposure to server architecture, air and liquid cooling technologies, laboratory testing, engineering documentation, and cross-functional product development.
Responsibilities:
- Support the mechanical and thermal development of rack-mount server platforms, subsystems, and components.
- Assist with the design and evaluation of heat sinks, fans, air ducts, cold plates, brackets, sheet-metal parts, and other cooling or structural hardware.
- Build and instrument server prototypes for thermal, airflow, acoustic, vibration, and mechanical testing.
- Measure component temperatures, system airflow, pressure, power, and environmental conditions using laboratory equipment and data-acquisition tools.
- Execute documented test plans, maintain accurate test records, analyze results, and summarize findings in clear technical reports.
- Support workload and stress testing of CPUs, GPUs, DIMMs, drives, power supplies, and other heat-generating components.
- Perform engineering calculations and assist with CAD, tolerance analysis, thermal modeling, CFD, or FEA under the guidance of senior engineers.
- Investigate test anomalies and prototype issues using structured troubleshooting and root-cause methods.
- Participate in design reviews and collaborate with electrical, firmware, manufacturing, reliability, and supplier teams.
- Research emerging server-cooling technologies, materials, and design practices, including air cooling and direct liquid cooling.
- Follow laboratory safety procedures, maintain an organized workspace, and contribute to continuous improvement of test methods and documentation.
Education & Experience:
- Currently pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical field.
Knowledge & Skills:
- Completed coursework in heat transfer, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, statics, mechanics of materials, or mechanical design.
- Fundamental understanding of conduction, convection, pressure drop, airflow, and mechanical load paths.
- Ability to apply engineering principles to practical problems and communicate results clearly.
- Basic proficiency with spreadsheets and technical presentations.
- Strong attention to detail, organization, curiosity, and willingness to work hands-on in a laboratory environment.
- Ability to collaborate effectively in a multidisciplinary engineering team.
