Mill is a waste prevention technology company reimagining what it means to eliminate waste, starting with food. We build smart systems and infrastructure for homes, businesses, and municipalities that transform food scraps from landfill-bound waste into valuable resources, including chicken feed. Tens of thousands of Mill’s residential food recyclers are already helping households divert millions of pounds of food scraps every year, paving the way for our upcoming launch of Mill Commercial—the industry’s first end-to-end solution for managing, understanding, and preventing food waste in commercial environments (e.g. grocery, restaurants, food services). At Mill, we are passionate about building easy-to-use, beautifully designed technologies that keep food in the food system and out of landfills.
As a Product Design Engineering intern at Mill, you’ll be working with a tight-knit, fast-paced team on a novel consumer product. Your day-to-day will include hands-on work with hardware components and lab equipment as well as CAD design tools like NX. Since we’re a small team, your work and learning will span design, tooling, and testing as we push towards launch. This internship is for someone who wants to learn and be creatively challenged.
Responsibilities
- Work closely with the Mill cross functional team on the design and validation of new products.
- Develop prototypes and execute tests in order to drive design towards mass production maturity.
- Support 3D CAD design and 2D documentation.
- Support engineering build activities, partnering with suppliers and CMs to troubleshoot and resolve manufacturing quality issues.
Minimum Qualifications
- BS, MS or PhD in Mechanical Engineering (obtained or in progress)
- Working knowledge of manufacturing processes and material selection for the design and development of electro-mechanical systems.
- Proficient in 3D CAD (prefer Nx).
- Proficient in a variety of rapid prototyping methods.
- Strong analytical and communication skills.
Preferred Qualifications
- Experience with simulation tools (FEA and thermal) and statistical analysis methods.
- Experience with designing for high volume manufacturing (DFM/DFA).
The estimated base hourly range for this position is $35 to $45, which does not include the value of benefits or a potential equity grant. A wide range of factors are considered in making compensation decisions, including but not limited to skill sets, market conditions, experience and training, licensure and certifications, and business and organizational needs. Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor an employment visa for this role

Our research provides core building blocks to unlock comfortable, intuitive, and helpful Wearable AI, empowering everyone to harness the superpowers of this emerging technology in their daily lives.

Who we are

Aurora’s mission is to deliver the benefits of self-driving technology safely, quickly, and broadly.

The Aurora Driver https://aurora.tech will create a new era in mobility and logistics, one that will bring a safer, more efficient, and more accessible future to everyone.

At Aurora, you will tackle massively complex problems alongside other passionate, intelligent individuals, growing as an expert while expanding your knowledge. For the latest news from Aurora, visit aurora.tech http://aurora.tech or follow us on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/auroradriver.

 

What we are looking for

Aurora hires talented people with diverse backgrounds who are ready to help build a transportation ecosystem that will make our roads safer, get crucial goods where they need to go, and make mobility more efficient and accessible for all. We’re searching for Hardware Engineering Summer 2027 Intern for our LiDar Team in Mountain View, CA.

Our Hardware Engineering organization is fundamental to the development of the Aurora Driver - our revolutionary self-driving technology.

Our work spans mechanical and electrical engineering, computer science, product strategy, R&D, ongoing service, and more.

The Aurora Driver is a complex system comprising a primary computer, the Aurora Control Interface (ACI), multiple sensors (like lidar), and various vehicle peripherals. Our teams are responsible for packaging these components into various platforms to meet our rigorous performance, reliability, and safety expectations. To engineer this novel design, the Hardware team works closely with cross-functional internal teams and external partners, using data and analysis to inform our physical products.

In this role you will

 - Complete an impactful internship project aligned with Aurora’s current priorities and product vision

 - Work with a dedicated Mentor for project guidance and coaching, and collaborate closely with other full-time team members

 - Learn more about Aurora, connect with other Interns and employees, and develop new skills through events and hands-on experience

Required qualifications

 - Currently pursuing a Master's, or Ph.D. in a relevant engineering discipline (Electrical Engineering, Solid State Physics, or Optoelectronics) or a related field.

 - Returning to a degree-granting program after the internship concludes (Summer/Fall 2026).

 - Prior experience or coursework in sensor technologies (like LiDar or Radar).

 - Proficiency in Python or similar object-oriented programming languages

Desirable qualifications

 - Experience working with radar, lidar or other optical sensing systems

 - Experience working with integrated photonics chips or systems

 - Experience with frequency domain analysis/modeling and verification of system models against experiment

 - Experience taking projects from concept to field testing

Compensation

The hourly pay rate for this internship in Mountain View is:

 - $52.00 per hour for interns pursuing a master’s degree; and

 - $58.00 per hour for interns pursuing a doctoral degree.



Working at Aurora

At Aurora, we bring together extraordinarily talented and experienced people united by the strength of our values. We operate with integrity, set outrageous goals, and build a culture where we win together — all without any jerks.

We believe in-person work increases collaboration, empathy, and our ability to lead effectively. As a result, Aurorans are expected to work from the office at least 3 days per week, with some roles requiring more frequent in-office presence, up to 5 days per week, based on operational needs.

Our Careers page https://aurora.tech/careers provides insight into what it is like to work at Aurora, and you can find all the latest updates in our Newsroom https://aurora.tech/newsroom.



Our commitment to safety

At the core of everything we do is our commitment to safety. Building best-in-class self-driving technology will take time, and we believe that each employee at Aurora has a role in contributing to safety, every step of the way. Aurora expects commitment to our safety policies from every employee, and seeks candidates who take an active responsibility, can contribute to building an atmosphere of trust, and invest in the organization’s long-term success by prioritizing working safely, no matter what.



Our commitment to inclusion

Aurora considers candidates without regard to their race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, pregnancy status, parent or caregiver status, ancestry, political affiliation, veteran and/or military status, physical or mental disability, or any other status protected by federal or state law. Aurora considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law. We are also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, you may contact us at careersiteaccommodations@aurora.tech.





For California applicants, information collected and processed as part of your application and any job applications you choose to submit is subject to Aurora’s California Employment Privacy Policy.

Company Description
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Job Description
Primary Function of Position
You will join Future Forward, Intuitive's advanced concepts group, and report to an engineering lead on the team building AI for the next generation of robotic-assisted surgery. You will own an open-ended research and prototyping project in areas such as supervised autonomy and automation for robotic-assisted surgery, and AI that helps care teams deliver care more consistently and efficiently. The work draws on computer vision, generative AI, robotics, and agentic AI, and we will shape the exact project with you based on your background and the team's priorities. A successful internship ends with a working prototype, clear evidence of how well it works, and findings the team can keep building on.
Essential Job Duties
- Own an open-ended research and prototyping project, scoped with your mentor.
- Explore how computer vision, generative AI, and agentic AI can be applied to new problems in surgery and the operating room.
- Build working prototypes and evaluate them against clear baselines.
- Work closely with researchers, engineers, and clinical experts.
- Share your results through documentation and a final presentation and contribute to publications or patent filings where results warrant it.
Qualifications
Required Skills and Experience
- Research or applied experience in at least one of computer vision, generative AI, robotics or autonomy, or agentic AI (LLM agents and tool use).
- Strong Python skills and hands-on experience with a deep learning framework such as PyTorch.
- A track record of taking a loosely defined problem to a result, shown through publications, open-source work, or projects others have used.
- Sound experimental practice: you can set up a fair comparison and tell a real improvement from noise.
- Clear written and verbal communication with both technical and non-technical audiences.
University Hiring Program Eligibility Requirements:
- University Enrollment: Must be currently enrolled in and returning to an accredited degree-seeking academic program after the internship.
- Internship Work Period: Must be available to work full-time (approximately 40 hours per week) during a 10-12 week period starting May or June. Specific start dates are shared during the recruiting process.
Required Education and Training
- Current enrollment in a Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, or related degree-seeking program at the Doctorate level.
- Master's level students would also be considered based on two or more years of relevant industry or research experience.
Working Conditions
- None
Preferred Skills and Experience
- Publications at leading venues such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CoRL, RSS, ICRA, or IROS.
- 3D vision, scene understanding, or spatial reasoning.
- Generative models (for example diffusion or vision-language models) or LLM agents applied to real-world tasks.
- Robot learning, robotics simulation (for example NVIDIA Isaac Sim/Lab or MuJoCo), or ROS 2.
- Industry experience building ML or AI systems that other people relied on.
- Interest in or exposure to healthcare, surgical, or medical robotics.
Additional Information
Due to the nature of our business and the role, please note that Intuitive and/or your customer(s) may require that you show current proof of vaccination against certain diseases including COVID-19. Details can vary by role.
Intuitive is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We provide equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants and employees, and prohibit discrimination and harassment of any type, without regard to race, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, color, age, religion, protected veteran or disability status, genetic information or any other status protected under federal, state, or local applicable laws.
Mandatory Notices
U.S. Export Controls Disclaimer: In accordance with the U.S. Export Administration Regulations (15 CFR §743.13(b)), some roles at Intuitive Surgical may be subject to U.S. export controls for prospective employees who are nationals from countries currently on embargo or sanctions status.
Certain information you provide as part of the application will be used for purposes of determining whether Intuitive Surgical will need to (i) obtain an export license from the U.S. Government on your behalf (note: the government’s licensing process can take 3 to 6+ months) or (ii) implement a Technology Control Plan (“TCP”) (note: typically adds 2 weeks to the hiring process).
For any Intuitive role subject to export controls, final offers are contingent upon obtaining an approved export license and/or an executed TCP prior to the prospective employee’s start date, which may or may not be flexible, and within a timeframe that does not unreasonably impede the hiring need. If applicable, candidates will be notified and instructed on any requirements for these purposes.
We will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records in accordance with fair chance laws.
Accommodation & Accessibility Notice:
Intuitive is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. If you require assistance or an accommodation during any part of the application or interview process, please contact People Services at [email protected] .
We provide market-competitive compensation packages, inclusive of base pay (paid at an hourly rate), benefits, and a housing allowance. It would not be typical for someone to be hired at the top end of range for the role, as actual pay will be determined based on several factors, including relevant skills and experience for this internship, degree-seeking academic program (PhD, Master’s, Bachelor’s, etc), year in school, and location. The hourly rate is prorated against the intern program salaries listed and total program compensation will be based on internship duration.

Our Team
Semtech's New Product Introduction (NPI) Product Engineering Team is the central engineering function behind every new product we bring to market. Our team of focused and talented engineers takes full ownership of new product development — driving each program from conception through end-of-life with a commitment to flawless execution. Working closely with all internal cross-functional teams, our engineers define and drive DfT testability requirements, test coverage, production characterization (across process, voltage, and temperature variations), ATE-to-bench correlation, cost and yield optimization, test time reduction, project logistics, and seamless transfer to full-volume manufacturing. We take pride in delivering high-quality products that exceed customer expectations and drive business success — and our versatile, results-driven team makes it happen.
Job Summary:
Engineering Interns are an integral part of Semtech's Engineering team, provided with experiences that are both technically challenging and educationally stimulating. This role supports new product development activities — from early-stage development through production transfer — working closely with senior engineers and cross-functional teams to build foundational skills and contribute to program success. Under the guidance of senior engineering staff, the intern will participate in a wide variety of tasks associated with research, design projects, and product transfers to offshore production facilities. This is an excellent opportunity for a motivated engineering student eager to develop deep technical expertise in high-performance optical, analog/mixed-signal semiconductor IC products in cutting-edge CMOS and BiCMOS technologies.
Responsibilities:
- Develop technical skills and product knowledge under technical mentorship and guidance from senior engineers.
- Learn and follow New Product Introduction (NPI) processes and procedures, assisting senior engineers in maintaining documentation compliance.
- Work closely with senior engineers in developing product characterization plans for wafer-level and bench testing, gaining exposure to test coverage requirements across product specifications, operating conditions, and data-driven limit-setting processes.
- Utilize state-of-the-art ATE and lab equipment to collect and analyze device data, ensuring products meet specifications and manufacturability targets before production release.
- Develop analytical skills through hands-on ATE and lab data analysis of Semtech's high-performance mixed-signal IC products, supporting product characterization, correlation, and release activities while contributing to the execution and adherence to product specifications and quality standards.
- Review and help optimize test coverage, test limits, and guard banding under senior engineers’ guidance, applying best engineering practices to improve overall test efficiency, test time and test cost.
- Collaborate cross-functionally with diverse engineering and functional groups to improve product yield, quality, and specification compliance.
- Generate comprehensive reports and presentations with creative and clear analysis methods that highlight the relationships between process, voltage, temperature and device performance.
Qualifications:
- Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Electrical and/or Computer Engineering, with at least 3 years of coursework completed
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with keen attention to detail
- Good written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present data and findings clearly
- Must be methodical, organized and have the ability adapt to shifting priorities in a fast-paced engineering environment
- Self-motivated with the initiative to take ownership of assigned tasks and follow through with minimal supervision
- Safety-conscious with clean, orderly work habits and a methodical approach to engineering tasks
- Collaborative team player who works effectively with individuals of diverse personalities, backgrounds, and skill levels

About the Company
General Matter enriches uranium.
We are designing, building, and operating the world’s lowest-cost enrichment services, here in the US.
In the process, we are restoring America’s ability to produce nuclear fuel to power AI, advanced manufacturing and critical industries our country relies on to remain competitive.
Fuel drives the cost of advanced reactor electricity production, and enrichment drives the cost of the fuel that advanced reactors consume. Reliable, low-cost enrichment is the catalyst for the nuclear Renaissance now under way.
Our mission is to make nuclear not only the cleanest and safest source of baseload power, but also the most affordable. We believe abundant nuclear energy will lead to a post-scarcity society.
We were incubated inside Founders Fund, like Anduril and Palantir before us, and are backed by over a dozen of the world's top venture capital firms.
Our lean, world-class team of engineers and operators is applying a first-principles approach to solving the problem of nuclear fuel production.
We are a mission-driven company with a culture of urgency, accountability, and transparency.
Help us build a high-energy society by making the cleanest, safest form of baseload energy the most affordable.
About This Role
We are seeking a Civil Engineering Intern with an environmental focus to support critical infrastructure and environmental initiatives at our nuclear fuel cycle facility. As a Civil Engineering Intern, you will assist in designing, analyzing, and evaluating civil infrastructure solutions that align with environmental regulations and nuclear safety standards. You will work closely with environmental compliance, operations, and regulatory teams to support the facility's sustainability goals, water and soil management requirements, and structural integrity standards.
Responsibilities
- Assist in the design and evaluation of stormwater management systems, secondary containment structures, wastewater treatment facilities, and foundation designs for nuclear-related infrastructure.
- Support regulatory compliance efforts by helping ensure civil engineering work aligns with NRC, EPA, DOE, and state environmental regulations related to nuclear fuel cycle operations.
- Support site and environmental assessments for soil stability, groundwater protection, flood mitigation, and seismic resilience.
- Assist in designing and optimizing waste handling and storage systems to help minimize environmental impact.
- Help design and maintain hydrology and stormwater management systems that prevent contamination and control runoff from nuclear facilities.
- Support structural analysis efforts to help assess facility structures against natural hazards, aging infrastructure concerns, and potential accidental loads.
- Collaborate with nuclear, mechanical, and environmental engineers, health physicists, and regulatory specialists to help develop holistic solutions.
- Support project coordination on civil/environmental engineering projects, helping track schedules, budgets, and safety requirements.
- Assist in developing engineering-based mitigation plans for flooding, erosion, and environmental containment in case of accidents or natural disasters.
Basic Qualifications
- Current undergraduate or graduate student pursuing a degree in Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering, or a related field.
- Strong understanding of engineering fundamentals.
- General knowledge of applicable industry standards for industrial facility construction and environmental compliance.
- Familiarity with AutoCAD, GIS, or civil engineering design software (e.g., Civil 3D, HEC-RAS, HY-8).
- Collaborative team member who thrives in fast-paced, multidisciplinary environments and is eager to learn.
Preferred Skills and Experience
- Evidence of exceptional ability (prior projects, portfolio of work, completed products, etc).
- Coursework or project experience with stormwater management, hydrology, or geotechnical analysis.
- Interest in nuclear fuel cycle, radioactive waste management, or radiological environmental assessments.
- Exposure to seismic and flood hazard assessments.
- Experience in a fast-paced engineering environment or a highly technical role requiring a resourceful, entrepreneurial approach to complete tasks within tight timeframes or budget constraints.
Additional Requirements
- Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary.
Equal Opportunity Employer
General Matter is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with General Matter is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.
Compensation and Benefits
The hourly pay range for this internship is $30–$40 per hour, depending on the candidate's current standing in school (i.e. sophomore, senior).
Interns will receive a monthly housing stipend, and are eligible for overtime pay. Please note that the stated hourly range is an estimate and may be adjusted based on market conditions, business needs, or other factors.

Odyssey https://odyssey.ml is an AI lab pioneering general world models: causal, multimodal systems that learn to predict and interact with the world over long horizons. This foundational technology promises to revolutionize robotics, science, healthcare, education, gaming, defense, and beyond.

Odyssey’s founders previously pioneered the most complex application of physical AI: self-driving cars. They’ve now brought together a world-class research team from DeepMind, Tesla, Waymo, Meta, Apple, and Wayve, who have made significant contributions to language models (DeepMind Gemini), video models (DeepMind Veo), world models (Wayve GAIA), and autonomous systems (Tesla FSD).

Odyssey has raised significant venture capital from GV, Amazon, AMD, EQT, NVIDIA, Natural Capital, In-Q-Tel, Elad Gil, Jeff Dean, Guillermo Rauch, Garry Tan, Kyle Vogt, and researchers from OpenAI, DeepMind, MSL, Recursive, and Thinking Machines.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Odyssey is looking for talented research interns for 2026. We offer the opportunity for PhD students to collaborate with our machine learning research teams, pushing the boundaries of what’s possible in state-of-the-art visual AI. You will define and pursue a research project which advances state-of-the-art general-purpose world models. You'll have the support of Odyssey's research and engineering teams, data, and computational resources. We encourage seeing the impact of your research in the models we ship publicly!




WHO YOU ARE

You should be progressing towards a PhD or similar graduate degree, with some examples of research you’re able to share. You also should be able to work from one of our offices in Palo Alto or London. The internship may be done any time during the year.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

As part of this, you will define and pursue a 3-6 month research project towards publishable research in general-purpose world models. Odyssey’s goal is to expand what's possible in visual AI. THE PROCESS

As part of your application, please submit a short research proposal for a project you’d like to pursue. This should be at most a page and it is intended to help scope projects. Projects will be refined with successful applicants and the Odyssey research team.

Our staff is expected to be in office at least three times a week. A lot of our progress comes from working through problems together, and we want you in the room for that.

Your Impact at LILA
Lila's SCADA system spans cloud and on-premise infrastructure: Ignition gateways on EC2, a historian on RDS PostgreSQL, MQTT brokers, and edge nodes at each site. Today no single view shows the health of all of it, so the team learns about failures from users rather than from monitoring.
As a co-op on the Hardware & Controls Engineering team, you will build that view: a live connectivity diagram showing how every piece connects and which links are up, backed by dashboards covering database, gateway, and edge node health. The work is read-only end to end, with read-only AWS access and SELECT-only database access, so you can explore the full system safely.
You will be based at our Alewife site in Cambridge, working alongside controls engineers and the IT/OT team. Expect wide exposure across AWS, Linux, industrial networking, Ignition, and data visualization, and a clear picture of how an industrial SCADA system fits together end to end.
What You'll Be Building
- Build a live topology view of edge nodes, brokers, gateways, and databases with per-link status and last-seen timestamps
- Surface RDS PostgreSQL health: CPU, memory, storage growth, connection counts, replication lag, and slow queries
- Dashboard Ignition gateway and EC2 metrics, including JVM heap, tag quality, Sparkplug birth and death rates, and scan timing
- Monitor on-premise edge nodes for reachability, uptime, resource use, and last publish time
- Integrate existing sources (CloudWatch, Performance Insights, Ignition gateway metrics, broker status) into one interface
- Document the setup so the team can extend and maintain it after the term ends
What You'll Need to Succeed
- Pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in engineering, computer science, or a related field
- Available full time for the Spring 2027 co-op term, on-site at Alewife
- Proficiency in Python for scripting and data collection
- Comfortable working in Linux from the command line
- Working knowledge of networking fundamentals: IP addressing, subnets, ports, and routing
- Clear written communication for documenting dashboards and findings
Bonus Points For
- Exposure to AWS, particularly EC2, RDS, CloudWatch, or IAM
- Experience with Grafana, Prometheus, or similar observability tooling
- Familiarity with Ignition, MQTT or Sparkplug, or other industrial SCADA tooling
- JavaScript or React, useful for building inside Ignition Perspective

This co-op sits with the nucleic acid design group in LSAI, which builds models and design strategies for RNA and DNA sequences. You'll work at the intersection of machine learning, sequence modeling and nucleic acid biology, on problems such as UTR design, regulatory element design, and using large reasoning models for scientific discovery. You'll own a defined research project with mentorship from ML scientists, and you'll work closely with experimental scientists to connect your models to real biological data.

Lila Sciences is looking for a hands-on engineering co-op to help build and test the automated systems that run our laboratory workflows. Your Impact at LILA
Lila Sciences is hiring a co-op to join the Materials Science team within the Autonomous Science Platform. You will characterize electrodeposited metal films and develop the measurement methods that make those results repeatable. Deposition is handled by other scientists on the team; your focus is measurement, method development, and data quality.
The role spans electrical, surface, structural, and mechanical techniques: four-point probe for sheet resistance and resistivity, laser confocal metrology for thickness, step height, and roughness, XRD and EBSD for phase, texture, and grain structure, and hardness testing for mechanical properties. Much of the work is standing these methods up: defining sample prep, acquisition settings, and acceptance criteria so results hold across operators and sample batches.
You will work alongside scientists and engineers in a lab built for high-throughput, automated experimentation, and your protocols will feed directly into how these measurements get scaled.
What You'll Be Building
- Develop sample prep and measurement protocols for general characterization tools on electrodeposited films: four-point probe, hardness testing, and SEM/EBSD.
- Prepare samples for SEM and EBSD (mounting, polishing, surface cleanup)
- Run four-point probe, laser confocal metrology, and hardness measurements
- Analyze XRD data (phase ID, texture, peak shift, crystallite size) and EBSD data (grain size, orientation, texture)
- Validate measurement repeatability and establish data quality criteria
- Analyze and visualize characterization data, then document methods and failure modes
What You'll Need to Succeed
- Pursuing a bachelor's, master's, or PhD in Materials Science, Physics, Chemistry, Mechanical/Chemical Engineering, or a related field
- Hands-on experience operating materials characterization instruments in a lab
- Hands-on experience with hardness testing (micro- or nano-indentation, or others)
- Hands-on experience with metallographic or SEM sample prep
- Experience analyzing XRD data
- Working knowledge of thin films, metal microstructure, or surface metrology
- Careful experimental technique and detailed record keeping
- Available for the full Spring co-op term, January through May
Bonus Points For
- Master's or PhD candidates preferred
- Python for data analysis and visualization
- Experience analyzing EBSD data (e.g., MTEX, OIM, AZtec Crystal)
- Hands-on SEM and/or FIB experience
- Direct experience with four-point probe, optical profilometry, or laser confocal systems
- Familiarity with electrodeposited metals or electrochemical materials processing
- Experience developing or qualifying a new measurement method (e.g., gauge R&R)
- Exposure to automated or high-throughput laboratory workflows

As an intern at Affirm, you will be a contributing member of our outstanding engineering team, and as such you will work on meaningful projects and frequently ship code. Recent grads and past interns have built a real-time high-throughput data processing pipeline, developed an extensive automated testing framework, and built out our proprietary financial platform that is central to our long term company mission.
We are excited to meet and consider strong students for our 12-16 week internships. We are a dynamic organization that is happy to tailor projects to your skills, and we will work with you throughout the interview process to determine which team will be best for you.
What You'll Do
Interns are responsible for developing and shipping a project and verifying that it works in production. Because things are changing fast at Affirm, we do not specify intern projects in advance, instead you will collaborate with your mentor and manager when you start to spec a project that will best contribute to your team.
- This role will ship code and monitor the deployment of your work. Our intern projects are not isolated or intended to be thrown away: your team will depend on your contributions!

- There are opportunities to attend events with other interns and full-time Affirmers! Past events have included virtual cooking classes, executive fireside chats, cable car trolley tours, and Giants games.
- Interns present their work to the entire engineering organization at the end of the internship.
What We Look For
- Passion and dedication to changing consumer banking for the better
- Experience with Python, C/C++ or Java
- Frontend experience in WebApps/JavaScript/AngularJS/React
- Strong communication skills
- Experience with object oriented programming
- Deployment and testing frameworks
- API development/documentation
- AWS or other PaaS frameworks
Compensation is a set amount for the Intern role with no range.
USA hourly base pay: $50.00

Remote-first with flexibility built in

Some positions may occasionally require in-person work at an Affirm office, and a few are office-based due to the nature of the work. All new hires will be invited to attend an in-person onboarding experience.
Benefits designed for you
Our benefits reflect our commitment to care, transparency, and flexibility. Here are a few highlights:
- Health coverage at no cost: We cover 100% of premiums for employees and their dependents.
- Spending stipends: Monthly stipends support your tech setup, and the ability to choose health and wellness options that are right for you.

Shift Technology :
Shift is the leading AI platform for insurance. Shift combines generative, agentic, and predictive AI to detect fraud, assess risk, and recommend actions throughout the claims process. Our teams tackle complex data challenges and bring advanced models into production at scale, giving insurers deeper insights into their data while helping their customers get paid faster and enjoy a smoother claims experience. Our technology is adopted and trusted by the world’s leading insurers.
The QA Engineering Team 🧪:
The Quality Assurance team, part of Engineering, makes sure that Shift can ship fast and safely. Our AI-driven software is deployed for insurers worldwide, across many multi-tenant environments, and we use Generative AI, LLM agents, and modern automation to solve quality challenges at this scale. Here are just a few of the areas we work on:
- Release validation: risk-based testing and delivery automation;
- Automated regression suites and test automation;
- Functional test coverage and test gap analysis;
- Test data generation and test environment provisioning;
- AI-powered QA tooling, built with LLMs and agents, that engineers and QA leads use every day
Working with Engineering teams and QA leads, we replace manual QA effort with intelligent tooling, and we measure the time it saves.
Your key responsibilities🧑💻:
You’ll own an end-to-end project that moves a real QA bottleneck from manual effort to intelligent tooling. You will build something the QA engineering teams use in their day-to-day work, not a proof of concept that stays on a shelf. Your subject will be defined with you during the selection process, within one of these example missions:
- AI-driven release validation: build a “release copilot” that analyzes release tickets and code changes to compute risk scores and generate risk-based test plans. It also helps run bug bash sessions (scope, assignment, triage, duplicate detection) and drafts test reports and release notes.
- Functional coverage and test gap analysis: use code intelligence and LLMs to detect shipped features, feature flags, and endpoints, map them against environment configurations and automated regression suites, and show untested areas in a live coverage dashboard.
- Synthetic test data and environment provisioning: design a data generation and seeding pipeline (CLI / API) that produces realistic, deterministic, and privacy-compliant datasets, so teams can provision and reset test environments on demand, integrated into CI/CD.
Along the way, you’ll learn how QA, Engineering, and Product work together to ship AI software to insurers around the world. Your project will go beyond a prototype: you will validate it on real releases, hand it over with documentation, and present the results to leadership.
- Your profile and requirements✅:
- You are currently in your final year (BAC+5, Master 2 or engineering school) in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data, or AI.
- You have solid programming skills in Python , TypeScript/JavaScript , or C# .
- You have a good grasp of software testing fundamentals , Git , and REST APIs .
- You are autonomous and rigorous, with a strong sense of ownership.
- Nice to have: hands-on experience with LLMs, prompt engineering, or agent frameworks (LangChain, Copilot, OpenAI/Claude APIs); test automation (Playwright, Cypress); CI/CD (GitHub Actions, TeamCity); Docker/Kubernetes; SQL or lightweight dashboards (Streamlit, React, FastAPI).

- Language requirements: English is mandatory at a fluent level (French is a plus).

🤸♀️Flexibility, autonomy and adaptability are part of our core values : We are a horizontal organization without bureaucracy (65% of staff are in tech roles) but optimal and reduced line management, focus on delivery and development while having a hybrid model.

Shift is the leading AI platform for insurance. Shift combines generative, agentic, and predictive AI to detect fraud, assess risk, and recommend actions throughout the claims process. The QA Engineering Team 🧪:
The Quality Assurance team, part of Engineering, makes sure that Shift can ship fast and safely. - Functional test coverage and test gap analysis;

- AI-powered QA tooling, built with LLMs and agents, that engineers and QA leads use every day

We are seeking an AI Engineering intern who will work on real AI agentic automation problems, designing, prototyping, and developing AI-powered agents to help the business and engineers achieve faster, smarter work. AI tools change every quarter. Your project will use the best models, agent frameworks, and protocols available in summer 2027. You will work on current practice, not today's stack.
Launch your career developing real, impactful AI solutions in the lightning-fast world of fintech!

Our summer program will be 10-12 weeks from May - August 2027 with the expectation of being in the office 3-4 days per week, as determined by the sponsor. - Strong curiosity and willingness to explore new, rapidly evolving technologies

Job Description
Our team develops HPE Slingshot, an industry-leading interconnect used in some of the world’s largest HPC and AI systems. As an intern, you’ll work alongside experienced architects, logic designers, and verification engineers on a switch or NIC ASIC verification project for a future generation of Slingshot. You’ll learn industry-standard SystemVerilog and UVM verification techniques, participate in technical design and debug discussions, and see how our team is applying emerging agentic AI workflows to solve complex engineering problems.
We are looking for students interested in careers in design verification, HPC and AI systems, or high-performance interconnects. Ideal candidates will have ASIC or VLSI experience through university coursework, industry experience, or self-study. Experience with agentic AI coding tools and workflows is preferred but not required.
Responsibilities
- Develop SystemVerilog and UVM testbench components, including models, monitors, scoreboards, and checkers
- Write constrained-random tests
- Develop and analyze functional coverage to identify verification gaps
- Debug regression failures and help identify, log, and resolve logic bugs
- Work directly with ASIC designers and architects
- Use scripting, automation, and AI-assisted tools to improve the verification process
Requirements
- Pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field
- Coursework in digital design and computer architecture
- Experience with object-oriented programming
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
- Clear written and verbal communication skills
- Willingness to ask questions, explain your reasoning, and participate in technical discussions
Preferred skills
- Experience with a hardware description language such as Verilog, SystemVerilog, or VHDL
- Experience with Python, Perl, Tcl, or another scripting language
- Experience working in Linux development environments
- Academic, research, or personal projects involving digital hardware
- Experience working as part of a distributed team

Job Description:
Hewlett Packard Enterprise advances the way people live and work. We bring together the brightest minds to create breakthrough technology solutions, helping our customers make their mark on the world. The HPE Cray Slingshot team develops the backbone technologies that move data through the fastest supercomputers on the planet, and with this technology comes many interesting design challenges that push the limits of modern compute.
Job Responsibilities:
· Assist with VLSI / RTL design using System Verilog.
· Assist with creating System Verilog Assertions (SVAs) and use Formal Verification to prove design correctness.
· Assist with writing coverage to measure stimulus quality and perform coverage analysis to identify verification holes.
· Assist with creating scripts (Python, TCL, Perl) to improve design processes and efficiency.
Experience and skills required:
· Working toward a Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or equivalent.
· Self-driven with a positive, can-do attitude, and detail-oriented.
· Experience with System Verilog for synthesis (ASIC or FPGA).
· Proficiency in electrical engineering fundamentals, VLSI principles, digital logic, and computer architecture.
· Experience in executive written and verbal communication skills; mastery in English.
· Ability to work with cross functional teams (DV/Arch/Design/FW).
Preferred Skills:
· Understands the OSI model for layered networking stacks.
· Experience with Ethernet protocols, CPU or GPU systems, and high-speed peripherals.
· Understands the concepts of Formal Verification and design verification using UVM.
· A working knowledge of C/C++ or Python scripting.

Job Description:
Overview:
Join our ASIC team as an intern and gain hands-on experience in cutting-edge semiconductor development. Interns will have the opportunity to focus on one of three specialized areas — ASIC Design , ASIC Verification , or ASIC Tools & Methodologies —based on their interests and skills. You are not expected to perform all three activities ; instead, you will work closely with senior engineers in your chosen domain.
Responsibilities (based on chosen focus area):
ASIC Design:
- Participate in ASIC architecture investigation tasks , including evaluating design trade-offs and performance analysis.
- Create detailed functional and micro-architectural specifications
- Assist in RTL design using SystemVerilog , ensuring functionality, performance, and power goals.
- Support synthesis, linting, and design reviews.
ASIC Verification:
- Develop and maintain testbenches using SystemVerilog and UVM .
- Write test plans, assertions, create functional coverage models, and debug simulation failures.
- Contribute to regression setup and results analysis.
- Participate in emulation activities for pre-silicon validation.
Tools & Methodologies:
- Contribute to automation to accelerate ASIC development processes , flow improvements, and EDA tool evaluations.
- Develop utilities to enhance productivity and improve design/verification processes.
- Work with EDA tools for physical design , including synthesis, place-and-route, timing analysis, and sign-off flows.
- Support Design-for-Test (DFT) methodology development and integration.
General Responsibilities:
- Collaborate with team members to troubleshoot technical issues and propose solutions.
- Participate in team meetings, learn project methodologies, and share progress during periodic reviews.
- Actively engage in learning new technologies and best practices relevant to your focus area.
- Complete assigned tasks efficiently and incorporate feedback.
Education & Experience:
- Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field.
- Coursework in Digital Logic Design , Computer Architecture , or VLSI Design is highly desirable.
- Familiarity with ASIC concepts through academic projects or internships is a plus.
Knowledge & Skills:
- Programming & Scripting: Exposure to SystemVerilog , UVM , and basic knowledge of Python, C++, or similar languages.
- Understanding of ASIC design flow, verification methodologies, and EDA tools for physical design.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
- Ability to manage time and meet deadlines.
- Passion for high-tech and continuous learning.
- Knowledge of networking protocols, machine learning, or advanced computer architecture is a plus.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise offers you a highly dynamic, fast-paced, professional working environment and the chance to develop the skills you have gained at university in a real business environment. Start Date : February 2027

- Compute Hardware Support
- Storage Hardware Support
- Software Support, with exposure to technologies such as HPE Morpheus, VME, Linux, and Ubuntu

- Build hands-on knowledge of both hardware and software support, including technologies such as HPE Morpheus, VME, Linux, and Ubuntu
- Develop structured troubleshooting and problem-solving skills while working alongside experienced technical engineers
- Understand how technical support teams collaborate across different technology domains to resolve complex customer issues.
- Identify opportunities to improve technical processes and ways of working
- Collaborate with your fellow interns on a joint project, applying the knowledge and skills gained throughout the internship to solve a practical technical or business challenge
- Present and share your project outcomes, encouraging teamwork, knowledge sharing, and learning from your peers.
What you’ll need:
- Currently enrolled in a Bachelor or Master’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science or another IT related degree
- Fluent in written and verbal English
- Analytical troubleshooting and problem-solving skills
- Time management skills and working with strict deadlines

- The drive to seek out what’s next and to deliver exceptional results

- The desire to embrace new ideas and fresh thinking and seek out ideas different than your own
- Experience as an active leader on campus who strives to make a positive impact on the world

Job Description:
We are seeking a highly motivated Hardware Tools and Libraries Intern to help support our hardware design environment, EDA tools, and related libraries.
This role is ideal for a student interested in learning about complex hardware design environments, supporting hardware design processes, setup and installation of complex CAD tools, setup and replication of their related libraries.
The intern will learn about latest ASIC design tools and computer environment needed to run those tools, Schematic Capture and PCB design tools and libraries, and general computer environment that hardware engineers use daily to do their design and simulation work from concept to finish. This will be a hands-on position as a member of our hardware tools team, working in both Linux and PC environments.
Responsibilities:
Primary Focus: Hardware Tools environment
- On the hardware tools side of your internship, you will gain exposure and learn to:
- Develop new scripts or update existing scripts that monitor status and well-being of our design environment and servers that are used by hardware design teams
- Help debug and root cause issues that arise with CAD design tools and their related environment, setup files, configuration files and server/network requirements
- Interact with IT team and identify user issues that requires IT involvement such as user login and environment issues, machine issues, network access and filer access issues between PC and remote Linux servers.
- Help download and install complex design tools from vendor’s website to our design environment, create/update related setup files, initial test of the environment and confirming all is ok before handing it over to the end users
- Write simple to complex scripts that run on Linux or PC (depending on the task). Learn about, document, and update existing scripts that automate engineering design flow and help improve efficiency of daily tasks, or help implement better methodology
Secondary Exposure: Schematic symbols and footprint libraries
- Schematic symbol libraries in Viewlogic and Cadence System Capture tools
- Footprint libraries for Cadence Allegro Layout tools
- Assist with monitoring library replication from main central site to remote design centers in other geographies
- Debug and fix any issues with the existing replication setups
Education & Experience:
- Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or Computer Engineering
- Coursework in programming and scripting
- Strong interest in hardware design and its related environment and methodology
- Analytical mindset and problem-solving ability
- Working knowledge of and be comfortable working in Linux environment
- Strong desire to learn and investigate new areas of interest
Knowledge & Skills:
- Familiarity with ASIC and/or PCB hardware design process
- Experience with Python, Tcl, Unix Shell, or other scripting languages
What You’ll Gain
- Real-world experience developing engineering automation tools
- Exposure to professional ASIC design environments
- Understanding of high-speed hardware design tools
- Mentorship from senior tools and libraries engineers
- Practical application of programming in hardware development workflows

Job Summary
We are seeking Technical Support Engineer Interns to join the Wireless Technical Support organization. The interns will support customers, partners, and internal teams by assisting with the investigation, troubleshooting, and documentation of wireless networking issues related to Mist cloud-managed solutions, wireless access points, and associated technologies .
The ideal candidate is a currently enrolled university student in a technical degree program who has a strong interest in networking, cloud technologies, troubleshooting, and customer support.

- Assist Technical Support Engineers with the analysis and troubleshooting of wireless networking incidents.
- Support the investigation of issues related to wireless access points, cloud-managed networking platforms, client connectivity, authentication, and network performance.
- Collect and review technical information, including:
- Device and client logs.
- Event timelines.
- Configuration details.
- Packet captures and basic network traces.
- Connectivity and performance data.
- Help identify potential causes of wireless problems, including coverage, interference, roaming, authentication, DHCP, DNS, VLAN, and connectivity issues.

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in:
- Computer Science.
- Computer Engineering.
- Electrical or Electronics Engineering.
- Information Technology.
- Telecommunications.
- Networking or a related technical field.
- Basic understanding of computer networks and Internet technologies.
- Academic, laboratory, personal, or project experience with networking is desirable.

Required Knowledge and Skills
- Basic understanding of networking concepts, including:
- Ethernet and wireless networking.
- IPv4 and IPv6 fundamentals.
- TCP/IP.
- DNS and DHCP.
- VLANs and basic switching.
- Subnets and default gateways.
- Authentication and access control concepts.
- Basic understanding of Wi-Fi concepts, such as:
- SSIDs.
- 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, and 6 GHz wireless bands.
- Channels and channel utilization.
- Signal strength and interference.
- Roaming and client connectivity.
- Basic familiarity with troubleshooting methodologies and logical problem solving.
- Basic knowledge of command-line tools such as ping, traceroute, nslookup, or equivalent utilities.
- Basic programming or scripting knowledge, preferably Python, is desirable.
- Ability to read and understand technical documentation.
- English proficiency at B2 level or higher , particularly in written and spoken technical communication.
- Strong analytical, organizational, and time-management skills.
- Ability to communicate clearly with team members and document technical information.
- Strong interest in networking, wireless technologies, cloud solutions, and customer support.
- Collaborative, proactive, and solution-oriented mindset.
- Ability to work independently on assigned tasks while knowing when to request guidance.

- Familiarity with wireless access points, WLAN controllers, cloud-managed networking, or network monitoring tools.
- Exposure to Wi-Fi standards, including 802.11 technologies.
- Basic knowledge of network authentication concepts such as:
- WPA2/WPA3.
- 802.1X.
- RADIUS.
- Captive portals.
- Familiarity with packet analysis tools such as Wireshark.
- Basic understanding of Linux operating systems.
- Coursework or hands-on experience with Python, APIs, or automation.

SeatGeek is looking for a Security Engineering Intern to join our Security team. As an intern, you’ll gain hands-on experience across all aspects of our security program: from application security and threat modeling to detection engineering and incident response. You’ll help protect our users, systems, and data while learning how security operates at scale in a modern, cloud-native environment.
You’ll join a team focused on building proactive, secure-by-default systems through a combination of automation, visibility, and collaboration. Whether you’re assisting in code reviews, building security tools, or supporting incident response efforts, you’ll have the opportunity to learn from experienced engineers and contribute to meaningful projects that strengthen SeatGeek’s overall security posture.
What you'll do
- Collaborate with engineering teams to provide security guidance on new products and technologies
- Assist in threat modeling and architecture reviews for upcoming features and products
- Participate in regular security assessments through basic penetration testing and code reviews of SeatGeek products
- Learn and promote secure coding practices by working closely with developers
- Help engineer and enhance security controls to harden our AWS environment and improve visibility
- Contribute to automation and tooling projects that scale security across the company
- Support incident response efforts by helping identify vulnerabilities, tune alerts, and enhance detections
- Participate in Purple team (Red team / Blue team) exercises to understand both offensive and defensive perspectives
- Share ideas to continuously improve our security programs and shape their future
What you have
- You’re graduating in spring/summer 2028
- Proficiency in two or more programming languages (Python, C#, Go) and a solid grasp of coding and code review (yes, there’s a coding interview)
- Ability to think like an attacker when securing applications, using that mindset to identify potential vulnerabilities and drive meaningful improvements in code security and defensive measures
- Understanding of secure software development practices, threat modeling, and knowledge of common security vulnerabilities (like OWASP Top Ten)
- Curiosity and a desire to learn how things work under the hood
- (Preferred) Contributions to the security community (public research, blogging, presentations, etc.)
- (Preferred) Experience or strong interest in automating security tasks and scaling security processes through tooling.
- (Preferred) Familiarity with modern architectures, including microservices, Kubernetes, AWS, and other cloud technologies.
- (Preferred) Regularly participate in CTF, bug bounty hunting, and hackathons (bonus points if you share your Bugcrowd/HackerOne/HackTheBox profiles)
Our stack
- Languages: Python, C#, Go,, SQL, and Terraform
- SCM & CI/CD : GitLab
- Infrastructure as Code : Terraform, CloudFormation
- Cloud Platform: AWS
- Central Logging and Monitoring: Datadog
- Container Orchestration: Kubernetes
- Endpoint Detection & Response: CrowdStrike
- Secrets Management: HashiCorp Vault
- Dashboarding: Datadog, Hex, and Looker
Internship perks
- $360 per quarter to spend on tickets to live events
- Monthly commuter card for transportation
- Subscription to Headspace
- Free lunch & snacks is provided every day in the office
- Weekly planned events like comedy/broadway shows, sports games, museum visits and more
- Housing stipend

ABOUT PERIODIC LABS

We’re an AI and physical sciences company building state-of-the-art models to accelerate breakthroughs across materials, energy, and beyond. Backed by world-class investors and growing rapidly, we operate at the pace the frontier requires. Our team brings deep expertise, genuine ownership, and an insatiable drive to push the boundaries of what’s scientifically possible.



ABOUT THE ROLE

Periodic Labs is developing AI that can both simulate science and verify its predictions to train on the full scientific method. A central challenge in that mission is connecting materials discovery with real, scalable device-relevant form factors. Materials our AI predicts and our lab synthesizes must ultimately be validated through thin films, patterned structures, and device-relevant process flows for applications across semiconductors, memory, photonics, and advanced materials.

We are looking for a hands-on Research Intern with experience in cleanroom-based microfabrication or nanofabrication. This person should have practical exposure to lithography, deposition, and etch processes for silicon-based microelectronic, photonic, MEMS, or optical devices.

In this role, you will support process development and experimental execution while contributing to the buildout of Periodic’s internal thin-film and nanofabrication capabilities. Your work will help generate high-quality experimental data that feeds directly into our AI training pipeline.



WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Execute hands-on nanofabrication processes for silicon-based microelectronic, photonic, MEMS, or optical devices, including lithography, thin-film deposition, etch, substrate preparation, and related cleanroom workflows.

 - Support lithography processes such as spin coating, baking, mask alignment, exposure, development, lift-off, and optical inspection.

 - Operate or support thin-film deposition processes such as sputtering, evaporation, PVD, PLD, ALD, PECVD, or related techniques.

 - Run or assist with etch processes such as wet etching, plasma etching, RIE, ICP-RIE, or other dry etch workflows.

 - Prepare substrates, manage process flows, track samples, and maintain detailed experimental records that meet the metadata and data quality standards required for AI training.

 - Perform basic structural, optical, electrical, or morphological characterization, potentially including profilometry, ellipsometry, SEM, optical microscopy, XRD/XRR, 4-point probe, or related metrology.

 - Work with senior scientists and engineers to troubleshoot process issues, identify failure modes, and iterate on recipes or workflows.

 - Collaborate with materials science, AI, and automation teams to connect fabrication results with model predictions and experimental planning.

 - Follow rigorous laboratory safety and facility protocols, including those required by external shared cleanroom facilities.


YOU WILL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE

 - Currently pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in electrical engineering, materials science, applied physics, mechanical engineering, chemical engineering, chemistry, or a related field.

 - Hands-on experience in a university cleanroom, nanofabrication facility, semiconductor lab, photonics lab, MEMS lab, or related research environment.

 - Practical exposure to lithography, deposition, and etch processes. You do not need to be equally deep in every module, but you should understand how these steps connect in a device fabrication flow.

 - Experience working with silicon-based microelectronic, photonic, MEMS, optical, or semiconductor devices.

 - Comfort spending real time at tools, following cleanroom protocols, logging process details, and learning new equipment quickly.

 - Strong documentation habits and attention to detail. You record what actually happened in the experiment, not just what was intended.

 - Ability to work independently in shared research facilities while escalating issues appropriately and learning from senior team members.


ESPECIALLY STRONG CANDIDATES MAY ALSO HAVE

 - Experience with full or partial device fabrication flows involving lithography, deposition, etch, and characterization.

 - Hands-on experience with specific tools or techniques such as mask aligners, spin coaters, sputtering, evaporation, ALD, PECVD, RIE, ICP-RIE, profilometry, ellipsometry, SEM, or 4-point probe.

 - Experience fabricating silicon photonics, MEMS, optoelectronic devices, sensors, thin-film devices, or other micro/nanoscale structures.

 - Experience working in shared cleanroom environments, including completing facility-specific safety training, navigating tool reservation systems, and operating within shared-use norms.

 - Exposure to functional materials in thin-film or device form, including oxides, nitrides, metals, semiconductors, superconductors, magnetics, ferroelectrics, or multilayer stacks.

 - Interest in working at the intersection of experimental science, nanofabrication, and AI-driven discovery.


MECHANICS

Location: Menlo Park, CA. This role is expected to be on-site, with work taking place at Periodic’s lab and external cleanroom facilities in the Bay Area.

Term: Internship / fixed-term position.

Compensation: Competitive and based on experience.

Visa sponsorship: We sponsor visas and will do everything we can to assist in this process with our legal support.

Itron is innovating new ways for utilities and cities to manage energy and water. We create a more resourceful world to protect essential resources for today and tomorrow. Join us.
This part-time Electrical Engineer Intern will support Itron’s lab team on site in San Jose, California. As part of a new and growing laboratory environment, the intern will work alongside experienced engineers to help build, organize, maintain, and improve the lab while supporting engineering testing and development activities.
This is a hands-on engineering role. In addition to software and electrical engineering work, the intern should be comfortable working with hand tools and power tools, assembling equipment, building test fixtures, running cables, and performing the practical physical work required to establish and maintain an engineering lab.
Duties & Responsibilities:
- Identify and troubleshoot issues across Itron mesh networks, smart-city RF communications, lab computers, connected devices, and test equipment.
- Set up and execute engineering tests, verify data quality, analyze results, and compile clear and accurate test reports.
- Collaborate with senior engineers on laboratory projects, prototypes, technical investigations, and process improvements, contributing innovative ideas and adapting to changing engineering needs.
- Help build out and maintain a new engineering laboratory, including assembling equipment, organizing work areas, installing and modifying test setups, routing cables, and supporting other hands-on lab activities.
- Safely use hand tools and power tools, including drills, drivers, crimpers, wire strippers, soldering equipment, and measurement tools, to build and modify laboratory equipment.
- Build, assemble, install, and modify custom test fixtures, cable assemblies, equipment racks, enclosures, mounting hardware, and other laboratory equipment.
- Perform hands-on mechanical and electrical assembly work as needed to support lab infrastructure and engineering projects.
- Interpret engineering drawings, schematics, wiring diagrams, bills of materials, and assembly instructions when constructing or modifying equipment.
- Inspect, troubleshoot, test, and document custom-built equipment to verify electrical safety, mechanical integrity, and performance before use.
- Support equipment organization, maintenance, calibration tracking, inventory, and the safe operation of electrical test setups.
- Develop Python-based automation tools for test execution, data processing, equipment control, and reporting.
- Use source control and issue-tracking practices to document changes, maintain traceability, and collaborate effectively with the engineering team.
- Communicate progress, risks, assumptions, and test evidence authentically and clearly, taking accountability for assigned work and escalating concerns appropriately.
- Maintain organized code, test procedures, equipment, and documentation so work can be understood and reproduced by other engineers.
- Support a safe, collaborative, customer-centric lab environment focused on developing reliable technology and solutions for the Utilities & Energy industry.
Required Skills & Experience:
- Currently enrolled in an accredited electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or related degree program, with at least two years of college-level coursework completed.
- Hands-on experience using common hand tools and/or power tools through employment, internships, school projects, technical programs, construction, maintenance, manufacturing, automotive work, maker activities, or similar practical experience.
- Comfort performing physical, hands-on work in a new laboratory environment, including assembling equipment, working with tools, building or modifying test setups, organizing equipment, and assisting with general lab buildout activities.
- Ability to safely use or learn to use tools such as drills, drivers, crimpers, wire strippers, soldering equipment, and common measurement tools.
- Mechanical aptitude and the ability to assemble, modify, troubleshoot, or repair equipment using written instructions, drawings, or guidance from engineers.
- Ability to translate an engineering need into a practical solution, including identifying parts and materials and developing an assembly and verification approach.
- Ability to program in Python and read, troubleshoot, and modify existing code.
- Basic understanding of software development practices, including modular design, debugging, testing, and documentation.
- Awareness of electrical and physical workplace hazards and commitment to following established safety procedures when using tools or working around energized equipment.
- Ability to work collaboratively and adapt quickly as the lab environment, equipment, and project priorities evolve.
- Strong accountability and attention to detail when building, testing, documenting, or modifying equipment.
- Professional written and verbal communication skills and an authentic, collaborative approach to working with engineers and other team members.

Ocean Spray Cranberries, Inc. is a leading multi-national consumer packaged goods company (CPG), specializing in the sales of Cranberry products. Formed as a Grower-Owned Cooperative in 1930, Ocean Spray® is owned by a diverse network of over 700 Cranberry Farmers. These growers, many of which are multi-generational farming families who have been a part of the Cooperative for decades, are the foundation for all that we do.  Ever aware of our long-term commitment to our Growers, we care deeply about sustainability— in regard to both our business metrics and the environment—and believe that a focus on strong environmental management is an integral part of the way we manage our business.
At Ocean Spray, our purpose is to generate a passion for our Farmer’s fruit around the world by connecting our farms to families for a better life. Living out our values of Grower Mindset, Sustainable Results, Integrity Above All, Inclusive Teamwork (GRIT) has made Ocean Spray® a creative, entrepreneurial, energetic, and fun place to work.
Who We Are Looking For
The process development team at Ocean Spray Cranberries is committed to producing our high-quality branded products in locations throughout the world as well as exploring innovative technologies to unlock the potential of cranberries for the future. We fulfill that commitment by designing and executing scale-up strategies to bring the vision of our talented product developers to life at full-scale. We work in the laboratory, in our own scale-up plant, and at production facilities located in the United State and abroad. As an intern for this team, we are looking for someone passionate about data analysis and engineering, who will work with cross functional teams to execute their collective vision.
What You Will Do & What You Will Learn
You will gain hands-on experience with mass and heat transfer while supporting the development and improvement of food and beverage manufacturing processes. You will work alongside an accomplished team of engineers with varied backgrounds and experiences.
What You’ll Need
- Currently pursuing or recently completed (as of Winter/Spring 2026) Bachelor or Master of Science in Engineering (Chemical, Mechanical, or Food)
- Previous Laboratory or Work Experience
- Microsoft Office Proficiency and advanced Excel knowledge.
- Curiosity and will to learn
- Knowledge and Basic understanding of Experimental Design
Hourly Pay Range
$25.00 - $32.00
Duration & Location:
- Position will start June 8, 2027, and run for 6 months.
- Traditional work week but with summer Fridays 8:00am-12:30pm; flexibility and off-site work may be required for project travel, experimental test runs, customer discovery.
- This position will be based at our corporate headquarters in Lakeville, MA (about 45 minutes south of Boston, Exit 6 off Route 495), with opportunities to work at our pilot plant located at 152 Bridge Street in Middleboro, MA.
Who We Are
You might have our iconic cranberry juice in your fridge or have gotten into heated holiday debate about what’s better - canned or fresh cranberry sauce. But did you know that the hardworking people growing the superfruit in our products are 700 family farmers that own our cooperative? They entrust us with what is most precious to them to create new and innovative products that will delight consumers and grow this beloved brand today and into the future.
Team Members, Farmers, Consumers And Communities Alike--we Value What Makes Us Unique And Strive To Connect Our Farms To Families For a Better Life By Living Our Values

Job Description:
DataRobot delivers AI that maximizes impact and minimizes business risk. Our platform and applications integrate into core business processes so teams can develop, deliver, and govern AI at scale. DataRobot empowers practitioners to deliver predictive and generative AI, and enables leaders to secure their AI assets. Organizations worldwide rely on DataRobot for AI that makes sense for their business — today and in the future.
This effort is about building a multi-target joint probabilistic foundation model that can be used across industries to tackle some of the hardest real-world problems. The ambition goes beyond what tabular and time-series foundation models usually do: one model should support temporal forecasting, unordered tabular regression and classification, missing-data completion, and mixed-modality inputs and outputs while learning coherent joint structure across connected variables, rows, horizons, and scenarios. The primary objective is to create real value in serious use cases rather than optimize benchmark scores in isolation, although strong results on standard benchmarks are expected to follow closely.
This role is designed as a research-engineering internship for someone operating at post-doctoral level, or very close to it, who wants to shape the architecture of a probabilistic foundation model. The center of gravity is the model itself: the encoders that read temporal, tabular, and mixed-modality inputs, the attention and sequence mechanisms that carry structure across variables, rows, and horizons, and the distributional output heads and decoding schemes that turn hidden states into coherent joint predictions. We are looking for someone who can reason precisely about what an architecture can and cannot represent, and who then implements, trains, and evaluates the resulting PyTorch models in a production-quality codebase. A background in stochastic modeling is a strong plus rather than a prerequisite: the model is trained on synthetic data drawn from stochastic dynamics, so a candidate who can also reason about stochastic differential equations and design synthetic data generators can contribute on both sides of the training loop.
Required Skills:
- Strong PyTorch skills and hands-on experience building and training deep models.
- Solid understanding of Transformers, attention variants, and long-context or state-space sequence architectures, including the tradeoffs between quality, memory, and latency.
- Experience with probabilistic modeling in neural networks: distributional output heads, likelihood-based or proper-scoring-rule losses, mixture or flow models, or related uncertainty-aware learning setups.
- Strong foundation in probability and statistics, enough to reason about densities and masses, dependence between variables, and calibration.
- Ability to connect architectural ideas to working GPU-native implementations, controlled experiments, and diagnostics that show why a change helped.
- Strong engineering habits: readable code, tests, reproducible experiments, and disciplined evaluation of model changes.
- Ability to debug training instability, reason about why results changed, and iterate quickly from hypothesis to evidence.
Strong Plus:
- Working knowledge of stochastic processes and stochastic differential equations: drift and diffusion, jumps, regime switching, mean reversion, heavy tails, and how such dynamics are simulated numerically.
- Experience designing synthetic data generators or simulation-based training curricula, and an understanding of how the training distribution shapes what a model learns.
- Depth in a domain with rich stochastic structure such as finance, energy, commodities, or a similarly quantitative field.
- Familiarity with tabular or mixed-modality deep learning: categorical, ordinal, count, and bounded targets alongside continuous ones.
What You Can Expect To Work On:
- Designing and improving the core model architecture: input encoders for temporal, unordered tabular, and mixed-modality data; attention factorizations across variables, rows, and horizons; the distributional output heads and decoding strategies that produce coherent joint samples.
- Running controlled architecture studies, from ablations and scaling behavior to memory and throughput profiles, and turning the results into design decisions.
- Building scalable PyTorch implementations that support larger input and output spaces, better throughput, and tighter memory budgets.
- Studying how architectural choices, data-generation choices, and inference constraints interact to change benchmark quality and real-world usefulness.
- For candidates with the stochastic-modeling background: extending the synthetic-data engine with richer stochastic dynamics, constraints, dependence structures, heavy tails, and regime behavior.
- Turning research ideas into robust implementations and credible empirical results.
What You Should Expect:
- Work that sits close to the core of the project rather than at the edges.
- A fast research loop where good ideas can move quickly from hypothesis to implementation to benchmark.
- A real chance to contribute to research that aims for top-tier, state-of-the-art outcomes rather than only incremental internal work.
- A team that values rigorous thinking, clean code, and practical usefulness at the same time.
- Exposure to problems that combine deep learning, stochastic modeling, and real deployment constraints instead of isolating only one of those dimensions.
- A role that fits someone with broad interests who wants to work across both advanced modeling and serious implementation work rather than staying narrowly specialized.
