At Aftershoot, we’re building more than just AI tools; we’re building a global community of photographers who spend less time behind their screens and more time behind the lens. Every feature we create, every update we ship, is designed to make post-processing easier, faster, and smarter for photographers around the world. From culling to editing to retouching. Our AI tools do all the heavy lifting, so photographers can focus on what they do best: capturing moments, telling stories, and creating magic.
We’re a fast-growing, passionate team backed over 100K+ active users globally.
But we’re just getting started. Our mission is clear: solve the biggest pain points in photography, and keep evolving with photographers who use our tools daily.
If you care deeply about building meaningful products, working with curious and driven teammates, and being part of a team that genuinely loves what they do, we’d love to meet you.
Let’s create the future of AI in photography, together.
🚀 About the Role
A wedding photographer shoots 4,000 photos on a Saturday.
Before Aftershoot, that meant three nights hunched over a screen, clicking through near-identical frames, missing dinner, missing their kids, missing the life they take pictures of for everyone else.
With Aftershoot, it takes an hour.
That hour is the entire product. 100,000+ photographers around the world trust us with it. Culling, editing, retouching - our AI does the grunt work so they can go back to doing the thing they actually love.
Which means when we ship a bug, we don't ship an inconvenience. We ship somebody's ruined Sunday. That's where you come in.
Responsibilities
Every engineer here builds a piece of the product. The PM holds the plan for it. Design holds the intent.
You're the only person on the team whose entire job is to know what the product actually does .
Not what the ticket said. Not what the spec promised. What happens when a photographer drags in 12,000 RAW files, loses Wi-Fi halfway through, closes the laptop lid, and reopens it four hours later on battery.
We're not hiring you to tick boxes on a test sheet. You'll write code, own an automation suite, and hold the call on whether something is fit to go in front of 100,000 photographers. We're hiring you to become the person we can't ship without.
Here's the bar we're setting, out loud:
Six months in, when an engineer and a PM disagree about how a flow is supposed to behave, someone in that room should say "just ask [your name]" and that settles it.
You will know this product better than the people who built it. That's not a stretch goal. That's the job.
Required Skills
- Basic programming in JavaScript or TypeScript
- Comfort with browser developer tools
- A grasp of testing fundamentals — test cases, severity, the defect lifecycle, what regression actually means
- Sharp analytical instincts and genuinely strong attention to detail
- Clear written and verbal communication (a bug report is writing)
- Real eagerness to learn automation, not just tolerance for it
- BE/B.Tech, BCA, MCA, or B.Sc in CS/IT — freshers and final-year students very welcome
Preferred Skills (Good To Have)
- Playwright, Selenium, or Cypress
- Git / GitHub
- REST APIs and API testing
- Anything you've built and shipped yourself, however small
You will work with
- Captain: Neha
- Team Members: Vikas, Aditi and the rest of the Aftershoot team.

Ocean Spray Cranberries, Inc. is a leading multi-national consumer packaged goods company (CPG), specializing in the sales of Cranberry products. Formed as a Grower-Owned Cooperative in 1930, Ocean Spray® is owned by a diverse network of over 700 Cranberry Farmers. These growers, many of which are multi-generational farming families who have been a part of the Cooperative for decades, are the foundation for all that we do.  Ever aware of our long-term commitment to our Growers, we care deeply about sustainability— in regard to both our business metrics and the environment—and believe that a focus on strong environmental management is an integral part of the way we manage our business.
At Ocean Spray, our purpose is to generate a passion for our Farmer’s fruit around the world by connecting our farms to families for a better life. Living out our values of Grower Mindset, Sustainable Results, Integrity Above All, Inclusive Teamwork (GRIT) has made Ocean Spray® a creative, entrepreneurial, energetic, and fun place to work.
Position Description
The Intern will be required to work on project(s) relevant to Food Safety & Quality Assurance and present his or her project(s) at the end of the internship. As a Food Safety & Quality Assurance Intern, you may be exposed to multiple food safety & quality aspects through orientation meetings, shadowing, and on the job training:
- Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and development and implementation of Corrective
- Actions/Preventive Actions (CAPA)
- Risk assessments of products, processes and ingredients
- Ingredient/product testing
- Experimental design and data analysis
- Key Process Indicators (KPIs) and Process Performance Metrics
- Preparing and presenting projects
Potential Projects Include
CAPA Program Enhancement & Training Development
Assess current CAPA processes, forms, and documentation practices across manufacturing sites and identify opportunities for improvement. Develop standardized CAPA templates, job aids, and guidance materials. Create a CAPA training program for plant and functional teams. Present recommendations and implementation roadmap to FSQA leadership.
Ingredient Risk Assessment & Risk Profiling Enhancement
Review the current ingredient risk assessment methodology and supporting documentation against industry best practices and emerging approaches to ingredient risk evaluation. Evaluate current risk factors, scoring criteria, and risk categorization methods and identify opportunities to improve risk visibility, consistency, and prioritization. Develop recommendations for enhancing risk-profiling tools and processes. Present findings and proposed improvements to FSQA leadership.
Minimum Knowledge, Skills And Ability Requirements
- Must be a current student enrolled in a Master’s Degree or PhD Program in Food Science, Food Microbiology, Food Chemistry or other related areas

- Must be project oriented and able to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing
- Highly organized, self-motivated with the ability to work independently
Pay Range
$30.00 - $32.00
Duration & Location:
- Position will start June 8, 2027, and run for 10-12 weeks.
- Traditional work week but with summer Fridays 8:00am-12:30pm; flexibility and off-site work may be required for project travel, experimental test runs, customer discovery.
- Interns will have the opportunity to participate in multiple events throughout the summer including leadership panels, a day of fun in Boston and learning sessions from various business functions.
- This position will be located at our corporate headquarters in Lakeville, MA (about 45 minutes South of Boston – Exit 6 off of Rte 495). If necessary, this internship can be facilitated virtually.

You might have our iconic cranberry juice in your fridge or have gotten into heated holiday debate about what’s better - canned or fresh cranberry sauce. They entrust us with what is most precious to them to create new and innovative products that will delight consumers and grow this beloved brand today and into the future.

현재까지 실리콘밸리 최정상 투자사로부터 (ICONIQ, SoftBank, Tiger Global, Y Combinator) 누적 총 2억2천만달러 (약 2,450억 원)의 투자를 유치하였으며 국내 최초 기업가치 1조원 이상의 글로벌 유니콘 기업입니다. 캘리포니아 산 마테오의 본사와 서울의 R&D센터 및 APAC 오피스 그리고 뉴욕, 런던, 싱가포르, 인도, 캐나다 등에 오피스를 두고 있습니다.
Intern, AI Agent Engineering
AI 에이전트 엔지니어링 인턴은 엔지니어링 및 제품 팀과 협력하여 지능형 에이전트를 구축, 통합 및 배포합니다.
최신 웹 프레임워크, LLM API 및 툴링 파이프라인을 사용하여 프로토타입부터 프로덕션까지 실무 경험을 쌓게 됩니다. 인턴십 기간은 8~12주 입니다.(기간 논의 가능)
이런 일을 하실 수 있어요
- 에이전트 프로토타이핑 및 개발
- 프롬프트 엔지니어링으로 Hallucination 탐지, 대화 Resolution 등 마이크로 API 개발업무를 합니다.
- 내부 데이터셋과 도구를 활용해 AI Agent의 정확도를 테스트하고 검증합니다.
- 검색 증강 생성(RAG), 지식 기반 및 맞춤형 툴체인을 지원하는 백엔드 API를 통합합니다.
- 프롬프트 엔지니어링 및 툴링
- 다양한 사용 사례에 맞는 프롬프트를 제작, 테스트 및 세부 조정합니다.
- 프롬프트 버전 및 에이전트 배포를 위한 CI/CD 파이프라인을 설정합니다.
- 통합 및 배포
- 웹, 채팅 및 API 중심 환경에 에이전트를 임베드합니다.
- 실시간 성능 지표를 모니터링하고 로그, 대시보드 등의 관측 기능을 구현합니다.
- 협업 및 문서화
- 팀이 시니어 엔지니어, 제품 관리자 및 UX 디자이너와 긴밀히 협력할 수 있도록 지원합니다.
이런 분과 함께 하고 싶어요
- Python: 깔끔하고 유지 관리가 용이한 Python 코드 작성 경험
- Backend: Django, FastAPI, Express 등 서버 측 프레임워크를 사용한 백엔드 개발 실무 경험
- 협업: 뛰어난 의사소통 능력, 문서화 기술, 그리고 애자일한 팀에서의 협업 경험
- 산업기능요원 보충역 지원 가능
이런 점이 있으시면 더 좋아요
- 프롬프트 엔지니어링 프레임워크(예: LangChain) 사용 경험
- 클라우드 플랫폼(AWS Lambda, Vercel, GCP Cloud Functions)에 대한 이해도
- AI 제품 관련 UX 디자인 또는 제품 관리 경험
- Django 또는 유사한 Python 웹 프레임워크 사용 경험
이런 점을 얻을 수 있어요
- 첨단 에이전트 기반 AI 개발 및 시스템 배포에 대한 심층 분석
- 엔지니어링, 제품 및 디자인 전문가와의 교차 기능 협업
- 시니어 AI 엔지니어의 멘토링
- 실제 고객 사용 사례, 성능 튜닝 및 프로덕션급 툴 활용 경험

Overview
SUMMER 2027
Shure offers a challenging, fun, and rewarding summer internship program. The twelve-week program is offered to undergraduate and graduate students. We offer internships with a variety of work arrangements from onsite interns to fully remote in US. Each intern will receive a competitive salary. Additionally, Interns who are asked to relocate to Illinois for onsite internships will receive a housing stipend to cover living expenses. Applications will be collected, reviewed, and selected candidates will be contacted in late fall/early winter.
Under direct supervision of manager/mentor, the Automated Test Engineering (Hardware) Intern assists in the design of electronic and acoustical production test fixtures and systems to test the functionality of company products in all production facilities.
This Internship is Onsite and based in our Niles, IL location.
Responsibilities
- Assist in developing written test plans based on new product requirements and product schematics.
- Assist in developing new test capabilities using off-the-shelf solutions, software-defined test instrumentation, or custom-designed hardware.
- Creates and maintains schematics, bills of materials, test specifications, and other necessary documentation to support test systems and fixtures.
- Creates and maintains functional test programs to automate test equipment measurements, signal path switching, and product control.
- Provides basic electrical verification and troubleshooting of test fixtures, components, and test racks (continuity, voltages, etc.).
- Troubleshoots measurement issues such as voltage levels, RF (radio frequency) output power, RF and audio frequency response, RF sensitivity, and noise floor.
- Analyzes the reliability and capability of test fixtures, software, and systems, using statistical tools.
- Assists in the construction of functional test fixtures, which entails soldering wires/connectors, and populating printed circuit board components.
- Performs other duties as assigned
Qualifications
- In-process of a bachelor’s or Advanced degree in Electrical Engineering (Preferably Junior/Senior)
- Basic working knowledge of Microsoft Office tools
- Basic troubleshooting and analytical skills
- Experience with common measurement instruments: DMM and Oscope
- Highly-organized and willing to learn
- Able to follow standard instructions, practices and procedures provided by mentor
- Self-motivated, team player, detail oriented
- Good verbal and written communication skills
Applicants for this position must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Shure will not sponsor applicants for this position for work visas.

Shure’s mission is to be the most trusted audio brand worldwide – and for over a century, our Core Values have aligned us to be just that. THE MIX MATTERS Don’t check off every box in the job requirements? No problem! PAY TRANSPARENCY
Modeled by extensive market analysis and economic best practices, Shure offers competitive intern compensation that is reviewed and adjusted annually by our Total Rewards Team to attract, hire, and retain the industry’s top intern talent. Overview
Hexagon Autonomous Solutions is seeking a highly motivated Digital Hardware Engineering Intern to join our GNSS Positioning Digital Team for a one-year term from May 3, 2027, to May 2, 2028. This role emphasizes digital hardware design, test development, and hands-on hardware verification work to support innovation in precision positioning and anti-jamming technologies.
You will gain practical experience with a wide range of digital systems and test equipment, including spectrum analyzers, signal generators, GNSS constellation simulators, oscilloscopes, power meters, and programmable power supplies while developing automation solutions in Python and contributing to design verification, prototype testing, and product development.
Location: Hexagon is a global company with locations around the world. This position is based onsite in Calgary, AB.
Responsibilities
As a Digital Hardware Engineering Intern , your contributions will include:
- Automating test setups using Python to control power supplies, thermal chambers, oscilloscopes, and signal generators.
- Designing, executing, and documenting product performance tests and test procedures.
- Performing signal analysis using oscilloscopes and logic analyzers.
- Configuring and operating equipment for GNSS and anti-jam system testing.
- Collecting and analyzing test data to evaluate system performance and identify issues.
- Troubleshooting test failures and performing root-cause analysis.
- Supporting design verification activities and participating in reviews of digital hardware and subsystems.
- Hand-building and debugging test prototypes and performing component-level qualification testing.
- Developing test plans and scripts to accelerate hardware testing.
- Compiling high-quality written reports using standard templates.
- Contributing to process improvements in digital hardware test automation and laboratory workflows.
Qualifications
Must-Have:
- Registered in an Engineering Internship/Co-op Program (Electrical, Electronic, or Computer Engineering) and completed at least the second or third year of studies by the start of the work term.
- Strong academic credentials.
- Proficiency in Python programming.
- Strong oral and written communication skills.
- Available for a 12-month, full-time (37.5 hours/week) internship in Calgary, Alberta.
Key Success Factors:
- Confident self-starter with strong attention to detail and a “first-time-right” mindset.
- Comfortable working both independently and in a collaborative team environment.
- Motivated by challenging technical work with a focus on quality and precision.
- Able to follow complex instructions while knowing when to ask for help.
Nice-to-Have:
- Coursework, specialization, or interest in digital hardware design, GNSS, or wireless communications.
- Familiarity with hardware test equipment (oscilloscopes, signal generators, power supplies, spectrum analyzers).
- Understanding of digital design principles, GNSS signal characteristics, or interference/jamming concepts.
- Experience with Python or other scripting languages for data processing and analysis.
- Ability to read and understand electronic schematics.
This job posting closes on October 4, 2026.

Join us and play your part in something special!
Underwriters, claims handlers and operations teams at Markel spend hours on work a computer can do well: reading broker emails, keying the same data into two systems, checking documents against rules and rebuilding quote letters by hand. We build working tools that take that work off their plate—AI-assisted underwriting workbenches, automated email flows and links between the systems people already use.
We move quickly and we build for real people. A typical project goes from a conversation with a business leader to a working proof of concept in days. Then we test it, harden it and hand it over. You'll join as the second person on this work, so you'll learn fast and see your work in use early. Along the way you'll learn how specialty insurance runs and how to put AI to work safely inside a regulated business.
What you'll do
– Build and improve proof-of-concept tools, including browser-based workbenches that underwriters use to read submissions, price risks and produce quotes.
– Connect systems through APIs: send requests, handle sign-in and tokens, map the data that comes back and deal with errors gracefully.
– Write Python scripts that turn spreadsheets, PDFs and Word documents into clean data—and turn data back into finished documents.
– Build and maintain Power Automate flows, SharePoint lists and Copilot Studio agents that triage email, review documents and send reminders.
– Put large language models to work: write the prompts and extraction schemas, then build test sets that show whether the AI got it right and what it cost.
– Test before anyone relies on your work, using automated browser checks, unit tests and side-by-side checks against the source data.
– Deploy tools on our cloud data platform, Databricks, while keeping access, secrets and cost under control.
– Write the documentation that lets someone else pick up a project: setup notes, runbooks, user guides and change logs.
– Join meetings with underwriters and business leaders, capture what they need and turn it into clear requirements.

– A bachelor's degree
– Working skill in at least one programming language, ideally Python or JavaScript, shown through coursework, an internship or your own projects.

– Strong Excel skills (lookups, pivot tables, formulas) and comfort working with large data sets.
– Clear writing. You can explain what you built and why to someone who doesn't code.

– Good judgment with data. You'll handle customer and broker information, so you ask before you share or send
– Business acumen

Job Summary:
Job Description:
Are you interested in being a part of a company that has a positive social impact? Do you want to join a growing team with a modern engineering culture?
At BiblioCommons, we build SaaS solutions for public libraries that directly impact the lives of millions and foster learning, literacy and culture within the digital world. We are constantly improving our products through user research, client interaction, and the input of our creative staff. Join a team of passionate professionals making public libraries accessible, delightful, and engaging.
A lot of companies tout 'social impact', here at BiblioCommons we serve over 8 million diverse users each month by partnering with close to 200 public libraries in Canada, the US and New Zealand. Libraries are more than just book stacks; they are public spaces that foster learning, connection, and community and BiblioCommons is bringing that community online with clever software that powers the world's largest libraries.
Engineering @ BiblioCommons
BiblioCommons offers an opportunity to work in an environment that combines the challenges and complexity of a large-scale, data-intensive application with the creativity and fun of a sophisticated consumer web offering, central to the daily web interactions of millions of users.
We’re a highly collaborative team that applies innovative solutions to challenging problems. We believe strongly in automation and invest heavily in it. We’re also committed to doing things right and always looking for ways to do them better. Today, that means building an AI-first software development lifecycle, where engineers use agentic coding tools like Claude Code to plan, build, test, and review changes across our platform.
We are hiring two Junior Full-Stack Engineers for 16-month PEY internships to maintain and build elegant, high-performance web experiences that help millions of users discover more physical and digital content. You will work across the full stack, primarily through Claude Code: directing an AI agent to explore our codebase, write and refactor code, generate tests, and investigate issues, while you own the thinking, the judgment, and the quality of everything that ships.
By AI-native, we mean someone for whom working with AI agents is already the natural way to build software, and who understands the code well enough to own it. We care less about how fast you can prompt and more about how well you can direct, verify, and improve what an agent produces.
You will enjoy and be successful in this role if you are:
- Great at debugging and not afraid to step out of your comfort zone.
- Accountable and take ownership of your work, including every line of code an AI agent writes on your behalf.
- Supportive and enjoy working as part of a team.
- Passionate about self-improvement, growth, and tackling new challenges.
- Reliable and consistent in the effort you bring.
- Never content with the status quo. You are always looking to automate, improve processes, and follow best practices.
- AI-native: AI agents are already your default way to learn, build, and solve problems, not an occasional experiment.
- Healthily skeptical: you verify AI output instead of trusting it, and you can tell when an agent is confidently wrong.
How you will make an impact:
- Enhance and maintain our platform applications, front end and back end, that serve millions of users, using Claude Code as your primary development tool.
- Turn tickets into clear specs and plans before implementation, and use them to guide the agent through well-scoped, reviewable changes.
- Debug and perform root cause analysis on integration issues, using AI to trace code paths, read logs, and test hypotheses quickly.
- Review, test, and refine AI-generated code so that what you ship is clean, robust, performant, and secure.
- Maintain quality as a priority by writing meaningful tests and validating them yourself.
- Improve developer productivity by refactoring key areas of the Core UI codebase.
- Contribute to our shared AI tooling, such as Claude Code custom commands, skills, and project context files, so the whole team gets faster.
- Work across multiple frameworks and programming languages, using AI to ramp up quickly on unfamiliar parts of a large, mature codebase.
- Communicate effectively to flag challenges or blockers to deliver on time.
What will you bring to the team:
- Hands-on experience building software with AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or similar) through coursework, personal projects, hackathons, or previous internships.
- Ability to break a problem into clear, well-scoped instructions and give an agent the context it needs to succeed.
- Solid fundamentals in data structures and algorithms. You need to understand the code to judge it.
- Knowledge of JavaScript, HTML5, and CSS3.
- Some knowledge of RESTful APIs and how web applications fit together, from browser to database.
- Excellent problem-solving and debugging skills.
- Excellent communication skills and collaboration across teams.
- Passion and motivation to learn new technologies.
- Interest in building highly responsive consumer web application interfaces at scale.
Bonus Points for:
- React, Ruby, and Rails knowledge.
- Previous programming experience in any object-oriented language.
- Experience customizing AI coding workflows, such as custom commands, skills, subagents, hooks, or MCP server integrations.
- A portfolio, GitHub repo, or short write-up showing something you built with an AI agent and what you learned about working with one.
- Knowledge of cloud-native applications.
- Basic computer networking knowledge (connectivity issues, LANs, firewalls, etc.).
Salary Range:
- $50,000 - $65,000
Worker Type:
Student (Fixed Term) (Trainee)

JOB DESCRIPTION

As a Member of Technical Staff (Research) at Trajectory, you will design and build the post‑training stack that lets our customers’ models continually learn from real production workflows. You will own end‑to‑end experiments across data, training, and evaluation: shaping telemetry into learnable signals, training and serving custom LLMs and agents, and designing novel algorithms. You’ll work directly with the founders and design partners, make foundational technical and product decisions, and help define both the culture and architecture of a company whose core mission is to enable continually learning intelligence.




REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience training or serving large language models

 - Experience building RL environments or evaluation suites for LLMs

 - Proficiency in PyTorch, JAX, or similar ML frameworks

 - Strong experimental design skills

 - Master’s / research experience




PREFERRED

 - Background in pre- or post-training RL for LLMs

 - Experience with high-performance computing or large-scale clusters

 - Contributions to open-source ML research or infrastructure

 - Demonstrated technical creativity (research, OSS, side projects)

 - PhD (last year of PhD), working on AI / RL open source projects




ABOUT TRAJECTORY

Trajectory is a research and product lab creating the platform for continual learning.

AI is the most capable software ever built, and the least able to learn. Every valuable correction and edit that happens in a product evaporates at the next session. A few teams have closed this gap by hand-coupling their models to their products: Composer, Claude Code, Windsurf SWE-1.

Trajectory is the first scalable approach for every company: our platform unlocks the signal already sitting in product use, so companies can continuously post-train large-scale agentic models that outperform the frontier. Working with leading AI companies, including Decagon, Clay, Harvey, Mercor, and Rogo.

Founded by researchers from Deepmind, OpenAI, Meta, Apple, Amazon, and Scale. $15M led by Conviction, with Fei-Fei Li, Jeff Dean, and founders of Notion, Braintrust, Modal, Hugging Face, and Dropbox.

At Rhoda AI, we’re building the next generation of generalist intelligent robots. We own the full robotics stack from high-performance hardware and robot systems to the infrastructure and state-of-the-art foundation world models that control our robots. Our robots are designed to be generalists capable of operating in complex, real-world environments and handling long-tail edge cases, made possible by our cutting edge research and end-to-end system design. We've raised over $450M and are investing aggressively in model research, infrastructure, hardware development, and manufacturing scale-up to make generalist robotics a reality.

Level: Internship or co-op, MS students; 4–6 months duration - starting as soon as possible

You’ll help decide how our robots see. Our robots work around people in real warehouses, and every sensor has conditions that defeat it: bright sunlight, shiny floors, glass, dust, heat. Your experiments will tell us which settings to ship, where each sensor breaks and why, and what we should do about it. You’ll work directly with our perception and hardware engineers, and your findings go straight into sensor choices, settings and the requirements our detection algorithms are built against. This is a hands-on internship for someone who understands optical physics and wants to see their work running on real robots.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Design experiments that answer real engineering questions, such as which sensor settings work best for each job, and whether a sensor still sees a person in direct sunlight

 - Explain why a sensor fails, from the physics up: ambient light, dynamic range, multipath, reflectance, angle of incidence, heat

 - Propose and test what to do about each failure: a different setting, a filter, a mounting change, or a check the software can run

 - Build the scenes, targets and scenarios that reproduce real-world conditions in the lab, and in the field when the lab isn’t enough

 - Use sensor SDKs and firmware to sweep and tune settings such as exposure, gain, frame rate, range modes and filtering

 - Write Python to process images and point clouds and turn raw data into clear numbers: range, accuracy, noise, dropout

 - Present findings and recommendations to engineers who will act on them


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Pursuing an MS in Optics, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Computer Vision or Robotics, with research or lab experience designing experiments

 - Strong grasp of optical sensing physics: image formation, noise, dynamic range, time-of-flight and LiDAR principles

 - Hands-on with cameras, LiDAR, time-of-flight or other optical sensors in a lab or on a robot

 - Comfortable with sensor SDKs, drivers and configuration

 - Python for numerical analysis and image or point-cloud processing (NumPy, OpenCV, Open3D or similar)

 - Curiosity to dig past “it doesn’t work” to the cause, and creativity in finding fixes

 - Explains results clearly, in writing and with plots, to people outside your specialty


NICE TO HAVE

 - Camera or sensor calibration

 - Thermal or infrared imaging

 - Optical modeling or sensor simulation

 - ROS 2 and recorded-data tools

At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before.

Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen.


ROLE OVERVIEW

REGENT is standing up two production lines for the first time — Squire and Viceroy — and that shift is opening up real, substantial work across our Electric Propulsion Unit (EPU) systems. As our EPU Intern, you'll sit inside the Electrical Systems team and work across the full arc of propulsion development: conceptualization, design, integration, and sustainment, across multiple platforms. You'll move fluidly between data analysis, electrical documentation, CAD, and hands-on test support, with direct exposure to motor performance evaluation, component-level testing, and on-water testing of the propulsion systems that move Seagliders through the water.

This isn't a role built around a narrow, pre-scoped task list. There's a meaningful amount of EPU work ahead of us on both Squire and Viceroy, and this internship exists to carve out a real piece of it for you to own — not to shadow, not to simulate, but to actually contribute to systems that will fly on REGENT's vehicles. You'll work alongside engineers who care about rigor as much as speed, and who'll expect you to bring your engineering fundamentals and build fast from there.

We're looking for someone who already has strong footing in electric machines, propulsion fundamentals, and CAD, and who's excited to apply that foundation to a fast-moving, dual-platform propulsion effort rather than a textbook problem set. If you want an internship where the scope is broad because the work is real, this is the seat for you.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own Real EPU Scope: You'll take on a defined piece of Electric Propulsion Unit work spanning both the Squire and Viceroy platforms, not a simulated side project. The work is real and waiting for someone to pick it up.

 - Evaluate Motor Performance: You'll dig into motor and drive data to characterize torque, speed, losses, and efficiency across operating conditions. This analysis directly informs decisions on both production lines.

 - Document Electrical Systems: You'll read and create schematics, wiring diagrams, and harness documentation for EPU hardware. This work unlocks your ability to interpret both vendor documentation and REGENT's own systems.

 - Build in CAD: You'll produce mechanical drawings and models in a 3D CAD environment, applying basic GD&T as you go. Your CAD work will directly support integration efforts across both platforms.

 - Support Test Campaigns: You'll get hands-on exposure to both component-level testing and on-water testing of propulsion hardware. By the midpoint of your term, you'll be comfortable with EPU layout and power distribution across current and future REGENT platforms.

 - Reduce and Interpret Data: You'll use Python, MATLAB, or Excel to process test data, build efficiency and performance models, and run mission-profile analyses. Much of the role runs through turning raw data into decisions.

 - Connect Propulsion to Power: You'll relate propeller or thruster performance — thrust, torque, advance ratio, efficiency — back to electrical input power. That connection sits at the core of how EPUs get designed and sustained here.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Engineering Fundamentals In Place: You're a rising senior or graduate student in mechanical, electrical, aerospace, or robotics engineering. These fundamentals are the foundation this role builds on from day one.

 - Motor and Drive Knowledge: You have working knowledge of electric machines, including BLDC/PMSM torque and speed constants, back-EMF, losses, and efficiency maps, along with motor controllers, ESCs, and basic power electronics.

 - Scripting and Data Chops: You're proficient in Python or MATLAB for processing test data and building performance models, with strong Excel skills for fast turnaround analysis. You're comfortable being the person who turns a pile of data into an answer.

 - Propulsion Fundamentals: You understand how propeller or thruster performance, including thrust, torque, advance ratio, and efficiency, relates to electrical input power. Coursework in fluid mechanics or marine or aero propulsion is a strong signal here.

 - CAD Fluency: You're proficient in a 3D CAD tool and can produce clear, accurate mechanical drawings, with a basic understanding of GD&T. That fluency will help you pick up REGENT's systems quickly.

 - Comfort With Electrical Documentation: You can read and create schematics, wiring diagrams, and harness documentation. That skill is what lets you move confidently through both vendor and REGENT engineering documentation.




WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision.

Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds.

You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat.

At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before.

Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen.


ROLE OVERVIEW

REGENT's mechanical team is in the middle of a defining stretch of work: carrying Squire, our production Seaglider, through a full design and release cycle, while simultaneously shaping Viceroy from early concept into preliminary design. As a Mechanical Engineering Co-Op, you'll be dropped right into both efforts — designing parts in CAD, producing drawings, and supporting release on a vehicle headed toward production, while also contributing iterative design work on a program that's still taking shape. This isn't an adjacent, watch-and-learn co-op experience; you'll be trusted with real parts, real drawings, and real ownership from day one.

You'll join Hardware Engineering's Mechanical team, helping take Squire from prototype to production. The fast-moving team values sound judgment in early design and disciplined production execution. If you have a foundation in mechanical design and assembly complexity and want ownership of flight hardware bound for the water, this role could shape your education or launch a career building Seagliders that will reinvent coastal transportation.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design and Release Squire Hardware: You'll design mechanical parts in CAD and carry them through release, stepping into a production cycle where your drawings become real hardware on REGENT's Seaglider platform. It's the kind of direct contribution that goes well beyond a typical co-op assignment.

 - Help Shape Viceroy From Concept Forward: You'll jump into Viceroy while it's still being defined, doing the iterative CAD work that shapes a vehicle's geometry before anything is locked in. Bring solid engineering instincts and your early ideas will hold up, not get reworked from scratch.

 - Draft With Precision: A large part of your time will go toward engineering drawings and tolerancing, turning design intent into documentation our team and manufacturing partners can actually build from. If you already have a good eye for drafting, this is where it gets put to work immediately.

 - Support Manufacturing and Integration: You'll work alongside technicians during build and integration, helping fit checks go smoothly and feeding what you learn on the floor straight back into your CAD models. It's a fast feedback loop that sharpens your design judgment quickly.

 - Own Systems End to End: You'll take a reasonably scoped project from concept through integration, with support from senior engineers, and build toward real ownership of at least one system on the vehicle. By the end, you'll have a portfolio of work that stands on its own, whether you're headed back to finish school or straight into a full-time role.


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Comfort Inside Complex Systems: Whether it came from an internship, a competition team, or a school project that got surprisingly real, you've worked inside assemblies where parts depend on each other. You're used to thinking several components deep instead of in isolation.

 - CAD as Second Nature: You're comfortable living in CAD day to day, not just opening it when a class requires it. Whatever your tool of choice, you pick up new CAD environments quickly.

 - An Eye for Drawings: You've spent real time with engineering drawings and tolerancing, enough to know that a good drawing is what keeps a part's design intent alive once it leaves your screen and heads to manufacturing.

 - Instincts That Hold Up: You have a working sense of load paths, material choices, and how manufacturing methods shape part design. That means your early ideas are something the team can build on, not something they have to rebuild.

 - Steady Under Ambiguity: You're not thrown off by incomplete information or a plan that's still taking shape. You can make a reasonable call, move forward, and adjust as new information comes in.

 - A Builder's Instinct: If you've spent time in a machine shop or messing around with rapid prototyping, you know the value of walking over, testing a quick fit, and bringing what you learn straight back into the model. That loop matters a lot while Viceroy is still taking shape.

 - Real Pull Toward Vehicles: You're genuinely into aerospace, marine, or vehicle programs, not just checking a box for your resume. You'll be helping shape hardware on a Seaglider headed toward production, and that should be exactly the kind of thing that gets you excited to show up.


WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision.

Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. wd:asml:j-00356203:
Introduction to the job
The DUV Reticle Stage IBS MDU team is responsible for engineering activities supporting the reticle stage, a precision mechatronic subsystem within ASML’s DUV lithography systems. Our mechatronics engineers use MATLAB-based analysis tools to evaluate system dynamics and performance using large sets of measurement data.
As our analysis needs evolve, these engineering tools need to evolve with them. Many have been developed and extended over time by different engineers, which means that understanding the existing methods often requires combining code investigation, technical documentation, and knowledge from experienced engineers. We are looking for a co-op student who is excited to work at the intersection of mechatronics, data analysis, signal processing, and software development .
Role and responsibilities
Your primary assignment will be to develop and improve MATLAB-based analysis tools for DUV Reticle Stage dynamic performance , with a particular focus on power spectral density (PSD) analysis and visualization .
You will work closely with experienced ASML mechatronics engineers to understand existing analysis methods, identify requirements, implement improvements, and validate the results against existing engineering analyses.
Your responsibilities will include:
- Develop and update MATLAB tools for analysis and visualization of Reticle Stage dynamic performance data, particularly PSD and frequency-domain analysis.
- Learn how existing analysis tools and methods work by reviewing MATLAB code, available documentation, and example datasets.
- Interview and collaborate with mechatronics engineers to gather requirements and uncover engineering knowledge that may not yet be fully documented.
- Translate engineering requirements into maintainable MATLAB functions, analysis workflows, and visualizations.
- Validate new or modified analysis methods against known datasets and existing engineering results.
- Investigate discrepancies and work with subject-matter experts to determine whether they originate from data processing, algorithms, assumptions, or implementation.
- Improve usability and documentation so future engineers can understand and confidently use the analysis tools.
- Participate in code reviews and incorporate feedback from the mechatronics engineering team.
This assignment offers the opportunity to work on a real precision-mechatronics system while gaining hands-on experience with engineering data analysis, signal processing, MATLAB development, and collaborative problem solving.
This position is located on-site in Wilton, CT. It requires onsite presence to attend in-person work-related events, trainings and meetings and to further ensure teamwork, collaboration and innovation. Must be available for 6 to 9 months
Education and experience
We are looking for a college junior or senior pursuing a bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Robotics, or a related engineering field , who is available for a 6-month co-op assignment .
To be successful in this role, you should have:
Technical skills
- Experience programming in MATLAB through coursework, projects, research, or previous internships/co-ops.
- Understanding of fundamental mechanical dynamics and vibrations .
- Familiarity with signal processing and frequency-domain analysis , such as Fourier transforms, frequency response, or power spectral density.
- Ability to work with experimental or measurement datasets and create clear engineering plots and visualizations.
- A structured approach to testing and validating computational results.
- Familiarity with Git, SVN, or another version-control system is beneficial but not required.
Personal skills
- Strong curiosity and willingness to dig into an unfamiliar technical problem.
- Comfortable approaching engineers, asking questions, and gathering information from multiple subject-matter experts.
- Able to take loosely documented requirements and turn them into a structured engineering solution.
- Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail, particularly when validating numerical results.
- Able to work independently while actively seeking feedback and collaborating with an engineering team.
- Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document technical work for future users.

wd:asml:j-00355336:
Introduction to the job
ASML US, including its affiliates and subsidiaries, bring together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon.
Founded in 1984, ASML is the world’s leading provider of lithography systems for the semiconductor industry, manufacturing complex machines that are critical to the production of integrated circuits or microchips. The mission of the Mechanical Development department is to design and develop the complex mechanics for these machines, which are some of the highest precision products ever produced in the world. This position is based on-site in Wilton, CT, which has both R&D and manufacturing operations. We design and produce multiple sub-system modules that are shipped to our headquarters in Veldhoven, The Netherlands where they are integrated into the full lithography machine.
Role and responsibilities
As a Summer Intern in Mechanical Design Engineering, you will participate in developing portions of the lithography system and/or associated tooling. You will work on sub-systems involving robotics, mechatronics, precision mechanics, and/or opto-mechanics. Precision machine design at ASML starts with understanding the functional requirements and deriving specifications. You will collaborate with design engineers and system architects in a multidiscipline project team to develop concepts, perform engineering analysis, build and test prototypes, generate detailed CAD designs, create engineering drawings, partner with suppliers, and support system integration and testing.
This position is located on-site in Wilton, CT. It requires onsite presence to attend in-person work-related events, trainings and meetings and to further ensure teamwork, collaboration and innovation. Must be available for 12 weeks for one of these sessions starting with the following dates: 6/2/2027 or 6/14/2027
Education and experience
Candidate towards a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD degree in Mechanical Engineering with minimum 2 years completed.
The hired candidate must have ability to communicate effectively in the English language both written and oral.
We are seeking an individual with a strong background in mechanical design and engineering. A background in mechanical design of mechatronics, precision design, or complex optical systems is desirable, as well as good complex mechanical system intuition.
Preferred skills for this job include:
- Mechanical design exposure to kinematics, dynamics, material properties and behavior, and structural analysis.
- Experience with 3D solid modelling for design conceptualization and realization.
- Basic experience with mechanical analytical techniques, including “first principle” engineering equations and Finite Element Analysis such as stress, strain, deformation, modal response, etc.
- Demonstrated ability to derive conclusions from analysis and make practical recommendations.
- Strong technical writing, communication and presentations skills.
Skills
Working at the cutting edge of tech, you’ll always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way do that. You won’t work in a silo. Instead, you’ll be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you’ll collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You’ll have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems.

- High energy self-motivated team player with strong desire to learn.

- Potential to develop into a technical leader in the organization.

▪ Execute ECN’s (Engineering Change Notices)

▪ Create and maintain product BOM’s & Routings in ERP software CSI9 (CloudSuite Industrial)

- Innovation Challenge

Johnson Controls invites you to apply for an internship opportunity located in Milwaukee, WI. This role is designed to provide a hands-on learning experience through meaningful work assignments and challenging objectives.
As part of our Milwaukee HVAC Branch, you will gain exposure to Controls Systems Engineering, Controls Installation, and System Commissioning while working alongside experienced technicians, project managers, and engineers.

- Work with experienced technicians, project managers, and engineers to support the specification, installation, and commissioning of new construction projects.

- Learn how to install, inspect, commission, and troubleshoot control systems.
- Generate controls and equipment submittals and support the approval process.

- Pursuing a degree in Mechanical Engineering, Construction Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

- Strong technical proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and other Microsoft Office applications.
- Strong organizational and communication skills.
- U.S. citizen or legal right to work in the U.S.
- Ability to adapt to changing priorities and shifting business needs.
- Strong initiative, persistence, and a desire to learn.
- Highly motivated and driven to succeed.
Preferred Qualifications
- Basic understanding of computer networking.
- Demonstrated problem-solving skills.
- Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment.
- Dedication to teamwork and collaboration.
Why Join Us
At Johnson Controls, you'll gain hands-on experience while working alongside industry professionals on real-world HVAC controls and building technology projects. You'll have the opportunity to develop technical skills, expand your professional network, and contribute to solutions that help create smarter, healthier, and more sustainable buildings.

Introduction to the job
ASML US, including its affiliates and subsidiaries, bring together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon.
Founded in 1984, ASML is the world’s leading provider of lithography systems for the semiconductor industry, manufacturing complex machines that are critical to the production of integrated circuits or microchips. The mission of the Mechanical Development department is to design and develop the complex mechanics for these machines, which are some of the highest precision products ever produced in the world. This position is based on-site in Wilton, CT, which has both R&D and manufacturing operations. We design and produce multiple sub-system modules that are shipped to our headquarters in Veldhoven, The Netherlands where they are integrated into the full lithography machine.

MorphLabs · New York City · 5-month internship, on-site · Rolling applications
About MorphLabs
MorphLabs is building non-invasive telekinesis: a brain interface that turns movement intent into action, starting with people underserved by existing technology.
We are starting with continuous, intuitive prosthetic control for upper-limb amputees, decoding movement intent from EEG in real time, without surgery or reliance on muscle sensors. We develop the hardware and models together, treating signal quality, learning and control as one problem. Prosthetics are where we start, not where we stop.
We are a small, scrappy, high-throughput team in NYC. We have raised a substantial pre-seed round, with our seed round underway, and we move quickly between research and building.
The role
Our headset has to fit many different heads, hold electrodes in steady contact with the scalp, stay comfortable through a full day, and look like something a person would choose to wear in public. It also has to work alongside a prosthetic hand. Every one of those is a design problem, and each one affects the signal our models learn from.
As a Design Intern, you'll spend five months on the physical design of that system, working directly with the founding team and our hardware engineers. You'll own a well-scoped project from first sketch to tested part, and be expected to ship something real: a headset revision we build, a fit or retention design we adopt, or a clear finding that changes what we try next.
Most of the work is industrial design: fit, materials and mechanisms, plus a hand in how the headset looks and feels, carried all the way through mechanisms and working prototypes. Some of it is product and interface design for the software people use to set up, calibrate and control the system.
This is not a side project. Interns work on the same hardware, participants and open problems as the rest of the team.
What you'll do
- Form and identity. Work with the founders on how the headset looks, feels and wears: proportions, materials, color and finish, so it reads as something people choose to wear, not a lab instrument.
- Fit and comfort. Design for a wide range of head shapes and sizes, keep it comfortable through a full day, and make it fast to put on and adjust.
- Electrode retention. Design mechanisms that keep electrodes in stable contact with the scalp, and work with the hardware team to measure how each change affects signal quality.
- Miniaturization and enclosures. Work with our electrical engineers to package smaller boards and batteries into enclosures that are lighter, sturdier and easier to service.
- Prosthetic integration. Design the mounts, housings and interfaces that connect our system to prosthetic and robotic hands.
- Prototyping and testing. Move quickly from sketch to CAD to physical parts, test them on real people, and let each result shape the next iteration.
- Design for manufacture. Prepare parts for production runs and document designs so they can be built the same way every time.
- Product and interface design. Help design the setup, calibration and control screens that participants and users interact with, so the system is clear to use for people with and without limb differences.
What you'll have
- Ownership. What you design goes into the headset we build and test, not a concept deck.
- Direct access to the founders. You'll work beside the people making the decisions, with no layers in between.
- Your designs on real heads, every day. We record new EEG daily, so your prototypes get worn and tested constantly.
- Our own hardware. We build our own headset, electrodes and amplifier, so no part of the system is off limits to redesign.
- An IRB already in place , covering both healthy participants and patients.
- The resources to do the work. Equipment and materials won't be the bottleneck.
Who we're looking for
We're hiring industrial designers who build: students, recent grads, or anyone whose portfolio shows physical products they designed and made themselves. We judge your work, not your school, degree or résumé. You don't need a background in neuroscience, BCI or prosthetics.
What we expect:
- A portfolio of physical products you designed and built yourself, with a clear account of what was yours
- Form you can defend: the proportions, materials and finishes you chose, and why
- Sketch to CAD to physical prototype, many times over, with each round changing because of what you learned
- Design work that had to fit the human body for hours: wearables, medical devices, protective or sports gear
- Enough mechanical sense to make your designs actually work: tolerances, materials, mechanisms and assembly
- Testing with real people, and design changes you made because of what you saw
- Speed: iterations in days, not weeks
What sets candidates apart:
- Experience with wearables, medical devices or consumer hardware
- Design for manufacturing experience, such as injection molding, machining or sheet metal
- Experience packaging electronics: enclosures, cable routing, battery and thermal constraints
- Product or interface design for software, especially for people with disabilities
- Experience with prosthetics, orthotics or assistive technology
- Work with soft goods, textiles or flexible materials
The bar is high on purpose. If your portfolio clears it, apply, whatever your background.
Logistics and Compensation
- Duration: 5 months, full-time
- Location: Onsite, New York City
- Compensation: $6500/Mo
- Start Date(s): December 1st or January 5th
- Rolling applications

Job Description
Envision spending time working with energetic colleagues and inspirational leaders, all while gaining world-class experience in one of the most dynamic organizations in the pharmaceutical industry. This is a reality for AbbVie’s Co-Op's.
Engineering supports and enables all functions throughout the facility by operating the building utilities and control systems, maintaining the entire facility, providing technical support, managing capital projects, qualifying systems, and providing drafting support.
Core Job Responsibilities & Deliverables
The Reliability Engineer Co-Op position reports to the Reliability Engineer or Reliability Manager and is responsible for:
- Utilizing our Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) to direct the strategy and execution of facility systems, predictive and preventive maintenance.
- Supporting the development, execution, and maintenance of the site, asset reliability program, and associated projects.

- Working closely with Project Engineering, Controls Engineering, Site Operations, and Maintenance to fulfill primary job responsibilities, and will regularly interface with site engineering management regarding the status of the Reliability program.
- Supporting Asset Maintenance Plan to ensure adequate levels of sustaining effective maintenance job plans and critical spare parts for each plant asset.
- Supporting Reliability Engineer as needed.

- Exposure to computerized maintenance management and business systems, including Maximo, SAP, and SharePoint

Mechanical Engineering Intern
- Position Description -
Position Overview: As a Mechanical Engineering Intern you’ll step into the world of automation innovation by supporting our skilled engineering team, including Project Managers, Controls Engineers, and Mechanical Design Engineers. You’ll contribute to the design, development, and testing of cutting-edge automation systems. This internship offers a hands-on introduction to CAD modeling, robotic systems, and manufacturing processes, providing a dynamic platform to apply your academic knowledge, develop technical skills, and launch your engineering career under expert mentorship.
Rotational Development Path:
- Rotation 1 – Foundations: Gain familiarity with SolidWorks, mechanical drawings, Axis standards, common purchased components, project release procedures, and documentation. Contribute to projects by creating basic drawings, completing documentation packages, and executing simple design tasks.
- Rotation 2 – Expansion: Execute more complex design tasks including detailing and revisions to existing tooling. Be able to create purchase requisitions and complete design release procedures in full. Assist in creating drawing packages for projects. Work with other departments to provide machine layouts, simulation files, controls component lists, and certification files.
- Rotation 3 – Application: Be able to complete drawing packages for full project scopes. Gain further understanding of principles of designing for machining, assembly, and maintenance. Support customer projects through revisions, simple assembly design, and completion of more complex drawing packages. Demonstrate increased design independence and meet assigned deadlines, while continuing to maintain design quality.
Key Responsibilities:
- Assist in creating 3D models and 2D technical drawings for automation components (e.g., fixtures, conveyors) using CAD software (SolidWorks preferred).
- Support the design of basic mechanical parts, such as brackets or mounts, under the guidance of senior engineers.
- Participate in prototype assembly, testing, and troubleshooting, gaining practical experience with robotic and automated systems.
- Help maintain engineering documentation, including Bills of Materials (BOMs) and design records, ensuring accuracy and organization.
- Conduct introductory tolerance analyses or component measurements to support design validation.
- Research industry standards (e.g., OSHA, ANSI) and material properties to assist project teams.
- Collaborate with engineers to brainstorm solutions and document findings for ongoing projects.
Qualifications:
- Education: Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s degree program in Mechanical Engineering or a related field (minimum 2 years completed preferred).
- Experience: No prior professional experience required; coursework, projects, or personal engineering pursuits a plus.
- Technical Skills:
- Basic familiarity with CAD software (e.g., SolidWorks, AutoCAD) from coursework or self-study.
- Introductory knowledge of mechanical principles, fasteners, or robotics concepts.
- Comfort with Microsoft Word and Excel for documentation and data tracking.
- Communication: Clear verbal and written skills, eager to learn and engage with a team.
- Problem-Solving: Curious, detail-oriented mindset with an aptitude for tackling technical challenges.
- Attributes: Enthusiastic, proactive, and adaptable, with a strong desire to grow in automation
- Teamwork: Be open to feedback and collaborate effectively with engineers and cross functional departments.
- Initiative: Show curiosity, take on small tasks proactively, and seek learning opportunities.
- Adaptability: Adjust quickly when project scopes or priorities shift.

JOIN CONTORO ROBOTICS – REVOLUTIONIZING WAREHOUSE AUTOMATION WITH CUTTING-EDGE ROBOTICS

At Contoro Robotics, we're on a mission to solve labor challenges through advanced robotic solutions. Headquartered in Austin, TX, our fast-growing startup is transforming the supply chain industry with our flagship warehouse automation technology. Our team is made up of top-tier experts in robotics, AI, and logistics, working together to push the boundaries of automation.

We’re looking for talented and ambitious individuals to join us on this journey—helping shape the future of robotics while growing alongside a world-class team. If you're passionate about innovation, problem-solving, and making a real-world impact, we want to hear from you!

Job Title: Robotics Engineer Intern - Test & Validation (Automation team)

Location: Austin, TX
About

Contoro Robotics is an Austin based startup focused on warehouse automation. We design a state-of-the-art autonomous truck unloading system capable of lifting boxes over 60 lbs. As a Test & Validation Intern, you'll be the person who runs our robots through structured test procedures and reports results that directly inform whether features ship to customer sites. You'll work closely with a senior test engineer who designs the tests and feature owners who triage failures, ensuring our Systems and Automation teams have fast, reliable feedback on every change they make. This is a hands-on role — you will be working with real robots, real boxes, and real test data every day.

In this role, you will:

 - Execute predefined test procedures across tiered test levels (from single-box handling to full simulated site conditions)

 - Record and report test results accurately, including logging failure modes, timestamps, and environmental conditions

 - Set up and tear down test environments per documented runbooks (conveyor configurations, box arrangements, sensor calibration checks)

 - Flag test failures and route them to feature owners with supporting data (logs, video, metrics)

 - Maintain test result dashboards so Systems, Automation, and Operations teams have real-time visibility into product readiness

 - Track regression by re-running previously passing tests after code or hardware changes

 - Assist the senior test engineer with test environment maintenance and instrumentation upkeep

 - Document any test setup issues or runbook gaps encountered during execution

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Are pursuing a degree in robotics, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, or a related field

 - Are detail-oriented and comfortable with repetitive, structured tasks that demand precision

 - Can clearly document and communicate what you observed versus what you expected

 - Have basic familiarity with Linux command line and can follow technical runbooks

 - Have exposure to ROS, sensor data, or robotic systems (preferred, not required)

 - Can work on-site at Contoro's office in Austin, TX for the duration of the internship

 - Are available throughout two continuous terms (e.g., Spring + Summer  Summer + Fall)

We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.
We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.
Job Description
AECOM is seeking a highly motivated Structural Engineering Intern for our transportation department in the Glen Allen, VA office. As an intern in the transportation department, you will assist in the design and inspection of various highway structures.
This position is expected to begin Summer 2027.
Internships at AECOM offer students in undergraduate and graduate programs the opportunity to gain valuable hands-on experience in engineering, design, and infrastructure projects that make a real-world impact. Interns work with cutting-edge technology, learn industry best practices, and collaborate with experienced professionals in a globally recognized firm. The program fosters both technical and professional skill development while providing networking opportunities that can enhance future career prospects. Additionally, AECOM’s dedication to innovation and sustainability enables interns to contribute to meaningful projects that help shape communities and the built environment.
The responsibilities of this position may include, but are not limited to:
- Perform assignments requiring application of standard techniques, procedures and criteria to carry out engineering tasks.
- Prepare engineering related calculations.
- Perform quantity takeoffs and cost estimates.
- Review shop drawings.
- Assist in the inspection of bridges, culverts, and tunnels.
- Prepare details for construction drawings using CAD software.
- Work under the supervision of a project manager or senior-level team member.
Qualifications
Minimum Requirements:
- Candidates must be pursuing a Bachelor’s Degree in Civil Engineering or in another related field and must have completed at least 1 year of study. Candidates who have graduated with a Bachelor’s Degree and plan to continue with the Master’s Degree are eligible to apply for these positions. Graduates must have been enrolled in their bachelor’s degree in the most previous school term with an interest in pursuing an advanced degree in the same or similar discipline at the conclusion of the internship.
Preferred Qualifications:
- Completed courses related to statics, strength of materials, introductory steel design, and introductory reinforced concrete design.
- Ability to follow procedures and pay attention to detail.
- Good written and oral communications skills.
- Familiarity with Microsoft Office and AutoCAD.
- Proficiency in developing calculations using software like Excel or Mathcad.
- Interest in bridge design is desired.
Additional Information
- Relocation assistance is not available for this position.
- Sponsorship for US employment authorization is not available now or in the future for this position.
- This position requires a hybrid work schedule which incudes in office work in Glen Allen, VA. The selected candidate must be available to work in Glen Allen, VA on a scheduled basis.

Build what most people think is impossible.
Hypersonica is building sovereign European hypersonic capability.
We are developing technologies that sit at the edge of what is currently possible, and we are doing it with small, talent dense teams of exceptional people.
Our culture takes inspiration from the operating philosophy behind Skunk Works. Small teams. Exceptional talent. High trust. Minimal bureaucracy. The freedom, tools and responsibility to solve problems that have not been solved before.
We are looking for interns who want to work in that environment.

The Opportunity
This is not an internship where you spend three months shadowing someone, preparing slides or waiting to be given something meaningful to do.
You will work alongside some of the best engineers and operators in Europe on real problems connected to real hardware and real programmes.
Depending on your background, that could mean contributing to areas such as:
- Engineering, propulsion, aerodynamics, structures, materials, avionics, GNC, software, electronics, manufacturing, test, quality, simulation, data or operations.
The exact problem matters less than how you approach it.
You will be given responsibility early, expected to think independently and encouraged to challenge assumptions.
If you see a better way of doing something, we want to hear it.
Who we are looking for
We are not simply looking for the highest grades. We are looking for people with exceptional potential. People who are deeply curious. People who ask why something has to be done a certain way. People who are not restricted by what they already know, what has been done before, or what others believe to be possible.
You might be a great fit if:
- You learn extraordinarily quickly.
- You enjoy solving difficult problems with incomplete information.
- You naturally break problems down to first principles.
- You build things because you are curious about whether they can be built.
- You are comfortable being wrong, learning quickly and trying again.
- You care deeply about the quality of your work.
- You want feedback and are equally comfortable giving it.
- You can communicate clearly with people very different from yourself.
- You want responsibility rather than supervision.
- You would rather create something than inherit a finished system.
What we value
- Mission alignment.
- Exceptional subject matter ability.
- The ability to execute in ambiguity.
- A builder mindset.
- A willingness to be on site, close to the hardware and the people building it.
- We believe in radical candour. High performing people should be able to challenge one another, give direct feedback and change their minds when the evidence demands it.
- We also believe that the strongest teams are built from different perspectives, backgrounds and ways of thinking.
What you will get
- The chance to work on technology that very few people in the world ever get close to.
- Direct exposure to exceptional engineers and technical leaders.
- Real ownership.
- Real hardware.
- Real problems.
- A very steep learning curve.
- And, if you are exceptional, the opportunity to build a career with us after university.
Who should apply
We are interested in outstanding students from leading universities across the Germany and Europe, including Oxford, Cambridge, TUM, LMU and others, however:
- Your university matters less than your ability.
- Your degree matters less than what you can do with it.
- Your experience matters less than how quickly you can learn.
- We are particularly interested in people who can point to something they have built, researched, competed in, broken, redesigned, coded, tested or taught themselves simply because they wanted to understand whether it could be done.
Security and Eligibility Requirement
Due to the nature of the work we undertake, applicants must be a EU/Nato/German citizen, and be eligible for German Security Clearance.
One final thing
If you are looking for a comfortable internship with a clearly defined playbook, Hypersonica probably is not for you.
If you want to spend your internship surrounded by exceptional people trying to build technology years ahead of where most believe it should be possible, we would like to hear from you.
Come and build something that does not yet exist.

About Us

Reframe Systems is a Physical AI and robotics company on a mission to make high-performance housing attainable and abundant in the communities where people want to live. Through our vertically integrated delivery model and highly automated microfactories, we deliver climate-resilient homes and buildings with greater speed and predictability than traditional construction.

Our volumetric modular buildings are produced in our Andover, MA microfactory, with a growing pipeline across North America and a new microfactory on the way. We are building a system that balances repeatability with site-responsive design, enabling homes adaptable to each site, community, and customer need. Our cross-disciplinary team brings together architecture, robotics, design engineering, software, factory operations, and field delivery to change how housing gets delivered.

We're reimagining the future of housing through a smarter and more sustainable system that empowers people to live better. Come build it with us.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for a Mechanical Engineering Co-op to join our team at FAB1, our first full-scale microfactory in Billerica, MA, this fall. This role is built for someone who loves the full loop of engineering: sketch it, model it, build it, test it, and fix it — fast. You'll rotate across active projects on our Mechanical Engineering team, working alongside engineers designing the workcells, fixturing, and production infrastructure that make our factory run.

This is a hands-on role. You'll spend real time in the shop — cutting, welding, printing, and machining your own parts — not just handing drawings off to someone else. We move quickly here, so we need someone who can take a rough idea, iterate on it in CAD, get a physical version in hand, and improve it based on what they learn, on a tight timeline.

What You'll Do

 - Design and Iterate Fast: Take on real mechanical design problems across FAB1 projects — fixtures, workstations, material handling, tooling — and move quickly from concept to CAD to working prototype.

 - Build What You Design: Fabricate and assemble your own prototypes and production hardware using mills, lathes, laser cutters, welders, 3D printers, and standard shop tools.

 - Rotate Across Projects: Work across multiple active workstreams on the ME team rather than a single fixed project, picking up context quickly and contributing wherever the team needs hands and ideas.

 - Test and Improve: Validate your designs on the shop floor, troubleshoot what doesn't work, and iterate toward a production-ready result.

 - Support Documentation: Produce clear CAD models and basic technical drawings that a teammate or vendor could build from.

 - Learn the Full Stack: Get exposure to how mechanical design connects to robotics, automation, and factory operations in a live manufacturing environment.

Qualifications

 - Currently pursuing a BS in Mechanical Engineering or a related field; junior or senior standing preferred.

 - Solid CAD skills (Onshape, SolidWorks, Fusion 360, or similar) and the ability to go from a rough idea to a modeled part quickly.

 - Comfortable and safe operating shop tools and equipment — mills, lathes, laser cutters, welding, 3D printing, hand and power tools.

 - A fast learner who can pick up new tools, processes, and project context with minimal ramp-up.

 - Bias toward action: you'd rather build a rough prototype and learn from it than perfect a design on paper.

 - Strong communicator who works well within a team and can take direction from multiple engineers across rotating projects.

 - Available for a full-time, semester-length co-op in Billerica, MA this fall.

Nice to Have

 - Prior shop, machine design, or robotics club/competition experience (FSAE, FRC, Baja SAE, etc.).

 - Experience with sheet metal, weldments, or basic structural design.

 - Exposure to manufacturing, construction, or factory automation environments.

 - Familiarity with GD&T fundamentals.
