wd:neogen:req-11230:
Come Be Part of a Mission that Matters!
Engineering Equipment & Metrology Internship
Location: Lexington, KY
Type: Onsite
This is more than just an internship. It’s an opportunity to turn engineering knowledge into hands-on experience and make a measurable impact on manufacturing operations.
At Neogen , we believe in developing the next generation of innovative thinkers, problem-solvers, and industry leaders. Our internship program offers meaningful, hands-on experience where you'll have the opportunity to apply your classroom knowledge, collaborate with experienced professionals, and contribute to projects that support our global operations.
The Opportunity
As an Engineering Equipment & Metrology Intern , you'll gain valuable, real-world experience in manufacturing engineering, equipment troubleshooting, metrology, calibration, and continuous improvement while working alongside Neogen's experienced Engineering team. This is an exciting opportunity to see how engineering principles, technical problem-solving, and precision measurement come together to support reliable manufacturing operations. You'll play an active role in several meaningful engineering initiatives, including the rehabilitation and testing of existing equipment, support for new manufacturing technology, improvements to metrology and calibration processes, and workplace organization initiatives.
From helping restore equipment performance and executing structured tests to improving asset documentation and implementing practical shop-floor solutions, your contributions will help strengthen equipment readiness, operational efficiency, and engineering processes. Throughout your internship, you'll receive hands-on mentorship and guidance while developing the technical, analytical, and professional skills needed to succeed in engineering, manufacturing, equipment reliability, or quality-related careers.
What You'll Do
- Bring Equipment Back to Peak Performance: Support the rehabilitation and operational readiness of Neogen's existing CS01 machine, assisting with troubleshooting, equipment assessments, and testing to help confirm proper functionality.
- Gain Hands-On Equipment Testing Experience: Assist with developing and executing approved testing protocols, documenting results, and maintaining accurate technical records for the CS01 equipment.
- Support New Manufacturing Technology: Collaborate with Engineering professionals on the new MFT machine, contributing to equipment observations, testing activities, issue tracking, and technical documentation.
- Drive Shop-Floor Improvements: Apply 5S workplace organization principles to identify and implement practical improvements that enhance organization, efficiency, safety, and standardization within the manufacturing environment.
- Explore Metrology & Calibration: Help review equipment asset information and support improvements to metrology and calibration processes, gaining insight into how accurate measurements contribute to manufacturing quality and reliability.
- Strengthen Asset Management: Assist with reviewing and improving asset records within ACE, supporting more consistent documentation, equipment tracking, and periodic review practices.
- Apply Engineering Problem-Solving: Investigate equipment-related challenges, analyze available information, and collaborate with Engineering professionals to identify practical improvement opportunities.
- Develop Sustainable Standards: Create and update technical documentation, visual workplace standards, testing records, and process resources that support consistency and long-term improvements.
- Collaborate Across Teams: Work alongside engineers, technicians, manufacturing associates, and other cross-functional partners to better understand how equipment performance and engineering decisions impact daily operations.
- Measure and Communicate Results: Track project progress, document findings, and share technical recommendations and next steps with Engineering leadership.
All equipment testing, troubleshooting, and improvement activities will be performed under appropriate Engineering supervision and in accordance with established safety and quality procedures.
What You'll Gain
At Neogen, we believe the best learning happens through experience. Throughout your internship, you'll have the opportunity to:
- Gain hands-on experience working with manufacturing equipment and real-world engineering projects in an active production environment.
- Learn how engineers assess equipment performance, troubleshoot technical challenges, and support equipment rehabilitation and operational readiness.
- Develop practical experience in equipment testing, test protocol execution, technical documentation, and results analysis.
- Gain exposure to new manufacturing equipment and understand how Engineering teams support equipment evaluation, testing, and implementation.
- Explore the fundamentals of metrology, calibration, and precision measurement , including their importance in maintaining reliable manufacturing processes.
- Learn how equipment asset information, calibration records, and periodic review practices support quality and operational consistency.
- Apply 5S and continuous improvement principles to create more organized, efficient, and sustainable manufacturing workspaces.
- Strengthen your ability to interpret technical information, organize engineering data, and communicate findings.
- Develop experience coordinating multiple engineering assignments, prioritizing activities, and collaborating with cross-functional teams.
- Build confidence in technical problem-solving, professional communication, and presenting recommendations to Engineering leadership.
Your Final Project: At the conclusion of your internship, you'll have the opportunity to present your accomplishments to Engineering and site leadership, highlighting equipment testing and readiness, metrology and calibration improvements, completed 5S initiatives, and recommendations for continued progress.
What We're Looking For
Education
Currently pursuing a degree in one of the following fields or a related technical discipline:
- Mechanical Engineering
- Electrical Engineering
- Manufacturing Engineering
- Industrial Engineering
- Mechatronics
- A comparable engineering or technical field
Relevant coursework in Machine Design, Manufacturing Processes, Instrumentation, Controls, Statistics, Quality, or Project Management is preferred.
Technical Skills
- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Word for organizing data, documenting findings, and preparing technical reports.
- Foundational understanding of engineering principles, mechanical or electrical systems, or manufacturing equipment.
- Basic data analysis skills and the ability to interpret technical information.
- Ability to read technical documents, equipment instructions, or engineering specifications.
- Interest in equipment troubleshooting, testing, metrology, calibration, or manufacturing process improvements.
- Willingness to learn how to develop and maintain clear, accurate testing protocols and equipment records.
- Familiarity with manufacturing equipment, measurement tools, or quality systems is beneficial but not required.
- Ability to follow established safety procedures and work effectively in an active manufacturing environment.
Skills That Will Help You Succeed
- A hands-on, curious mindset and enthusiasm for understanding how equipment and manufacturing systems operate.
- Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving abilities.
- Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to producing accurate, reliable results.
- A proactive, self-motivated approach with a willingness to take ownership of meaningful work.
- Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple projects and priorities.
- Effective written and verbal communication skills.
- Confidence collaborating with engineers, technicians, manufacturing associates, and cross-functional teams.
- Adaptability and a willingness to spend time on the manufacturing floor learning directly from equipment and operations.
- Openness to coaching, constructive feedback, and continuous learning.
- A strong commitment to safety, quality, accountability, and continuous improvement.
What Success Looks Like
By the end of your internship, you'll have contributed to advancing meaningful engineering initiatives while developing valuable technical and professional skills that will support your future career in engineering, manufacturing, equipment reliability, or metrology.
Success will be demonstrated through:
- Improved Equipment Readiness: Support for successful rehabilitation and verification of the CS01 machine's intended operation through defined testing, with protocols, results, and equipment status clearly documented.
- Meaningful New Equipment Support: Completion of assigned MFT machine support activities, including equipment observations, testing documentation, issue tracking, and technical records.
- Sustainable Workplace Improvements: Implementation of selected 5S initiatives with documented visual standards and clear practices to help maintain improvements.
- Stronger Asset Management: Improved accuracy, organization, and usability of ACE asset information supporting metrology and calibration equipment.
- Enhanced Metrology & Calibration Processes: Contributions to a more consistent and effective periodic review process for measurement and calibration-related assets.
- Actionable Engineering Recommendations: Development of practical improvement recommendations, documented findings, and a clear list of remaining actions for continued Engineering follow-up.
- Professional Growth: Demonstrated development in equipment troubleshooting, technical documentation, engineering analysis, project coordination, and cross-functional collaboration.
Throughout the internship, progress will be supported through regular mentor check-ins, ongoing coaching, and established project milestones.
Your Final Presentation
At the conclusion of your internship, you'll showcase your work and the impact of your contributions through a presentation to Neogen's Engineering and site leadership teams.
Your presentation will highlight:
- Project Overview: A review of the engineering initiatives supported throughout the internship, including equipment readiness, testing, metrology, calibration, and workplace organization objectives.
- Equipment Rehabilitation & Testing: An overview of the CS01 machine's initial condition, rehabilitation activities, testing methods, documented results, and operational readiness.
- New Equipment Support: A summary of contributions to the MFT machine project, including testing activities, technical observations, documented findings, and outstanding items.
- Metrology & Calibration Improvements: An explanation of improvements to ACE asset records, periodic review practices, and supporting documentation.
- 5S & Continuous Improvement Results: A demonstration of completed shop-floor improvements, including before-and-after observations, visual standards, and methods for sustaining progress.

You'll also have the opportunity to answer questions, discuss lessons learned, and demonstrate the technical and professional skills developed throughout your internship.

Come Be Part of a Mission that Matters!
Manufacturing Intern – Sample Collection Solution Prep Optimization
This is more than just an internship. It’s an opportunity to turn scientific knowledge into real-world solutions and make a meaningful impact on manufacturing operations.
At Neogen , we believe in developing the next generation of innovative thinkers, problem-solvers, and industry leaders. Our internship program offers meaningful, hands-on experience where you'll have the opportunity to apply your classroom knowledge, collaborate with experienced professionals, and contribute to projects that support our global operations.
The Opportunity
As a Manufacturing Intern – Process Optimization & Quality Improvement , you'll gain valuable, real-world experience in manufacturing operations, process improvement, data analysis, and quality systems while working alongside Neogen's experienced Manufacturing, Quality, and Engineering teams.
This is an exciting opportunity to see how science, data, and continuous improvement come together to strengthen manufacturing processes and product quality. You'll play an active role in a meaningful improvement project within Neogen's Solution Preparation (SOLP) operations , helping identify opportunities to improve process consistency, optimize solution usage, reduce material waste, and enhance equipment performance.
From analyzing production data and observing manufacturing processes to developing visual work standards and evaluating pH measurement technology, your contributions will help support more consistent operations, better decision-making, and sustainable improvements.
Throughout your internship, you'll receive hands-on mentorship and guidance while developing the technical, analytical, and professional skills needed to succeed in manufacturing, chemical engineering, quality, or process improvement careers.
What You'll Do
- Drive Meaningful Process Improvements: Partner with Manufacturing, Quality, and Engineering professionals to support a focused improvement project within Neogen's Solution Preparation (SOLP) operations.
- Turn Data into Actionable Insights: Collect, organize, and analyze historical batch-record data, including pH measurements, adjustment quantities, repeat adjustments, and other process observations to identify trends and opportunities for improvement.
- Improve Process Consistency: Evaluate historical production results and help develop practical, standardized solution-adjustment guidance that supports greater consistency and efficiency, subject to Manufacturing and Quality review and approval.
- Bring Visual Standards to Life: Observe solution preparation activities, document expected solution appearances, and capture controlled photographs to support clear, user-friendly visual standards within standard operating procedures (SOPs).
- Explore Inventory & Waste Reduction: Analyze production demand, solution batch sizes, preparation schedules, expiration dates, usage patterns, and remaining or discarded materials to identify opportunities to optimize planning and reduce avoidable scrap.
- Evaluate Manufacturing Technology: Research and compare pH meters and probes based on measurement suitability, reliability, ease of use, cleaning and storage requirements, and total cost to develop informed equipment recommendations.
- Support Equipment Testing: Assist with planning and executing an approved trial of a recommended pH meter or probe, when feasible, documenting results, performance observations, and implementation considerations.
- Strengthen Standard Work: Help develop and improve technical documentation, visual work instructions, and process guidance that support consistent manufacturing practices.
- Collaborate Across Teams: Work alongside manufacturing operators, production leads, Quality professionals, and engineers to understand process challenges and develop practical solutions.
- Measure and Communicate Results: Track project progress, summarize findings, and share data-driven recommendations with Manufacturing leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.
All testing, documentation changes, and process improvement activities will be conducted under appropriate supervision and in accordance with established safety, quality, and change-control procedures.
What You'll Gain
At Neogen, we believe the best learning happens through experience. Throughout your internship, you'll have the opportunity to:
- Gain hands-on experience working within a regulated manufacturing environment and learning how solution preparation processes support product quality and consistency.
- Develop practical experience analyzing manufacturing batch records, pH measurements, and process performance data.
- Strengthen your ability to identify trends, evaluate variability, and apply structured problem-solving to real-world manufacturing challenges.
- Learn how scientific principles and data analysis contribute to process optimization and improved manufacturing efficiency.
- Gain exposure to standard operating procedure (SOP) development , visual work standards, controlled documentation, and cross-functional approval processes.
- Explore material planning, solution usage, expiration management, and waste-reduction opportunities within manufacturing operations.
- Learn how manufacturing equipment is evaluated for technical performance, reliability, usability, and operational suitability.
- Develop experience supporting controlled equipment trials, documenting test results, and preparing technical recommendations.
- Understand how Manufacturing, Quality, and Engineering teams collaborate to evaluate and implement process improvements.
- Build confidence in technical communication, project ownership, and presenting data-driven recommendations to leadership.
- Gain valuable insight into career opportunities in manufacturing, chemical engineering, process engineering, quality, and continuous improvement.
Your Final Project: At the conclusion of your internship, you'll have the opportunity to present your accomplishments to Manufacturing, Quality, Engineering, and site leadership, highlighting your process analysis, proposed documentation improvements, solution-usage recommendations, pH equipment evaluation, and opportunities for continued operational improvement.
What We're Looking For
Education
Currently pursuing a degree in one of the following fields or a related scientific or engineering discipline:
- Chemical Engineering
- Chemistry
- Biochemistry
- Industrial Engineering
- Manufacturing Engineering
- A comparable science or engineering field
Relevant coursework in General Chemistry, Analytical Chemistry, Statistics, Data Analysis, Process Engineering, Quality Systems, or Manufacturing is preferred.

T-Mobile is synonymous with innovation–and you could be part of the team that disrupted an entire industry! We reinvented customer service, brought real 5G to the nation, and now we’re shaping the future of technology in wireless and beyond. Our work is as exciting as it is rewarding, so consider the career opportunity below as your invitation to grow with us, make big things happen with us, above all, #BEYOU with us. Together, we won’t stop!
Get hands-on experience, training—and a leg up on a bright future.
T-Mobile didn’t become a leader by following the playbook. We got here by breaking it. We’re a disruptor that now plays on a higher tier, and we’re still raising the bar for millions of customers nationwide. If you want to work somewhere that sets the standard instead of matching it, this is your place.
This is an 11-week paid learning experience where you’ll do real work, not busywork. You’ll build relationships with other interns and leaders across the company, and you’ll be paired with mentors who will challenge you to grow skills that matter. We’ll give you hands-on projects with real stakes, and we expect your creativity and sharp ideas to make an immediate impact. You’ll work alongside T-Mobile employees who have your back and who still believe the best ideas can come from anyone.
What It’s Like
You’ll join the team responsible for execution performance across T-Mobile’s Reverse Logistics Return Centers. We’re small enough that you’ll be seen and heard, and big enough that your work matters. The pace is fast: at over 1M devices a month, this is a high-velocity operation. You’ll sit onsite at the return center alongside our TMO Operations and Supplier Operations teams. A typical week mixes time on the floor with the people doing the work, analysis of live process data, and working sessions to share what you’re finding.
What You’ll Do
You’ll evaluate real processes inside the return center and recommend changes that make them faster, leaner, and more accurate. Every device that comes through needs the right routing and disposition decision, so small improvements add up to real dollar and customer impact. Your work will help T-Mobile get devices back to retail and customers faster, keeping us ahead.
Key Responsibilities
- Evaluate targeted return center processes, including handoffs between processes, to find efficiency opportunities
- Analyze the inventory pipeline and aging to identify where devices stall and why
- Map device touchpoints and measure dwell time to expose delays and waste
- Conduct process time studies on the floor to establish baselines and standard work
- Quantify the impact of improvement ideas on required labor, velocity, cycle time, and inventory levels
- Translate data and findings into clear recommendations for operations leaders and non-technical audiences
- Partner with TMO and Supplier Operations teams to test, refine, and drive adoption of changes
What It Takes
- You’re curious and challenge assumptions. You ask why a process works the way it does, and whether it needs to.
- You move with urgency and are comfortable in a high-volume, fast-moving environment.
- You use analytical thinking to solve problems, and you explain your findings in plain language.
- You collaborate well and earn trust with cross-functional teams, including the people on the floor.
- Familiarity with Lean, Six Sigma (Green Belt), Kaizen, 5S, DMAIC, value stream mapping, time and motion studies, and root cause analysis is a plus.
- Certifications or credentials, completed or in progress, are a plus: Lean Six Sigma Yellow or Green Belt, IISE Lean, APICS/ASCM (CSCP, CPIM), or data analytics skills (Tableau, Power BI, SQL, Python).
Minimum Qualifications
- At least 18 years of age
- Legally authorized to work in the United States now and in the future
- Must have one or more course(s) remaining in a Bachelors or Graduate degree program post internship
- Employees of T-Mobile or Metro by T-Mobile are ineligible for external Summer Internships, please see Magenta Accelerator if interested
Never stop growing!
As part of the T-Mobile team, you know the Un-carrier doesn’t have a corporate ladder–it’s more like a jungle gym of possibilities! We love helping our employees grow in their careers, because it’s that shared drive to aim high that drives our business and our culture forward. By applying for this career opportunity, you’re living our values while investing in your career growth–and we applaud it. You’re unstoppable!

Job Description
At WSFS Bank we empower our Associates to grow their careers, we guide our Clients to secure their financial futures, and we actively support our Communities so they can fully thrive. Careers with WSFS Bank offer an inclusive and supportive culture, competitive salary, opportunities to advance, and more. We are the premiere, locally headquartered bank and wealth management company in the region and are honored to consistently be named a Top Workplace by our Associates, who make a difference every day for the people, businesses, and Communities we serve. We Stand For Service® is more than part of our name, it’s our mission and our purpose.
We are seeking ambitious, high-performing College students with a strong interest in pursuing a career in financial services to join the WSFS Bank 2027 Summer Internship Program. This paid, 10-week internship provides a dynamic and engaging experience featuring meaningful project work, one-on-one mentorship, executive exposure, professional development opportunities, volunteer initiatives, networking events, and collaboration with fellow interns.
Interns will gain valuable hands-on experience while working alongside industry professionals and contributing to real business initiatives across a variety of bank departments. This is an exciting opportunity to build your skills, expand your professional network, and explore rewarding career paths with one of the region’s leading financial institutions.
DT Process Engineering & Automation - Assist with process improvement initiatives by partnering with project leads to identify efficiencies, assessing automation opportunities, and support business process discovery and research using Six Sigma methodologies. Analyze and interpret data using Excel and Power BI to provide insights, track performance, and support decision-making. Participate in team and project meetings, provide status updates, and gain hands-on experience developing low-code applications and automation solutions with Microsoft technologies, including Power Automate, while building knowledge of banking operations and process improvement practices.
What Our Internships Offer :
- Work alongside professionals across multiple business lines and gain exposure to real-world projects, operations, and strategic decision-making.
- Follow a comprehensive learning program that includes personal and professional development activities and resources.
- Opportunity to support and present on projects, research, or operational activities within an assigned business area to Senior Leaders.
- Build meaningful connections through dedicated mentorship and collaboration with peers and experienced professionals.
- Engage with leaders across the organization through networking events, panel discussions, and career-focused conversations.
- Participate in volunteer initiatives, employee resource groups, and social exclusive events designed to foster connection and professional growth.
- High-performing interns may be considered for continued employment opportunities with WSFS Bank upon successful completion of the program.
Minimum Qualifications :
- Must be at least 18 years of age.
- Pursuing an undergraduate degree with the intention to return to your studies following the internship experience.
- Must have completed a minimum of one (1) full year of college by May 2027.
- A business-related or related college major is preferred.
- Must be able to participate in this full-time position (40 hours per week) within a continuous program, starting first week of June and ending early to mid-August.
- Must be available for in-person and virtual interviews.
- Must be available for in person orientation with Human Resources.
- Ability to work up to 5 days on-site at a physical office location within the WSFS Bank footprint.
- Must have reliable transportation.
- Fundamental computer proficiency, including Microsoft Office, is required.
- Excellent oral and written communication is required.
- Must have critical thinking and analytical skills.
- Must have organizational skills and proven ability to work independently and collaboratively.
WSFS Bank will only consider candidates who are presently authorized to work for any employer in the United States and who will not require work visa sponsorship from WSFS Bank now or in the future in order to retain their authorization to work in the United States.
Salary Range:
$18.00 - $21.00 Per Hour
Individual base pay may vary on additional factors such as the candidate’s experience, job-related skills, relevant education, geographic location, and other specific business and organizational needs.
In addition to base salary, WSFS Financial Corporation (WSFS) and its subsidiaries may offer eligible Associates discretionary and formula-based incentive and retention awards. WSFS provides a competitive benefits package, which includes medical, dental, and vision coverage; a 401(k) plan; life, accident, and disability insurance; flexible spending accounts (FSAs) and health savings accounts (HSAs); and wellness programs. Additional benefits may include paid parental leave, military leave, vacation and other paid time off, sick leave in accordance with applicable state laws, and paid holidays. Benefit offerings are subject to eligibility requirements, legal limitations, and may vary based on an Associate’s location and employment status. For more information about Associate benefits, please visit https://www.wsfsbank.com/about/careers/
WSFS Bank is inclusive and supportive of individual needs. If you have a physical or other impairment that might require an accommodation, including technical assistance with the WSFS Bank Careers website or submission process, please contact us via email at careers@wsfsbank.com.

Company Description
Work with Us. Change the World.
At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.
There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.
We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.
Job Description
AECOM is hosting an exclusive, invitation-only hiring event in Arlington on November 18-19, 2026. This is a great opportunity to learn and connect with AECOM for career opportunities starting Spring/Summer 2027.
The event kicks off on Wednesday evening with a networking mixer from 6-8 pm, where you can hear from AECOM staff about various projects, career paths, and the company itself. You’ll also have the chance to meet other students, recent graduates, and AECOM professionals from across our business lines.
On Thursday, interviews will take place at our Arlington office. This is a fantastic opportunity to learn about and connect with AECOM for early career opportunities.
AECOM is seeking a highly motivated Structural Engineering Intern for our transportation department in the Hunt Valley, MD office. As an intern in the transportation department, you will assist in the design and inspection of various highway structures.
This position is expected to begin Summer 2027.
Internships at AECOM offer students in undergraduate and graduate programs the opportunity to gain valuable hands-on experience in engineering, design, and infrastructure projects that make a real-world impact. Interns work with cutting-edge technology, learn industry best practices, and collaborate with experienced professionals in a globally recognized firm. The program fosters both technical and professional skill development while providing networking opportunities that can enhance future career prospects. Additionally, AECOM’s dedication to innovation and sustainability enables interns to contribute to meaningful projects that help shape communities and the built environment.
The responsibilities of this position may include, but are not limited to:
Job responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
- Perform assignments requiring application of standard techniques, procedures and criteria to carry out engineering tasks.
- Prepare engineering related calculations.
- Perform quantity takeoffs and cost estimates.
- Review shop drawings.
- Assist in the inspection of bridges, culverts, and tunnels.
- Prepare details for construction drawings using CAD software.
- Working under the supervision of a project manager or senior-level team member.
Qualifications
Minimum Requirements:
- Candidates must be pursuing a Bachelor’s Degree in Civil Engineering or another related field and must have completed at least 2 years of study. Candidates who have graduated with a Bachelor’s Degree and plan to continue with the Master’s Degree are also eligible to apply for these positions. Graduates must have been enrolled in their bachelor’s degree in the most previous school term with an interest in pursuing an advanced degree in the same or similar discipline at the conclusion of the internship.
Preferred Qualifications:
- Completed courses related to statics, strength of materials, introductory steel design, and introductory reinforced concrete design.
- Ability to follow procedures and pay attention to detail.
- Good written and oral communications skills.
- Familiarity with Microsoft Office and AutoCAD.
- Proficiency in developing calculations using software such as Excel or Mathcad.
- Interest in bridge design is desired.
Additional Information
- Relocation assistance is not available for this position.
- Sponsorship for US employment authorization is not available now or in the future for this position.
- This position requires a hybrid work schedule which includes in-office work in Hunt Valley, MD. The selected candidate must be available to work in Hunt Valley, MD on a scheduled basis.
At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.
About AECOM
AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options , well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.
AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.
What makes AECOM a great place to work
You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.
As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on LinkedIn, Facebook , Instagram , X and YouTube.
Job Description
Envision spending 6 months working with energetic colleagues and inspirational leaders, all while gaining world-class experience in one of the most dynamic organizations in the pharmaceutical industry. This is a reality for AbbVie AbbVie Co-Ops.
The Quality Assurance Validation department is responsible for plant validation including validated system (Equipment/Process), risk/design and change control compliance. Our team ensures alignment with Global Quality Systems for validation and related functions, e.g. engineering, risk management.
Key responsibilities include:
The Validation Engineering Co-Op will support the planning and execution of tasks reporting into the QA Validation department. This role will support various areas of manufacturing and/or Quality Control (QC) and interact heavily with our quality organization. Expectations of the role include:
- Execute task as required to implement the Validation Master Plan
- Participate with external engineering and QC departments on new installations, system modifications and decommissioning
- Draft and execute validation plans, and validation protocols in compliance with cGMP practices
- Ensures investigations of validation failures are completed thoroughly and documented accurately
Qualifications
Basic Qualifications
- Currently enrolled in university, pursuing a Bachelor’s in Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or Biomedical Engineering or other related field
- Must be enrolled in university for at least one semester following the co-op
- Expected graduation date between May 2028 – Dec 2028
- Organization, attention to detail, communication, self-starter, ability to ask questions, time management, etc.
- Experience working in Microsoft Suite, especially Excel, Word, PowerPoint
- Must be able to commit to a 6-month duration in-person at AbbVie Bioresearch Center (ABC) in Worcester, MA (July - December).
Preferred Qualifications
- Equipment-based or instrumentation / installation project exposure a plus

Competitive pay

We’re Watts. Together, we’re reimagining the future of water.
We feel proud every day about what we do. We're all part of the same crucial mission, no matter what function we support -- it's to provide safe, clean water for the world, and to protect our planet's most valuable resource.
What we do:
For 150 years, Watts has built best-in-class products that are trusted by customers in residential and commercial settings across the world. We are at the forefront of innovation, working with cutting-edge technology to provide smart and connected, sustainable water solutions for the future. Watts is a leading brand with a quality reputation — and we have a dynamic future ahead.​
The Watts Internship Program is your chance to bring what you’ve learned in the classroom to life! You’ll dive into real-world projects, gaining hands-on experience while learning how business really works from the inside. During the program, you’ll get to roll up your sleeves and make an impact on day-to-day operations. Plus, you'll have tons of opportunities to network with passionate professionals across manufacturing, industrial engineering, and more—sparking new ideas through cross-department collaboration. It’s all about expanding your skills, challenging yourself, and exploring where your ambitions can take you!
Scope of Position
This motivated and detail-oriented individual, as part of the Quality and Production Engineering Team, will support projects that improve production efficiency, optimize workflow, and support operational excellence. This role offers hands-on experience in a fast-paced manufacturing environment through collaboration with Production Engineers, cross-functional teams, and production operators.
This position reports to the Operations Manager. This role is onsite and is based in Fort Worth, TX.
Primary Job Duties and Responsibilities
- Support Production Engineers by contributing to project execution and daily operational tasks.
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including Purchasing, Sustaining Engineering, and Production Supervisors, to advance project goals.
- Design and develop fixturing and tooling solutions to enhance production cell efficiency.
- Create and revise factory floor layouts to optimize space utilization and workflow.
- Engage directly with production cells and operators on the factory floor to observe, learn, and support operations.
- Analyze cycle times for assemblies and unit production to identify bottlenecks and improvement opportunities.
- Measure and document improvements resulting from implemented changes to validate impact and support continuous improvement efforts.
- Support Watts’ commitment to continuous improvement by identifying process inefficiencies, communicating findings transparently, and taking accountability for assigned project deliverables.
- Assume responsibility for other projects and duties as assigned by the Quality and Engineering Manager or Company management.
Required Qualifications
- Current student (sophomore, junior or senior status).
- Pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing or Mechanical Engineering.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
- Passionate about engineering, with a genuine desire to contribute meaningfully to team objectives and make an impact.
- Demonstrated commitment to integrity and respect in interactions with others, fostering a positive and inclusive work environment.
- Strong sense of accountability, taking ownership of tasks and following through on commitments.
- Understanding of and adherence to applicable laws, codes, policies, regulations, and safety practices and procedures, as applicable.
- Must be authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship now or in the future.
- Must successfully establish employment eligibility and satisfactorily complete background checks, including required pre-employment testing as a condition of employment.
Preferred Qualifications
- Familiarity with CAD software for fixture design, tooling, or factory floor layouts.
- Exposure to manufacturing processes through coursework, projects, or previous work experience.
- Basic understanding of Lean manufacturing principles or continuous improvement methodologies.
General Applicable Company Competencies
- Commitment to Watts’ values of integrity, accountability, continuous improvement and innovation, and transparency.
- Punctuality and dependability.
- Ability to be flexible and adapt to changing work priorities and stressful conditions.
- Adherence to all personnel policies, procedures, and standards of process as implemented by Watts.
- Maintain productive and collaborative relationships with other Watts employees.
- Adherence to Watts’ seven cultural beliefs: Growth Mindset, Customer-Focused Innovation, Constant Communication, Clear Goals, Collaborate Globally, Be Inclusive, and Take Action.

While performing the job duties, you will be working onsite at the Fort Worth, TX location in both office and manufacturing environments. You may occasionally be required to perform responsibilities outside the typical office setting, including working directly with production cells and operators on the manufacturing floor. Appropriate personal protective equipment must be worn as required. Your scheduled work hours will be communicated to you by your manager.

- Ability to remain seated at a desk or workstation for extended periods.
- Ability to physically move around the office, organize or transport files, packages, or other office-related materials.

- Ability to wear personal protective equipment, which may include, but is not limited to, safety shoes, hearing protection, and safety glasses.

We believe in what we build and what we build, builds the world around us. Hospitals, hotels, schools, bridges, airports and more.
Come build a career you believe in.
About the Role
As a Manufacturing Engineering Intern at Wheatland Tube (a division of Zekelman Industries), you will support projects that improve operational efficiency, productivity, and product quality across the plant. Working closely with the Department Manager, Maintenance and cross-functional departments, you'll assist in facility layout planning, process flow optimization, and continuous improvement initiatives.
We are seeking a student who is currently pursuing a degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field and has at least one academic year remaining before graduation following the internship. This role offers an excellent opportunity to gain hands-on experience with manufacturing systems, data analysis, and industrial engineering tools while building a foundation for future internship and career opportunities within Zekelman Industries.
This is a full-time, on-site internship located at our state-of-the-art, automated Rochelle, IL facility. The official Zekelman internship program runs from May 24, 2027 through August 13, 2027 .
This role is perfect for someone who is detail-oriented, eager to optimize systems, and thrives in fast-paced manufacturing environments.
What You’ll Do
- Plan and design layouts for plant efficiency using CAD tools and drafting software
- Analyze workflows and material movement to generate scale drawings for optimal personnel and equipment placement
- Establish and support labor standards using work measurement programs and time study analysis
- Collect and analyze operational data to improve process effectiveness and plant layout
- Lead or assist in continuous improvement projects to enhance quality, throughput, and cost savings
- Develop and refine manufacturing processes, equipment functionality, and standard methods
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to identify root causes of net yield loss
- Maintain and enhance documentation such as work instructions, routings, and blueprints
- Analyze prime net yield and other performance indicators to support profitability initiatives
- Conduct experiments to optimize operations and report findings to the management team
- Promote and follow healthy and safe work practices in accordance with Zekelman policy
- Perform other duties as assigned
Who You Are
- Current college student pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Industrial or Manufacturing Engineering
- Strong analytical skills with a keen attention to detail
- Proficient in Microsoft Office, especially Excel
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills
- Highly organized and capable of managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
- CAD or drafting experience a plus (AutoCAD, SolidWorks, etc.)
- Available to travel for the Internship Summit, hosted at a Zekelman Industries location
What You’ll Get
Zekelman Industries offers a PAID internship experience with meaningful work, professional development, and the opportunity to make a real impact. Interns also enjoy:
- Hands-on experience improving manufacturing operations and systems
- Opportunities to work directly with operations, quality, and engineering teams
- Access to company-wide networking events, team-building activities, and learning sessions
- Regular feedback and mentorship to support your technical and career development
- Participation in a company-wide Intern Summit
Zekelman Industries offers competitive compensation and excellent benefits, including low-cost, high-quality medical and dental benefits.  In addition, we have an amazing tuition assistance program, a bonus plan, a 401(k) plan with a generous company match, immediate vesting, and much more.

Your Impact
As a Store Operations Industrial Engineering Intern at Lowe’s, you’ll work with the Store Labor Engineering team on projects that support workforce management, store productivity, and a simple and seamless customer experience. You’ll gain hands-on experience conducting in-store time studies, analyzing workload requirements, identifying process improvement opportunities, and developing engineered labor standards that help stores effectively manage labor costs while maintaining customer service standards.
This role is ideal for students who are passionate about using industrial engineering, data analysis, and process improvement to solve real-world retail challenges.
Summer Internship Program
Whether you’re starting your professional journey or pivoting to a new field, Lowe’s offers the resources and opportunities you need to thrive.
Our 10-week summer internship program (May 24 – July 30, 2027) immerses you in real-world retail operations. You’ll work directly with industry experts across our stores, distribution centers, and corporate offices, gaining practical experience through hands-on projects that make meaningful contributions to our business and communities.
To succeed in this role, we seek future leaders who:
• Drive innovation with fresh perspectives and an eagerness to learn.
• Bring dynamic energy while staying open to inspiration.
• Take on challenges with sharp thinking and embrace new opportunities.
• Build strong partnerships through collaborative teamwork.
• Push boundaries to discover what’s possible.
Do Your Best Work in Mooresville
This internship is based at our headquarters in Mooresville, North Carolina. Our corporate office is a space where you can collaborate and do your best work. Take a walk, grab a bite (or a cup of coffee), work out or get a check-up – we invest in you so you can find your inspiration.
What You Will Learn
• How store workforce management and labor productivity support Lowe’s strategy and the customer experience.
• How to gather and analyze workload requirements for store tasks and activities through in-store time studies.
• Analytical techniques used to translate time-study data into engineered labor standards.
• How to identify, quantify, and communicate opportunities to improve productivity, eliminate waste, and enhance store processes.
• How to evaluate alternative approaches to labor optimization while balancing labor costs and customer service standards.
• How to translate large data sets and labor analysis into clear recommendations and compelling presentations for senior leadership.
• How industrial engineers collaborate, share experiences, and apply process-improvement principles within a large retail environment.
Minimum Qualifications
• Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s Degree in Industrial Engineering or a related field from an accredited university.
• Expected graduation dates of December 2027 or May 2028.

• 3.0 cumulative GPA or higher.
• Proficient in MS Office Programs (specifically Word, Excel, and PowerPoint).
• One to two years of prior experience working in a retail environment.
• Strong collaborative, troubleshooting, problem-solving, communication, data analysis, and presentation skills.
• Ability to consider human behavior and interactions with environmental and work-area conditions when developing processes.
• Strong oral, written, and interpersonal communication skills.
• Accuracy and attention to detail, with strong analytical, data collection, and reporting skills.
• Experience developing engineered labor standards.

Job Description
RESPEC is seeking a Student Structural BIM Intern to join our 2027 Summer Internship Program in our Rapid City office. This position offers an excellent opportunity for students interested in structural drafting, BIM modeling, and design support to gain real-world experience within a growing North American engineering consulting firm.
This hands-on internship is within RESPEC’s Facilities (Structural) Market Sector and focuses on Building Information Modeling (BIM) and structural drafting support. The intern will work closely with structural engineers and designers to assist with the development and coordination of structural models and construction documents.
Under the guidance of experienced staff, the intern will receive mentoring and exposure to professional consulting services, interdisciplinary collaboration, and real project workflows. Responsibilities may include:
- Assist in developing and maintaining structural BIM models using software such as Revit under the guidance of senior staff
- Support the preparation of structural drawings, details, and model-based documentation for various project phases
- Coordinate with structural engineers and BIM technicians to incorporate design changes and redlines into models
- Perform basic model checks to help identify clashes, inconsistencies, or missing information
- Organize and manage BIM files in accordance with company standards and project requirements
- Extract quantities, schedules, and basic model data as needed to support engineering tasks
- Participate in coordination meetings and gain exposure to multidisciplinary workflows (structural, architectural, MEP)
- Follow established BIM standards, templates, and best practices while learning industry workflows
Qualifications
- Currently pursuing an associate’s degree in drafting, architectural/structural engineering technology, or a related field
- Interest in structural design and BIM workflows
Preferred Qualifications:
- Coursework or experience related to structural drafting or BIM
- Proficiency or working knowledge of Autodesk Revit; AutoCAD experience a plus
- Strong attention to detail and organizational skills
- Ability to manage time effectively and meet deadlines
- Strong problem-solving skills and willingness to learn
- Effective verbal and written communication skills
- Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment
Additional Information
Compensation: Compensation depends on experience. No benefits are offered except those that are required for statutory purposes.
All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

None required. However, if your assignment is longer than 179 days cumulatively within a calendar year, you must go through the Personal Identity Verification process. This process includes completing an online background investigation form and receiving approval of the background check.
National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA)
The 2025 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), Section 3112, generally prohibits citizens of China, Russia, Iran and North Korea without dual US citizenship or legal permanent residence from accessing specific non-public areas of national security or nuclear weapons facilities. The restrictions of NDAA Section 3112 apply to this position. To be qualified for this position, Candidates must be eligible to access the Laboratory in compliance with Section 3112.

Wireless and Medical Devices
Per the Department of Energy (DOE), Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory must meet certain restrictions with the use and/or possession of mobile devices in Limited Areas. Depending on your job duties, you may be required to work in a Limited Area where you are not permitted to have a personal and/or laboratory mobile device in your possession. This includes, but not limited to cell phones, tablets, fitness devices, wireless headphones, and other Bluetooth/wireless enabled devices.
If you use a medical device, which pairs with a mobile device, you must still follow the rules concerning the mobile device in individual sections within Limited Areas. Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities require separate approval. Hearing aids without wireless capabilities or wireless that has been disabled are allowed in Limited Areas, Secure Space and Transit/Buffer Space within buildings.
How to identify fake job advertisements
Please be aware of recruitment scams where people or entities are misusing the name of Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) to post fake job advertisements. LLNL never extends an offer without a personal interview and will never charge a fee for joining our company. All current job openings are displayed on the Career Page under “Find Your Job” of our website. If you have encountered a job posting or have been approached with a job offer that you suspect may be fraudulent, we strongly recommend you do not respond.
To learn more about recruitment scams: https://www.llnl.gov/sites/www/files/2023-05/LLNL-Job-Fraud-Statement-Updated-4.26.23.pdf

Our goal is to create an accessible and inclusive experience for all candidates applying and interviewing at the Laboratory. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please use our online form to submit a request.
California Privacy Notice

Graco manufactures and markets premium equipment to move, measure, control, dispense and spray a wide variety of fluid and powder materials. What does that mean? Well, we pump peanut butter into your jar, and the oil in your car. We glue the soles of your shoes, the glass in your windows and the screen on your phone. We spray the finish on your vehicle, coatings on your pills, the paint on your house and texture on your walls. Graco is part of your daily life.
The Graco Intern Program offers more than just work experience—it’s a chance to make an impact. As an intern, you’ll take on projects that matter to the business, contribute to initiatives that drive progress, and develop skills that prepare you for what’s ahead. Throughout the program, you’ll expand your industry knowledge, collaborate with professionals who are passionate about doing things the right way, and experience a culture that thrives on new ideas and continual growth. You’ll also take part in events designed to support both your learning and personal development. The program concludes with a final presentation where you’ll showcase your achievements and the difference you’ve made.
Job Purpose:
To support the Strategic Business Unit and the Manufacturing Cell and apply coursework to real-world applications as a Manufacturing Engineer Intern. Position involves providing ideas, inputs and analysis as a project team member.
What You Will Do at Graco
- Provide general production support for machining and/or assembly areas by participating in hands-on troubleshooting issues and providing technical assistance
- Assist in evaluating the need for machine and/or assembly area upgrades
- Participate in capital equipment justification as needed
- Review and analyze standards and operational layouts to suggest improvements
- Assist in the selection and implementation of tooling and fixtures for machining and/or assembly jobs
- Participate in cost of quality improvements, root cause analysis and corrective action
- React to changing priorities in a timely manner
- Report man-hour estimates
What You Will Bring to Graco
- Currently enrolled and pursing a Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical or Industrial Engineering or comparable Engineering program
- Minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale
- Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills
- Ability to work independently and as an effective team member
- Mechanical aptitude and desire for hands on work
Accelerators
- Experience with CAD software such as AutoCAD
- Experience with 3D printers
Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. This role is not eligible for immigration sponsorship now or in the future (e.g., H-1B, TN, F-1 OPT).
At Graco, you truly make a difference. Your unique talents contribute to our organizational growth and future. Not only do you make a difference, but Graco’s culture empowers employees to create their own career path. Whether you choose to advance within your current department or explore new opportunities in different divisions, you have the ability to build your future. Our managers are here to provide support and guidance as you continue to grow within your career.
Graco has excellent opportunities available to individuals who want to be part of a fast-moving, growing company that is committed to quality, innovation and solving fluid handling problems for our customers. Graco is proud to be named a Best Place to Work by Fortune Magazine in 2016, 2018, 2019, 2021 & 2022. Graco offers attractive compensation, benefits and career development opportunities. Graco’s comprehensive benefits include medical, dental, stock purchase plan, 401(k), tuition reimbursement and more.

We’re Watts. Together, we’re reimagining the future of water.
We feel proud every day about what we do. We're all part of the same crucial mission, no matter what function we support -- it's to provide safe, clean water for the world, and to protect our planet's most valuable resource.
What we do:
For 150 years, Watts has built best-in-class products that are trusted by customers in residential and commercial settings across the world. We are at the forefront of innovation, working with cutting-edge technology to provide smart and connected, sustainable water solutions for the future. Watts is a leading brand with a quality reputation — and we have a dynamic future ahead.​
The Watts Internship Program is your chance to bring what you’ve learned in the classroom to life! You’ll dive into real-world projects, gaining hands-on experience while learning how business really works from the inside. During the program, you’ll get to roll up your sleeves and make an impact on day-to-day operations. Plus, you'll have tons of opportunities to network with passionate professionals across manufacturing, industrial engineering, and more—sparking new ideas through cross-department collaboration. It’s all about expanding your skills, challenging yourself, and exploring where your ambitions can take you!
What You’ll Do
We are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented intern to join our Quality and Production Engineering Team. This role offers a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience in a fast-paced manufacturing environment while contributing to meaningful projects that support operational excellence. Key responsibilities include:
- Support Production Engineers by contributing to project execution and daily operational tasks.
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Purchasing, Sustaining Engineering, and Production Supervisors to advance project goals.
- Design and develop fixturing and tooling solutions to enhance production cell efficiency.
- Create and revise factory floor layouts to optimize space utilization and workflow.
- Engage directly with production cells and operators on the factory floor to observe, learn, and support operations.
- Analyze cycle times for assemblies and unit production to identify bottlenecks and improvement opportunities.
- Measure and document improvements resulting from implemented changes to validate impact and support continuous improvement efforts.
- Travel percentage: 0%
Who You Are
- Current student pursuing your bachelor's degree in manufacturing/mechanical engineering .
- Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
- Demonstrates a strong passion for engineering and a genuine desire to contribute meaningfully to team objectives.
- Committed to integrity, respect, and fostering a positive, inclusive work environment.
- Exhibits a strong sense of accountability, with the ability to take ownership of tasks and follow through on commitments.
- Must be authorized to work in the United States without current or future sponsorship requirements.
The expected salary range for this position is $22 - $26 an hour. Actual compensation will be dependent upon individual skills, experience, qualifications, and applicable laws.
What’s In It for You
People-First Culture – Enriching and caring for people is at the core of who we are; this includes executing our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) strategy, and providing you with meaningful career growth opportunities, a positive and safe work environment, and affirmation that you are heard, valued, and respected.
Flexible PTO Policy – Work-life balance is important at Watts and our interns receive one (1) hour of flexible PTO for every thirty (30) hours worked. Your flexible PTO can be utilized for any type of absence.
Paid Holidays – Celebrate the holidays with your loved ones and still get paid! You will receive paid holidays off during your time as an Intern with Watts. Where a holiday falls during the weekend, it will be observed on an adjacent weekday.
Lunch and Learns – Throughout your internship, there will be opportunities for you to sign up to learn and network with some of the key strategic leaders and thought partners within our core operating model!
Sustainability – For five years in a row, Watts has been named one of "America's Most Responsible Companies" by Newsweek. Join our journey as we continue to distinguish Watts as a responsible and committed corporate citizen.
Working Conditions
Work in both office and manufacturing environment. May occasionally be required to perform job responsibilities outside the typical office setting.
While performing the responsibilities of this job, the employee is frequently required to walk, talk, and/or hear. The employee is occasionally required to stand, sit, and use hands to finger, handle, or feel. You must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include: close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.
Watts in it for you :
Please note that the following benefits apply only to permanent roles and do not apply to internship roles.
- Competitive compensation based on your skills, qualifications and experience
- Comprehensive medical and dental coverage, retirement benefits
- Family building benefits, including paid maternity/paternity leave
- 10 paid holidays and Paid Time Off
- Continued professional development opportunities and educational reimbursement
- Additional perks such as fitness reimbursements and employee discount programs
- Learn more about our benefit offerings here: https://tapintowattsbenefits.com/
How we work:
At Watts, our culture is team-oriented and supportive. Employees here genuinely care about the quality of their work, and about each other. Our people are the heart of who we are and contribute to our longevity and continued success.
And this is a place where you can have a big career. No matter your role, there are opportunities for learning and development, and your daily contributions make a meaningful impact on the lives of people who use our products and on the future of water.
Watts is committed to equal employment opportunity. We follow a policy of administering all employment decisions and personnel actions without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, pregnancy, national origin, sexual orientation, age, physical or mental disability, genetic disposition or carrier status, marital status, military or veteran status, minorities, or any other category protected under applicable federal, state, or local law. Consistent with the obligations of state and federal law, Watts will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities. Any employee who needs a reasonable accommodation should contact Human Resources.
wd:barr:r-102315:
The role – what you’ll do
Barr is seeking a structural engineering intern to join our Ann Arbor team for the summer of 2027. In this role, you will support our structural engineering group on a variety of technical assignments related to hydropower facilities, wind turbine foundations, and industrial processing facilities—including fuels, power plants, mining, and other heavy industrial sites. You’ll contribute to structural design and analysis, prepare plans and specifications, assist with cost estimating, and participate in construction inspection and observation. This role may include short-term travel for field assignments.
The ideal candidate for this position is detail-oriented, technically curious, and eager to learn. You bring strong communication and problem-solving skills, a collaborative mindset, and a flexible working style that aligns with Barr’s values of client focus, integrity, and continuous improvement.
Your impact – key responsibilities
- Technical knowledge: apply foundational engineering principles to assist with engineering calculations and modeling for a variety of industrial and energy-related structures.
- Project support: support the preparation of engineering drawings, technical specifications, and design documentation. Contribute to project reports and help develop cost estimates for engineering solutions.
- Fieldwork: participate in site visits and inspections to observe construction activities and help ensure compliance with design intent.
- Software: use word processing, spreadsheet, and structural engineering software to support project tasks and team collaboration.
- Team collaboration: work closely with engineers and project managers while gaining hands-on experience in a professional consulting environment.
About the opportunity
- Hybrid: a hybrid work arrangement may be considered for this position. A hybrid work arrangement refers to splitting time worked between a Barr office and a home office. This position is based out of Barr's Ann Arbor, Michigan, office.
- Travel expectation: willingness to travel and periodically adjust personal schedule to meet project needs (up to 30% travel and fieldwork possible; project needs will vary).
- Work environment: ability to work in locations that may feature rough terrain typical of construction, manufacturing, or rural outdoor sites with limited accessibility, moving machinery, and other conditions typical of industrial facilities. Candidates must be able to perform job duties with or without reasonable accommodation.
Physical requirements for the role may include:
- Ability to conduct fieldwork in varying outdoor conditions (e.g., heat, cold, rain, uneven terrain).
- Must be able to lift and carry equipment and materials weighing up to 50 pounds.
- Capable of standing, walking, kneeling, or crouching for extended periods.
- Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) as required by site conditions.
About you – required core competencies
- Education: civil engineering degree with at least two semesters of physics and three semesters of mathematics. Must be in junior or senior standing, with a minimum of one full-time semester of undergraduate or graduate coursework remaining after the internship.
- GPA: minimum GPA of 3.2/4.0.
- Software: strong computer skills, including word processing and use of spreadsheets. Familiarity with the Microsoft Office Suite.
- Driver’s license: possession of a current, valid driver’s license and acceptable driving record.
- Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship by Barr, now or in the future.
Compensation : Anticipated range of $22.66–$30.46 hourly. Compensation will vary based on relevant experience, education, skill level, and other compensable factors. Employees in this position may also be eligible for a discretionary cash bonus based on team and individual performance. This position is classified as non-exempt (hourly) under the Fair Labor Standards Act.

- Profit distribution: Barr has a "no retained earnings" model and distributes all profit to our employees through our annual bonus distribution plan, ESOP, and dividends to shareholders

As a global leader in animal health, we are dedicated to innovation and delivering products and services to prevent and treat disease in farm animals and pets. Making animals’ lives better makes life better – join our team today!

As a Summer 2027 Quality Control Intern with Elanco Animal Health, you will be part of the Animal Health Manufacturing (AHM) Lab team at our Fort Dodge, Iowa manufacturing plant , to deliver a practical solution to reducing analytical variability, a manufacturing technical project, or implementation of new lab methods. Interns will have exposure to many career path s and diverse subject matter experts as many projects have site-wide impact.
Your Responsibilities:
- Understand the Animal Health Manufacturing process, document using GMP guidelines, and understand the importance of the Quality Unit
- Work within cross-functional teams to implement process or Quality Control lab improvements
- Learn about quality control, fermentation, product recovery, product finishing, or companion animal packaging
- Study design improvement processes
What You Need to Succeed (minimum qualifications):
- Education : Currently enrolled in an Engineering major including (but not limited to) Chemical, Mechanical, Electrical, or Process
- Top S kills : Experience in Microsoft Suites and a willingness to learn
What will give you a competitive edge (preferred qualifications):
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills
- Strong organizational and time management skills
- Must be able to work exceptionally well independently and with minimal supervision
Additional Information:
- Travel: 10% - to corporate facility in Indianapolis, IN for opening/closing
- Location: Fort Dodge Manufacturing Plant, Fort Dodge, IA

10159988
Job Description:
About the Role & Program
Company Overview : At Disney, we are storytellers. We make the impossible, possible. We do this through using and developing innovative technology and opening the boundaries to bring stories to life through our movies, products, interactive games, parks and resorts, and media networks. Now is your chance to join our talented team as a Professional Intern in any of our segments that delivers unparalleled creative content to audiences around the world.
Department Overview: Want to be part of a world-class organization, learning new skills that you can apply in the “real world”? How about free admission to theme parks and all the shopping and restaurants you can get your hands on? If this doesn't sound like your typical Industrial Engineering position, that’s because it’s not! Our program is designed to develop you professionally and increase your practical knowledge of the many operating areas within the Company. You will have a wide range of opportunities to provide analytic and consulting support to various lines of business including Merchandise, Attractions, and Entertainment. It may even serve as a springboard in launching a successful career. You will have the opportunity to network and learn from other Industrial Engineers and make friendships that cover the globe.
Learn more: Disney Engineering: Role Spotlight | Industrial Engineering - YouTube
This internship is a full-time commitment in the Orlando, FL area from August 2027 – December 2027 OR May 2027 – December 2027 dependent on the business needs.
What You Will Do
- Conduct Industrial Engineering analysis projects, particularly in operational planning support, workload planning and forecasting, capacity utilization, and efficiency/process improvements
- Ensure the appropriate methodology, measurements, tools and quantitative techniques (e.g. data collection, computer simulation, statistics, process flow analysis, etc.) are applied in projects
- Lead and participate in team efforts and work on projects which require interfacing with all levels of cast and management
Required Qualifications & Skills
These are the minimum qualifications you need to be considered for this position:
- Proven strong verbal and written communication skills
- Proven strong interpersonal skills
- Proven strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills
- Willingness to learn new software application
Preferred Qualifications
- Prior related work experience with a focus on problem-solving
Education
- Currently enrolled in an Industrial Engineering program with an intended graduation date on or after December 2027
- Cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher (please note: no rounding) – transcript submission is required
Eligibility Requirements & Program Information
Candidates for this opportunity MUST meet all the requirements below:
- Be enrolled in an accredited college/university pursuing a degree taking at least one class at time of application posting OR currently participating in a Disney College Program or Disney Internship​
- Be at least 18 years of age​
- Possess unrestricted work authorization​
- Have not completed one year of continual employment on a Disney internship or Disney College Program
Additional Information
- Able to have a consistent, reliable work schedule throughout the internship
- Fully available Monday – Friday and occasional evenings and/or weekends depending on project needs for the duration of the internship, 40 hours each week
- Able to provide own housing for the duration internship program in the Orlando, FL area
- Able to provide reliable transportation to/from work and across Walt Disney World property for on-site projects
- Be compliant with The Disney Look appearance guidelines while at work
- Limited housing opportunities may be available for Florida-based Disney Interns through American Campus Communities. For more information, click here .

s an  organization  we are committed to developing the next generation of Makers and Bakers. As part of Manufacturing, you’ll use your skills, our systems, and a wide array of raw materials to help create the delicious, finished products our consumers love. As a Manufacturing Co-Op, you will gain hands-on experience in a fast-paced manufacturing environment, working closely with site engineering, operations, and production teams to improve the efficiency, reliability, and overall performance of manufacturing processes. A significant portion of the program will be spent on the production floor, building an understanding of how products are manufactured, observing day-to-day operations, attending production and control meetings, and identifying opportunities to improve how our lines and equipment operate.
Throughout the co-op , you may support projects focused on process optimization, loss analysis, waste reduction, equipment performance, and production efficiency. This could include analyzing production data and line performance, identifying sources of downtime or material loss, investigating root causes, and partnering with site teams to develop and implement solutions. Co-Ops may also have the opportunity to lead or participate in Kaizen events and other continuous improvement initiatives, using methodologies and principles such as Lean Six Sigma, World Class Manufacturing (WCM), and Total Productive Maintenance (TPM).
Projects may also include updating process maps for specific areas of the plant, evaluating production or packaging processes, optimizing key pieces of equipment, and supporting improvements to standard operating procedures. Co-Ops may work directly with operators and technical teams to understand current processes and help update process documentation, training materials, work instructions, or operating manuals to ensure improvements can be effectively implemented and sustained.
This Co-Op is designed to provide exposure to the full manufacturing environment ; from understanding what happens directly on the production line to using data and continuous improvement tools to solve real operational challenges.
