As a Manufacturing Engineering Intern at Lexington Medical, you will spend the summer on a running production line that builds a surgical stapler, tracking yield, downtime, and cycle time, and owning one process improvement project from concept through implementation. You will troubleshoot alongside the operators and technicians who run the line, bring your own analysis to production support meetings, and present your results to engineering leadership before you leave.
About Lexington Medical
Lexington Medical designs and manufactures AEON™ surgical stapling technology at our headquarters in Bedford, Massachusetts, just outside Boston. Our products are used in minimally invasive surgery, where precision, reliability, and quality matter every time. Because engineering, manufacturing, and quality work together under one roof, the people building and supporting our products are close to both the process and the decisions behind it.
About the Role
As a Manufacturing Engineering Intern at Lexington Medical, you will work alongside manufacturing engineering on an operating line producing AEON™ surgical stapling products. Day to day, you will monitor line performance, troubleshoot equipment and process issues in real time with operators and technicians, analyze process data for trends, and propose changes such as fixturing updates or workflow revisions. Alongside that, you will own one manufacturing improvement project end to end, aligning with Manufacturing, Engineering, and Quality as you go. Because all three groups work in the same building in Bedford, getting that alignment means walking down the hall rather than waiting on a meeting invite.
Responsibilities
- Monitor line performance metrics, including yield, downtime, and cycle time.
- Partner with operators and technicians to troubleshoot equipment and process issues in real time.
- Perform repairs and maintenance on custom production equipment.
- Participate in daily and weekly production support meetings.
- Assess current processes for bottlenecks and inefficiencies and analyze process data to identify trends and improvement opportunities.
- Generate solutions, such as fixturing updates or workflow changes, and present them to the larger manufacturing team.
- Implement approved changes by training operators, commissioning equipment, or making other line changes as needed.
- Own a manufacturing improvement project from concept through implementation and present the outcome to engineering leadership.
Qualifications
- Currently enrolled at an accredited university in an undergraduate or graduate program in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, or a similar technical discipline.
- CAD experience (SolidWorks or similar)
- Your resume should show a demonstrated ability to build and debug mechanical or electromechanical assemblies, whether from coursework, a project team, a lab, or personal projects.
- Comfortable working with hand tools, shop equipment, and production machinery on the floor.
- Able to read mechanical drawings and work from SOPs and written work instructions.
- Able to clearly communicate analysis and observations to engineering team.
Skills that are a plus:
- Comfort analyzing data in Excel or a similar tool
- Time on a build team such as Formula SAE, Baja, or robotics
What Success Looks Like
- You have an understanding of your improvement project and have iterated on potential solutions.
- You have aligned all stakeholders of your proposed change (Ex. Manufacturing, Engineering, and Quality).
- By the end of the internship, the change is running on the line and you have presented the impact it has had to the engineering team.
Location & Work Arrangement
This position is based at our headquarters in Bedford, Massachusetts, in the Greater Boston area, and is an on-site role. The internship runs from June 2027 through August 2027, on-site five days per week.
Hourly Rate
$25 — $35 USD

Trane Technologies, the global leader in innovative climate solutions, hands on summer internship allows participants to explore a career in Energy Engineering through the following:
- A 12-week Summer internship program that will challenge and develop your technical, business, leadership, and communication skills.
- Gain insight into an Energy Engineering Career with Trane Technologies, focusing on solutions that provide our customers with the most energy-efficient buildings.
- Work on a variety of engineering aspects, including energy analysis projects, completion of field energy audits, client interviews, completion of estimates, and development of energy conversation measures, and project management.
- This internship will provide you with the experience to pursue a career in Energy Engineering and creates the opportunity to join our industry leading Graduate Training Program (GTP) after graduation.
What you will do:
Our internship program provides you with the opportunity to learn more about us while you collaborate with peers across North America. As an Energy Engineer Intern, you may experience and assist in:
- Partnering with Account Managers and Energy Engineers to diagnose energy opportunities with customer’s facilities and provide small energy projects that solve customer issues/opportunities.
- Providing technical analysis/review for energy projects; providing project risk assessment.
- Shadowing and performing building “walk-throughs” and identifying energy conservation measures (architectural, mechanical, electrical, etc.) in commercial, institutional, and industrial facilities.
- Collaborating on the development of existing reporting capabilities from a software standpoint and a usability perspective and investigate new technologies.
- Prescribing best methods for measurement and verification of system performance during the acquisition phase.
- Analyzing data outputs for trends and/or any deviations that need further investigating.
- Assisting with opportunity technical qualification including Preliminary Audits, Benchmarking, Site Surveys, and Interviews.
- Collecting, analyzing, and developing benchmark summary reports to illustrate the pertinent details of building and/or system performance.
What you will bring:
- Actively enrolled in a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Engineering, (preferred disciplines: Energy, Mechanical or Electrical) throughout the entire duration of the summer internship.
- Candidates must have completed at least their sophomore or 2nd year before the start of the summer internship to be eligible for internship positions.
- Be a U.S. citizen or have the legal right to work in the U.S. without requiring sponsorship now or in the future.
- This posting is for multiple opportunities. Some positions may be remote while others may require a hybrid or onsite assignment at one of our facilities across North America.
- Possess a valid driver’s license for a minimum of 12 months, ability to provide proof of insurance, and have no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to:
- DUI in the previous 3 years
- Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless / Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.

Who We Are
Vermeer equips customers doing important work around the world. We are global, driven by innovation and growing. The equipment we make manages natural resources, connects people and feeds and fuels communities. We live out a caring culture, we demonstrate agility, we keep a focus on customers and are stewards of our resources. These beliefs drive our culture, determine how we treat others and steer our business.
Work Shift
1 - First Shift
Job Summary
Are you energized by solving problems and improving how things are made? As a Quality Engineer Intern at Vermeer, you’ll support real-world projects that enhance production processes and drive operational excellence. This internship offers hands-on experience in monitoring, analyzing, problem solving, and improving product performance—preparing you for a full-time engineering role upon graduation.
What You’ll Do
1. Review and analyze internal and external quality performance for whole goods, upstream production, plant quality, and/or supplier quality; communicate trends and findings to manufacturing leadership.
2. Support Root Cause and Corrective Action (RCCA) and problem-solving activities for assigned issues; help implement solutions to reduce quality issues and defects.
3. Assist in executing and auditing control plans and manufacturing processes for compliance and effectiveness; partner with manufacturing engineering to implement mistake-proofing and process improvements.
4. Collaborate with suppliers to problem-solve and verify quality improvements.
5. Participate in process capability studies and continuous improvement activities with process engineering, including Statistical Process Control (SPC) methods such as Process Capability Index (CPK) and control charts using statistical software such as Minitab (or similar).
6. Support critical Quality Management System (QMS) processes and participate in quality improvement projects and teams.
What We’re Looking For
- High School diploma required. Current student pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Engineering.
- Awareness of quality tools and techniques, such as Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP), Core Tools, SPC methods, and CPK, with exposure to statistical software such as Minitab (or similar).
- Awareness of lean manufacturing principles and using Lean Sigma/Six Sigma methodology to improve quality, including Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control (DMAIC).
- Experience with troubleshooting and root cause analysis; exposure to Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA) and Eight Disciplines (8D) problem solving preferred.
- Ability to work in a team environment, operate assembly and measurement tools and devices, and read prints and Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T).
Travel
- No travel is expected of this position.
Work Location
ONSITE: A team member’s day-to-day work is best done on a Vermeer campus. If work content can be occasionally completed at an offsite location, discuss potential arrangements with your manager.

Explore your next opportunity at a Fortune Global 500 organization. Envision innovative possibilities, experience our rewarding culture, and work with talented teams that help you become better every day. We know what it takes to lead UPS into tomorrow—people with a unique combination of skill + passion. If you have the qualities and drive to lead yourself or teams, there are roles ready to cultivate your skills and take you to the next level.
Job Description:
This is not a remote position, you must live within the geographic area of Louisville, KY.
The Summer 2027 Co-Op Program Dates Are: 5/10/2027-8/13/2027
The Co-Op position will be assigned to one of the following Industrial Engineering departments: Aircraft Maintenance IE, Air Region IE, Flight Operations IE, Gateway IE, or Fuel Analytics and Sustainability.
Some of the common shared job duties for each department include performing operational observations in the field along with researching data utilized to analyze projects, create procedures, evaluate project proposals, and prepare presentations and reports based on findings. They participate in projects focused on reducing costs through improved processes and procedures. This position may also perform data queries and develop reports to streamline communications and performance reporting.
Some distinct functions of each department are below:
Aircraft Maintenance IE
ACMX IE: ​ Aircraft maintenance projects related to materials flow, staffing, time studies, and maintenance equipment.
ACMX BI: Projects using ACMX data to create analysis/decision tools and reports using Power BI, Google Cloud Platform, SQL, Excel, etc.
Air Region IE:
Ramp Special projects include evaluating opportunities with technology, new equipment or facility/process redesign to lower labor requirement or improve aircraft arrival time to destination.
Flight Operations IE
Flight IE is the industrial engineering group that supports flight district functions like pilot scheduling, pilot training, flight operations. These projects also include process improvement projects, staffing analysis, and data analysis for those groups.
Gateway Planning Building and Facilities IE
Supports facility planning and design projects at all US Domestic Gateways. Areas of oversight include facility and ramp design, facility expansion projects, leasehold improvements, and capacity management of facility sort engines. Job responsibilities include developing project feasibilities and dataset management, organizing and leading internal and external cross functional teams, and determining project financial feasibility or potential return on investment.
Fuel Analytics and Sustainability IE
The Fueling Analytics and Sustainability Co-Op will work on 1-2 projects evaluating and/or executing a fuel efficiency initiative for UPS Airlines. They will be required to communicate well with other work groups, including Aircraft Maintenance, Ground Service Equipment, Pilots, Flight Dispatchers, and Operations Supervisors. They will help us contribute towards sustainability goals by working on projects that reduce jet fuel burn and thus carbon emissions.
Co-Op Responsibilities:
- Identifies the impact of a problem on multiple areas of the business; recommends improvements to existing processes or programs.
- Identifies and implements process improvements collaborating with analysts, users, and project sponsors.
- Utilize work measurement, design data development, statistical analysis, and discussion with management and/or operations to identify issues and solutions that impact both short-term and long-term strategies.
Co-Op Qualifications:
- Currently enrolled in or recently graduated from (within the last 24 months) an undergraduate Industrial Engineering or related program, seeking a Bachelor’s Degree or International equivalent
- Working knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel, Access, and Outlook
- Strong interpersonal communication skills
- Sufficient and effective knowledge in programming and algorithms is desired, but not required
- Ability to work full time and in-person (40 hours/week) from our Louisville, KY site.
This is not a remote position, you must live within the geographic area of Louisville, KY.
Employee Type:
Intern

UPS is an equal opportunity employer. UPS does not discriminate on the basis of race/color/religion/sex/national origin/veteran/disability/age/sexual orientation/gender identity or any other characteristic protected by law.

Must be a U.S. Citizen or National of the U.S., an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence, or an alien authorized to work in the U.S. for this employer.

Company Description
Work with Us. Change the World.
At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.
There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.
We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.
Job Description
AECOM is seeking a highly motivated Structural Engineering Intern for our transportation department in the Roanoke, VA office. As an intern in the transportation department, you will assist in the design and inspection of various highway structures.
This position is expected to begin Summer 2027.
Internships at AECOM offer students in undergraduate and graduate programs the opportunity to gain valuable hands-on experience in engineering, design, and infrastructure projects that make a real-world impact. Interns work with cutting-edge technology, learn industry best practices, and collaborate with experienced professionals in a globally recognized firm. The program fosters both technical and professional skill development while providing networking opportunities that can enhance future career prospects. Additionally, AECOM’s dedication to innovation and sustainability enables interns to contribute to meaningful projects that help shape communities and the built environment.
The responsibilities of this position may include, but are not limited to:
- Perform assignments requiring application of standard techniques, procedures and criteria to carry out engineering tasks.
- Prepare engineering related calculations.
- Perform quantity takeoffs and cost estimates.
- Review shop drawings.
- Assist in the inspection of bridges, culverts, and tunnels.
- Prepare details for construction drawings using CAD software.
- Work under the supervision of a project manager or senior-level team member.
Qualifications
Minimum Requirements:
- Candidates must be pursuing a Bachelor’s Degree in Civil Engineering or in another related field and must have completed at least 1 year of study. Candidates who have graduated with a Bachelor’s Degree and plan to continue with the Master’s Degree are eligible to apply for these positions. Graduates must have been enrolled in their bachelor’s degree in the most previous school term with an interest in pursuing an advanced degree in the same or similar discipline at the conclusion of the internship.
Preferred Qualifications:
- Completed courses related to statics, strength of materials, introductory steel design, and introductory reinforced concrete design.
- Ability to follow procedures and pay attention to detail.
- Good written and oral communications skills.
- Familiarity with Microsoft Office and AutoCAD.
- Proficiency in developing calculations using software like Excel or Mathcad.
- Interest in bridge design is desired.
Additional Information
- Relocation assistance is not available for this position.
- Sponsorship for US employment authorization is not available now or in the future for this position.
- This position requires a hybrid work schedule which incudes in office work in Roanoke, VA. The selected candidate must be available to work in Roanoke, VA on a scheduled basis.
At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.
About AECOM
AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options , well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.
AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. We’re Watts. Together, we’re reimagining the future of water.
We feel proud every day about what we do. We're all part of the same crucial mission, no matter what function we support -- it's to provide safe, clean water for the world, and to protect our planet's most valuable resource.
What we do:
For 150 years, Watts has built best-in-class products that are trusted by customers in residential and commercial settings across the world. We are at the forefront of innovation, working with cutting-edge technology to provide smart and connected, sustainable water solutions for the future. Watts is a leading brand with a quality reputation — and we have a dynamic future ahead.​
The Watts Internship Program is your chance to bring what you’ve learned in the classroom to life! You’ll dive into real-world projects, gaining hands-on experience while learning how business really works from the inside. During the program, you’ll get to roll up your sleeves and make an impact on day-to-day operations. Plus, you'll have tons of opportunities to network with passionate professionals across manufacturing, industrial engineering, and more—sparking new ideas through cross-department collaboration. It’s all about expanding your skills, challenging yourself, and exploring where your ambitions can take you!
Scope of Position
This innovative and detail-oriented individual, as part of the Operations team, will support the identification and implementation of shop floor process improvements aimed at increasing efficiency, reducing costs, and enhancing production output. The Manufacturing Engineering Intern will work with cross-functional teams to support continuous improvement initiatives and gain hands-on experience with manufacturing processes.
This position reports to the Senior Manager of Advanced Manufacturing & Continuous Improvement. This role is onsite and is based in St. Pauls, NC.
Primary Job Duties and Responsibilities
- Help create and maintain shop floor work instructions, including specifications, engineering changes, process controls, and tooling requirements.
- Participate in lean manufacturing initiatives that support continuous process improvement.
- Collaborate with hourly employees and teams across Quality, Safety, Sourcing, and other functions on manufacturing projects.
- Support the scoping, planning, and execution of manufacturing engineering requests under the guidance of the Manufacturing Engineering team, including improving manufacturing efficiency, implementing engineering changes, improving product quality, and addressing production line technical issues.
- Analyze and document existing manufacturing processes to identify improvement opportunities.
- Support Watts’ commitment to continuous improvement by identifying process inefficiencies, communicating findings transparently, and taking accountability for assigned project deliverables.
- Assume responsibility for other projects and duties as assigned by the Manufacturing Engineer Manager or Company management.
Required Qualifications
- Current student (sophomore, junior or senior status).
- Pursuing a degree in Manufacturing, Mechanical, or Industrial Engineering.
- Ability to present complex data effectively through charts, tables, graphs, and pivot tables.
- Ability to work independently and manage assigned tasks with appropriate guidance.
- Ability to communicate professionally and effectively with colleagues across departments and levels of the organization.
- Passionate about your work, with a genuine desire to contribute meaningfully and make an impact.
- Demonstrated commitment to integrity and respect in interactions with others, fostering a positive and inclusive work environment.
- Strong sense of accountability, taking ownership of tasks and following through on commitments.
- Understanding of and adherence to applicable laws, codes, policies, regulations, and safety practices and procedures, as applicable.
- Must be authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship now or in the future.
- Must successfully establish employment eligibility and satisfactorily complete background checks, including required pre-employment testing as a condition of employment.
Preferred Qualifications
- Knowledge of Lean manufacturing principles.
- Familiarity with quality standards and process improvement methodologies, such as Six Sigma.
General Applicable Company Competencies
- Commitment to Watts’ values of integrity, accountability, continuous improvement and innovation, and transparency.
- Punctuality and dependability.
- Ability to be flexible and adapt to changing work priorities and stressful conditions.
- Adherence to all personnel policies, procedures, and standards of process as implemented by Watts.
- Maintain productive and collaborative relationships with other Watts employees.
- Adherence to Watts’ seven cultural beliefs: Growth Mindset, Customer-Focused Innovation, Constant Communication, Clear Goals, Collaborate Globally, Be Inclusive, and Take Action.
Working Conditions
While performing the job duties, you will be working on-site at a manufacturing facility and will perform the majority of your duties in an office environment. You may, at times, be required to be present on the manufacturing floor and will be required to wear the appropriate personal protective equipment. You will be required to work in the office at the St. Pauls, NC location (Monday–Friday). Your scheduled work hours will be communicated to you by your manager.
Physical Requirements
Specific physical abilities required for this position include, but are not limited to:
- Ability to remain seated at a desk or workstation for extended periods.
- Ability to physically move around the office, organize or transport files, packages, or other office-related materials.
- Ability to read documents, use a computer, and perform data entry tasks.
- Ability to communicate clearly with management and coworkers, particularly in meetings or phone calls.
- Ability to operate standard office equipment such as computers, printers, phones, and copiers.
- Ability to stand for long periods of time.
- Ability to lift and carry up to 20 pounds.
- Ability to push and pull up to 20 pounds.
- Ability to physically move around the manufacturing floor.
- Ability to read documents and communicate clearly with management and coworkers.
- Ability to wear personal protective equipment, which may include, but is not limited to, safety shoes, hearing protection, and safety glasses.
Pay Range: $21-27
The expected hourly range for this position is $21–27 hourly. Actual compensation will be dependent upon individual skills, experience, qualifications, and applicable law.
What’s In It for You
People-First Culture – Enriching and caring for people is at the core of who we are; this includes executing our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) strategy, and providing you with meaningful career growth opportunities, a positive and safe work environment, and affirmation that you are heard, valued, and respected.

About the Company
General Matter is enriching uranium in America.
Our goal is to design, build, and operate the world’s lowest-cost enrichment services in the United States.
Our mission is to restore America’s ability to produce nuclear fuel—fuel that will power AI, advanced manufacturing, critical industries, and the next generation of nuclear reactors.
Ultimately, our work will help power national ambitions and enable a high-energy society.
We were incubated by Founders Fund, like Anduril and Palantir before us, and are backed by top-tier investors. Our lean, world-class team of engineers and operators is applying a first-principles approach to solving the problem of nuclear fuel production.
We are a mission-driven company with a culture of urgency, accountability, and transparency.
Help us build a high-energy society by making the cleanest, safest form of baseload energy the most affordable.
About This Role
As a Summer Field Engineer Intern at General Matter, you'll be on the ground in Paducah during active construction of our flagship uranium enrichment facility. It's a first-of-a-kind plant being built on the site of the former Paducah Gaseous Diffusion Plant, which helped fuel America for sixty years. You'll be the link between design and the field, helping turn drawings and specifications into installed work, catch problems before they cost the schedule, and build the record that shows the plant was built right.
Most construction interns are one of dozens on a job at a large contractor, with little ownership of real work. Here you'll sit on the owner's team for one project of national importance. You'll take on meaningful scopes of work and work directly alongside the superintendents, engineers, and quality team delivering it. You'll see how a nuclear facility comes together, and you'll help build it.
If you seek high impact and are excited by fast-paced, intense, Skunkworks-style projects, we encourage you to apply to join our team.
Responsibilities
Field Engineering & Constructability
- Help interpret drawings, specifications, and shop drawings for craft and subcontractor crews, and flag constructability issues to engineering before they reach the field
- Assist in drafting and tracking RFIs and submittals for assigned work packages from the first question through the engineering response and closure
- Perform quantity takeoffs, track installed quantities and percent complete, and support field progress reporting to project controls and the master schedule
- Help verify survey, layout, and as-built data for foundations, embeds, underground utilities, and structural steel
- Support coordination of material deliveries, laydown, and equipment needs with superintendents and subcontractors to keep work fronts moving
Quality & Documentation
- Support coordination of inspection and test plan hold points with Quality Control, and help verify that installed work meets drawings, specifications, and nuclear quality requirements
- Maintain daily reports, progress photos, and field records that become part of the facility's permanent quality and turnover record
- Support punch-list walks, as-built markups, and turnover package preparation for completed systems
Safety & Field Coordination
- Help prepare Job Hazard Analyses and take part in daily safety meetings, toolbox talks, and field safety walks
- Serve as a day-to-day field contact for subcontractor foremen on assigned tasks, raising issues early and closing them out quickly
- Own a defined intern project over the summer, such as tracking a site utility system or a building's foundation work, and present your results to the project team
Basic Qualifications
- Currently pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in Civil, Construction, Mechanical, or Electrical Engineering, or Construction Management, with an expected graduation date after summer 2027
- Evidence of exceptional ability (construction internships or co-ops, engineering competition teams, hands-on projects, completed builds, etc.)
- Ability to read and interpret construction drawings and specifications
- Ability to work outdoors on an active construction site in all weather conditions, including walking uneven terrain, climbing ladders and stairs, and wearing required PPE
- Valid driver's license
- Ability to obtain and maintain required security clearance and access authorization
- Available for the full 12-week summer 2027 internship in Paducah, Kentucky
Preferred Skills and Experience
- Prior construction internship or co-op experience, especially on industrial, power generation, data center, semiconductor, or other mission-critical projects
- EIT certification or a passing score on the FE exam
- OSHA 10 or OSHA 30 certification
- Familiarity with Procore, Bluebeam, AutoCAD/Civil 3D, or Primavera P6
- Exposure to nuclear, DOE, or NQA-1 quality programs
- Leadership on an engineering competition team (ASCE Concrete Canoe, Steel Bridge, Solar Decathlon, etc.) or in a student organization
- Military service, trades experience, or other hands-on leadership experience
- Bias toward action and comfort making decisions with incomplete information in a fast-paced, resource-constrained environment
- Interest in building a long-term career on a single flagship project rather than moving from job to job
Additional Requirements
- Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary.
Equal Opportunity Employer
General Matter is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with General Matter is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.
Compensation and Benefits
The hourly pay range for this internship is $30–$40 per hour, depending on the candidate's current standing in school (i.e. sophomore, senior).
Interns will receive a monthly housing stipend, and are eligible for overtime pay. Please note that the stated hourly range is an estimate and may be adjusted based on market conditions, business needs, or other factors.

You will put reinforcement learning and optimization to work on problems that decide how a fleet of plants gets built: how to sequence construction across many sites, where to place capital under uncertainty, and how to keep a distributed site secure. As a Data Science & Machine Learning Fellow, you formulate the problem, build a simulation or optimization model, evaluate it rigorously, and help move it toward a deployed decision system. About the Role
Pascal develops solid refrigerant technologies for cooling a warming world. We have translated our core technology into a commercial-scale refrigerator prototype. The next phase of development requires continued advances in materials, composites, and processing methods, along with reliable tests that connect material properties to system performance.
Pascal is seeking a Materials Science Intern to support our materials development efforts. Working closely with Pascal’s materials scientists, you will prepare and improve solid refrigerant materials and composites, characterize their properties, and evaluate them in custom test rigs and prototypes. This is a hands-on experimental role. You will help answer current technology-development questions and use the results to decide what to make and test next.
We welcome applications from undergraduate and master’s students at different stages of their training. The scope of the role will reflect the intern’s experience and Pascal’s current technical priorities. We care more about strong scientific fundamentals, curiosity, careful experimentation, and the ability to learn quickly than about prior experience with every technique listed below.
What You’ll Do
● Prepare, formulate, and process solid refrigerant materials and composites and help move promising formulations from bench-scale samples to larger batches.
● Plan and run experiments to understand how composition, processing, and structure affect material and system performance.

wd:nvidia:jr2024171:
We are recruiting outstanding Research Interns to work on autonomous vehicles, robotics, and physical AI! Intelligent machines that can perceive, reason, and safely interact with people and the physical world are rapidly becoming a reality. Self-driving cars, autonomous delivery and construction vehicles, mobile manipulators, and other robotic systems are moving closer to widespread deployment. However, fundamental research challenges remain before these systems can operate safely, reliably, and autonomously in complex, unfamiliar environments.
For example, how can we:
- Develop new training paradigms that use perception and interaction to train autonomous vehicle and robot policies in closed loop?
- Equip autonomous systems with online and offline assurances that meet the requirements of safety-critical applications?
- Enable vehicles and robots to navigate across new environments, tasks, and embodiments?
- Build systems that reason under uncertainty and interact safely and naturally with people and other agents?
These are some of the exciting questions being explored by NVIDIA’s Autonomous Systems and Physical AI Research (ASPIRE) group. Our diverse, interdisciplinary team conducts foundational research spanning foundation model design, embodied reasoning, safety, closed-loop training and evaluation, and agentic workflows for Physical AI development. We also investigate related areas including decision-making under uncertainty, deep learning, reinforcement learning, simulation, and the verification and validation of safety-critical AI systems. Our focus is on fundamental research, and lab members are encouraged to publish their work and open-source their code. NVIDIA is known for its collaborative culture, and our researchers work closely with experts across the company in autonomous vehicles, robotics, perception, simulation, and machine learning. This creates opportunities to influence real-world products while retaining the freedom and bandwidth to conduct groundbreaking, publishable research.
What you’ll be doing:
- Designing and implementing cutting-edge techniques for autonomous vehicles, robotics, and physical AI.
- Conducting original research and publishing your results.
- Collaborating with research colleagues, internal product teams, and external researchers.
- Transferring technology you’ve developed to relevant product groups.
What we need to see:
- Currently pursuing a PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field.
- Relevant research experience in autonomous vehicles, robotics, embodied AI, or autonomous systems.
- Strong knowledge of the theory and practice of vehicle or robot autonomy—or expertise in a related area, with a strong interest in applying your work to autonomous systems.
- A track record of research excellence, demonstrated through publications at leading conferences and journals—such as RSS, ICRA, CoRL, IJRR, NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, TAC, etc.—and through other research artifacts such as open-source software.
- Exceptional Python programming skills; experience with C++ and parallel programming, such as CUDA, is a plus.
- Experience with machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills are required, along with the ability to thrive in a dynamic, research-focused team.
Are you intellectually curious, collaborative, and motivated to solve complex problems at the intersection of AI and the physical world? If so, you may be a great fit for NVIDIA.

wd:asml:j-00355102:
Introduction
ASML US brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines and metrology that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon.
We are currently recruiting for an internship located at our office in San Jose, CA
Roles and Responsibilities
As a Computational Imaging and Metrology Engineering Intern, you will support product engineering activities focused on simulation, performance analysis, and technology development. You will use scientific and engineering principles to evaluate complex systems and contribute to data-driven engineering decisions.
- Simulate imaging and metrology performance across a variety of tool configurations and operating conditions.
- Design and execute studies to evaluate system performance, investigate technical challenges, and support product improvements.
- Analyze simulation results and engineering data to identify trends, root causes, and optimization opportunities.
- Develop key performance indicators (KPIs) and analytical methods to measure system effectiveness.
- Support investigations related to customer-reported technical challenges and performance questions.
- Collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams to develop and validate new product capabilities.
- Document technical findings and communicate recommendations through reports, presentations, and engineering reviews.
Education and Experience
- Currently pursuing a bachelor's degree, master's degree, or PhD in Physics, Materials Science and Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics, or a related technical discipline.
- Experience through coursework, research, academic projects, or internships involving optics, imaging, metrology, semiconductor technology, or computational modeling.
- Familiarity with simulation techniques, scientific computing, or data analysis methodologies.
- Experience using programming languages such as MATLAB, Python, C, or C++ is preferred.
- Exposure to algorithm development, statistical analysis, or engineering optimization methods is beneficial.
Skills
· Routinely required to sit; walk; talk; hear; use hands to keyboard, finger, handle, and feel; stoop, kneel, crouch, twist, reach, and stretch. Occasionally required to move around the campus.
· Occasionally lift and/or move up to 20 pounds.
· May require travel (specify domestic and/or international) dependent on business needs.
· Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.
Inclusion and diversity
ASML is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values and respects the importance of a diverse and inclusive workforce. It is the policy of the company to recruit, hire, train and promote persons in all job titles without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation, or gender identity. The Tactical and Autonomous Processing Department of the Applied Research Laboratory (ARL) at Penn State University is seeking undergraduate students for internship opportunities. PETRONAS Canada is a great place to launch a career that is enriched with knowledge, technical skills and mentorship. Our summer student program provides an opportunity to experience real-world challenges, collaborate with diverse teams, network with other students and create a vision for your future career path.
This position is working within PETRONAS Canada LNG Ltd. (PCLL). T-Mobile is synonymous with innovation–and you could be part of the team that disrupted an entire industry! We reinvented customer service, brought real 5G to the nation, and now we’re shaping the future of technology in wireless and beyond. Our work is as exciting as it is rewarding, so consider the career opportunity below as your invitation to grow with us, make big things happen with us, above all, #BEYOU with us. Together, we won’t stop!
Get hands-on experience, training—and a leg up on a bright future.
T-Mobile didn’t become a leader by following the playbook. We got here by breaking it. We’re a disruptor that now plays on a higher tier, and we’re still raising the bar for millions of customers nationwide. If you want to work somewhere that sets the standard instead of matching it, this is your place.
This is an 11-week paid learning experience where you’ll do real work, not busywork. You’ll build relationships with other interns and leaders across the company, and you’ll be paired with mentors who will challenge you to grow skills that matter. We’ll give you hands-on projects with real stakes, and we expect your creativity and sharp ideas to make an immediate impact. You’ll work alongside T-Mobile employees who have your back and who still believe the best ideas can come from anyone.
What It's Like:
Help shape how AI agents and developer tools can make software engineering at T-Mobile more effective. This internship focuses on the intersection of software engineering, large language models, and practical workflow automation. Work may span agent integrations, developer experience, testing, and evaluation, with an emphasis on reliable and maintainable solutions. You will collaborate with engineers to turn real workflow problems into working prototypes and use evidence to understand where AI helps and where human judgment remains essential.
What You'll Do:
Build a scoped AI agent or developer-tooling project that addresses a concrete engineering workflow. Implement integrations with approved APIs or tools, add automated tests and evaluation cases, and instrument the solution so its behavior can be inspected and debugged. Compare results against a baseline to assess correctness, usefulness, and failure modes. Document your design decisions, incorporate feedback, and demonstrate the resulting prototype along with clear recommendations for next steps.
Key Responsibilities:
• Partner with engineers to define a focused use case, requirements, and measurable success criteria.
• Build and test agent tools, API integrations, or developer workflow automations using Python and/or TypeScript.
• Create evaluation datasets and regression tests to measure quality and identify failure modes.
• Add logging and tracing to investigate errors, latency, and tool behavior while following data-handling and security requirements.
• Document implementation choices, share progress, and deliver a working demonstration and handoff.
What It Takes :
Foundational programming skills in Python and/or TypeScript/JavaScript, demonstrated through coursework, research, personal projects, or equivalent experience. Familiarity with Git, APIs, debugging, and automated testing. Interest in LLMs, AI agents, and developer experience, plus a willingness to test assumptions and critically review AI-generated code and outputs. Ability to break down ambiguous problems, communicate clearly, and collaborate on feedback. Exposure to agent frameworks, MCP, RAG, evaluation tools, CI/CD, or cloud platforms is helpful but not required. No specific certifications are preferred.
Minimum Qualifications
- At least 18 years of age
- Legally authorized to work in the United States now and in the future
- Must have one or more course(s) remaining in a Bachelors or Graduate degree program post internship
- Employees of T-Mobile or Metro by T-Mobile are ineligible for external Summer Internships, please see Magenta Accelerator if interested
Relocation assistance will be provided to program participants who reside more than 50 miles from the internship location.
Intern wages range from $27/hour to $50/hour. The successful candidate’s actual pay will be based on education/STEM vs non-STEM designation.
Never stop growing!

We love helping our employees grow in their careers, because it’s that shared drive to aim high that drives our business and our culture forward. By applying for this career opportunity, you’re living our values while investing in your career growth–and we applaud it. You’re unstoppable!

url:https://www.metacareers.com/jobs/166:
Our team builds synthetic data and simulation tools & infra to train AI agents that use computers to complete everyday tasks. We are looking for a PhD intern to research how to generate tasks that require stronger planning and reasoning, with an initial focus on planning and navigation workflows.
The intern will design generation methods, build prototypes, and run experiments to understand which kinds of task difficulty help agents learn. The project combines research with practical engineering and offers an opportunity to contribute to training data for frontier models.
url:https://www.metacareers.com/jobs/140:
Meta Reality Labs brings together researchers and engineers to invent the future of visual computing.
Our teams develop technologies that enable people to capture, create, understand, and interact with immersive visual experiences across Meta’s products and AR/VR platforms. We work at the intersection of artificial intelligence, computer vision, computer graphics, and computational photography.
Our research spans 3D generation across assets, characters, and worlds, together with rigging and animation. We are working on neural 3D generation (e.g., mesh, gaussian splats, topology, texture) as well as agentic 3D generation and understanding (e.g., 3D code generation, robotic simulation).
As a Research Scientist Intern, you will help advance the state of the art through an ambitious research project.
You will collaborate with researchers and engineers to develop new models, representations, datasets, and evaluation methods—with opportunities to publish your work and influence future products used by people around the world.
url:https://www.metacareers.com/jobs/175:
Meta Fundamental AI Research (FAIR) is looking for Research Scientist Interns to rethink the systems that power frontier AI research. AI workloads are changing faster than the infrastructure beneath them: large-scale training, inference, evaluation, and autonomous AI agents now compete for the same accelerators. Many of the resulting questions about how to share, schedule, and operate compute at scale have no established answers.
Our team works across the stack, from hardware-software co-design and performance modeling to cluster scheduling, resource management, and the infrastructure needs of agentic AI. The goal is to make AI research faster, more efficient, and more predictable at any scale.
In this role you will embed with a world-class, multi-disciplinary team of research scientists and engineers to pursue an open research question end to end- from problem framing through experimentation to publication. Interns are expected to drive their own project with mentorship, not execute a predefined task list. Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty four (24) weeks long, and we have various start dates throughout the year.

- Our Summer 2027 Internship Program is 2 months and will run from June 1st to July 31st
- All interns are expected to be on-site within commuting distance from Freeport, ME for the full 2-month program
As an intern in our Engineering Department, you will be given specific projects to complete throughout the summer within your department and the results of your projects will have a direct impact on our company.
Position Purpose: Apply Industrial Engineering methodologies in planning activities for moderately complex equipment and workflow layouts in the Order Fulfillment Center and the Manufacturing Division. May assign duties to non-exempt technicians.
Responsibilities:
- Assist in compiling labor cost data to help manage existing and future operational or production activities.
- Prepare feasibility studies relevant to capital expenditures for components of new processes. Perform basic cost studies and ergonomic analyses to support recommendations. Share data with more senior engineers.
- Assist Intermediate Industrial Engineer in compiling labor and material cost estimates for new equipment.
- May mentor and support non-exempt technicians
Analyze methods, layout and workflow of component processes of basic size and moderate complexity to increase efficiency and productivity.
- Utilize ergonomic analysis to develop safest methods and layout of workspace.
- Determine most effective work methods for components of operations or production and recommend improvements and changes.
- Design workplace layout and assist in determining cost of improvements.
Compile and assimilate data related to components of operational or production processes.
- Determine standard time for each operation using time study analysis of motion patterns.
- Establish standard data for operations or production.
- Maintain current labor standards.
Share engineered standards and ergonomic information with employees.
- Communicate changes in standards to leadership.
- Work with employees upon the implementation of new standards and ergonomic improvements.
- Serve as a resource to supervision in addressing questions and concerns related to standards and ergonomics.
Skills and Qualifications:
- BSIE/BSIT or other engineering
- Some applicable Industrial Engineering experience
- Strength in applying Industrial Engineering practices and methodologies
- Strength in understanding operations decisions and impacts to changes
- Some understanding of financial impacts to business decisions
- Basic project management experience
- Demonstrated effective relationship and team building skills
- Demonstrated success delivering results with focus on process effectiveness
- Proven ability to work collaboratively with diverse groups

wd:oceanspray:r5426:
Ocean Spray Cranberries, Inc. is a leading multi-national consumer packaged goods company (CPG), specializing in the sales of Cranberry products. Formed as a Grower-Owned Cooperative in 1930, Ocean Spray® is owned by a diverse network of over 700 Cranberry Farmers. These growers, many of which are multi-generational farming families who have been a part of the Cooperative for decades, are the foundation for all that we do.  Ever aware of our long-term commitment to our Growers, we care deeply about sustainability— in regard to both our business metrics and the environment—and believe that a focus on strong environmental management is an integral part of the way we manage our business.
At Ocean Spray, our purpose is to generate a passion for our Farmer’s fruit around the world by connecting our farms to families for a better life. Living out our values of Grower Mindset, Sustainable Results, Integrity Above All, Inclusive Teamwork (GRIT) has made Ocean Spray® a creative, entrepreneurial, energetic, and fun place to work.
Who We are Looking For:
The process development team at Ocean Spray Cranberries is committed to producing our high-quality branded products in locations throughout the world as well as exploring innovative technologies to unlock the potential of cranberries for the future. We fulfill that commitment by designing and executing scale-up strategies to bring the vision of our talented product developers to life at full-scale. We work in the laboratory, in our own scale-up plant, and at production facilities located in the United State and abroad. As an intern for this team, we are looking for someone passionate about data analysis and engineering, who will work with cross functional teams to execute their collective vision.
What You Will Do & What You Will Learn:
You will gain hands-on experience with mass and heat transfer while supporting the development and improvement of food and beverage manufacturing processes. You will work alongside an accomplished team of engineers with varied backgrounds and experiences.
What You’ll Need:
- Currently pursuing or recently completed (as of Winter/Spring 2026) Bachelor or Master of Science in Engineering (Chemical, Mechanical, or Food)
- Previous Laboratory or Work Experience
- Microsoft Office Proficiency and advanced Excel knowledge.
- Curiosity and will to learn
- Knowledge and Basic understanding of Experimental Design
Hourly Pay Range:
$25.00 - $32.00
Duration & Location:
- Position will start June 8, 202 7 , and run for 6 months.
- Traditional work week but with summer Fridays 8:00am-12:30 pm; flexibility and off-site work may be required for project travel, experimental test runs, customer discovery.
- This position will be based at our corporate headquarters in Lakeville, MA (about 45 minutes south of Boston, Exit 6 off Route 495), with opportunities to work at our pilot plant located at 152 Bridge Street in Middleboro, MA.
Who We Are:
You might have our iconic cranberry juice in your fridge or have gotten into heated holiday debate about what’s better - canned or fresh cranberry sauce. But did you know that the hardworking people growing the superfruit in our products are 700 family farmers that own our cooperative? They entrust us with what is most precious to them to create new and innovative products that will delight consumers and grow this beloved brand today and into the future.
Team members, farmers, consumers and communities alike--we value what makes us unique and strive to connect our farms to families for a better life by living our values:
- G rower Mindset – We embrace our grower-owners innovative spirit and heritage through confidence, learning and focus on the future.
- Sustainable R esults – Guided by purpose, we are focused on delivering results for our grower-owners.
- I ntegrity Above All – We are ethical, doing the right thing for our grower-owners, customers, consumers and each other
- Inclusive T eamwork – We build diverse and inclusive teams that strengthen our cooperative.
All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or veteran status.

Join Niagara Bottling, a leading beverage manufacturer built on the mission of providing high-quality affordable beverages since 1963. Through innovation, collaboration, and a shared commitment to ​embracing adventure, we are revolutionizing the beverage manufacturing industry while creating opportunities for Team Members to make an impact. Together, we are connected by possibility.
Manufacturing Intern - Louisville
Interns spend the summer working directly on high impact projects within one of our manufacturing departments. Interns work in a fast-paced, innovative environment where they will be asked to be a key part of our operations. During this 10-12 week internship, participants are encouraged to think outside the box and use a continuous improvement mindset to approach projects and come up with solutions. Interns gain hands on experience in work related to their field of study. Essential Functions
- Rotate through multiple areas of the manufacturing plant to gain an overall understanding of the manufacturing process.
- Provide support to plant team members to gain hands on experience with production methods, machines, and processes.
- Assist with research on new and existing projects and support major decision making.
- Receive intellectual and creative opportunities to tackle a problem and develop proposed solutions.
- Attend department meetings and action plan based on feedback.
- Learn to collaborate and communicate across all levels of the organization.
- Create a presentation on internship experience, projects, and outcomes and present to department leadership.
- Please note this job description is not designed to contain a comprehensive list of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without prior notice.
Qualifications
- Minimum Qualifications:
- 0 Years – Experience in Field or similar manufacturing environment
- 0 Years – Experience in Position
- 0 Years – Experience managing people/projects
*experience may include a combination of work experience and education
- Preferred Qualifications:
- 2 Years– Experience in Field or similar manufacturing environment
- 2 Years – Experience working in Position
- 2 Years – Experience managing people/projects
*experience may include a combination of work experience and education
Competencies
This position embodies the values of Niagara’s LIFE competency model, focusing on the following key drivers of success:
- Lead Like an Owner
- Makes safety the number one priority
- Keeps alert for safety issues and escalates immediately
- Effectively prioritizes tasks based on department goals
- Shows respect to others and confronts interpersonal issues directly
- Prioritizes resolution of customer issues effectively
- Responds promptly and honors commitments to internal and external customers
- InnovACT
- Makes recommendations to continuously improve policies, methods, procedures, and/or products
- Demonstrates adaptability by reacting appropriately to unexpected changes in situations or circumstances
- Increases performance through greater efficiency
- Find a Way
- Seeks to develop technical knowledge through learning from other experts
- Understands interdepartmental impact of individual decisions and actions
- Seeks solutions rather than placing blame
- Empowered to be Great
- Consistently looks for ways to improve one’s self through growth and development opportunities
- Communicates clearly and promptly up, down, and across
- Communicates effectively to manage expectations
Education
- Minimum Required:
- Current Junior/Rising Senior pursuing a Bachelor's Degree
Certification/License:
- Required: N/A
- Preferred: N/A
Foreign Language
- Required: None Required
- Preferred: None Required
Benefits
Our Total Rewards package is thoughtfully designed to support both you and your family:
Regular full-time team members are offered a comprehensive benefits package, while part-time, intern, and seasonal team members are offered a limited benefits package.
- Paid Time Off for holidays, sick time, and vacation time
- Paid parental and caregiver leaves
- Medical, including virtual care options
- Dental
- Vision
- 401(k) with company match
- Health Savings Account with company match
- Flexible Spending Accounts
- Expanded mental wellbeing benefits including free counseling sessions for all team members and household family members
- Family Building Benefits including enhanced fertility benefits for IVF and fertility preservation plus adoption, surrogacy, and Doula reimbursements
- Income protection including Life and AD&D, short and long-term disability, critical illness and an accident plan
- Special discount programs including pet plans, pre-paid legal services, identity theft, car rental, airport parking, etc.
- Tuition reimbursement, college savings plan and scholarship opportunities
- And more!

Category Labs (formerly known as Monad Labs) is a team of systems engineers and researchers on a mission to design and build at the frontier of decentralized technology. We strive to deliver significant improvements over existing blockchain solutions. After raising $225M in Series A funding, led by Paradigm, we are growing our team.

We’re the team behind Monad, a high-performance, EVM-compatible Layer 1. We write the core software that runs it: a parallel-execution EVM https://github.com/category-labs/monad, a custom state database, and a BFT consensus client https://github.com/category-labs/monad-bft, all developed in the open.




THE ROLE

 - We’re hiring Summer Research Interns to pursue advanced research in mechanism design, cryptoeconomics, distributed systems, programming languages, cryptography, and governance. This list isn’t exhaustive; if you bring a valuable and relevant perspective, we encourage you to apply.

 - This internship offers a rare chance to work at the frontier of decentralized systems: advancing the underlying science and technology while delivering real impact at scale.

 - Research projects will draw on the challenges of building a first-of-its-kind blockchain, as well as new directions that decentralized systems make possible. You’re also welcome to propose your own projects.

 - You’ll learn from Category Labs’ researchers, engineers, and fellow interns, while contributing as an independent and equal peer.

 - Depending on your availability and the needs of the project, the internship can be extended into part-time employment and may lead to future collaborations.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Conduct novel, rigorous research on the topics above.

 - Contribute to technical publications, including peer-reviewed papers, blog posts, and white papers.

 - Partner with the engineering team to build prototypes, run simulations, and design experiments that test your models and assumptions.

 - Engage with team members and visiting researchers to refine ideas and share insights from your own work.



Past interns have shipped real work (small sample):

 - A Private RPC for Public Blockchains https://www.category.xyz/blogs/a-private-rpc-for-public-blockchains: Introduced write-public ORAM, a new primitive for reading blockchain state without revealing what you read, and built an open-source private RPC that keeps up with Monad’s throughput.

 - Timing Games in Responsive Consensus Protocols https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.25144: Modeled why validators delay block proposals, and designed dynamic block rewards that make proposing promptly the winning strategy.

 - On the Geographic Incentives of Multiple Concurrent Proposers https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.33958: Proved how proposers choose where to locate in multi-proposer systems, and when that leads to co-location versus geographic diversity.




WHO YOU ARE

 - You’re currently enrolled in a PhD program in computer science, economics, mathematics, the social sciences, or a related field. Exceptional master’s and undergraduate students will also be considered.

 - You’re passionate about decentralized systems and have enough foundational knowledge to hit the ground running.

 - You communicate clearly and can explain complex ideas in simple terms, making research accessible to a broader audience.

 - You have a clear research vision and the drive to pursue innovative ideas aligned with Category Labs’ mission.

 - You’re collaborative, self-motivated, and adaptable, eager to tackle hard problems and pick up new concepts quickly in a fast-paced environment.




WHY WORK WITH US

 - Challenging problems: You’ll work on extremely challenging problems with massive impact. See our Blogs https://www.category.xyz/blogs and Publications & Talks https://www.category.xyz/papers-talks for a flavor of the problems we are solving in the real world.

 - Huge opportunity: The Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) standard is ubiquitous, but existing EVM-compatible chains are very slow. Monad’s core innovations offer developers the best of both worlds (portability and performance) and are a game-changer for mass user adoption in crypto.

 - The right team: You’ll be part of a small, exceptional team (engineers and researchers make up 90% of the team).

 - Open by default: Our core software is public on GitHub.

 - Culture: We’re a lean team working together to achieve very ambitious goals. We are united in our culture of collaboration, low ego, and high-quality output. As an early member of our team, you’ll help to shape our culture.

 - Compensation: You’ll receive competitive pay, plus housing support.

 - Resources and growth: We’re well-capitalized, with backing https://x.com/monad_xyz/status/1777687376136982767 from leading venture funds like Paradigm, Electric Capital, Greenoaks, Dragonfly, and Coinbase Ventures. We keep a lean team, and this is a rare opportunity to join. You’ll learn a lot and grow as our company scales.




HOW WE USE AI

We’re an AI-native team, and we expect researchers to use AI and adapt to the technology as it evolves. A few things we believe:

 - AI is leverage, not a crutch. You must stand behind the correctness and quality of your work (including writing and presentation) even if it was produced with the help of AI.

 - As part of the research process, you must understand the output from AI before sharing it with your collaborators. Any output that you were not able to review must be marked as such.




INTERNSHIP DETAILS

 - The internship runs roughly 12 weeks, between May 17 and August 30.

 - Residency in New York City is strongly preferred but not required.

 - The anticipated rate for this role is $4,500 per week, plus a $500 per week housing stipend or corporate housing. Pay may vary based on experience and scope.




APPLICATION AND TIMELINE

Please include, in addition to the application below:

 - Resume/CV

 - Letters of recommendation (1-2 letters, optional but recommended).
   
   - Recommenders should email their letters of support to recruiting@category.xyz with the "[name of the applicant], Research Intern 2027" in the subject line.

 - For full consideration, please submit applications by December 7, 2026.




VISA & WORK AUTHORIZATION

 - We welcome international applicants and will consider visa and work authorization support on a case-by-case basis. Please note your current status and location in your application so we can discuss options early.

Job Description
Solidigm is seeking talented and motivated graduate students for our Hardware, Electrical Validation & Product Engineering Internships in the United States. This evergreen posting supports multiple internship opportunities across electrical validation, hardware bring-up, signal integrity, SSD product engineering, and performance characterization.
As an intern, you will work on real engineering challenges supporting Solidigm's data center SSD products, including testing and validating hardware and system behavior, analyzing electrical and reliability data, and supporting product characterization.
This internship is ideal for graduate students who enjoy hands-on problem solving, using lab equipment, and analyzing complex data to help bring data center storage products from development through validation.
Key Responsibilities
Interns may be assigned one or more of the following responsibilities based on project needs, team priorities, and individual strengths:
- Support validation and characterization of SSD hardware, components, interfaces, and platforms; execute test plans and verify electrical and functional requirements.
- Assist with validation and debug of high-speed signals and interfaces such as PCIe, including signal-integrity, power-integrity, and interoperability investigations.
- Use lab equipment—oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, protocol analyzers, and automated test systems—to collect data and troubleshoot issues.
- Validate SSD behavior in system environments; reproduce issues and analyze logs to support root-cause investigations.
- Support product characterization of performance, power, thermals, and reliability; analyze trends and communicate findings.
- Develop or improve test scripts, dashboards, and automation frameworks to improve validation efficiency and reporting.
- Analyze benchmark, telemetry, and test-log data to identify trends, anomalies, or product risks.
- Support technical analysis of SSD products, customer requirements, and competitive benchmarking.
- Collaborate with cross-functional hardware, firmware, validation, and product teams; document test methods and findings.
Qualifications
Minimum Qualifications
- Currently pursuing a Master's or Ph.D. degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline.
- Foundational knowledge of analog and digital circuits, computer architecture, or electronic systems.
- Experience with a programming or scripting language such as Python, C, C++, or MATLAB.
- Familiarity with Linux-based development or test environments.
- Strong analytical, debugging, and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a technical team environment.
Preferred Qualifications
- Experience using lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, or protocol analyzers.
- Familiarity with PCIe, NVMe, NAND flash, SSDs, or data center server platforms.
- Coursework or project experience in signal integrity, power integrity, or electronic validation.
- Experience with hardware bring-up, board-level debug, or system integration.
- Exposure to test automation, data collection, or test-framework development.
- Familiarity with performance benchmarking, telemetry, or log analysis.
- Interest in technical marketing, applications engineering, or customer-facing technical communication.
Additional Information
What You'll Gain
As a Solidigm intern, you will have the opportunity to:
- Work on meaningful projects tied to real data center SSD products and engineering priorities.
- Gain hands-on experience with hardware validation, electrical characterization, and lab automation.
- Collaborate with experienced engineers, architects, and cross-functional teams.
- Develop practical skills in lab measurement, debugging, and technical communication.
- Present your work and contribute to solutions that may influence future products.
- Grow your professional network through mentorship and intern program activities.

Job Description
At Bosch Research in Pittsburgh, we are looking for an enthusiastic research intern to advance the state of the art in foundation models for wireless sensing and perception. The intern will explore how large-scale self-supervised and multimodal learning can enable generalizable representations of human activities and environments from radio-frequency (RF) signals and wireless channel measurements.
The research will focus on developing foundation models that learn reusable representations from diverse wireless sensing data and transfer across sensing tasks, environments, devices, and users. Potential applications include human presence detection, activity recognition, motion understanding, and fine-grained behavioral and contextual understanding.
The intern will work closely with Bosch researchers on the following responsibilities:
- Develop novel foundation-model architectures and representation-learning methods for RF signals and wireless channel measurements.
- Investigate self-supervised, contrastive, generative, and multimodal learning approaches for large-scale wireless sensing data.
- Study model generalization and adaptation across environments, users, devices, and downstream perception tasks.
- Develop and evaluate methods for fine-tuning, few-shot learning, or zero-shot transfer to downstream wireless perception applications.
- Conduct comprehensive experimental evaluations and comparisons with state-of-the-art approaches.
- Develop a proof-of-concept demonstration of the proposed technology.
- Summarize research findings and contribute to a high-quality research publication and/or patent application.
Required Qualifications:
- Currently enrolled in a PhD program in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Robotics, or a related field.
- Strong background in machine learning, deep learning, or representation learning.
- Experience working with wireless sensing or RF signal data, including channel measurements or related time-series signals.
- Strong understanding of modern deep-learning architectures and training techniques.
- 2+ years of programming experience in Python and strong proficiency with PyTorch.
- Ability to independently design, implement, and evaluate research ideas.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Qualifications
- Experience with self-supervised learning, foundation models, transformers, contrastive learning, or generative models.
- Experience with wireless sensing for applications such as presence detection, activity recognition, localization, or smart-home sensing.
- Experience collecting and processing wireless channel measurements, complex I/Q samples, signal-strength data, or related RF sensing data.
- Experience with RF data-acquisition pipelines, wireless signal preprocessing, or time-series feature extraction.
- Experience with multimodal learning involving wireless signals, language, vision, audio, or other sensor modalities.

- Strong publication record in leading machine learning, sensing, mobile computing, or robotics venues such as ICLR, NeurIPS, ICML, SenSys, IPSN, MobiSys, MobiCom, IMWUT/UbiComp, or IROS.

The Bosch Research and Technology Center North America with offices in Sunnyvale, California, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and Cambridge, Massachusetts is a part of the global Bosch Group (www.bosch.com), a company with over 70 billion euro revenue, 400,000 employees worldwide, a very diverse product portfolio, and a history spanning over 125 years. Job Description
We have multiple openings for Postdoctoral Researcher Positions to conduct mentored research in atomistic and data-driven modeling of materials for energy applications. You will work closely with a multidisciplinary team in support of projects sponsored by the Basic Energy Sciences, Transportation Technologies Offices, and Office of Electricity within the Department of Energy, and internal LDRD programs. This position is within the Quantum Simulations Group within the Materials for Emerging Applications and Extreme Conditions section of the Materials Science Division in the Physical and Life Sciences Directorate.
This position requires full-time on-site presence due to the nature of the work.
Note: This is a two-year Postdoctoral appointment with the possibility of extension to a maximum of three years. Eligible candidates are recent PhDs within five years of the month of the degree award at time of hire date.
You will
- Perform electronic structure theory-based simulations of complex materials, such as oxides and multi-element systems.
- Perform thermodynamic and kinetic analyses of chemical reactions and phase transitions at surfaces and interfaces.
- Perform non-equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations & first-principles calculations to study materials response under externally applied stimuli.
- Derive structure-composition-property relationships using statistical, analytical, and machine-learning based methodologies.
- Develop machine-learning interatomic potentials and surrogate models based on physics-informed descriptors for property evaluation and prediction.

- Experience in the application of density functional theory and/or advanced electronic structure theory for simulating complex materials, including oxides and multi-element systems
- Experience performing large-scale molecular dynamics simulations on high-performance computing environments.

Proficient verbal and written communication skills to collaborate effectively in a team environment, prepare written reports and present and explain technical information.
- Interpersonal skills necessary to interact with scientists, engineers and other technical and administrative staff in a collaborative, multidisciplinary team environment.
